README.docx:
HR Systems Knowledge Base
This SharePoint folder is the HR Systems team's searchable index of How To Guides and Change Management knowledge articles. It currently holds 251 documents — 201 How To Guides across 15 topic areas, and 50 Change Management knowledge articles across 7 topics — sourced from the team's working library.
What's in here
Dashboard.html — open this in your browser to search and filter the full index. Click "Open in SharePoint" on any result to open the document.
How_to_Guides_Index.docx — Word-format directory of all 201 How To Guides with a clickable table of contents.
Change_Management_Index.docx — Word-format directory of all 50 Change Management articles with a clickable table of contents.
How To Guides\ — the source documents (201 files).
Change Management\ — the source documents (50 files).
How to use the dashboard
Open Dashboard.html in your browser (Edge or Chrome both work).
Use the search bar to filter by keyword across titles, sections, and summaries.
Click "Open in SharePoint" to open any document, or "Copy link" to grab the SharePoint URL.
Adding or updating a document
Email Kevin (work2@lelitte.co.uk). He maintains the index and re-runs the build when documents are added or revised.
Last refreshed: April 2026.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this guide is to provide an overview of the  CorePortal Payroll Employee Self-Service 
(ESS) widgets and how they are used. This includes: 
• A list of Payroll ESS widgets. 
• How to configure tabs and add widgets. 
• All menu options and other configurable elements required to support the tabs and widgets. 
 
 
 
 
1.2. What is ESS for Payroll? 
Employee Self-Service (ESS) widgets allow employees to view and interact with their employee records 
on CorePortal. For Payroll, there are widgets specifically designed to allow employees to interact with 
their payroll information, e.g. payslips, bank accounts etc.  
 
These widgets are shared with employees on the Employee Dashboard on CorePortal. 
 
 
1.3. List of Payroll ESS Widgets 
The following table provides a list of the CorePortal widgets that are available specifically for Payroll.  
Widget Description 
My Payslip Allows employees to view their payslips. 
My Bank Accounts 
Allows employees to view and update their bank 
account details.  
Tax Details Allows employees to view their current tax details.  
P60 Documents Allows employees to view their P60 Documents.  
PRD60 Certs Allows employees to view their PRD60 Certs.  
Important Dates 
Allows employees to view their next pay date and 
next booked time off date.  
 
 
 
 
  
 Note: This document only covers payroll ESS widgets.

4. CoreHESA Generation Process  
4.1. HESA Generation Process Overview 
The following is a summary of the key stages in the HESA generation process: 
 
1. Ensure the year has been rolled forward.  
The CoreHESA module should be set up for the current reporting year. See 4.9 HESA New 
Year Rollover Process  for steps on how to roll the year forward and confirm that this is 
ready for the new year. 
 
2. Confirm configuration for the new year. 
It is recommended to review the CoreHESA configuration for exemptions and field settings, 
to confirm that these meet the current year’s requirements. There may be a need to update 
the configuration for the current year e.g. 
• To reflect changes from HESA to the required fields  e.g. map new fields for 
2018/2019. 
• To reflect changes to the underlying PeopleXD reference data. 
Refer to the guidance in 3. Configuring HESA for further details on how to view and update 
configuration for the various configurable elements.  
 
3. Create the initial data set (and repeat as necessary). 
Generate the first set of HESA records from PeopleXD data.  
See 4.2 Generate Data - Create the Initial Data Set for guidance on how to complete this. 
This can be done many times to allow you to validate the person and contract records 
created based on your configuration. You many need to repeat this many times, to capture 
changes you make to the configuration. 
 
4. Mapping engine picks up changes to employee records. 
Once the initial data set has been generated, the CoreHESA mapping engine and tracker 
log pick up changes to employee and contract records on PeopleXD. These are run through 
the mapping engine and the relevant person and contract records are updated 
automatically. 
See 4.3 HESA Mapping Engine and HESA Tracker Log for full details on this step. 
HESA - User Guide

5. Correct Data / Bulk Upload Data 
You can directly update the CoreHESA records without impacting the PeopleXD record i.e. 
you can change the actual HESA fields directly on the person or contract record if needed. 
This can be done manually for an individual or in bulk using the data load screens.  
See 4.6.5 Uploading Data / Corrections for full details why and how they can be achieved. 
 
6. Generate the XML file. 
This can be done at any stage from when the initial data set is created. This is a useful way 
to validate the configuration. The XML can be loaded to the HESA validation engine. Any 
errors flagged by HESA can then be corrected on the system e.g. 
• Changes to configuration. 
• Manually correct a person or contract record. 
• Bulk upload changes. 
Once all changes have been applied, the XML can be generated for the final time and 
submitted to HESA. 
 
7. New Year Roll Over process 
This is the same as step 1 and ensure s that you are setting up CoreHESA for the next 
reporting year. This can be done at any time after the XML has been sent but must be done 
before you begin processing HESA for the next reporting year.

4.3. HESA Mapping Engine and HESA Tracker Log  
When the HESA records are being generated, the HESA Mapping engine is responsible for mapping 
the PeopleXD employee and contract data, to the corresponding CoreHESA  person and contract 
records. For each record, each field is processed in the mapping engine in the following order: 
 
1. Is the employee exempt? 
2. Is there a default value set? 
3. Apply SQL Mapping Rules 
4. Apply CoreHR Mapping References 
5. Business rule validation engine (optional)  
 
The HESA tracker log is a record of CoreHESA records that have been created or updated. Once the 
initial data set (Full Generation) has been created for the current reporting year, any changes to 
employee / contract records in PeopleXD will be processed by the HESA tracker log and mapping 
engine. This will apply any rules, mappings and default values as appropriate.  This information is 
passed to the tracker log by a scheduled job that runs every 10 minutes. This includes: 
• Any new employees created on PeopleXD. 
• Any updates to existing employee records that have already been processed. Update s 
apply to the following: 
o Salary Details including Allowances  
o Qualifications Details  
o Appointment Details  
o Professional Body Details  
o Employment History Details  
o HESA UDF Details (Not Standard UDFs)  
o Diversity Details  
o Personal Profile Details  
When a new starter is created in PeopleXD, or an update above occurs then it will be processed by 
the HESA Tracker Log. For each update that is created a corresponding row will be visible on the 
tracker log as seen on the main screen:

1. Overview 
 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 
The purpose of this guide is to help users configure the Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility.  
Parallel Run allows users to report on the parallel tables and to review or report  where differences 
may have occurred in the transferring of hours for a previously completed back office Live Run.  
 
By using the Parallel Ru n, you can compare to existing Live runs completed through back  office 
and ensure there are no errors before migrating to live running of the Portal version of Generate 
Timesheets. 
 
This is particularly useful for those sites with large amounts of hours being transferred  and is an 
added backup to those who are migrating from using the previous back office feature to the one 
on Portal. 
 
The step-by-step process of retrieving hours and transferring them to payroll is covered in a 
separate document, see WFM v28 Generate Timesheets User Guide.

1.3. What is the Parallel Mode? 
 
Generate Timesheets in Parallel Mode. 
 
As mentioned in the previous section, Generate Timesheets has been moved from the back office 
to Portal.  In order to support the transition, the portal version of Generate Timesheets runs  a 
parallel mode to support the re-generation of a previously transferred period that was completed 
via the back office. 
 
The features within the Parallel Mode are the following: 
 
• WFM company:  Parallel Mode can be enabled per WFM company.  If a client has more 
than one company using Portal, the parallel mode can be run separately for each. 
 
• Validation: Parallel mod e is run to validate those calendars or periods which have 
previously been migrated to show that there are no discrepancies found. 
 
 
• Leavers: Parallel Transfers do not impact the live mode.  Employees are not marked as 
leavers. 
 
• Analysis and Review: Parallel Run details are stored into backup tables for analysis and 
review.  For further information see Tables for Parallel Run.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
This document provides you with guidance on how to move to Workforce Management on CorePortal 
(“Portal”) for both administrator and manager users. The document also provides training material on 
how Workforce Management in Portal can be used to support: 
• Existing processes previously completed in Back Office such as:  
o Maintaining the WFM elements of an employee’s record 
o Maintaining employee schedules 
o Assigning and maintaining balance assignment 
o Recording and maintaining absences 
o Viewing and maintaining time and attendance information 
o Exception management 
o Sign off hours 
o Generate Timesheets 
o Running future calculations  
o Setting up certain reference data including shift  types, work groups, and personalised 
paycode groups 
• New functionality in Portal: 
o New WFM Configuration Area 
o Replacement of Employee's Appointments – Transfer Remaining Entitlement and 
Absence Records 
 
 
 
This guide covers the steps required to move both manager users and admin users to WFM on Portal.  
Managers will continue t o access the Workforce Management Dashboard (aka WFM Manager 
Dashboard), while admin users will use the new WFM Admin Dashboard. 
Note: Occupational Absence and Roster are not included within the scope of this document.  
Roster screens were previously available on Portal, and no additional screens are included here. 
Some existing Roster screens have been made available on Person Maintenance – see section 
3.11 for admins and section 8.1.1 for managers. 
The Occupational Absence screens have been available on the Payroll Dashboard from Feature 
Pack 10. Recording of absences in WFM is covered with the scope of this document.

The Workforce Management Admin dashboard is where a WFM administrator can manage their WFM 
related processes on Portal. To access the WFM Admin Dashboard  users will need to be assigned 
menu access. A specific menu profile will be available on your environment to grant access for each 
feature on the WFM Admin Dashboard. Details on how to configure your menu profile for WFM admin 
and complete this step is outlined in Section 5.1 below. 
 
Once assigned access, t he WFM Admin  Dashboard can be  accessed by selecting WFM Admin  
Dashboard from the quick jump menu.

object.  
For example, if searching for the tab called “WFM Configuration”, the Quick Jump will return:

2.2. Dashboard Overview 
The Workforce Management Admin dashboard contains 8 tabs as standard – WFM Person 
Maintenance, Generate Timesheets, Calculate Hours, WFM Configuration, Advance Period, Employee 
Calendars, Sign Off Hours, and Balance Maintenance. 
 
 
Note: The Employee Calendars and Balance Maintenance features are available from Feature 
Pack 15. Feature Pack 15 is available on UAT from 04 October 2021 and will be available on 
Production from 25 October 2021.  
The Sign Off Hours  screen and Generate Timesheets improvements are available from Feature 
Pack 14. Feature Pack 14 is available on UAT from 20 September 2021 and will be available on 
Production from 11 October 21. 
All other features are currently available on UAT and Production.

6.1. What is Parallel Mode? 
Note: You only need to review this section if you currently run generate timesheets in the back 
office. If you run generate timesheets but currently do this on Portal, you do not need to review this 
section. Also, if you do not run generate timesheets you do not need to review this section. 

 
 
Page 43 of 93 
When Parallel Mode is enabled for Generate Timesheets, you can generate timesheets on Portal for a 
CoreTime input period that was previously transferred in  Live mode from the  back office. Parallel 
timesheets from WFM will be transferred to a parallel table which will allow you to run reconciliation 
reports against what was actually transferred to Payroll when the same period was completed from back 
office.  
Please review Section 1 of the WFM V28: Generate Timesheets Parallel Run User Guide  for more 
information. Section 1.3.4 of the same guide will show you how to enable Parallel Mode, as this will be 
disabled by default. 
 
6.2. How do I Complete a Parallel Run? 
Please see Section 2 of the WFM V28: Generate Timesheets Parallel Run User Guide for the steps 
to run Generate Timesheets in Parallel Mode, and for the steps to create and run reports from Insight 
to reconcile the parallel transfer to the live transfer. 
You can complete multiple parallels ahead of your retirement date. Once you are happy that the 
timesheets that are transferring via Portal match what is transferring via back office, Parallel Mode can 
be disabled. This means that timesheets will now be tra nsferring directly to Payroll when generate 
timesheets is run from Portal.  
You will need to ensure that you have at least one Generate Timesheets parallel completed on 
your Production environment ahead of your retirement date, as the TAF019 Generate Timesheets 
screen in back office will not be available after your retirement date. 
 
6.3. Should I Run a Parallel on UAT? 
A generate timesheets parallel  on UAT  is not mandatory. T he Generate Timesheets parallel  on 
Production will reconcile timesheets sent via back office with timesheets sent via Portal, which can be 
run for multiple CoreTime periods ahead of your retirement date. However, it is advised to run Generate 
Timesheets in Parallel Mode and in Live mode first on UAT. This will ensure that you are familiar with 
the process for both the parallel mode and the live mode ahead of running these on Production. 
The steps for running a generate timesheets parallel are detailed in section 3 of the WFM V28: Generate 
Timesheets Parallel Run User Guide.

There are two options available when enabling Employee onboarding:

Suitable if you are setting up onboarding for the first time on CoreHR OR you do not intend to

be completed before Employee onboarding is enabled.

To enable Employee onboarding:

available to new starters will not be there anymore and instead Employee Onboarding will 
be made available for employees to complete their tasks i.e. the Social Hub. 
• Employee Onboarding is not available in the Classic UI.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure auto enrolment. This 
will include how to set parameters used to control auto enrolment. 
 
 
1.2. What is Auto Enrolment? 
Auto Enrolment is a government initiative and requires every employer of staff normally working 
in the UK to put their qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and to make contributions 
towards their employee's pension. 
Employees will be automatically enrolled into the workplace pension scheme if they are not 
already active members of a workplace pension scheme that meets a set of minimum standards. 
The employer must make pension contributions to the pension scheme , and the worker may also 
have to contribute. Workers who do not want to join the scheme may opt -out for a three-year 
period. But, employers are required to continue automatically enrolling el igible workers who’ve 
opted out, every three years. 
 
Eligible employees are workers who: 
• Are aged between 22 and State Pension Age; 
• Earn over the earnings threshold, and 
• Work, or ordinarily work in the UK and have a contract of employment (i.e. so is a worker 
and not a self-employed contractor), or who have a contract to provide work and / or 
services personally (so can’t sub-contract to a third party).

Using Pipe "|" Delimiter for CSV Files 
The Data Migration Tool uses Pipe Delimited CSV files only. Files uploaded to the Data Migration Tool 
must be Pipe Delimited.  It is essential to configure your PC to create CSV files using the "|" separator 
and not a comma. If not done, the Data Migration Tool does not recognise the Data Migration Template 
File, and it will fail to upload.  
 
 Note:  
• It is recommended to select all columns and update the type from “General” to “Text.”  
• This ensures that any data fields that require a leading zero are not be automatically updated 
by MS Excel. For example, if this update isn’t applied and a Personnel Number of “000321” is 
entered, Excel automatically removes the leading zeros and update the data to “321.” 
 
 
 Note:  
• Only a .CSV file format that is recognised when uploading.  
• It is important to save the file using the File > Save As option and selecting .CSV file type 
each time the file is amended. This ensures the file saves in the correct format.  
• The name of the file is not important. The file can be saved using any name required. The 
system identifies the file using the template name in row 1.

Table of Contents 4.3. Post Validation for People Management  
The Person and Additional Contract Data Migration File s now validate the information against the 
locked/linked levels specified on the Post Profile Definition. This helps maintain the integrity of the data 
loaded into XD.   
 
  
The Person File can overwrite other levels against the Post Profile, so validation will not apply.  
 
 
 
  
 Example:   
If a Post Profile is locked to a Department, and a different Department is specified on the Person 
File, then the record fails validation.  
 
 
 Example 2:   
The Company and Management Unit are locked/linked levels on the Post Profile Definition, and the 
Person File specifies the Company, the Management Unit and the Location. 
• The Person File  fails if the Company or Management Unit do not match the  Company or 
Management Unit on the Post Profile Definition. 
• However, if the Company or Management Unit on the Person File does match, and the 
Location does not match the Location on the Post Profile Definition – No error generates, the 
Person File creates the employee with the Location specified.

1. Introduction 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the key concepts and terminology that will be 
used on People Management when managing employee contracts.  
 
2. Overview 
 
2.1. Posts & Contracts 
 
A Contract on CoreHR may also be referred to as a Post Appointment. 
• As reviewed in the Managing Post Profiles user guide, all available posts in the company are 
setup and maintained on CoreHR. These posts are used to form the blueprint of an employee 
contract and include key details such as the job title, the location in the organisation, pay scale, 
sanctioned headcount etc. 
• Contracts are created directly from these posts and will inherit these key details. The hr 
administrator may then update the employee’s contract with details specific to that employment 
e.g. start date, contract hours etc. 
 
 
For every new contract activity for an employee on People Management (i.e. new hire, replacement 
contract, additional contract or rehire) the first step is to select a post that has been already set up on 
CoreHR. That post will then be used to form the basis of the new contract for the employee. However, 
the hr administrator will still have the ability to update and amend the details for each individual contract 
of employment, as required. 
 
 
2.2. Access to Posts 
 
Whenever a new contract is to be created on People Management, the first step required is to select a 
post. Wherever the Post drop down list (or Post and Sequence lists) is displayed, the list of posts 
displayed to the end user may vary. This is due to: 
• The user’s HR Users Access. 
• The types of posts that have been setup on CoreHR. 
 
HR Access 
 
Users of the People Management Dashboard must be granted specific access in order to see posts. 
This access is linked directly to the Organisational Hierarchy that has been defined for the organisation. 
It is possible to grant users access to all posts so that they can complete the aforementioned activities 
for all areas of the business. In a more devolved HR team, there may be a requirement to restrict access 
Move to Portal - People Management Contracts Key Concepts 
 
Page 6 of 70  
 
for users to specific groups of posts e.g. all posts in Division A. This is prescribed for each individual user and 
full details on this are available in the CoreHR University User Data Access user guide for this feature. 
 
Post Types 
 
As reviewed in the CoreHR University Managing Post Profiles user guide, the Post Profile records set up on 
CoreHR can be configured as: 
• Auto-Authorised 
• Auto-Commenced 
• Non-Auto 
 
When searching for posts, all auto posts will return, based on the user’s HR Access. 
 
 
However, if a post has been defined as non-auto, this will only be available to the user if a Post Appointment 
has been Planned and Authorised. 
 
 
 
2.3. Calculating the Contract FTE 
 
The FTE on a contract identifies whether the employee is working full-time or part time in that  contract. This 
may be input directly by the hr administrator or CoreHR may calculate this automatically based on other contract 
fields. 
 
The calculation of the FTE is based on the following fields: 
 
 
 
For example: 
 
• Standard Hours per Week = 37.5 
• Mary is contracted work 37.5 Hours pw so 37.5 / 37.5 = 1 FTE 
• Jack is contracted to work 18.75 Hours pw so 18.75 / 37.5 = 0.5 FTE The 
FTE cannot be greater than 1 on an employee’s contract.

5.1 Overview of Start Date Corrections 
 
What Contracts can be Updated? 
 
This functionality is used to change the start date that has been set up for an employee’s contract. This 
is applicable in the following scenarios: 
1. New Hire 
2. Rehire 
3. Additional Contract 
 
 
For options 1 & 2 above: 
1. New Hire: When a start date is changed for the contract that was set up for the employee as a 
new hire, the following dates are updated: 
a. Contract Start Date 
b. Date First Joined 
 
 
2. Rehire: When a start date is changed for the contract that was set up for the employee as a 
rehire, the following dates are updated: 
a. Contract Start Date 
b. Latest Start Date 
 
 
Changes to additional contracts will not result in any update to the Date First Joined or the Rehire Date. 
If the substantive contract is updated, the corresponding Substantive Date is also be updated. 
What Contracts Cannot be Updated? 
 
The start date for the following contracts cannot be updated using the Amend Contract Start Date 
functionality: 
 Replacement Contracts. 
 Contracts that have been processed on Payroll. 
 
What Else is Updated for the Employee’s Contract? 
 
The following elements of the employee’s contract will be reviewed and potentially updated, when the 
start date is changed. 
 Salary 
 Allowance 
 Cost Allocations 
 Pension 
 BIK

Contract amendments refer to any date driven amendments that HR are required to make to an 
employee’s existing contract. 
 
These amendments may be pay impacting e.g. a change in hours. These may also be amendments 
that have no downstream impact on the employee’s salary e.g. change of work group, category etc. 
 
It is possible to record these changes on People Management for an employee’s existing contract. A 
timeline or history of all amendments will be tracked for that contract and are ava ilable to the hr 
administrator to review on screen. 
 
 
8.2 Amendments with No Salary Impact 
 
This refers to the amendment of an existing contract that does not require a corresponding update to 
the employee’s associated salary record. 
 
To amend an employee’s existing contract: 
• Quick jump to the Command Centre widget in People Management. 
• Click View at Employees and Search for the employee. 
• Click View in the employee’s relevant row. 
• Be sure that the correct contract is selected. 
• In the Contracts tab, click Update in the Amendments section.

1. Overview 
The ‘Document and Email Generatio n’ feature on CoreHR allows a user to automatically generate 
documents / letters / emails based on employee data e.g. employee contracts, letters of offer, hr forms 
etc. 
 
This feature is primarily available to users in HR Admin and Recruitment Admin. 
 
Pre-configured templates are created and stored centrally on the system. A user can generate a version 
of this document  (MS Word or PDF)  which may be populated automatically using data held for 
employees in HR Admin and applicants  & interview panel members  in Recruitment. It is possible to 
generate an individual document per record, or multiple versions of the  same document for multiple 
records. Once a document has been generated, there is an option for this to be automatically stored on 
the system against an employee’s record, for future reference. 
 
The main users of this feature will be: 
 HR Administrator 
o Create and manage document and email templates 
o Generate documents and emails in HR Admin 
o Upload documents to employee records 
 Recruitment Administrator 
o Create and manage document and email templates 
o Generate documents and emails in Recruitment Admin 
o Upload documents to applicant records 
 Manager 
o Generate documents for an employee (if designated access to) 
o Review documents for employes on their team 
 Employee  
o Review documents stored against their record 
 
The purpose of this guide is to provide guidance on: 
 Key concepts & terminology associated with this feature 
 How to create and manage templates on CoreHR 
 How to generate and review a document or email for one or many records  
 How to configure CoreHR to enable the feature for the various users who will require access  
  
HR: Document & Email Generation             
 
Page 5 of 75 
1.1. Key Concepts 
1.1.1. Document 
A ‘document’ refers to a file (MS Word or PDF) that can be generated from CoreHR by merging 
employee data into templates that have been stored on the system. These may be used to create 
employee contracts, pre-populated HR forms, applicant correspondence etc.  
 
Documents that have been generated on CoreHR may be downloaded by the user to further amend 
and print, as required.  
 
Documents may also be automatically stored against an employee’s record on the ir Employee Profile 
screen, as part of the document generation. 
 
A user may also upload a document to the Employee Profile, independent of generation process e.g. 
uploading a copy of a passport. 
 
1.1.2. Email 
System generated emails can be produced and sent automatically from CoreHR to an employee or an 
applicant. Emails are typically used to support the recruitment process e.g. to send an invitation for 
interview to a candidate. However, these may also be generated to employees within HR Admin. 
 
1.1.3. Template 
Templates can be stored on the system to support the production of both documents and emails. 
 Document Templates: These are created using MS Word mail merge functionality and uploaded 
to CoreHR 
 Email Templates: These are created and maintained directly on CoreHR  
 
1.1.4. Template Group 
Templates (document or email) may be grouped into various categories e.g. Contracts, Recruitment, 
Salary etc. This is an optional grouping and does not need to be used for all or any templates. 
 
1.1.5. Document Type 
This is used to group documents that have been generated on  the system or uploaded independently 
to an employee’s or applicant’s record. This is an important setting for controlling the visibility of and 
access to documents for HR and Recruitment Admins as well as Employees and Managers  
 
  
HR: Document & Email Generation             
 
Page 6 of 75 
1.1.6. Data Source 
Standard mail merge functionality employs the use of ‘Data Sources’ which are essentially temporary 
files pre-populated with the record data that will become merged into a document or email template.  
 
In this feature, each screen in HR Admin or Recruitmen t Admin from which a document / email can be 
generated from, is linked to a specified data source (or data sources). This data source is a set of 
employee / applicant / contract / record fields which will be mapped to a template.  
 
Templates are configured, mapped to these fields. When a document or email is generated, a temporary 
file (not available to the user) will become populated with data for corresponding record(s). This will 
them update the mappings in the generated document / email.

2. How to Use 
2.1. Template Configuration Centre 
The ‘Template Configuration Centre’ provides the facility to create and manage all document and email 
templates that will be used as part of the document and email generation process, throughout CoreHR.  
To access the ‘Template Configuration Centre’: 
 Go to the HR Admin Dashboard 
 Select the Data Centre tab

2.2.2. Additional Configuration 
The ‘Additional Configuration’ feature provides the ability to include ‘UDF’ and ‘T&C Allowance’ data 
related to an employee or their contract in a document that is generated from CoreHR. This is useful to 
allow for the inclusion of data held for employees in customised ‘UDFs’ i.e. the items listed under the 
‘Other Information’ section of the Employee Profile . These are specific to each implementation of 
CoreHR, therefore these need to be configured and mapped individually per template, as they are not 
picked up by default in the data source. 
 
Please note : This is an optional configuration feature and does not need to be configured for all 
templates. 
 
This feature is only available to templates that are configured using the following 4 data sources:

 PERS_POST_PERSON_MERGE 
 PERS_POST_APPOINTMENT_MERGE 
 PERS_RECRUIT_APPLICANT_MERGE 
 
When the data source file  (‘persdata.txt’) is downloaded as part of the template creation, note th at the 
file contains fields specifically for UDFs and Allowances  
 
 
These will appear at the very end of the data source in the following format: 
 Udf_Allowance_1….. Udf_Allowance_5 
 Udf_Field_1….. Udf_Field_20 
 
As such, there is capacity to include 20 UDF items and 5 allowances, per template.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Pro Rata Length of Service Increments 
functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. This includes: 
• What is Pro Rata Length of Service Increments and when is it used? 
• Detailed guidance on the configuration options within Pro Rata Length of Service Increments. 
 
 
1.2. What is Pro Rata Length of Service Increments? 
The Pro Rata Length of Service Increments functionality makes it possible to pro rata anniversary-based 
length of service increments. 
 
The service increment calculation, to determine the number of additional days awarded, can be based 
on: 
• Dates (days) 
• Weeks 
• Months 
 
Therefore, the  increment calculation takes the date s, weeks, or months , between the employee’ s 
anniversary date and the end of the annual leave year into consideration. 
 
For example, where the increment calculation is configured as ‘days’ based, this instructs the system to 
calculate the service increment from  the start of the year , to the date im mediately before the service 
date. To do this, the system: 
• Adds the full -service increment entitlement, then deducts the part of the year (days) to be 
excluded from the additional days awarded. 
• Applies the employee’s FTE to the remainder.  
• Adds to the employee’s opening entitlement. 
• Rounds the result, based on the Rounding Rule specified at the balance level. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Note:   
If an employee is leaving an organisation, this also impacts their service increment.

1.3.1. Length of Service – Calculate on: Anniversary 
If the Length of Service is calculated by Anniversary, the system d oes not look t o contract history to 
determine service history. This parameter: 
• Uses the start date recorded on the personnel master record to determine the anniversary date. 
• It does not factor in any personnel contract history, such as gaps in service. 
 
 
1.3.2. Length of Service – Calculate on: Post Appointment Anniversary 
If the Length of Service is calculated by Post Appointment Anniversary; the system looks to the contract 
history to determine when the anniversary is due. 
 
This parameter enables the Use Service in Company and Exclude Leave parameters: 
Parameter Explanation 
Use Service in 
Company 
When ticked On, all the employee’s  service within the organisation is 
considered by the system. i.e. all the employee’s contracts. 
Exclude Leave 
When ticked On, service breaks (such as career breaks) are excluded 
when determining the total service for the employee. For example, if an 
employee joined the organisation on 11- June-2013 and took a 1- year 
career break:  
• Exclude Leave On - 5 years’ servic e is completed 11 -June-2019 
i.e. the c areer break is excluded from  the service history 
calculation, adding an extra year to the 5-year service required. 
• Exclude Leave Off – The 5 years’ service is completed 11- June-
2018 i.e. the career break is included in  the service history 
calculation.

2. Pro Rata Service Increments Examples 
2.1. Example 1: Full Time Employee 
After 5 years’ service, employees are due 2 days Pro Rata Length of Service Increment. This is based 
on their anniversary date. 
Example Variable  
Full Time Entitlement 22 Days 
5 years’ service completed on 11th June 2018 
Employee on FTE 1.00 therefore, leave for the year is 22 days (full entitlement). 
Pro Rata prior to Anniversary 
Date 
Use Dates 
 
 
 
System Calculation:  
• Full year Increment is 2 days, Anniversary date is June 11th 
• Part year excluded, is 161 days (from January 1st to June 10th) 
• Excluded value = 0.8822 days (2 days / 365 * 161) 
• 2 days – 0.8822 days = 1.1178 
• Impact remaining by the FTE (1.1178 * 1.00) 
• Actual service increase is 1.1178 days 
 
Opening Entitlement:   22.00 days  
     +1.1178  
    23.1178 days (rounded, if req.) 
 
New Entitlement:   23.50* days (or nett 1.50 days)

Available on 
Day 
You can indicate whether each checklist item should be made available at a 
specific time after the employee’s start date. For example, confidential 
information that should not be made available to a new employee before their 
join date. 
• By default, this is set to ‘0’. This means there is no rule in place, and the 
checklist item can be made accessible before the employee join date. 
• If you set this to ‘1’, the checklist item is accessible to the employee on 
day one of employment. This is their join date within the organisation.

accessible after the employee’s join date, but also to provide a more 
tailored onboarding experience where certain checks can be made 
available in week 1, week 2, etc.

employee. This can aid completion or inform the employee why certain 
information is being requested.

checklist items should be ordered correctly and must be 
placed before any checklist items that do not have this 
restriction.

1.2. Overview 
1.2.1. What is Onboarding? 
Onboarding checklists are assigned to employee records on CoreHR. These are essentially a list of 
tasks that must be reviewed and completed by the employee on CorePortal.  
 
Once a checklist has been assigned to the employee, they will be prese nted with the ‘Onboarding 
Dashboard’ when they login to CorePortal. The ‘Onboarding Dashboard’ includes 2 tabs by default:  
 
• Home: Displays a welcome message and some key elements associated with the employee’s 
contract e.g. their department, manager, location etc. 
 
 

People Management v25: Onboarding Checklists – User Guide          
  
CoreHR Internal 
Page 6 of 46 
• Checklist: The actual list of tasks that the employee must complete as part of their onboarding 
e.g. confirm address, upload a photo, confirm bank details etc. 
 
 
 
This dashboard will always be the first screen that they see on login, until they have fully completed the 
checklist i.e. all tasks are ‘Completed’. 
 
 
1.2.2. How are Checklists Maintained? 
Onboarding checklists are created and manged by the hr administrator, via the ‘Onboarding Checklists’ 
widget on the People Management Dashboard.  
 
On install of CoreHR a ‘Default Checklist’ is created. This checklist will be assigned to all employees by 
default. The checklist configuration may be updated as required e.g. to add new / remove existing 
checklist items, change the display of the ‘Home’ tab etc. 
 
It is possible to have one or many active checklists on CoreHR. If more than one checklist is available, 
then the checklists may be assigned to different groups of employees e.g. a checklist for senior 
management, a checklist for fixed-term staff etc. The amount of checklists defined on CoreHR is optional 
and based on the organisation’s requirements. It is possible to simply use the existing ‘Default Checklist’ 
for all employees.

1.2.3. Are Onboarding Checklists Mandatory? 
The ‘Onboarding’ feature is an option al feature on CoreHR. This is parameter driven and can be 
switched on or off.  
 
Please note: If this feature is switched on, it will be applicable for every active employee on the system. 
It is not possible to exclude any employees from this.

2.5. Assigning Checklists 
2.5.1. How are Checklists Assigned to Employees? 
CoreHR automatically assigns checklists to employees via a scheduled system job. This job runs every 
5 minutes and will identify any new employees that are not currently assigned to a checklist.  
 
• For any employees created before the next scheduled run, they will be automatically 
assigned to the ‘Default Checklist’. 
 
• When the job runs, the sys tem will identify any new employees and confirm if they should 
be assigned to another checklist, based on the criteria groups defined i.e.  
o If multiple active checklists exist, the system will identify the required checklist for 
the employee using the criteria groups defined. 
o If an employee does not match a checklist criteria group, then they will remain with 
the default checklist. 
o If only the default checklist exists, the employee will remain assigned to that.  
 
• If an employee has started their checklist, their assignment will not be updated i.e. 
o If an employee has started the default checklist, then they will retain the default 
checklist. 
o If an employee has not started their checklist i.e. they are at 0%, they will be 
reassigned 
 
• Only an employee’s substantive appointment will be checked against the criteria groups for 
each checklist.  
o If the employee does not match, then they will get the default checklist.  
o No other appointments will be checked against the criteria groups.

1.2. Overview of Start Date Corrections 
1.2.1. What Contracts can be Updated? 
This functionality is used to change the start date that has been set up for an employee’s contract. This 
is applicable in the following scenarios: 
1. New Hire 
2. Rehire 
3. Additional Contract

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Payroll to manage 
statutory payments.  
 
 
1.2. What are Statutory Payments? 
Statutory payments are payments that are made to employees to cover earnings lost when they 
are absent from work either through illness or because they are becoming a parent. 
 
Payments covered include:  
• Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) 
• Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) 
• Additional Statutory Paternity Pay (ASPP) 
• Ordinary Statutory Sick Pay (OSSP) 
• Adoption Pay (SAP) 
• Shared Parental Leave 
• Redundancy

1. Overview 
 
The purpose of this document is to provide a step by step guide to setting up and configuring the 
Team Area structure for a roster within Workforce Management.  
 
The document provides details on how to setup the validation rules and roster rules that are then 
assigned to the different Team Areas. 
 
The document also explains how to assign the appropriate menu access to managers and system 
users and how setup managers with delegation access. 
 
 
  
WFM Roster V26: Team Area and Rule Setup

Page 4 of 38 
2. Team Area and Structure Setup 
 Team Area Parameters 
• A Roster Team Area is created to logically group similar employees working within the same 
team. For example, team areas might be based on the different departments in a retai l store such 
as menswear, womenswear, and household.   
• Depending on the needs of each team area different rules and criteria can be assigned to each 
team area to ensure each area is adequately resourced. Several rules can get associated / applied 
at a roster team level allowing for variation from team to team. 
• The Team Area Parameters screen is utilised to create the teams that will be accessible in your 
roster as well as defining, at the team level, the roster criteria (i.e. Area Rules, Validation Rules, 
Self-Rostering capabilities, etc.) that will be applied to the team in question ( and possibly to any

1. Overview 
 
1.1. Purpose of this Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2022/23 
and prepare for the 2023/24 tax year. This document covers the following: 
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget. 
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release. 
• The tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.  
• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task. 
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2023/24 tax year.  
 
 
1.2. What is Year End? 
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to: 
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.  
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.  
• Run the Year End Cleardown task. 
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.   
• Issue Employees with a P60.  
 
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks: 
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.  
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.  
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’ 
table. 
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years. 
 
The UK Year End Software Release provides our customers with the following: 
• The preloaded rate changes as outlined by HMRC for the new tax year. 
• The software updates required to process the legislative changes set out by HMRC.

5. Year End Cleardown 
 
5.1. What is the Year End Cleardown? 
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks: 
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.  
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.  
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’ 
table. 
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years. 
 
 
5.2. Running the Year End Cleardown 
Do not run your Year End Cleardown until: 
• All your Company’s Pay Groups are completed for the current tax year.  
• The RTI Files for the current tax year are successfully transferred to HMRC , including the 
Final EPS. 
• The totals from the Pre Year End Data Check Report are balanced. 
• All Statutory Payments Pay Codes are assigned as such.

6.5.2. Employment Allowance  
The Employment Allowance (EA) allows businesses and charities to reduce their Employer's Class 
1 NIC liability by up to £5,000 per tax year. 
 
The EA is only available to businesses and charities with an Employer's Class 1 NIC liability of below 
£100,000 in the preceding tax year.  
 
The EA is considered a form of de minimis state aid. There is a ceiling on how much state aid any 
Organisation can receive under the de minimis rules. For most businesses, this ceiling will be 
€200,000 over a three -year rolling period (different levels apply  to agriculture, fisheries, road 
transport, and industrial sectors). 
 
 Note:  
If claiming the EA, it is your responsibility to check: 
• Your Secondary Class 1 NICs liability for the previous tax year was less than £100,000.  
• You have space to accommodate the full £5,000 within your relevant three-year ceiling, 
regardless of how much EA you claim each year , if you receive any other form of  de 
minimis state aid.

The Generate Timesheets functionality is now available in Portal from either the Workforce 
Management dashboard or the Payroll Dashboard.  This means:

Hours based on payroll rules configured in WFM. 
• Transfer Hours: This allows you to review Control Totals and helps you decide whether 
the payroll Hou rs are correct to transfer.  The Transfer Hours p rocess will either send 
Payroll Hours to CoreHR Payroll or create an interface file for third party payroll 
integration.

2.1.13. TUPE date – Length of Service and Continuance Dates  
 
Changes have been made to Balance and Occupational Entitlements to introduce TUPE dates.  This 
takes in to account an employee’s length of service when the existing company is part of an 
acquisition and the employee is given a new start date. 
 
What has changed? 
• The system now has the option to factor in TUPE dates for service calculations when 
determining entitlements to Occupational and Leave Balances, so the employee’s full 
service is included. 
• There are  new drop-down values to the existing options on forms.   
o For balance entitlements, see Balance Parameters/Employee Start Date now has a 
Continuance/Tupe Date option. 
o For Occupational Absence, see  Absence Pay Parameters/ Length of Service Basis now 
has  Continuance/Tupe Date 
 
Example:   
An employee joined  Company A on  01-Jan-1999 
Their Occupational Sick Entitlement is 20 days.   After 10 years’ service, the employee gets an 
extra 5 days sick leave  
Company A is acquired by Company B on 01-Jan-2020 
The employee is given a start date with Company B of 01 -Jan-2020 & TUPE Date = 01 -Jan-1999 
(Company A)  
 
Employee Length of Service is now 21 years and 11 months in Nov 2020  
Therefore, the TUPE date is 1-Jan-1999 and the latest start date  is 01-Jan-20 
The employee’s starting figure for Occupational is 25 days (i.e., 20 + 5 days)    
  
 
 
Key Wins 
 
• The system gives an accurate representation of employee entitlements if they have worked 
for the previous organisation.

2.1.21. Annual Leave Balances and Impacts on Public Holidays 
and Part Time Staff  Coming Soon! 
 
The balance configuration for Annual Leave and Public Holiday Entitlements for Part Timers has 
been enhanced with a number of changes. 
 
New balance configuration 
 
The New Balance Configuration means there is no longer any need   to create multiple Annual 
Leave balances per differing FTE hours.   
 
Others benefits include: 
 
• The Days Values Generated is now based on the Employee’s FTE Hours divided by the 
Personnel Default Hours divisor (number of days). 
• There is now validation to ensure only one method can be selected.   
 
An example of this would be if an Employee’s FTE Hours are 20   and Personnel D efault Hours 
divisor is 5 days,  then 4 hours is calculated for the Public Holiday Day (20 \ 5= 4). 
 
Enhancement 
WFM Release Notes            
Access Limited Distribution Page 51 of 74 
 
 
Key Benefits 
 
• Deployment is now faster and with less administration, removing the need to create or 
maintain multiple balances. 
• Existing Balance Configuration where new contracts are structured no longer need to be 
reviewed. 
• Increased accuracy on Leave Entitlement calculation. 
 
 
Where Annual Leave Entitlements are linked to Public Holidays  
 
Previously, annual leave balances had a one -to-one relatio nship to  Public Holidays Schemes. 
Where Companies operate across multiple jurisdictions such as Ireland and the United Kingdom, 
the public holidays dates differ.  
 
The benefits of the current changes are:

1. Overview 
 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 
This guide aims to explain the Pay  Code screens which have been converted from Back Office to 
Portal. 
 
It covers the following: 
• The Pay Code Screen 
• Pay Code Screen Configuration  
• Configuring Pay Codes  
• Pay Code Groups 
• Data Migration 
 
 
1.2. What is the Pay Code Screen? 
 
The Pay Codes Screen maintains codes, which are automatically generated  by the system  and 
maintained on an ad-hoc basis by authorized personnel. Portal supports an unlimited amount of 
Pay Codes, such as Basic, Overtime or Lates. Pay Codes required for Time & Attendance purposes 
are determined by operational policies.   If you are linked to the  Pay system, the code and 
descriptions will already have been set up.  
 
1.3. How to access the Pay Code Screen 
 
The Pay Code Screen can be accessed by the following steps: 
 
1. Quick jump to the WFM Admin Dashboard. 
 
2. Select WFM Configuration. 
WFM: Pay Codes - User Guide            
Access Limited Distribution 
 Page 6 of 64 
 
 
3. Under Reference Data, Select Pay Codes. 
 
 
 
4. The Pay Codes Screen displays. 
 

WFM: Pay Codes - User Guide

 Page 7 of 64 
 
 
 
1.4. The Pay Codes Landing Page 
When the Pay Codes Landing Page displays, you are presented with a list of WFM pay codes. 
Within the page you can: 
 
• Search for a pay code 
•  Filter the grid for a particular pay code  
• Add a pay code group 
• View Payroll pay codes

The following fields are mandatory on the Pay Code Screen: 
 
Field Details 
Pay Code This identifies the code pertaining to the pay code. 
Name 
It is recommended that a meaningful short name be used to 
easily identify the Pay Code 
Abbreviation 
The abbreviation is used for the purposes of calendar displays 
and enquiries and for analysis purposes. 
Type 
This identifies the type of Pay Code e.g., Basic, Overtime, 
etc.  This should be specified when using Basic Rule Groups, for 
determining which Pay Codes should be used. 
Calculate Indicator This indicates whether calculations are in minutes or in decimal. 
Payroll Indicator You can choose either Decimal, Minutes or Non Payroll. 
Label You can label a pay code as belonging to a specific group. 
Overtime Codes When this toggle is enabled, overtime codes will be shown. 
Working Time Codes 
When this toggle is enabled, working time codes will be shown

7. FAQ’s 
Q. Can I access the PeopleXD Payroll pay codes? 
A. Yes, Select View payroll pay codes button on the landing page. Within the Available Payroll Pay 
Codes Screen select Open Payroll pay codes button; from here you can see the list of Payroll pay 
codes. 
 
Q. How can a user bring in a pay code from XD Payroll to WFM? 
A. Select View payroll pay codes button on the landing page. Within the Available Payroll Pay Codes 
Screen select the pay roll you want to bring onto WFM and from the 3 -dot menu select Import to 
Copy or Copy New. (For further guidance on this see section 1.7.1 and 1.7.2 of the Pay Codes - User 
Guide) 
 
Q. Is there a way to deactivate or delete a pay code? 
A. Yes, the Active toggle within the landing page allows a pay code to be deactivated.  However, in 
WFM you cannot delete pay codes. 
 
Q. Is it possible to order the pay code leave types when submitting a Leave Request? 
A. Yes, to configure Leave types on the Leave Request screen: Open the pay code landing screen. 
Select the pay code and from the 3-dot menu open the configuration screen.  
Within the Summary Tab - Pay Code Order field: 
If you wish a pay code to appear first, set the pay code order to 1. 
If you wish a pay code to appear 2nd, set the pay code to 2 etc. 
If the pay code order field is null, then the pay codes are listed in alphabetical order.

2. Contract Amendments 
2.1. When to Amend a Contract 
Contract amendments refer to any date driven amendments that HR are required to m ake to an 
employee’s existing contract. 
 
These amendments may be pay impacting e.g. a change in hours. These may also be amendments 
that have no downstream impact on the employee’s salary e.g. change of work group, category etc. 
 
It is possible to record t hese changes on People Management for an employee’s existing contract. A 
timeline or history of all amendments will be tracked for that contract and are available to the hr 
administrator to review on screen. 
 
 
2.2. Amendments with No Salary Impact 
This refers to the amendment of an existing contract that does not require a corresponding update to 
the employee’s associated salary record.  
 
To amend an employee’s existing contract: 
1. Quick jump to the Command Centre widget in People Management. 
2. Click View at Employees and Search for the employee. 
3. Click View in the employee’s relevant row. 
4. Be sure that the correct contract is selected. 
5. In the Contracts tab, click Update in the Amendments section.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the candidate anonymisation and CV 
parsing functionality in PeopleXD Recruitment. This includes: 
• How to configure this functionality 
• What data can be anonymised 
• Where data is anonymised 
• Viewing parsed CVs 
 
1.2. What is Candidate Anonymisation? 
Candidate anonymisation allows you to hide personal information about a candidate for specific 
stages of the recruitment process. For example, the candidate’s name, address information, and 
contact details can be hidden.  
 
1.3. What is CV Parsing? 
When enabled, CVs are parsed when they are submitted by a candidate, or when a user manually 
adds a CV to an existing candidate record.  
 
The following information is then available in PeopleXD:  
• Candidate Summary (Supplied by the candidate on their CV or derived by the Parsing 
process) 
• Employment History 
• Education History 
• Skills 
 
  
 Note: CV Parsing is only available to customers who have the following:  
• XD Recruitment Premium 
• The new careers website (powered by Access’s Volcanic product) 
If you have do have either of the above, please contact your account manager.

2. Configuration 
2.1. Configuring Candidate Anonymisation 
Candidate anonymisation can be enabled for a specific applicant status. To configure this, follow 
the below steps: 
1. Navigate to the Recruitment Dashboard. 
2. Click the Toolbox tab. 
3. From the My Recruit Toolbox widget, click Open on Applicant Status.  
4. Click the three dot menu on the relevant status, then click Status Details.  
5. Enable or disable the Anonymise Candidate Data toggle as required. 
6. Click OK. 
7. Repeat steps 4-6 for each status, then click Save. 
 
2.2. Configuring CV Parsing 
To configure CV parsing, follow the below steps:  
1. Navigate to the Administrator Dashboard. 
2. On the Site Manager Widget, click Open on Admin Settings. 
3. Search for the parameter enable_cv_parsing.  
4. Click Edit. 
5. Update to Y or N, as required.  
6. Click OK.  
  
 
2.2.1. CV Profile Tab Configuration 
Administrators can configure what information is redacted on the CV Profile tab. To do this, 
follow the below steps:  
1. Navigate to the Administrator Dashboard. 
2. On the Site Manager Widget, click Open on Admin Settings. 
3. Click Edit on the relevant parameter. 
4. Set to Y or N as required. 
5. Click OK. 
 Note: The parsing process is point in time. Once enabled, CVs added to candidate records 
or via the application process will be parsed. Cover letters are not parsed.

cv_hide_org_name If set to Y, Organisation names are hidden

2.2.2. Generated CV Configuration 
If the candidate has not supplied a profile, or the parsing process has not been able to attain 
one, then an automated summary can be output instead. This is called a Generated Summary. To 
output the generated summary in the scenario above, a parameter must first be enabled. To do 
this, follow the below steps:  
1. Navigate to the Administrator Dashboard. 
2. On the Site Manager Widget, click Open on Admin Settings. 
3. Click Edit on the cv_display_brief parameter. 
4. Set to Y. 
5. Click OK.

5. Important Considerations  
The anonymisation functionality covered in this document has been designed to mitigate against 
unconscious bias as much as possible. However, there are certain limitations as to what can be 
anonymised and where. It is recommended to rollout the Applicant One View screen to users 
where possible, and disable access to other screens that may show non-anonymised data. 
 
5.1. Candidate Status Changes 
Every status change against a candidate is recorded. The Applicant Status History view in XD 
Insight reports can be used to highlight potential issues regarding shortlisting bias at key stages 
of your recruitment process.  
 
5.1.1. Interview Panel Widget 
If users are shortlisting via the Interview Panel widget, it is possible to limit the statuses they can 
change a candidate to. This reduces the risk of them inadvertently changing the candidate to an 
incorrect status and viewing personal information. To configure this, follow the steps below:  
 
1. Navigate to the Recruitment Dashboard. 
2. Click the Toolbox tab. 
3. From the My Recruit Toolbox widget, click Open on Applicant Status.  
4. Click the three dot menu on the relevant status, then click Status Details.  
5. Enable or disable the Available for Interview Panel Update toggle as required. 
6. Click OK. 
7. Repeat steps 4-6 for each status, then click Save.

Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to grant Pay Group Access.  
Items covered include:  
• How to grant user access to a pay group. 
• How to remove pay group access from a user. 
 
 
1.2. How is User Access Managed on Payroll? 
User access to the CoreHR system can be broadly split into 2 categories: 
1. Menu Profiles 2. Data Access 
• Provides access to system 
functionality. 
• Menu options are linked to system 
elements, including: 
o Dashboards 
o Screens 
o Buttons 
o Menu options 
o Widgets 
• Typically aligned to a user’s role in 
the organisation , e.g. a profile for 
‘HR Administrators’, another for 
‘Payroll Administrators’ etc. 
• Provides access to the actual data / 
records stored on the system. 
• For Payroll, this incl udes access to the 
following records: 
o Employees 
o Pay Groups 
o Salaries 
• Different employees can have access to 
different sets of records on CoreHR, e.g. 
access to all records, access to  only a 
subset of records. 
 
 
Therefore, users of the Payroll Dashboard will need to be granted access for both categories, i.e. a user 
will need:  
1. A Menu Profile , e.g. PAYROLL_ADMIN, in order to see the Payroll Dashboard  and all 
functionality within that.  
2. Data access to see employee records, lookup salaries and run payroll. 
 
 
1.3. What is Pay Group Access? 
Access to data on the Payroll Dashboard is grouped at Pay Group level, i.e. payroll administrators can 
only see employees and process payrolls for pay groups to which they have access.   
 
Payroll v28: Configuring Pay Groups Access          
CoreHR Limited Distribution 
Page 5 of 12 
 
 
If an organisation has multiple pay groups on CoreHR, users must be granted access to the pay groups 
that they are required to support.  
 
For example, if an organisation may have 3 pay groups: 
• Monthly Payroll 1 
• Monthly Payroll 2 
• Monthly Payroll 3 
 
The following user access set up is possible: 
• A user may have access to all 3. 
• They may only have access to Monthly Payroll 1. 
• They may be granted access to Monthly Payroll 2 for a temporary period to cover a colleague’s 
absence. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Note:  
Pay Group access is also applicable for HR Administrators on the People Management Dashboard, 
to control their access to employee salary and allowance records. Further training on this is provided 
in the User Data Access configuration guide for People Management.

Contract or Rehire process.

The advantage of using the task list feature includes: 
• Ability to direct the user to ensure the required employee and contract details are updated.  
• One central location is provided to allow the user to jump directly to the required scree ns to 
update the data. 
• The task list can be closed and reopened as many times as necessary before completion.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Pay Groups.  
 
Items covered include:  
• How to add a Pay Group.  
• How to edit a Pay Group.  
• How to duplicate a Pay Group. 
• How to delete a Pay Group. 
 
 
1.2. What is a Pay Group? 
A pay group is used for grouping employees that have the same pay frequency. This means that all the 
employees in a pay group are processed together for payment. Employees havi ng common payment 
frequencies may be split over as many or as few pay groups as required. 
 
Every employee must be linked to a pay group, and each pay group must be linked to a company.

To add, edit, duplicate or delete a Pay Group:

There are many fields and indicators available in the set -up of pay groups. In the next section, we will

3.1. Add a Pay Group 
To add a new pay group: 
1. Go to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups. 
2. Click the blue Add button. 
 
3. Complete at least all mandatory fields marked with a red asterisk. 
4. Enter a unique code for the pay group. 
5. Add a description of the new code in the Description field. (Maximum of 30 characters). 
6. Populate the following fields.  
Field Description 
Pay Frequency 
Indicator 
W = Weekly, F = Fortnightly, M = Monthly, 4 = 4-Weekly or B = Bi-Monthly. 
Wages/Salary 
Indicator 
W = Wages or S = Salary. 
Start Period Enter a Start Period, e.g. 201901. The tax year start period.  
Input Period 
Enter an Input Period, e.g. 201926. This is determined by linking the input period 
specified to the calendar week on the payroll calendar.  
Completed Input Enter a Completed Input period, e.g. 201921. The last input period closed.  
Completed 
Update 
Enter a Completed Update period, e.g. 201917. The last payroll period closed. 
Payroll Period Enter the Payroll Period, e.g. 201926. The current payroll period.  
Maximum Hours 
Enter the maximum number of recorded hours an employee attached to this pay 
group can have worked. Employees who have worked chargeable hours greater 
than this value will be highlighted on the payroll observation report.  (allowable 
range 0 – 9999).  
Maximum Gross 
Enter the maximum gross pay an employee attached to this pay group can 
receive within the pay period. Employees earning a gross amount above this 
value will be highlighted on the payroll observation report. 
Maximum Nett  
Enter the maximum nett pay an employee attached to this pay group can receive 
within the pay period. Employees earning a net amount above this value will be 
highlighted on the payroll observation report. 
Pay Period 
Hours 
Enter Pay Period Hours, i.e. the standards hours for a payroll period week. Enter 
the default/contracted hours in a period for this pay group.  
Payroll v28: Configuring Pay Groups           
CoreHR Limited Distribution 
Page 8 of 14 
 
Pay Period Days 
Enter Pay Period Days, i.e. the standards days for a payroll period week. Enter 
the default days in a period for thi s pay group. These days are used when  
converting an employee’s annual rate to the hourly or daily equivalent for the 
purpose of paying hours or days, e.g. Basic Hourly pay or overtime  or daily pay.   
Days in Year  
Enter Days in Year, i.e. the days in the year for this pay group.  This is used to 
convert annual rates to daily , e.g. 260 days in the year.  This is used  when 
calculating hourly pay for employees whose rate is set up as an annual figure. 
 
Using the above three parameters , the formula for converting from Annual to    
Hourly is as follows:  
• Annual Rate /  Days in Year = Derived Daily Rate 
• Derived Daily Rate is multiplied by Days in  Period = Derived Periodical 
Rate.  
• Derived Periodical Rate is  divided by Pay Period Hours =  Derived 
Hourly Rate.  
 
 
 
 Note:  
For employees who do not work full time or whose hours are different, 
an override can be entered for each employee People Management. Pay 
Period hours are used when converting an employee’s annual rate to the 
hourly to pay hours, e.g. basic hourly pay or overtime.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure and setup the Talent 
module by creating reference data, job families, career paths and career development plans. 
These can be used by and broken down into the following groups: 
1. Employees 
2. Managers 
3. Talent / HR Administrators 
 
This guide includes: 
• What is configurable on the Talent Management Administration dashboard and how it  is 
managed. 
• A breakdown of default / standard security menu profiles that are available to be assigned 
to CorePortal users. 
• Advice on best practice configuration. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Note:   
• This guide does not include: 
o Steps on how to create appraisals, objectives, competencies, or 360 & Peer 
Reviews. 
o Guidance on dashboard configuration, for the purpose of amending the Talent 
administration tabs and widget layouts.

2. Initial Configuration 
2.1. Talent Management Administration Dashboard 
To use the Talent  Management module users must have access to the relevant widgets within 
CorePortal on the Employee Dashboard, Manager Dashboard and Talent Management Admin 
Dashboard.  The Talent Management Administrator dashboard is used to create appraisals, 
objectives, competencies, compensation and 360 cycles. Users can also manage that information 
created through business as usual processes or facilitating ad -hoc changes and general 
management of cycles throughout the year. This is created as a multi -tab dashboard with the 
various modules being allocated a specific tab.  The recommended approach is t o separate out 
each feature where necessary so managers and employees can see all options that are available 
to them within their own dashboards(s).

4.1. What are Scaled Reference Types 
These are reference items that can be assigned colours and levels to be used across the Talent 
Management product for both an employee and manager. The Appraisals section uses reference 
lists for system wide ratings.  
 
There are 2 types of Scaled Reference Items: 
1. General References 
2. Talent Factor References

The following reference data can be created to appear on the Talent Factors section on a Review 
form.

This information can be created to appear on the Talent Factors section on a Review form. It shows 
the level to which the employee is performing at currently. 
 
Current Potential 
This information can be used to track an employee’s development and potential to develop further 
in their current role. 
 
Readiness 
This information is related to how ready the employee may be to move into a specific talent pool 
within the organisation. 
 
Promotability 
This information can be used to give an employee a score to measure how eligible for a promotion 
that they may be in terms of performance levels. 
 
Flight Risk 
This information re fers to the level of risk of departing a  department or the company that the 
employee may be.

This process allows you to create a career path for job titles in your organisation. There are two 
methods that a career path can be created for employees. 
 
6.1.1. Automatic Career Paths 
These career paths are created by the historical movement of employees across job titles in your 
organisation.  For example, if Empl oyee A was commenced as a Budget Analyst, and then moved 
roles to become a Financial Administrator, the software includes this as a career path for Employee 
B who may be sitting in a Budget Analyst job title.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of this Document 
The purpose of this document is to provide full guidance on how to use the features provided by CoreHR 
to support your organisation’s legislative requirements. These include: 
• Managing GDPR Requests 
o Right to be Forgotten 
o Subject Access Requests 
• Reporting on GDPR  
• Report Sensitivity Classification 
• Sharing a Data Privacy Statement 
 
 
 
1.2. Overview of GDPR Features 
1.2.1. GDPR Request Centre 
The GDPR Request Centre screen can be made available to users to complete the following 
employee requests: 
• Subject Access Requests 
• Right to be Forgotten Requests 
 
The GDPR request centre allows you to: 
• Search for existing requests 
• Submit requests 
• Track their progress 
• View and download the reports and documentation that are output for Subject Access 
Requests 
• Delete requests 
 
1.2.2. Reporting on GDPR via Insight 
Insight provides full reporting capability for GDPR purposes including: 
• The ability to report on submitted requests. 
• The ability to report on the CoreHR system tables included in the ‘Subject Access Requests’ & 
‘Right to be Forgotten Requests’. 
 Note:   
Guidance on how to complete the required set up is covered in a separate GDPR (SAAS v27+)  
Configuration Guide.

2.2. GDPR Requests Screen Overview  
The GDPR Request screen is where the user submits GDPR requests for employees on CoreHR. 
Further details on how to submit requests are available on (3. Right to be Forgotten & 4. Subject Access 
Request) 
 
Any requests submitted on CoreHR will appear here.  
• These automatically clear down after a specified number of days (defaulted to 30 days but 
configurable per organisation). 
• Successfully completed ‘Right to be Forgotten’ requests are not displayed here. 
• Use the  button to access options to download any reports for Subject Access Requests 
OR delete the request. 
• Each user sees: 
o Requests that they have submitted. 
o R equests that been submitted by another user  for employees that they have been 
granted access to for GDPR.  
 
 
 
 
The table below describe the data displayed for each request.   
Column Description

The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the  Pay Code Access Groups

managers and employees when entering leave requests, absences and timesheets.

marked as manager only.

1. Introduction 
The purpose of this guide is to provide detailed guidance  on how to set up a new hire on People 
Management.  
 
There are a number of ways in which a new hire can be setup on People Management, depending on

• Auto-Authorised Post Profile 
• Auto-Commenced Post Profile 
• Planned & Authorised Post Appointment

refer to the Managing Post Profiles user guide for this information.

2.1.2. Commence Appointment 
When using an Auto Authorised Post Profile to create the contract, the  contract will initially be created 
in an appointed status. This means that: 
• the employee exists on the system and will return as active if using the employee search on 
the People Management dashboard. 
• the contract exists for the employee and is available to view on their employee record with a 
status of Pending. 
 
 
 
However, until the contract is commenced for the employee, the employee and their contract will not be 
available to the payroll team to process. The act of commencing the appointed contract on a specified 
Commenced Date will confirm that the employee has started in organisation and should be paid the 
contracted salary amount from that date. 
 
Follow these steps to commence the contract:

1. Overview 
 
1.1. Purpose of this Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2022/23 
and prepare for the 2023/24 tax year. This document covers the following: 
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget. 
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release. 
• The tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.  
• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task. 
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2023/24 tax year.  
 
 
1.2. What is Year End? 
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to: 
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.  
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.  
• Run the Year End Cleardown task. 
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.   
• Issue Employees with a P60.  
 
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks: 
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.  
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.  
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’ 
table. 
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years. 
 
The UK Year End Software Release provides our customers with the following: 
• The preloaded rate changes as outlined by HMRC for the new tax year. 
• The software updates required to process the legislative changes set out by HMRC.

The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks: 
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.  
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.  
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’ 
table. 
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years.

6.5.2. Employment Allowance  
The Employment Allowance (EA) allows businesses and charities to reduce their Employer's Class 
1 NIC liability by up to £5,000 per tax year. 

UK Payroll Year End 2023/24 – Portal User Guide            
Access Limited Distribution Page 43 of 75 
The EA is only available to businesses and charities with an Employer's Class 1 NIC liability of below 
£100,000 in the preceding tax year.  
 
The EA is considered a form of de minimis state aid. There is a ceiling on how much state aid any 
Organisation can receive under the de minimis rules. For most businesses, this ceiling will be 
€200,000 over a three-year rolling period (different levels apply to agriculture, fisheries, road 
transport, and industrial sectors). 
 
You are restricted from claiming the EA if: 
1. You are the Director and the only Employee paid above the 'Secondary Threshold'. 
2. You employ someone for personal, household, or domestic work – unless they are a care 
or support worker. 
3. You are a public body or business doing more than half your work in th e public sector – 
unless you are a charity. 
4. You are a Service Company working under 'IR35 rules' and your only income is the 
Intermediary's earnings (such as your Personal Service Company, Limited Company, or 
Partnership).

1. Introduction 
The Successful Applicants feature in People Management is relevant only if the Recruitment module is 
being used. This allows for the completion of contract details for successful applicants in a recruitment 
campaign for: 
• New hires 
• New contracts for existing employees  
o Replacement contracts 
o Additional contracts 
• Rehires 
 
In order for this option to be used, the successful applicant must be linked to a job offer in Recruitment 
and flagged as having accepted this offer. Only then will the applicant be available to the hr administrator 
to process. For full details on how this is managed from a recruitment perspective, please refer to the 
recruitment training material. 
 
The purpose of this guide is to provide instructions on how to complete the contract creation for 
successful applicants (new hires, existing employees and rehires) on People Management.
