1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this guide is to outline the steps needed to create and set up 360 reviews on the 
talent dashboard to be assigned to employees and managers for feedback. 
 
1.2. What are 360 Reviews? 
360 reviews are feedback opportunities that enable a group of colleagues to provide feedback on 
an employee’s performance and facilitate continuous evaluation.  Talent management 
administrators can create 360 review questionnaires and assign these either to all employees 
across the organisation or to employees that belong to a specific organisational group, e.g. all 
employees in Division A.  Employees can select from a list of the colleag ues, within their defined 
organisational group, and request that they provide feedback for them, using the assigned 360 
review form. 
 
The feedback is generally asked for by the manager to whom the employee reports  into. 
Colleagues who participate in the 36 0 usually include the persons line manager, several peers, 
reporting staff, and functional managers with whom the employee works regularly with. 
 
The goal of the feedback is to provide a balanced view to an employee of how others view his or 
her contributi on and performance in areas such as leadership, teamwork, interpersonal, 
communication, management, contribution, work habits, interpersonal interaction, accountability, 
vision and more, depending on the employee's job. 
 
Key characteristics of the 360 review include: 
• Availability to assign and request feedback for a specific period. 
• Visibility of feedback can be set for HR, the manager and the employee ; therefore 
controlling who has access to review submitted feedback. 
• The anonymity of feedback can be set for HR, the manager and the employee  hiding the 
name of the employee who provides feedback. 
• Review questionnaires can be created unique to each review, with the facility to define a 
number of mandatory or optional questions using multiple choice & free text style 
answers. 
XD Talent Management: 360 Reviews & Peer Reviews Configuration - User Guide       
     
 
Access Limited Distribution 
 Page 5 of 24 
• Notifications are automatically issued via the CorePortal notification centre to alert 
employees of: 
o any new 360 reviews they need to assign to their colleagues. 
o any feedback requests that have been assigned to them from their colleagues. 
• System reminders can be enabled to automatically send to employees within up to 7 days 
of the review due date, as a reminder to act on any outstanding review requests. 
 
 
1.3. What are Peer Reviews 
The Peer Review functionality allows a manager to send a review questionnaire to other employees 
in the organisation  and to request feedback from their team members . Talent management 
administrators can create peer review questionnaires and assign these either to all man agers 
across the entire organisation or to managers that belong to a specific organisational group , e.g. 
all managers in Division A. 
 
Key characteristics of the peer review include: 
• The availability to assign and request feedback for a specific period. 
• The visibility of feedback can be restricted for either HR, the manager or both. 
• The anonymity of feedback provided can be set to hide the name of the employee who 
provides feedback. 
• Review questionnaires can be created unique to each review, with the facility to define a 
number of mandatory or optional questions using multiple choice & free text style answers 
• Notifications are automatically issued via the CorePortal notification centre to alert: 
o managers of any new peer reviews they need to assign for their team members. 
o employees of any feedback requests assigned to them. 
• System reminders can be set to automatically send to employees within up to 7 days of 
the review due date, as a reminder to act on any outstanding review requests 
• An employee cannot view feedback provided about them via the peer review process. This 
feedback is visible only to their manager and to the talent management administrator.

vacancy that are not setup on a standard application form. Questionnaires can include:

A schedule on a vacancy is used to track interview rounds and assessments associated with the vacancy. 
For example 
• Pre-interview assessments for a group of candidates. 
• Multiple rounds of interviews. 
 
For each schedule you need to define key information such as dates, times and locations. Interview panel 
members can be assigned to one or all the schedules as required so that they can see the details of who is 
to be interviewed and access their application details. 
 
Applicants are assigned to each schedule as they progress through the vacancy process. For example, an 
applicant could be assigned to the following schedules: 
• Group assessment 
• Interview round 1 
• Interview round 2

5.8.3. Multi-Day Schedules 
 
What are Multi-Day Interview Schedules? 
A multi-day interview schedule is a schedule that is configured to take place over several days.  
 
 
When creating this type of schedule, it is possible to update the following schedule items per day: 
• Start Time 
• End Time 
• Morning Break Time 
• Lunch Time 
• Evening Break Time 
• Board Convenes Time 
 
This ensures that when the system automatically identifies available time slots for a schedule, the times 
associated with individual days are taken into consideration. 
It is possible to remove an entire date/dates between the defined start and end dates i.e. schedule dates do 
not have to run concurrently. 
 
It is also possible to ensure that weekend dates are included OR omitted when defining a multi -day schedule.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
This document will provide guidance on how to use and configure the HR Process Task Lists on CoreHR 
including: 
• Setting up a task list. 
• The steps available for each task list. 
• Managing access to configure task lists. 
• Managing access to use task lists for employee contracts.

1.2. What are HR Process Task Lists? 
Task Lists are used to define a set of steps that must be completed as part of a New Starter, New 
Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire or Leaver process.  
 
Once a new contract has been assigned to an employee as part of the new hire, rehire or new contract 
steps on People Management, the task list will pop up on screen. This will present the user with a list 
of mandatory and optional steps to be completed. The user can then click on a step and be redirected 
to the screen required to input the data e.g. if the step is ‘Allowances’, clicking on this will open the ‘Add 
Allowances’ screen.  
 
Different task lists can be created for each process type.  
 
The advantage of using the task list feature includes: 
• Ability to direct the user to ensure the required employee and contract details are updated.  
• One central location is provided to allow the user to jump directly to the required scree ns to 
update the data. 
• The task list can be closed and reopened as many times as necessary before completion.

2.5. Nominating Task List Step Owners 
Task list items can now be assigned to specified owner to complete.  
• The task ownership is identified using a specified org role/org group assignment.  
• For example, access to Assign User Access may be restricted to security administrators only. 
• If a user is not the owner and doesn’t have access to complete a task item, they will see the item 
on the Task List screen, which will flag the Org Role responsible for completing the task and they 
will be prevented from access the task itself. 
 
 
2.6. Restricting Task List Steps 
• Task list items can be restricted, allowing you to create tailored task lists for different employee 
categories and functions e.g. different task list items to be assigned to permanent v agency staff. 
• This is achieved using criteria groups i.e. only assign this task if the employee is in one of the 
defined Criteria Groups. 
• If no restrictions are set, the task is applicable to all employees.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 Note This guide is only applicable if an organisation is managing the assignment of pension 
schemes for employees at contract level, rather than person level. Please refer to the relevant Payroll 
training resources for guidance on managing pension scheme assignments at employee level.  
 
This document provides guidance on how to manage pension schemes for employees by directly 
assigning these to their contract records. This includes: 
• Linking pension schemes to post profile records. 
• Assigning a pension scheme to contracts. 
• Amending existing pension scheme assignments. 
• How the assignment of a pension scheme is ended. 
• The payslip impact of the ‘Pension by Appointment’ option. 
 
This docu ment does not provide guidance on how to manage pensions schemes f or employees at 
employee level.  
 
 
1.2. Pension by Appointment vs Pension by Person 
CoreHR provides the facility to capture Pension Scheme assignments for employee at either Person or 
Appointment level. An organisation will configure the CoreHR application to manage pensions using 
either of these options. Only one option can be enabled at a time. It is not possible to define a 
combination of these options 
 
1.2.1. Pension by Person 
Pension Schemes are assigned directly to the employee’s record.  
• This is managed in Payroll and not in HR.  
• This is completely independent of the employee’s assigned contracts i.e. contract amendments, 
new contracts etc. will not impact on the pension scheme assignment.  
 Note If this option is used, the Pension Contributions screen will be read-only. This means that 
the screen: 
• will display the details of any pension assigned to the person. 
• will not provide the ability to update or amend the pension assignments, regardless of the 
menu options assigned to the user.

1.2.2. Pension by Appointment  
Pension Schemes are assigned directly to an employee’s contract. 
• Different pension schemes can be assigned to different contracts. 
• If an employee has multiple active contracts, it is possible to have pension schemes assigned 
to all or some of these. 
• If a contract is ended, the pension scheme assignment is also automatically ended.

CoreHR provides an option to validate the rate entered for an employee’s salary, against minimum, 
living and / or apprentice wage rates. This is to inform the user if the salary they are providing for 
the employee’s contract is too low.  
 
Rates for minimum wage, living wages and apprentice wages can be setup on CoreHR. These 
can be added to on an annual basis, as new rates are released for each new tax year.  
CoreHR will calculate if the salary supplied for an employee’s contract meets the minimum / living 
/ apprentice wage rates based on: 
• The rates defined on CoreHR and their effective date. 

 
 
Page 53 of 79 
• The employee’s date of birth. 
• Contracted hours and weeks (or FTE Weeks per Year). 
• For apprentice rates, validation is applied to confirm that the employee / contract is 
apprentice. 
• Where multiple countries are setup, the appropriate rates for the employee’s Pay Group 
country. 
 
Minimum wage & apprentice rates are not mutually exclusive. The system will first check to see if 
the employee’s contract is an apprentice type contract.  
• If it is - apprentice rates are used in validation.  
• If it isn’t - minimum wage rates are used in validation.

1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 
The purpose of this guide is to help users configure the Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility.  
Parallel Run allows users to report on the parallel tables and to review or report  where differences 
may have occurred in the transferring of hours for a previously completed back office Live Run.  
 
By using the Parallel Ru n, you can compare to existing Live runs completed through back  office 
and ensure there are no errors before migrating to live running of the Portal version of Generate 
Timesheets. 
 
This is particularly useful for those sites with large amounts of hours being transferred  and is an 
added backup to those who are migrating from using the previous back office feature to the one 
on Portal. 
 
The step-by-step process of retrieving hours and transferring them to payroll is covered in a 
separate document, see WFM v28 Generate Timesheets User Guide.

1.3. What is the Parallel Mode? 
 
Generate Timesheets in Parallel Mode. 
 
As mentioned in the previous section, Generate Timesheets has been moved from the back office 
to Portal.  In order to support the transition, the portal version of Generate Timesheets runs  a 
parallel mode to support the re-generation of a previously transferred period that was completed 
via the back office. 
 
The features within the Parallel Mode are the following: 
 
• WFM company:  Parallel Mode can be enabled per WFM company.  If a client has more 
than one company using Portal, the parallel mode can be run separately for each. 
 
• Validation: Parallel mod e is run to validate those calendars or periods which have 
previously been migrated to show that there are no discrepancies found. 
 
 
• Leavers: Parallel Transfers do not impact the live mode.  Employees are not marked as 
leavers. 
 
• Analysis and Review: Parallel Run details are stored into backup tables for analysis and 
review.  For further information see Tables for Parallel Run.

• Insight reporting and analysis: This includes listings of the hours transferred in parallel 
mode. Exceptions reports  are generated on the parallel lists and are compared 
highlighting differences between the back-office run and portal runs.

2. Roster Availability 
2.1. Overview 
Roster Availability feeds into the employe e’s Roster contract and can be used when reviewing what 
times an employee  is available to  work within a day. This functionality provides e mployees with the 
ability to submit their Roster availability. This can be used where the employee’s availability may vary 
between weeks. For example, an employee may not be available to work every second Monday. 
 
The submission of availability to work can then be routed through an approval process, or it can directly 
update the employees’ contract, dependant on configuration.

3. Shift Swap 
3.1. Overview 
It is possible for employees to submit a request to swap a shift with another team member. Employees 
can also accept or reject a request for a Shift Swap with another employee. In order for the Shift Swap 
to be successful,  managers must first ap prove a request for a Shift Swap. The Shift Swap approval 
workflow is as follows: 
 
1. Employee 1 submits a Shift Swap with employee 2. 
2. Employee 2 is notified of the swap, and then accepts or reject the Shift Swap. 
3. If employee 2 accepts the Shift Swap, then the swap notifies the manager of employee 2. 
4. If the manager approves the Shift Swap, the Roster is then update for employee 1 and employee 
2, to reflect the Shift Swap. 
5. When the status of the swap changes to approved or rejected, both employees are updated of 
the approval/rejection.

2. Max Daily Pay Code Limit (Pay Code Setting) 
2.1. Overview 
There is a Max Daily Limit value that can be applied at Pay Code level. This prevents users from entering 
values greater than the value stored at the Pay Code level. 
 
This can be applied for the following examples of use: 
• Value Pay Codes: Meal allowance, cannot enter more the €10 / £10 per day. 
• Unit Pay Codes: On Call allowance, cannot enter a value greater than 1 on call. 
• Hours Pay Codes: Cannot enter more than 8.00 hours annual leave. 
 
For example, an employee cannot have more than a co nfigurable number of hours a nnual leave 
recorded on one Pay Code, per day, than the Max Daily Limit value applied at Pay Code level. 
• This prevents users from entering values greater than the value stored on the Pay Code. 
• Validation alerts can be configured to stop entry on all screens except the Approve/Sign Off 
screen, which can display: 
o Warning – the user is warned but can continue with Sign Off. 
o Stop – the user cannot continue with Sign Off.

3. Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit (Validation Rule) 
3.1. Overview 
There is a Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit value that can be applied at Pay Code Group level. This 
prevents users from entering values across multiple Pay Codes, greater than the Max Overall Daily Pay 
Code Limit, for the Pay Code Group. 
 
For example, an employee cannot have more than a configurable number of hours recorded on a day, 
across a list of Pay Codes. 
• The Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit value can be applied for a defined group of Pay Codes, 
and a daily value specified within the Control Parameters. 
• This prevents users from entering Pay Codes and hours greater than the daily value allowed.  
This can be applied for the following scenario: 
o If a configured max value of 7 hours is allowed per day, and values are recorded greater 
than this limit, across Pay Codes within the Pay Code Group:  
o The manger is stopped at Timesheet Input stage; OR 
o The manager is alerted at Approve/Sign Off stage.

The Shortlist Group feature is an extension of the Interview Panel functionality, which allows for the 
creation of groups of applicants who are then assigned out to individual panel members to review.

individual interview panel member to review

displayed to them will be restricted to the list of the applicants in their prescribed Shortlist Group.

4. Assessment Scorecards 
4.1. Assessment Scorecards Overview 
The Assessment Scorecard  feature allows individual interview panel members to submit unique 
assessment details per applicant across the various stages of the recruitment process. Shortlisting 
Assessment Scorecards can be created and linked to the Interview Panel widget. Each individual panel 
member can submit their own unique scorecard for each applicant that they are reviewing during 
the shortlisting process. 
 
Interview schedule Assessment Scorecards  can also be created and associated with each 
individual interv iew schedule. Each individual panel member can submit their own unique 
scorecard for each applicant for each round of interviews that they are assigned to. 
 
For both the shortlisting and interview schedule Assessment Scorecards , the recruitment 
administrator has the option to view the total averaged assessment score, for each round, per 
applicant. 
 
It is possible to add an Assessment Scorecard for inclusion in the interview panel shortlisting process 
i.e. providing panel members with an Assessment Scorecard to complete for each applicant. Repeat 
the steps outlined for each individual interview schedule as required. Use the Applicant Status value 
to link the scorecard to an interview schedule with the same status i.e. the  Status Of value on the 
schedule. 
 
The Assessment Scorecards  feature is used in conjunction with other standard  Recruitment 
features including the Interviews widget, the Interview Panel and Shortlist Groups. Please ensure 
that you refer to the corresponding training material for these features, in order to ensure 
these are configured as required.

5. Interview Scheduling 
5.1. What is a Schedule 
A schedule on a vacancy is used to track interview rounds and assessments associated with 
the vacancy. For example 
• Pre-interview assessments for a group of candidates. 
• Multiple rounds of interviews. 
 
For each schedule you need to define key information such as dates, times and locations. 
Interview panel members can be assigned to one or all the schedules as required so that 
they can see the details of who is to be interviewed and access their application details. 
 
Applicants are assigned to each schedule as they progress through the vacancy process. For 
example, an applicant could be assigned to the following schedules: 
• Group assessment 
• Interview round 1 
• Interview round 2 
 
This section provides guidance on how to manage schedules for the vacancy, including: 
• How to create a schedule. 
• How to assign schedules to applicants. 
• How to assign schedules to interview panel members. 
• How interview panel members can view the details of upcoming interviews that they 
are assigned to. 
• An overview of the Interview Panel screen.

5.7. Multi Day Schedules 
5.7.1. What are multi-day schedules? 
 
 
A multi-day interview schedule is a schedule that is configured to take place over several 
days. 
 
When creating this type of schedule, it is possible to update the following schedule items 
per day: 
• Start Time 
• End Time 
• Morning Break Time 
• Lunch Time 
• Evening Break Time 
• Board Convenes Time 
 
This ensures that when the system automatically identifies available time slots for a 
schedule, the times associated with individual days are taken into consideration. 
 
It is possible to remove an entire date between the defined start and end dates i.e. schedule 
dates do not have to run concurrently. 
 
It is also possible to ensure that weekend dates are included OR omitted when defining a 
multi-day schedule. 
 
Ensure that the Start Date and End Date fields date reflect the overall period for the multi -
day schedule i.e. start and end on different dates. 
 
 Note: This functionality is available for schedules with an Interview Type of “Individual”.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide clear guidance on how a user’s access to employee, contract 
and salary data is managed in People Management. 
 
This includes: 
• An overview of user access on CoreHR. 
• How access is managed for employee, contracts & post records.  
• How access is managed for the employee’s salary & allowance records.  
• How to assign user HR and Pay access.

2. How is User Access Managed on People Management? 
2.1. Overview 
User access to the CoreHR system can be broadly split into 2 categories: 
 
Menu Profiles Data Access 
• Provides access to system 
functionality. 
• Menu options are linked to system 
elements including: 
o Dashboards 
o Screens 
o Buttons 
o Menu options 
o Widgets 
• Typically aligned to a user’s role in 
the organisation e.g. a profile for hr 
administrators, another for payroll 
administrators etc. 
• Provides access to the actual data / 
records stored on the system. 
• For People Management, this includes 
access to the following records: 
o Employees 
o Posts 
o Salaries 
• Different employees can have access 
to different sets of records on CoreHR 
e.g. access to all records, access to 
only a subset of records. 
 
 
Therefore, users of the People Management  dashboard will need to be granted access for both 
categories i.e. a user will need: 
1. A Menu Profile e.g. COREPORTAL_HRADMIN, to see the People Management dashboard 
and all functionality within that. 
2. Data access to see employee records, search for posts and access salary information. 
 
 
2.2. Access by Organisational Structure 
Access to employee, post & contract data on People Management  is based on the Organisational 
Structure that has been set up on CoreHR. A user’s access will be aligned directly to an organisational 
unit or level that has been defined on the Org Structure.  
 
For example, a user may be granted access: 
• For the entire Company 
• For Department A and Department B only 
• For a particular Management Unit and all Departments within

2.3. Access by Pay Group 
A user requires an additional level of data access to see the salary records associated with an employee 
and their contract.  
• This is based on the Pay Group that the employee is a member of.  
• This is not at all based on the Org Structure.  
 
A user must be granted access to a Pay Group. They will then have access to all the salary records for 
employees in that Pay Group.  
 
This acc ess is n ecessary for the user to access salary, allowance and deductions data on People 
Management.  
 
However, Pay Group access alone will not provide the user with any additional access to the employee 
/ contract / post data on People Management.  
• At a minimum, a user must first be given access to see the employee and contract records on 
People Management (see 2.2 Access by Organisational Structure).  
• Only if a user can see the employee / contract AND if they have been granted access to the 
Pay Group that the employee is in, then they will be able to see the salary details.

Access to All Pay Groups

specific Pay Groups.  
 
If the user has access to an employee that is not in one of 
the specified Pay Groups, then they will not be able to see 
that employee’s payroll records. 
No Pay Group access 
User will not have access to any payroll data on People 
Management. 
Access to Pay Group but not O rg 
Structure 
User will only be able to access the payroll data for 
employees that are in the org units they have been granted 
access to.  
 
If the user has access to the employee’s Pay Group but not 
their Org Unit, they will not see that employee on People 
Management.

1.2. What is an Organisation Code? 
An organisation may be made of one or more individual companies which operate independently of 
each other. To distinguish between the different companies and how they operate for payroll, each 
organisation can configure multiple companies, with unique company codes. 
 
Organisations and their individual companies are also linked directly to pay groups. Each company may 
have multiple pay groups configured. To have access to a pay group, you must also have access to the 
company.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of this Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2021/22 
and prepare for the 2022/23 tax year. This document covers the following: 
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget. 
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release. 
• The tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.  
• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task. 
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2022/23 tax year.  
 
 
1.2. What is Year End? 
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to: 
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.  
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.  
• Run the Year End Cleardown task. 
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.   
• Issue Employees with a P60.  
 
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks: 
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.  
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.  
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’ 
table. 
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years. 
 
The UK Year End Software Release provides our customers with the following: 
• The preloaded rate changes as outlined by HMRC for the new tax year. 
• The software updates required to process the legislative changes set out by HMRC.

3.2.1. Overview 
On 7 September 2021 the government announced a new 1.25% Health and Social Care Levy to 
fund investment in the NHS and social care.  
 
The Levy will be effectively introduced from April 2022 when National Insurance Contributions 
(NICs) for working age employees, self-employed people and employers will increase by 1.25% and 
be added to the existing NHS allocation. This increased NIC rate is automatically applied from April 
2022 within the payroll system.   
 
From April 2023, the Levy will be formally separated from NICs and also apply to the earnings of 
individuals working above State Pension age and National Insurance Contribution rates will return 
to 2021-22 levels. A software update for this will be part of next year’s UK Year end update. 
 
To ensure taxpayers understand that their increased contribution is helping fund public services, 
HMRC are asking employers to put a message on payslip templates explaining what these funds 
will be used for. The message applies to all payslips for the Tax year 2022/23 and should read 
“1.25% uplift in NICs funds NHS, health & social care”. 
 
 
3.2.2. Add Payslip Message 
To add the payslip message, go to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups and populate the payslip message 
fields.

The requested wording from HMRC to use is:  
• “1.25% uplift in NICs funds NHS, health & social care”

3.3. NI Letters 
3.3.1. New Letters 
As part of the updates for Veteran & Freeport NIC calculation changes , five new NI Letters have 
been inserted into the system. These new NI letters are: 
 
• F – Freeport standard category letter 
• I – Freeport Married women and widows entitled to pay reduced NICs 
• S – Freeport employees above state pension age 
• L – Freeport employees who defer paying 12% NIC, only paying 2% because they are paying 
it in another job 
• V – Veterans NIC 
Users will now, once in the 2022/23 tax year on the system, be able to assign one of these new NI 
letters to an employee’s record. 
 
 
3.4. Veteran NIC 
3.4.1. Tax Year April 2022+ 
Veteran NIC relief provides a zero -rate of secondary Class 1 National Insurance contributions 
(NICs) on the earnings of a qualifying veteran for 12 consecutive months from the first day of their 
first civilian employment after leaving the regular armed forces.  
 
This zero-rate can be applied up to the (new) Veteran’s Upper Secondary Threshold (VUST). From 
April 22 onwards, employers will be able to apply the relief in real time through RTI. 
 
To give this relief to an Employee they are assigned the NI Letter V in the system. This is done via 
the Employee Tax Detail Screen.  
 
  
UK Payroll Year End 2022/23 – Portal User Guide            
Access Limited Distribution Page 13 of 101 
A new field: "Veteran NIC Date Effective" has also been added to the Employee Tax Details screen:  
• This field has been added to allow users to capture the original date of Veteran NIC 
Claim.  
• The system does not automatically move an employee off the veteran NIC letter. 
However, this new field will allow users to report on the employees to see how long they 
have been on the Veteran NIC letter.  
• The Insight Person Master view has been updated to support reporting on this new 
Veteran NIC Date Effective field. 
 
 
 
 
3.4.2. Tax Year 2021/22 
This Veteran NIC relief is available from April 2021.  
 
From April 2022 this relief is claimed via payroll submission. However, for retrospective claims 
from April 2021 to March 2022, employers will have paid the associated Secondary Class 1 NICs as 
normal and will now need to claim it back retrospectively from April 2022 onwards. 
 
This reclaim of Veteran NIC relief for the 2021 /22 tax year is not being supported through the 
software. Instead, where an employer wishes to claim Veteran NIC relief for the 2021/22 tax year, 
they would do so by sending a simple letter to HMRC.  

UK Payroll Year End 2022/23 – Portal User Guide

In this letter you will need to include 
• the reference (heading) ‘Overpaid NI contributions’ 
• the employee’s name, date of birth and National Insurance number 
• an explanation that you are reclaiming Veteran’s relief 
• the period(s) they have overpaid in 
• confirmation that they are claiming for a qualifying veteran and retain evidence to show 
this (HMRC may request to see this evidence at a later date) 
• the account number, sort code and account name for the bank account where they want 
their refund to be paid 
 
 
3.5. Freeport Workers 
3.5.1. Freeport NIC Category Letters 
The government intends to create up to 11 Freeports in various locations within the UK. From 6 
April 2022, a reduced rate of employer NICs will apply to all Freeport based businesses.  
 
This will mean all employers based within and employing people working within the Freeport 
geographic area can apply a zero-secondary rate of employer NICs for those employees’ earnings 
above the secondary threshold up to and including a newly established Freeport Upper 
Secondary Threshold (FUST). Anything above this rate will be charged at 13.8%.  
 
To be eligible, the employee must be a new hire after April 2022 and must not have worked for 
that employer (or a business connected to that employer) in the previous 24 months. They must 
also spend a minimum of 60% of their time working within the Freeport tax site.  
 
To support this change, four, new Freeport NIC category letters are to be introduced: 
•    F – standard category letter 
•    I – married women and widows entitled to pay reduced NICs 
•    S – employees above state pension age 
•    L - employees who defer paying 12% NICs, only paying 2% because they are paying it 
in another job 
 
The new category letters reflect existing NIC category letters A, B, C and J.

In the extremely rare circumstance that the employer has an employee for whom they would use 
a different NIC category letter (the example of Mariners is provided), then they would need to 
contact HMRC at the end of the tax year to establish a manual process by which to calculate and 
claim the relief. 
 
The new Freeport NI Letters and associated rates have been automatically preloaded within the 
software.

updated via Settings > Pension Scheme > Page 2.

• Change 2: Band Assessment to move to be based off actual earnings (from the current 
process based on whole time equivalent)  
o If using tiered pension schemes there is an option on Settings > Pension Schemes > 
Page 2 to configure the pension scheme to be based off actual earnings instead of 
FTE.  
o If using normal pension scheme set up the allocation of the pension scheme to 
an employee is already done manually and will remain a user decision.  
 
• Change 3: Aggregation of multiple part-time employments held with a single 
employer                 
o Sites will currently be configured as pension by person or pension by 
appointment.  
▪ Current Functionality  
• Where pension by person the aggregated earnings are 
automatically used to determine tier/contributions depending on 
the pension scheme set up.  
• Where pension by appointment each appointment earnings are 
assessed individually. 
▪ New Functionality  
• Where pension by person there is no change required.  
• Where pension by appointment a software change is being 
introduced that will allow users to identify which pension 
schemes are NHS Pension schemes and aggregate the earnings 
for band assessment purposes.

The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks: 
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.

2. Overview 
2.1. The Purpose of the Document 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the data migration functionality on 
People XD and highlight the enhancements made in v28 to support existing and upgrading customers. 
 This includes: 
• What is the data migration tool and when is it used? 
• How to complete a data migration. 
• How to resolve errors during upload. 
• How to clear down files (reverse the migration) for uploaded files and processed records.  
 
This document does not provide detailed gui dance on how to complete each of the data migration 
templates. Refer to the helper files that can be downloaded from the Data Migration Templates widget. 
 
The Data Migration Update Facility  widget is not covered in this document. Please refer to the Data 
Migration Update Facility user guide.  
 
2.2. What is the Data Migration Tool? 
The data migration process typically occurs when an organisation is initially implementing XD  and is 
used to bulk import their records.  
 
This includes: 
• Employees and their associated personal details. 
• Contracts and their associated elements, including salary details. 
• Occupational absences and payroll cumulative history. 
• Selected reference data elements. 
 
This tool provides a set of 26 data migration templates. These can be downloaded from XD and 
populated with actual system records. These files can then be loaded to XD, validated and processed 
so that the corresponding records are created on the system.  
 
2.3. Data Migration vs Updates 
The data migration tool is used to insert new records to XD. This is not used to change / update existing 
records. Both the Data  Migration Templates  and Data Migration Options  widgets are used for this 
process. 
 
The Data Migration Update Facility widget is used to update existing records. Please refer to the Data 
Migration Update Facility user guide.

configuration of Data Migration improvements.

4. Overview of the Data Migration Process 
The data migration process on XD is completed in four main steps: 
 
 
 
 
# Step Description 
1 Download Template Download the data migration template file from XD. 
2 Complete the Template 
Open the template in excel.  
Update the template with the required records.  
Save as a CSV file. 
3 Upload File to XD Upload the completed file in CSV format to XD.  
4 Process Records 
Update / edit records before processing. 
Process each record in the data migration file.  
Resolve issues for any records that fail to load. 
 
Important Considerations: 
• The data migration process requires the records to be supplied in a specific order and format. 
Therefore, template files are provided to ensure that the records are supplied in an acceptable 
format for processing to be created on XD.  
• There are many data migration template files available on XD, each used to upload different 
record types. The full list of these is available in 2.8 What Templates are Available?.  
• Certain configuration must already be completed on XD  before attempting to load a data 
migration file. Furthermore, there is a recommended order that should be followed when loading 
files to XD. More details on this available in 2.9 File Upload Order & Pre-Requisite Configuration
. 

Module V#: Document Title - User Guide            
 
• Downloading Records is new to v28 and only available to Super User and User profiles that 
have been authorised access to download functionality. See File Download

5.5. Uploading Status  
 
To avoid the UI timing out when a file is uploaded into the Data Migration tool, the user is re -directed 
back to the Data Migration Options (Upload Facility) widget if the file size is greater than the 300 record 
threshold. 
 
When a file is uploaded into the XD Data Migration tool (user clicks ‘ok’ on the ‘Upload’ modal) 
 
If the file has (less than) < 300 records then: 
• The File Detail/Edit screen will be automatically displayed as soon as the file finishes loading. 
• If the user closes out of the File Detail/Edit screen without processing any records then the

5.7. Clear Down Data Migration Files  
It is possible to clear down data migration files that have been loaded to XD. This will reverse any data 
migration actions completed for that file, including the removal of: 
• records that have been processed and are now on the XD database. 
• any reference data items that were dynamically created as part of the process, if they are not 
linked to any other non-data migration records. 
 
The clear down will remove all records, regardless of the file or record status i.e.

process. 
In Progress

“Failed” and “Ready”.

available to process.  
Complete records will be removed from the XD  database 
i.e. the data migration is reversed for those records.

 Note:  
• Only records that are “Ready”, “In Progress” or “Failed” will be cancelled. 
• If any records are processed and flagged as “Complete”, these will not be undone.  
• If any records are “Failed” and a change has been applied via Display Errors > Row Errors 
but not processed, these changes are lost. 
• If any changes have been made to the records, these are not saved and will need to be 
applied again before the file is processed 
 
 Note:  
The following files cannot be cleared down: 
• Balance Assignments File 
• RTI File 
Note that the RTI file load works like an update. It updates fields on the employee record 
(rather than inserting a new record). Therefore, to resolve incorrect RTI fields being loaded 
for an employee it is possible to upload a new RTI file for the employee and this will override 
the previous changes.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide detailed guidance on the ‘Wage Warnings’ feature 
on  PeopleXD, including: 
• Where the wage warning validation is applied. 
• How the warning validation is calculated. 
• How to configure ‘Minimum Wage’, ‘Living Wage’ & ‘Apprentice Wage’ rates on 
PeopleXD (per tax year). 
• Additional configuration required to enable the validation for ‘Minimum Wage’ / ‘Living 
Wage’ / ‘Apprentice Wage’ rates on PeopleXD. 
 
 
1.2. How do the Wage Warnings Work? 
1.2.1. What are Wage Warnings? 
 
PeopleXD provides an option to validate the rate entered for an employee’s salary, against 
minimum, living and / or apprentice wage rates. This is to inform the user if the salary they 
are providing for the  employee’s contract is too  low. 
 
Rates for minimum wage, living wages and apprentice wages can be setup on PeopleXD (see 
2. Configuring the Rates). These can be added to on an annual basis, as new rates are 
released for each new tax year. 
 
PeopleXD will calculate if the salary supplied for an employee’s contract meets the minimum 
/ living / apprentice wage rates based on: 
• The rates defined on PeopleXD and their effective date. 
• The employee’s date of birth. 
• Contracted hours and weeks (or FTE Weeks per Year). 
People Management: Wage Warnings – Configuration Guide

• For apprentice rates, validation is applied to confirm that the employee / contract is 
apprentice. 
• Where multiple countries are setup, the appropriate rates for the employee’s Pay 
Group country. 
 
Minimum wage & apprentice rates are not mutually exclusive. The system will first check to 
see if the employee’s contract is an apprentice type contract. 
• If it is - apprentice rates are used in validation. 
• If it isn’t - minimum wage rates are used in validation 
 
1.2.2. Where is Wage Warning Validation Available? 
 
The wage warnings are displayed on the following screens: 
• New Hire / Rehire wizard (Step 4 – Salary)

3. How is Validation Applied? 
3.1. Validation Steps 
 
The same validation checks are made when a salary is awarded on any of these screens: 
• New hire / rehire wizards 
• New Contract / Replace Contract wizards 
• Salary Amendment screens 
• Salary approval screen. 
 
The system will first check if the following details have been supplied for the contract: 
1. Date of Birth (Required to determine employee’s age) 
2. Contracted Hours 
3. Contracted Weeks 
If blank, the system will default to use the value in the FTE Weeks per Year parameter 
 
If any of the above are not present  on the contract, the following validation  messages are 
triggered: 
• “Minimum wage validation will not work without: Date of Birth, Contracted Hours” 
• “Living wage validation will not work without: Date of Birth, Contracted Hours” 
 

People Management: Wage Warnings – Configuration Guide 
Page 27 of 29 Access Limited Distribution 
 
 
 
 
 
Salary details need to be input: 
• Pay Group is required (to ensure that validation is made against the rates defined for that 
country) 
• Amount to be paid is required 
 
The system will check if this is an apprentice contract: 
• If the employee’s contract is a match for the  Reference Type configured for Apprentice 
Rate, then the validate will use these rates. 
• If the employee’s contract is not a match for the Reference Type configured for Apprentice 
Rate, then the validation will use the Minimum Wage rates. 
 
The system will then determine if the amount provided for the contract is valid. 
• If an hourly rate has  been provided, this is a straightforward check against the system 
rates. 
• If a non-hourly rate has been  provided, the system will use the contracted hours and 
contracted weeks / FTE weeks per year, to determine the hourly rate. 
 
Using the hourly rate, the validation will compare this to the rates stored for Apprentice 
/ Minimum Wage and Living Wage 
• If the rate is too low, a warning message will appear 
 
Note: These warning messages will only trigger if the corresponding Minimum / Living 
/ Apprentice Wage Warnings have been flagged as active.

• If the rate is >= the min rates, no further message will appear. 
 
3.2. Point to Note

still proceed to save the salary. This is a warning message only. 
• If different rates are held for each tax year, the validation will compare the salary using the 
rate that is active on the salary effective date. 
• If no rates exist, no validation is applied 
• If effective date for rates > that salary effective date, no validation is applied 
• If no Country is specified for the rates:

1.2.4. Leave Requests versus Absences

2.2. Managing Balance Assignments 
2.2.1. Balances Overview 
When assigning a new balance, only fields applicable to the balance selected are displayed. The table 
below provides explanations for each field: 
Field Explanation 
Reserved entitlement 
Refers to the portion of your entitlement that must be taken on certain days. 
You cannot choose when to take it. For example, a factory shutting down 
for two weeks in July. 
Floating entitlement 
Portion of your entitlement tha t you are free to take anytime  (subject to 
approval and outage periods) i.e. you get an entitlement at the start of the 
year and you can take the leave any time (you don’t have to wait until you 
have worked it up). 
Accrued entitlement 
Used for certain employees (casual employees, or employees working 
variable hours) . They accrue t heir entitlements to leave ov er time (as 
opposed to getting their full entitlement at the start of the leave period). 
Allowance This is Reserved + Floating + Accrued 
Carried Forward 
This holds the days/hours that were automatically carried forward from the 
previous period into this period. Managers/Admins can manually adjust this 
also. The Carried Over + Entitlement values = Balances. 
Taken 
These hours are calculated to the employee’s  T&A record b ased on 
Booked Absences or Approved Requests. (This can be overridden). 
Booked This is leave requested that has been approved but not taken. 
Requested 
This is leave requested that hasn’t been approved regardless of whether it 
is in the future or not. 
Remaining This is the remaining balance. This does not include requested leave. 
 
There are three main variations of the Assign New Balance screen:

example their Pay Scale, Organization Structure Element; their Company or Category.

• Variation 3: Other balances – not set up as either ‘Variation 1’ or ‘Variation 2’. 
 
View section 5.1 Balance Types for Balance Variation driving parameter configuration. 
 
In addition, the balance start date and end date fields are only displayed if the balance selected is set 
up as a Personal Calendar Balance.

user’s access outside of the JML processes

access to the system for a set number of days after their Leave Date

Employee Offboarding  
The Social Hub dashboard now caters for Offboarding as well as Onboarding and Cross-Boarding.  
 
This is initiated when an employee is made a leaver on People Management and allows HR to create 
tailored offboarding journeys for different staff groupings. 
 
The key elements of the Offboarding feature are:  
1. Checklists 
Assign checklists/tasks to employees to be completed as part of the leaver process.  
Checklist tasks can be assigned X days before the employee’s Date Left.  
Checklist tasks can be assigned by cri teria group, allowing HR to define different tasks for 
employees in different parts of the organisation, for permanent/temporary staff etc. 
 
2. Pages 
Pages can be assigned to employees to consume additional content created for them as part 
of their leaver journey.  
 
3. Surveys 
Surveys are new to Onboarding/Offboarding in v28 and allow HR to provide a questionnaire to 
the leaver to complete. The survey can be added as a checklist item for the leaver. 
 
4. Reviewing Employee Documents 
In v28, you can share documents that have been stored on the employee’s CoreHR record with 
them to review as part of a checklist task, during the offboarding process.  
 
5. Notifications 
The Notifications have been extended in v28 to ensure that reminders/updates are triggered for 
Offboarding checklist tasks, as well as Onboarding.  
 
6. Offboarding Progress 
New Offboarding Progress options are available for HR on the Command Centre widget and 
Managers on the My Team widget.

HR Process Task Lists Enhancements 
The HR Process Task List functionality has been enhanced in v28 to include a variety of new features.  
1. Leaver Task Lists 
A new Leaver tab is available on the HR Task List screen, which allows you to define a checklist 
of tasks to be completed when an employee is made a leaver on CoreHR e.g. to Assign Leaver 
Access. 
2. Task Owners 
Task list items can now be assigned to a specified owner to complete.  
• The task ownership is identified using a specified org role/org group assignment 
• For example, access to Assign User Access may be restricted to security administrators 
only. 
• If a user is not the owner and doesn’t have access to complete a task item, they will 
see the item on the Task List screen, which will flag the Org Role responsibl e for 
completing the task and they will be prevented from access the task itself. 
3. Task List Restrictions 
• Task list items can be restricted, allowing you to create tailored task lists for different 
employee categories and functions e.g. different task list items to be assigned to 
permanent v agency staff. 
• This is achieved using criteria groups i.e. only assign this task if the employee is in one 
of the defined Criteria Groups. 
• If no restrictions are set, the task is applicable to all employees. 
4. New Specific UDF Task 
A new task called Specific UDF is available to be added to all task lists. This allows you to select 
a specific UDF that you have set up on People Management for completion as part of the task.  
5. Optional Information 
The new Optional Information text field is available when configuring every task item. The 
information provided here is displayed to the user when completing the task, to give them further 
guidance on what they may need to do. 
6. All Tasks are Mandatory 
In earlier versions, tasks could be flagged as mandatory or optional.  
From v28, all tasks are mandatory by default.   
7. Tasks Can be Completed in Any Order 
In earlier versions, tasks could only be completed in the order they were presented on screen 
i.e. you couldn’t complete task 2 before task 1.  
From v28, tasks can be completed in any order.  
8. Task List Completes Automatically 
In earlier versions, when all tasks were completed a user was required to complete the task list 
as a separate action,

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
This guide is used to explain how to use the Payroll Instruction Forms via People Management. In order 
to capture and automatically share pay-affecting information with Payroll, as part of the 
joiner/mover/leaver processes e.g. holidays to be paid to a leaver, student loans for a new hire etc.  
 
Within this User Guide you will learn how to: 
• Create a custom form. 
• Add a new HR task list item of Payroll Instructional Form. 
• Assign a specific Org Role to this task. 
• View & action the task on Pay Portal. 
 
1.2. What is a Payroll Instructional Form? 
A Payroll Instructional Form is a method of communication that is sent to Payroll directly from HR in 
terms of details that are going to affect the employee’s payroll record once processed. Examples of 
these items include: 
 
1. Balance adjustments needed for holidays owed to an employee. 
2. Outstanding student loan payments. 
3. PAYE / Tax Code changes. 
4. Holiday/Average Pay calculations. 
5. Hours (i.e. Overtime). 
6. Adhoc Payments (i.e. Bonuses & once off payments). 
7. Pension changes. 
8. Pay Awards inc Position and Point updates/increases via AdHoc module (maybe this is covered 
in the Salary approvals piece) 
9. Late Leavers / Joiners / Rejoiners 
10. Temp Reinstatements 
11. Any cancel/manual payments to be processed 
12. Cost Allocation changes

• Uncovered shifts 
• Roster notifications

7. AutoRoster 
 AutoRoster Overview 
AutoRoster is a process that can be run to  automatically generate  a Team Area’s Roster. The 
AutoRoster process considers a set of rules, dictating the logic that gets applied, for filling the staffing 
requirements of a Team Area. This means that the AutoRoster process looks at the business logic and 
organisational rules you require the system to apply , when choosing the most appropriate employee s 
to fill each Roster gap. 
 
The AutoRoster process looks at the Validation Rules, that have been assigned to the Team Area, and 
the employee Roster Contract Details , that have been configured within the system. Based on these 
criteria, the process then rosters employees accordingly subject to their availability and suitability.  
 
It is possible for the  AutoRostering process to be configured so that certain days are priority . For 
example, busier days such as Saturdays or Sundays can be rostered to fill staffing requirements first. 
 
There are multiple ways to configure AutoRoster, subject to your organisational requirements. For 
further information on the AutoRoster configuration options, view the General Roster Configuration 
training material on CoreHR University. 
 
 
 Run AutoRoster 
To run the AutoRoster process for a Team Area: 
1. Select AutoRoster from the Workforce Management Dashboard.

3. Specify the Roster Week.

10. Time Exceptions 
 Time Exceptions Overview 
Time Exceptions are generated when an employee works over or under the hours they are scheduled 
to work. Exceptions are generated when the clocking’s entered on an employee’s timesheet do not 
match the Roster Details on the Workforce Management details. The Time Exceptions screen allows 
for full Exception Management. 
 
10.1.1. What is Exception Management? 
Exception Management is intended for use by managers, supporting the: 
• Listing of items to be Actioned, with Supporting Information. 
• Actions to be taken. For example, Approve/Reject, or Recode Exception  (where the options 
have been pre-determined). 
• Completion of Actions from a  single screen, with the ability to Drill Down  to employee’s 
Timesheet, Absence Record or Roster. 
• Access via single screen, highlighting the number of exceptions that require Action.  
 
Some example exceptions can include: 
• Employee clocks in/out earlier or later than Rostered 
• Employee does not show up to work 
• Employee forgets to clock out after work 
• Missed clockings 
 
 
For full detail and configuration regarding Exception Management , view t he Exception Management 
training material on CoreHR University.

WFM V28: Generate Timesheets - User Guide            
 
1. Overview 
 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide.  
 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to generate timesheets.  This functionality 
for generating timesheets was previously completed through the Back Office  and is now available on 
CorePortal.  This is a brand new CoreHR feature for V28.  There are no changes to the existing Payroll 
Rules and how they are configured. 
 
This guide will instruct you how to how to: 
• Retrieve Hours for Payroll.  
• View Generated Payroll Hours detail. 
• Transfer hours to Payroll. 
 
 
1.2. General Overview. 
 
The Generate Ti mesheets is now available in Portal – from either the Workforce Management 
Dashboard or the Admin  Dashboard.  This allows more streamlined payroll integration.  This gives you: 
 
• Improved functionality access alongside Payportal. 
• View details of converted hours before transferring them to Payroll. 
• The possibility of continuing tasks while the applications run in the background. 
• An estimation given of the length of the process. 
• Notifications given on completion of the processes.

2. Functionality Overview 
 
2.1. Process 
 
The Generate Timesheets process takes place in two steps: 
 
• Ready to Retrieve: Step 1: This converts T&A timesheets into Payroll Hours based on payroll 
rules configured in WFM. 
• Ready to Transfer : Step 2 : This transfers Payroll Hours to CoreHR Payroll  or c reates a n 
interface file where applicable. 
 
 
2.2. How to Retrieve Hours 
 
By using the Retrieve Hours function you are converting timesheets in to Payroll hours. This allows you 
to select specific calendars within a company and send them to Payroll.

5.4. Generate Timesheet and Balance Re calculation for Leavers (Back End) 
 
Currently some customers input employee end dates on the same day the Generate Timesheets  is in 
final mode.  If the end date is within the period being closed, the result is that the employee gets marked 
as a leaver before the rec alculation runs at the end of the Generate Timesheet process or overnight .  
Leavers are excluded from the balance recalculation.  The  implication is that the employees closing 
annual leave balance on CoreHR is incorrect and could lead to the employee being overpaid.  

WFM V28: Generate Timesheets - User Guide            
 
 
Additional Considerations: 
• The balance configuration must include links to pro-rata end dates, otherwise it’s excluded. 
• The balance open period should contain the T&A period being closed. 
• With Generate Timesheets, the balance recalculation only applies to leavers that fall within the 
current period being processed. 
 
 
5.5. Generate Timesheet Processing and Employee not on Payroll 
 
• In previous versions of the Generate Timesheets to payroll, the system stopped processing for 
future dated employees in WFM that had not been onboarded into payroll. 
• From V28 the stop has been altered to ‘warn’ where future date employee exists and no 
attendance has been recorded (i.e. start date is after the end of the current WFM period) 
 
 
Examples: 
• If employees are starting in the future (i.e start date later than the end of the period being 
processed) 
• If there are no attendance hours entered for the period. 
• Issuing of a warning message to allow the generate timesheet process to continue. 
• Warning message text “Warning - No Employee record on Payroll (Future new starter) 
 
Additional Considerations 
• Work Group is set to ‘Live’ and marked as Generate Timesheets. 
• Employee is not set as non-generate timesheets at person level. 
• If future dated employees have attendance recorded in the period being closed, the existing 
stop process remains.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Transfers feature in People 
Management, including: 
• How to create a transfer request. 
• How to view the status of a request. 
• How to approve / reject a request. 
• How to cancel a request. 
• How to complete a request and create the required contract. 
 
 
1.2. What are Transfers? 
1.2.1. HR Access 
In CoreHR, the hr administrator’s access to employees on the system is restricted based on their 
designated HR Access. This HR Access is aligned to an Organisational Unit e.g. this may be set to: 
• Company = ABC Solutions 
• Department = Human Resources 
• Division = Shared Services 
 
Every employee on CoreHR will be assigned to at least one contract. That contract will specify the 
Organisation Units that the employee’s position is aligned to e.g.  
• Company = ABC Solutions 
• Department = Human Resources 
• Division = Shared Services 
 
If the user has access to the Department e.g. Human Resources, then they will be able to see the 
employee record and their contract in that department.  
 
However, if the user doesn’t have access to the Department e.g. Finance, then they will not be able to 
see the employee record and their contract in that department.  
 
 
1.2.2. Transfer Requests 
If a hr administrator doesn’t have access to an employee on CoreHR, but requires the ability to transfer 
them into a new contract within their organisation, then they need to complete a ‘Transfer Request’.  
 
  
People Management v28: Employee Transfers – User Guide            
CoreHR Limited Distribution

For example: 
• John has one active contract in the Accounts department.  
• Mary is a hr administrator and only has access to employees in the HR and Payroll departments.  
• John will be moving to a new position with a new contract in the Payroll department. However, 
Mary cannot complete the Replace Contract steps that are usually used to replace one contract 
with a new contract, because she doesn’t have access to the employee on CoreHR.  
• Therefore, Mary must initiate a transfer request which will request for John to be: 
▪ transferred out of their current contract i.e. in Accounts. 
▪ transferred into a new proposed contract in their organisation i.e. in Payroll. 
• Barry is a hr administrator with access to the Accounts department. He must approve / reject 
this request, in order for Mary to be able to create the new replacement contract in Payroll. 
 
 
Further Considerations: 
• The request will always be initiated by the user who doesn’t have currently have access to the 
employee on CoreHR and who needs to create the new contract.  
• The request is never initiated by the person who already has access to the employee but will 
not be creating the new contract 
• If a user has access to the employee in the first place, they do not need to complete a transfer 
request. Instead, they can complete a Replace Contract process.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of Document 
The purpose of this guide is to provide an overview of user guidance and the configuration associated 
with the Overlapping Warnings feature. Items covered include: 
• Overlapping warnings configuration 
• Dashboard configuration 
• Security configuration 
• Viewing overlapping warnings 
 
 
1.2. Overview of Feature 
Overlapping Warnings display during the actioning of employee Leave Requests, alerting the approver 
at the approval/rejection stage. This feature alerts approvers if a Leave Request overlaps with: 
 
• An absence or approved Leave Request for another employee in the approver’s remit. 
• An un-actioned request for another employee in the approver’s remit. 
• A previously rejected request for the same employee.

2. Max Daily Pay Code Limit (Pay Code Setting) 
2.1. Overview 
There is a Max Daily Limit value that can be applied at Pay Code level. This prevents users from entering 
values greater than the value stored at the Pay Code level. 
 
This can be applied for the following examples of use: 
• Value Pay Codes: Meal allowance, cannot enter more the €10 / £10 per day. 
• Unit Pay Codes: On Call allowance, cannot enter a value greater than 1 on call. 
• Hours Pay Codes: Cannot enter more than 8.00 hours annual leave. 
 
For example, an employee cannot have more than a co nfigurable number of hours a nnual leave 
recorded on one Pay Code, per day, than the Max Daily Limit value applied at Pay Code level. 
• This prevents users from entering values greater than the value stored on the Pay Code. 
• Validation alerts can be configured to stop entry on all screens except the Approve/Sign Off 
screen, which can display: 
o Warning – the user is warned but can continue with Sign Off. 
o Stop – the user cannot continue with Sign Off.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on CoreInsight iCues including: 
• What are iCues? 
• How are they setup and managed? 
• Where are the corresponding alerts available and to who? 
• How to configure iCues on your CoreHR instance. 
 
1.2. What are iCues?  
iCues are intelligent trigger -based reports, designed to proactively send alerts to stakeholders, 
when certain thresholds are breached/events are occurring. 
 
Examples of how iCues could be used include: 
• Alert a manager when one of their employees is approaching the sick leave threshold. 
• Alert a manager of overlapping leave. 
• Alert an HRD when attrition rates spike. 
• Alert the FD when costs are increasing.  
• Alert an employee when they have a large annual leave balance remaining. 
• Alert an employee/manager of an important date e.g. anniversary, birthday etc. 
 
The foundation for an iCue is an intelligent report built in CoreInsight or downloaded from the 
Report Store, which is used to trigger a notification to a specified recipient.  
• The report  includes complex calculations that are used to determine when these 
thresholds are breached, or events are about to occur. 
• CoreHR runs the iCue report on a specified frequency (daily/weekly/monthly). 
• Pre-configured alerts can be sent to a specified recipient via a number of methods 
o CorePortal Notification Centre or iCue widget. 
o Email 
o Mobile App Alerts (Home screen) 
• Alerts may include a Call to Action , to redirect the recipient to a CorePortal  widget to 
complete an associated task e.g. if an employee is being alerted that they have a large

time off.  
• Alerts to managers can include Suggested Correspondence , to prompt the manager to 
forward a message directly to the affected employee e.g. if a manager is alerted that their 
team member is approaching their work anniversary, they may be presented with a pre -
configured message that they can update and forward to the employee.

The iCue is generated based on the frequency that you have defined in the iCue settings i.e. daily, 
weekly, or monthly.

generated to retrieve the data.  
• If records are found, alerts are sent the following morning to the specified recipients.  
• If no records are found, no alerts are triggered. 
• This is repeated based on your iCue frequency i.e. daily, weekly or monthly.

triggered and sent to the recipient e.g.

congratulate the employee personally.

congratulate them on their anniversary.

1.2.1. How are Files Uploaded? 
The Files feature in People Management is used to manage documentation associated with an 
employee’s record.  
 
Files may be linked to an employee’s record in a number of ways: 
• Directly uploaded by the hr administrator on People Management > Files screen. 
• Generated by the system and automatically uploaded by the Generate Document feature on 
CoreHR. 
• Uploaded by the employee via the My Profile > Documents screen. 
• Uploaded by the manager via the Employee Profile > Documents  screen OR as per the hr 
administrator (if hr tasks have been devolved to managers).

1.2.3. What are Document Types? 
When a document is uploaded, it is stored against a Document Type. This is essentially a categorisation 
or grouping that is applied to the document which can make it easier to store and search the files.  
 
When it comes to sharing access to documents with employees and managers via the Employee Profile 
screen, it is possible to define per Document Type, whether the employee / manager should be able to 
view and/or upload documents. If those settings haven’t been ena bled on the Document Type, then 
employees and managers will be restricted from viewing and/or uploading files against it.  
 
Document Types are defined as either: 
1. Person: i.e. files of this type are related to the employee directly and not one of their contracts.  
2. Contract: i.e. files of this type are related to a specific contract for an employee. 
 
Guidance on how to configure Document Types is provided in the Configuring Employee Files user 
guide. 
 
 
1.3. Security Options for Administrator Access to Files 
There are 2 security options available when granting access to administrators to access files on People 
Management.  
 
1. Access to All Files 
It is possible to allow the hr administrator to access all files stored for an  employee or their 
contracts i.e. access to all Document Types.  
 
2. Access Restricted by Document Type 
If required, the administrator’s access can be configured in such a way that access to view / 
upload files is restricted per Document Type.  
 
Guidance on how to configure each option is provided in the Configuring Employee Files user guide.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how the Payscale Restriction Matrix may 
be used on CoreHR to provide an additional element of control to the step of awarding a Pay Scale 
to an employee. This includes: 
• An overview of the Payscale Restriction Matrix feature. 
• How to configure matrix rules. 
• How to enable or disable the restriction. 
 
 
1.2. What is the ‘Payscale Restriction Matrix’? 
It is possible to restrict the list of Pay Scales that are available to a user to select for an employee’s 
salary, based on certain em ployee or contract attributes. A matrix of rules can be configured on 
CoreHR to identify the Pay Scales that are applicable to specific employee attributes e.g. Country, 
Division, Employment Status etc.  
 
When a hr administrator is creating the salary for an employee, the system will check to see if the 
record meets any of the rules defined on the matrix and will only display the Pay Scales that match 
those rules.  
 
For example, if the Pay Scales “Grade 1” and “Grade 2” should only apply to UK based employees, 
then the hr administrator will only see those Pay Scales when the employee’s address is based in 
Country of UK.  
 
Care needs to be taken when defining the matrix of rules to ensure that all employee scenarios 
are catered for because if an employee does not match any rule, no Pay Scale will be available.

1. Introduction 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how employee allowance records are managed 
on People Management. 
 
Guidance will be provided on the following topics: 
• Key concepts and terminology associated with allowances. 
• Creating an allowance. 
• Editing an existing allowance. 
• Ending an existing allowance. 
• Cancelling or deleting an allowance. 
• The impact of salary amendments on existing allowances. 
 
 
1.2. Allowances in HR vs Payroll 
The allowances that are setup in People Management for the employee’s contract are ‘permanent / 
reoccurring allowances’. These are allowances that are assigned to the employee’s contract for a fixed 
or open-ended period. Every ti me payroll is run for that employee’s contract , the allowance amount is 
calculated and included in the employee’s pay. 
 
For example: An employee is assigned a ‘Night Duty’ allowance of £25 per period (e.g. per month). The 
allowance was assigned to the empl oyee’s contract with a start date of 1 st March 2019. This is open-
ended i.e. no planned end date exists for the allowances and the intention is that the employee should 
continue to receive the allowance until further notice. Every month when Payroll is pro cessed, the 
allowance of £25 will be added to the employee’s calculated salary. 
 
Once-off allowance payments are not recorded in People Management. These are once off payment s 
that will be made for the employee for the current pay period e.g. a bonus payment. These are captured 
directly in Payroll. 
 
  
People Management v27: HR Allowances – User Guide            
CoreHR Internal 
Page 5 of 32 
1.3. Allowance Types 
There are a number of types of allowances supported on CoreHR. 
 
Allowance Type Description 
Value 
These Allowances will pay a single specified amount every pay period e.g. if an 
employee is on a monthly pay group and has a standard value allowance of 
£100, then £100 will be paid every month. 
 
There are 2 types of ‘Value’ based allowances: 
• Standard Value: A specified amount is defined on the Allowance Pay 
Code and that set amount is paid for all employees linked to it, for every 
pay period e.g. Night Duty allowance is set at £30 per period for 
everyone. 
• Variable Value : The amount to be paid is specific to the individual 
employee. This is not captured at the Pay Code level but it specified 
when setting up the allowance for the employee. This allows different 
employees to receive varying values for the same Allowance Pay Code 
e.g. Mary has a Night Duty allowance of £30 but John has a Night Duty 
allowance of £40. 
  
Please note: if an Allowance is required to have a standard value set up at Pay 
Code level for the majority of employees, but it is required to capture different 
values for that Allowance for a handful of employees, the Pay Code standard 
value can be overwritten when it is being set up for each employee. Please refer 
to Payroll user guides for further details on how these Allowance Pay Codes are 
configured for the options listed above. 
Percentage 
These Allowances will pay a percentage of the employee’s actual salary every 
pay period  
e.g. Tom gets £1000.00 per week gross pay. He gets a shift allowance of 12% 
of gross pay , so each week he is in receipt of and additional £120.00 shift 
allowance. Like the Standard Value Allowances the shift allowance percentage 
can be set up either at a Pay Code or employee level.  
Scaled 
Allows for a scale of specific allowance rates to be recorded on CoreHR and for 
a point on that scale to be assigned to the employee (similar to Pay Scale type 
salaries). 
• Fixed Point on Scale 
• Select Point on Scale 
 
People Management v27: HR Allowances – User Guide            
CoreHR Internal 
Page 6 of 32 
Allowance Type Description 
Scaled Allow ances are different from regular Allowances in two ways; firstly, 
they operate a rate depending on a point on scale and secondly , Scaled 
Allowances have a date effective. Having a date effective means that when 
calculating retrospection the Scaled Allowance can be taken into consideration. 
Negative 
This deducts a specified amount from the employee’s salary every pay period  
 
A negative Allowance is used in cases such as maternity pay or social welfare 
where the employee keeps a payment from the government a nd needs an 
amount deducted from their gross pay which is non-taxable and non-PRSIable. 
  
E.g. Mary is on maternity leave. She receives and keeps the cheque from social 
welfare of £244 per week. Her gross pay while working is £500 per week. We 
want to give Mary £500 gross which is made up of £266 of maternity pay from 
the company and £244 of social welfare maternity pay. 
  
To pay maternity pay correctly in this instance we do the following: 
• Allow the system to generate Gross Pay of £500 for Mary 
• Set Up a Negative allowance, deduct from the gross amount 
• Attach the allowance to Mary with a value of £244 Euro 
  
This will deduct £244 from Mary’s taxable and PRSIable gross pay. A record of 
the payment is on the system and can be queried from reporting and the pay 
history. 
  
Allowances, both positive and negative appear on the same side of a payslip.  
 
 
1.4. Allowances and the Pay Multiplier 
The pay Multiplier is not captured directly on the Allowance record. Instead this is inherited from the 
associated salary record on the Contract. 
 
For Example: 
• An employee is set up as a ‘New Hire ’ with a salary of £52,000 on 26 th March 201 8. The 
Multiplier is 1 i.e. the employee will receive the full salary amount. 
• They are assigned a standard value allowance of £25, also with a start date of 26th March 2018. 
• The employee’s contract is amended on 22nd May 2019 to reflect a reduction in contract hours. 
A corresponding salary amendment is recorded, and the Multiplier is reduced to 0.5. A new line

of salary history exists.  No allowance amendment is required. When processing payroll after 
22nd May 2019, the system will recognise that the salary Multiplier has been reduced to 0.5 and 
will reduce the allowance amount calculated to £12.50 from that date onwards. 
 
 
1.5. Pay Group ‘Annual Allowance Ind’ 
The ‘Annual Allowance Ind’ can be set on the Pay Group definition. This means that any allowance  
values entered on People Management will be for the annual amount e.g. £1,200 for the year, rather 
than £100 per period for a monthly payroll.  
 
If the ‘Annual Allowance Ind’ is enabled for the employee’s Pay Group, the user will be able to see this 
when adding an allowance and the screen will request an ‘Annual Value’ etc for the employee’s 
allowance.

2.6. Cancelling an Allowance 
Cancelling an allowance ensures that the employee does not get paid for this allowance. This is useful 
if the allowance has been set up in error by HR. This process ensures that  the cancelled allowance 
record: 
• The allowance is effectively ended in both HR and Payroll. 
• Is searchable in HR with a status of “Cancelled”. 
• Is searchable in Payroll with a status of “Cancelled”. 
 
An allowance can be cancelled if all of the following conditions are met: 
• The Allowance is fully “Approved” i.e. if using Salary Approvals, it is not possible to cancel an 
allowance that is in a status of “Outstanding”. 
• The allowance is visible in Payroll i.e. employee payroll setup has been completed . 
 
An allowance cannot be cancelled if one or all the following conditions are met: 
• Allowance is “Pending” or “In Approval”. 
• Allowance is not visible in Payroll i.e. this implies the employee payroll setup has not been 
completed. 
 
If the allowance is fully “Approved” but not visible to Payroll  (i.e. employee payroll setup has not been 
completed), then the Cancel option is not applicable. In this instance, it is possible to directly delete the 
allowance from the system (see 2.7 Deleting an Allowance for further guidance). 
 
 
To cancel an allowance: 
1. On the Allowances screen, click the  button for the allowance record to be cancelled. 
2. Select the option Cancel.

1. Overview 
 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 
The purpose of this guide is to show the changes which have been made to the Person 
Maintenance screens which have now been migrated to Core Portal .  The Person Maintenance 
Screen was previously  only available in back office forms.  It is now available in Portal. 
 
A new WFM Administrator dashboard is now available to Administrators to complete their key 
WFM tasks. As the Administrator tasks become available on Portal, they will be added to the 
Workforce Manage Admin Dashboard. 
 
The purpose of the Person Maintenance screen is to provide a central area where administrators 
can view and amend employee’s information that relate to Workforce Management.    
 
As part of the migration , a number of enhancements have been completed to provide 
administrators with key tasks they need to complete in the one place. 
 
To begin with the following will be available on the dashboard: 
 
• WFM Person Maintenance 
• Generate Timesheets 
• WFM Configuration 
.

10.4. Bradford Factor 
 
The Bradford factor is a tool which a manager can use to track an employee’s absences.  This tab 
shows a manager what the Bradford factor score is for an employee. 
 
• The Bradford factor is used to calculate an employee’s Bradford factor score. B= S² x D 
• S = total number of spells (instances) of absence for that individual in the given 
period 
• D = total number of days the individual was absent during the given period 
• Managers can specify their predefined Bradford factor rule.  This will then calculate 
the Bradford Factor Score against an employee. 
 
• The details of the score displays: 
• Period 
• Start/End Dates 
• Trigger Value 
• Trigger Level
