1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Employee Onboarding functionality in 
People Management and how this is used. This includes: 
• What is Employee Onboarding and when it used by employees? 
• The difference between ‘new starter onboarding’ and ‘existing employee cross-boarding’. 
• An overview of the Social Hub dashboard. 
• Detailed guidance on the main elements of the Social Hub dashboard and how they may be 
used. 
• Tracking employee onboarding progress as a manager or hr administrator. 
 
Employee Onboarding  is highly configurable to ensure that every organisation can manage the 
onboarding and cross-boarding experience based on their own requirements. This document does not 
cover configuration guidance. For full training on how to set up and configure each element of Employee 
Onboarding, see the Employee Onboarding v28: How to Configure - User Guide. 
 
 
1.2. What is Employee Onboarding? 
Employee Onboarding is a platform that supports onboarding guidance for new joiners and re-joiners, 
while also supporting continuous onboarding guidance for existing employees. For example: 
• New starter onboarding for employees joining or re-joining the organisation. 
• Cross-boarding for existing employees who move to new contracts,  appointments, and/or  
teams. 
• The requirement to release new Checklist Items to existing employees. 
• A platform encouraging existing employees to engage with their wider team. 
 
Employees can commence onboarding before the join the organisation i.e. before their sta rt date or 
rehire date. If this is the case, the employee will need a CorePortal account (to be created in the same 
way as you generally issue CorePortal accounts).  However, they will only have access to the Social 
Hub until their start date has elapsed. They will not be able to access any other part of the CorePortal 
e.g. Employee Dashboard won’t be available to them until they have started.:

The table below explains the difference between onboarding and cross -boarding, including important 
considerations regarding the use of Checklists for both scenarios. 
 
Scenario Explanation 
Onboarding 
An employee is joining an organisation for the first time, or is a rehire. 
 
Checklist Considerations: 
• Global Checklist Items with no restrictions can be made available to the

• If there are Checklist Items present that have been restricted to only be 
seen by employees within a Criteria Gro up the employee resides in,

An existing employee is given a new contract, for example, moving from one

no longer relevant, therefore, are no longer available for the employee 
to complete. 
• If there are Checklist Items present that have been restricted to only be 
seen by the employee upon entering their new role, these Checklist 
Items are now relevant, therefore, are available for the employee to

3.2.1. Checklists Overview (Tasks Outstanding List) 
The checklist allows the user to complete all Checklist Items  that require completion for the typical 
onboarding scenarios, listed below: 
• Starter/Re-hire Onboarding 
• Cross-boarding 
• Ad-hoc checklist items 
 
The employee is required to complete the Checklist Items in sequence, for example, if an employee 
completes the first Checklist Item , this then unlocks the next item for completion, and the full list 
continues in this sequence. This ensures that employees review and complete important steps before 
completing another. For example, it may be important for an employee to review the organisational 
policy documents before updating their bank account details. 
 
 Note: Checklist Items that are not yet accessible in the list are not clickable and have the Start 
button greyed out.

It is possible to configure Checklist Items to only be available after an employee start date (join date or 
re-join date). If this configuration is in place, the Checklist Items  are still displayed on the Tasks 
Outstanding checklist but remain locked until the applicable date. 
 
 
 
3.2.2. Completed Items 
When a user completes a checklist item it will move into the Tasks Completed tab. Within the Tasks 
Completed tab they will be able to access the information that they uploaded to review but will not be 
able to change it. 
 
 Note: 
• This restriction is only applicable to new starters or re-joiners. If an employee is completing 
cross-boarding, requiring completion of a checklist item with this restriction enabled for new 
starters or re-joiners, it is still accessible for cross-boarding employees. 
• Employees are required to complete the Checklist Items in sequence, therefore, Checklist 
Items that are only available after an employee start date should be positioned appropriately 
within the list.

The Tasks Completed tab displays completed items regardless of whether the employee has moved 
positions within the organisation, which in turn assigns them a new checklist to complete, with exception 
to the following: 
• Past completed Checklist Items are cleared for re-joiners. 
• If an administrator deletes a checklist item, it is also removed from the completed list.  
• Items that are re-released are no longer present in the Tasks Completed list, until completion. 
 
3.2.3. Onboarding Scenarios 
Employee Onboarding can support both new starter and continuous onboarding scenarios, for example: 
 
New Starter Onboarding 
If an employee is joining the company for the first time, or is a rehire: 
• Global Checklist Items with no restrictions can be made available to the employee to complete. 
• If there are Checklist Items that have been restricted to only be seen by employees within a 
Criteria Group the employee resides in, these items are available for the employee to complete. 
 
Continuous Onboarding 
If an existing employee is given a new contract e.g. moving from ‘Department A’ to ‘Department B’: 
• Global Checklist Items with no restrictions can be made available to the employee to complete. 
• If there are Checklist Items that have been restricted to only be seen by employees within a 
‘Department A’ defined Criteria Group, these Checklist Items are no longer relevant, therefore, 
are no longer available for the employee to complete. 
• If there are Checklist Items that have been restricted to only be seen by employees within a 
‘Department B’ defined Criteria Group, these Checklist Items are now relevant, therefore, are 
available for the employee to complete.

1. Introduction 
1.1. Purpose of this Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Minimum Wage Exception 
Report in Payroll.  
 
 
1.2. What is the Minimum Wage Exception Report? 
This Minimum Wage Exception Report generates in both a PDF and CSV format. It displays Employees 
whose calculated hourly rate is below the expected Statutory Rate that the system has been set to 
apply based on the Employees’ age. 
The Minimum Wage Check and Living Wage Check can be generated for Payrolls with any country 
code. However, the Minimum Wage for Apprenticeship Rates Check is only applicable to UK Payrolls. 
 
 
1.3. Prerequisites to Using the Minimum Wage Exceptions Report 
Before using the Minimum Wage Exception Report in Payroll, you must: 
• Configure the National Minimum Wage (NMW), National Living Wage (NLW) and the 
Minimum Wage for Apprenticeship Rates and Rules in People Management.  
• Configure the Pay Codes to be included in the Minimum Wage/Living Wage Check. 
• Configure the Periodic Employee Hours on the Pay Group. 
 
 
 
1.4. Overview  
This document covers the following areas: 
• How to configure a Pay Code so it is included in the Minimum Wage/Living Wage Check. 
• How to configure the Periodic Employee Hours on the Pay Group. 
• How to generate the Minimum Wage Exception Report.

For details on how to configure the National Minimum Wage (NMW), National Living Wage (NLW)  
and the Minimum Wage for Apprenticeship Rates and Rules in People Management, see the People

2.1.2. Pay Code Configuration

4. Enable the Minimum Living Wage Check indicator.  
 
 
5. Click Save.  
 
 
 
 
  
 Note:

1.2. What is a Payroll Calendar? 
A payroll c alendar must be generated for each company within an organisation . The following points 
should be noted: 
 
• A payroll calendar must be generated for each company within an organisation.  
• The calendar consists of the year broken up into week numbers, e.g. 202001, 202002, 202003 
etc. 
• The calendar tracks the period end date for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay groups. 
The period end date for monthly pay groups will always be the last day of the month.  
• The payroll calendar does not track the payment date.  
• Period end dates can be offset at a pay group level.  
• The calendar will always contain at least the current year and future years.

1. Overview 
1.1.  Purpose of the Guide 
This document provides guidance on how to use Insight including: 
• How to access Insight. 
• How to view reports. 
• How to create new reports. 
• How to manage reports e.g. updating report settings, sharing, scheduling etc. 
• Configuration & user access required for Insight.  
 
This is intended to provide general guidance on how to use Insight. This does not include: 
• Product specific reporting. 
• Advanced report examples. 
 
1.2.  What is Insight? 
Insight is an in-application reporting tool to help employees and managers gain perspective 
on their business operations. It encompasses the process of transforming your People XD 
data into reportable datasets and visualising that data into reports, graphs and tables that 
expose valuable insights.  
 
XD Insight is about visualising, understanding, and acting on data and provides users with 
the following features: 
• A reporting homepage to view recent reports that you have created, view reports 
that have been shared with you, have a full searchable l ist of all reports you have 
access to, Users can view, edit, and clone reports with the ability to launch the Create 
Report Wizard. 
 
• Users can create standard listing reports or cross tab reports. A report can be created 
from the various areas that are available to the user. E.g. Recruitment, Payroll, etc. 
The user can then select the fields they want as part of that report from the 
designated views within that area. If applicable, a user can edit, print, or export the 
report to excel. 
 
XD Reporting: Insight Fundamentals

• When editing a report, a user can edit a report to include or remove fields. It is 
possible to search fields and remove from the visual field list. The grid can be 
grouped or sorted by clicking on column headers. 
 
• Calculations can be added to the report using the manage calculations option. A field 
can be selected as well as a set of functions that are available from the CoreHR 
function library to create a calculated field. This can also be used as part of the charts 
that can be generated 
 
• Reports can be filtered based on columns that are part of the reporting area. 
Prompting can also be activated so a user can enter a value when a report is being 
run. E.g. Date ranges. 
 
• Reports can be shared in read only mode to a list of users available in the sharing 
navigation section. This can be updated at any time to add or remove users from the 
list, as necessary. The report name can be updated as well as the description of the 
report. A user can restrict the number of rows coming back in a report to speed up 
the report. A user can also hide duplicate rows where this may occur based on the 
report settings. 
 
• Multiple Chart types (Pie charts, Line charts and Bar charts) can be added t o the 
report. These can be saved as widgets and made available to managers on the 
Manager Dashboard. A schedule can also be created to send to a designated set of 
users on a given frequency.

4.4.4. Filters 
Filters Overview 
Filters are used to help restrict or limit the data returned in order to create a more meaningful 
report rather than a straightforward data extract for example 
• All employees in Department X. 
• All employees with a Date Joined in 2021. 
 
You can create nested filters. For example, a filter could be used to return all employees that left 
in January 2019, using a filter on their leave date: 
• On or after 1st Jan 2019 
• On or before 31st Jan 2019 
 
Prompts can be added to a filter. This means that when the report is run, a prompt is shown on 
screen asking for the value to filter by e.g. “Enter Year” or “Select the Pay Period”. This approach is 
useful as the report is dynamic and can be run to display different data sets every time, rather 
than pre-filtering of specific values.

actions which are to be approved or rejected.  The codes which have been configured and colour 
coded on the screen display on the calendar.

Employee :  
• My Calendar Widget 
• My Request Widget  
• Work week  Widget  
 
Manager :

Admin :  
• WFM Admin Dashboard

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
 
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the  Pay Code Access Groups 
functionality. 
It is intended for use by HR Administrators that manage the listings of Pay codes available to 
managers and employees when entering leave requests, absences and timesheets.  
 
This guide includes: 
• Pay Code Access Groups explained. 
• How to access and create Pay Code Groups. 
• How to assign Pay Codes Groups to Managers and Employees.   
• How to configure Managers and Employees to have access to the correct codes. 
 
1.2. What’s new for version 28!  
• In portal, Managers absence and timesheet entries can be linked to pay code groups 
assigned at employee level. The Manager input is reflective of pay code groups assigned 
to the employee and/or the employee appointment combination. 
• Managers can be granted access to additional pay codes within the group that are 
marked as manager only. 
 
 
1.3. About Pay Code Groups  
Pay Code Groups can be used to tailor the list of pay codes returned to employee and managers 
when inputting and viewing data. 
 
1.3.1. Employees  
By default, all Pay Codes are returned to employees in the data entry Timesheet Input and Leave 
Request screens.  
• Pay code lists can be tailored to selective pay codes through the use of Pay Code Groups.  
• Pay Code Groups can be assigned to the employee and or 
the employees’ appointment.

For further information on this see Section 3 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1.3.2. Managers and Administrators   
In the screens listed below, all Pay Codes are retuned to managers and administrators by default. 
As required, pay code lists which are available can be tailored to selective pay codes using Pay 
Code Groups. For managers and administrators, the pay code grouping is assigned at Manager 
username/organisation role level , work groups level or the employees record.  This last option is 
new for v28.  For further information see above. 
 
Manager and Administrator input applies to the following screens: 
 
• Timesheet Input  
• Absence Details 
• Time Exceptions  
• Record Absence Details (back-office) 
• Maintain hours (back-office)

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Data Migration Update Facility 
widget. This includes: 
• An overview of the Data Migration Update Facility widget. 
• What records can be updated using the Data Migration Update Facility widget. 
• How to update data using the Data Migration Update Facility widget. 
• The dependency on Insight reports for employee and contract updates. 
• Cancelling an update that is in progress. 
• Fixing errors identified during the update. 
• An appendix with detailed guidance for each of the 26 update options.  
 
 
 
 
1.2. What is the Data Migration Update Facility? 
The Data Migration Update Facility can be used to make bulk updates to: 
• 10 specific personal details on employee records (full list here in 1.3 Employee Updates).  
• 12 specific contract elements (full list here in 1.4 Contract Updates) 
• 4 reference data items (full list here in 1.5 Reference Data Updates) 
 
 
 Note:  
This document does not cover the Data Migration Templates and Data Migration Options widgets, 
as these are not part of the process for completing bulk updates. Refer to the Data Migration Tool 
user guide for further guidance. 
 
 

 Data Migration Update Facility v28 - User Guide             
CoreHR Limited Distribution 
Page 6 of 42 
The facility allows you to lookup existing records on the system and update these in bulk. For example:  
• Update the home phone number for a group of employees  at once using the Person - Home 
Phone option. 
• Update the descriptions for cost centre reference data items, using the Reference - Cost Centre 
Description option. 
 
This can be an efficient way to update records in bulk on CoreHR, rather than updating each individual 
employee / contract / reference data item via the standard CoreHR screens. 
 
This differs from data migration because this involves updating existing records on CoreHR, rather than 
uploading new records to CoreHR.

All elements of the employees ' personal record that can be updated in bulk are listed on the Data 
Migration Update Facility widget, with the prefix of "Person -". 
 
 
 Note:  
• Updates made to any records using this functionality are not audited.  
• Changes to contract records are made for the current active sequence. A new contract 
sequence is not created.

2.1. Updating Person / Contract Records 
To update existing employee / contract records, the system needs to know w hat records are to be

Follow the steps below to retrieve a list of employees / contracts in the update facility:

a. Reports must include the employee number.

c. All other columns included in the report do not display in the update facility but are

to it here.  
 
 Note:  
If the report should only display specific employee or contract records, then any filters required 
should be applied in Insight when creating the report either by: 
• Adding filters to pre-filter the report, before it is run in the data migration tool.  
• Adding prompts to the report to be filter when it is run in the data migration tool. 
 
For example, it recommended to always consider adding a filter on your report to show only active 
records e.g. employees that are active today, contracts that are commenced and not end-dated.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Data Migration Update Facility 
widget. This includes: 
• An overview of the Data Migration Update Facility widget. 
• What records can be updated using the Data Migration Update Facility widget. 
• How to update data using the Data Migration Update Facility widget. 
• The dependency on Insight reports for employee and contract updates. 
• Cancelling an update that is in progress. 
• Fixing errors identified during the update. 
• An appendix with detailed guidance for each of the 26 update options.  
 
 
 
 
1.2. What is the Data Migration Update Facility? 
The Data Migration Update Facility can be used to make bulk updates to: 
• 10 specific personal details on employee records (full list here in 1.3 Employee Updates).  
• 12 specific contract elements (full list here in 1.4 Contract Updates) 
• 4 reference data items (full list here in 1.5 Reference Data Updates) 
 
 
 Note:  
This document does not cover the Data Migration Templates and Data Migration Options widgets, 
as these are not part of the process for completing bulk updates. Refer to the Data Migration Tool 
user guide for further guidance. 
 
 

 Data Migration Update Facility v28 - User Guide             
CoreHR Limited Distribution 
Page 6 of 42 
The facility allows you to lookup existing records on the system and update these in bulk. For example:  
• Update the home phone number for a group of employees  at once using the Person - Home 
Phone option. 
• Update the descriptions for cost centre reference data items, using the Reference - Cost Centre 
Description option. 
 
This can be an efficient way to update records in bulk on CoreHR, rather than updating each individual 
employee / contract / reference data item via the standard CoreHR screens. 
 
This differs from data migration because this involves updating existing records on CoreHR, rather than 
uploading new records to CoreHR.  
 
 
 
 
1.3. Employee Updates 
All elements of the employees ' personal record that can be updated in bulk are listed on the Data 
Migration Update Facility widget, with the prefix of "Person -". 
 
 
 Note:  
• Updates made to any records using this functionality are not audited.  
• Changes to contract records are made for the current active sequence. A new contract 
sequence is not created.

2. How to Complete an Update  
2.1. Updating Person / Contract Records 
To update existing employee / contract records, the system needs to know w hat records are to be 
updated. This is facilitated using an Insight report. The report runs within the update facility and return 
the required employee / contract records on screen.  
 
 
 
Follow the steps below to retrieve a list of employees / contracts in the update facility: 
1. Create a report in Insight that identifies the set of records to be updated. 
a. Reports must include the employee number.  
b. Contract ID is not required for the contract updates (but is useful to add to ensure the 
correct set of data is retrieved in Insight).  
c. All other columns included in the report do not display in the update facility but are 
useful to add to the report to ensure the correct set of data is being retrieved, e.g. name, 
department etc. 
 
 
 
  
 Note:  
It is only possible to update records that you currently have access to on the system. When the 
Insight report is generated, records appear based on your ‘System Users’ access e.g. if you don’t 
have access to the employee / contract in People Management / Payroll etc, you won’t have access 
to it here.  
 
 Note:  
If the report should only display specific employee or contract records, then any filters required 
should be applied in Insight when creating the report either by: 
• Adding filters to pre-filter the report, before it is run in the data migration tool.  
• Adding prompts to the report to be filter when it is run in the data migration tool. 
 
For example, it recommended to always consider adding a filter on your report to show only active 
records e.g. employees that are active today, contracts that are commenced and not end-dated.

2.4. Fixing Update Errors 
If there is an error when processing the record, the status updates to "Failed". To resolved this: 
1. Click on the failed record. This is highlighted in blue.  
2. Click Display Errors. 
 
 
3. The Row Errors screen opens. 
a. Description = Why the record failed to load.  
b. Current Value = The item that failed to load for the record. 
 
 
 
 
4. To fix the error, enter a new value in the Updated Value column. 
If the value should be blank, switch on the Null Value indicator. 
 
Clicking Ignore Errors allows you to exit the scre en and clear the error / "Failed" status. The 
status returns to "Changed", and the record can be reprocessed. 
  
5. Click Apply Changes. 
 
6. The record now has a status of "Changed" and is ready to process again.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure the data migration functionality 
on CoreHR. This includes configuration to support: 
• The upload process via the Data Migration Options and Data Migration Templates widgets. 
• The Data Migration Update Facility.

2. Configuring the Data Migration Tool 
2.1. Dashboard Configuration 
 
 
This section provides an overview of the following: 
• How the Data Migration tab is made available on the Administrator Dashboard. 
• How the widgets are pre-configured for that tab. 
 
To add a tab: 
1. Quick jump to Dashboard Configuration 
 
 
 
2. Select Dashboard = Administrator Dashboard. 
3. Click Add Page Tab.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Note:  
It is recommended that all widgets required to support the data migration functionality are configured 
on a Data Migration tab on the Administrator Dashboard. This configuration is defaulted on install 
of CoreHR.

4. On the Edit Tab pop up, enter the following details: 
• Title = “Data Migration” 
• Name = “Data Migration” 
• Phrase Code = "Data Migration" 
• Icon = Database  
• Height = n/a 
• Position = the preferred order number, e.g. 3 indicates this will be the 3rd tab 
• Display on CoreMobile = Off 
 
 
 
5. Click Ok to create the tab.

The followings widgets should be added to the Data Migration tab. 
• Data Migration Options 
• Data Migration Templates 
• Data Migration Update Facility 
 
To add these widgets to the tab: 
1. Select the Data Migration tab on the list of tabs. 
2. Search for the widget name. 
3. Enable the Selected checkbox. 
4. Changes are saved automatically.  
 
 
 
 
 Note:  
There are other widgets prefixed with “Data Migration” that will appear in the widget search. These 
are used as part of a legacy data migration solution and are not relevant to this functionality. Only 
the 3 widgets listed above should be enabled.

3. User Access  
3.1. Default Data Migration Menu Profile 
A pre-configured menu profile is available. This includes all of the necessary V1 (previous data migration 
tool) and V2 (enhanced V28 data migration tool) menu options required for a user to: 
• Complete data migration uploads  
• Process Updates 
 
Menu Profile

3.2. Access to the Data Migration Widgets 
Each of the 3 data migration widgets are controlled using a single menu option:  
Menu Option Description 
CoreHR - Data Migration CoreHR - Data Migration 
 
Once the user has this option, they will have full access for each of the following widgets:  
• Data Migration Templates. 
• Data Migration Options.  
• Data Migration Update Facility.  
 
 
 
3.3. Access to Upload Data Migration Files and Complete Updates 
There is a complete set of Data Migration menu options that are used to control the following: 
• Data migration template download. 
• Data migration template upload. 
• Data migration template processing. 
• Update data retrieval. 
• Update data processing.

This is pre-configured on the default menu profile: COREPORTAL_DATAMIGRATION_USER

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of Document 
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Leave Requests and Absences 
functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. This includes: 
• What are Leave Requests and Absences and when are they used? 
• Assigning Balances to employees 
• Employee self-service overview 
• Manager self-service overview 
• Guidance on the configuration options within Leave Requests and Absences 
 
 
1.2. What are Leave Requests and Absences? 
It is possible to configure CorePortal to allow employees manage their own Leave Requests. This allows 
employees to submit Leave Requests to their managers for approval. It is also possible for employees 
to view and edit already submitted requests if required. 
 
From their Employee D ashboard, employees can review the status of their request s, and make 
amendments as required, via the My Requests widget. The My Requests widget is shown in the below 
screenshot.

Managers receive Notifications indicating they have requests that require action. They can then approve 
and/or reject  the employee Leave Req uests via the My Approvals screen. It is also possible for 
managers to drill into the employee’s balance information and view the Team Calendar to aid in approval 
decision making. The below screenshot details both Notifications, and the My Approvals Notifications 
widget. 
 
 
The below screenshot shows the My Approvals screen.

 Leave Types 
Leave Types are represented by configuring Absence Pay Codes within the system. By configuring a 
Pay Code as Absence, this allows for it to be available in the Leave Type drop-down lists, when an 
employee is entering a Leave Request, or a manager is entering absence for an employee. 
 
 
Some example Leave Types that can be configured within the system are listed below: 
• Annual Leave 
• Bereavement Leave 
• Certified Sick Leave 
• Force Majeure 
• Graduation Day 
• Jury Service 
• Parental Leave 
• Paternity Leave 
• Study Leave 
• Uncertified Sick Leave 
• Wedding Leave 
 
For further information on configuring a Pay Code as Absence, view section 6.3. Leave Request Pay 
Code Setup. 

WFM Time V27: Employee Balance Management User Guide            
CoreHR Internal 
Page 9 of 89 
 Balances 
Balances, such as Annual Leave, can be assigned to employee records within the system. Employees 
can then use these balances to submit Leave Requests  until fully used, subject to being Active 
Balances. It is possible for employees to review their balance information via the Balances widget. 
 
 
It is possible for managers and/or admin users to review and manage balances for employees within 
their Org Role remit. Managers can review employee balances, manage existing balances, and assign 
new balances. 
 
 
Types of balances include: 
• Auto Derived Entitlement 
• Maintain Only Balance 
• Other Balances 
 
For further information on Balances, view section 2. Employee Balances.

 Leave Request Workflow 
The below example outline s a high -level Leave Request workflow. An employee submits a Leave 
Request, which is then approved by their manager. 
 
The employee navigates to the My Requests widget and follows the process to submit a Leave Request. 
 
 
Once complete, the  employee receives a Notification, indicating that  the Leave Request  has been 
successfully submitted. 
 
 
The manager then receives a Notification indicating that they have a Leave Request requiring action. It 
is then possible for the manager to review and approve or reject the Leave Request. 
 
 

WFM Time V27: Employee Balance Management User Guide

Once the manager has  approved or rejected the Leave Request , the e mployee then receives a 
Notification indicating that their Leave Request has been either approved or rejected. 
 
 
For further information on Leave Request processes, view the applicable sections below: 
• 3. Employee Self Service 
• 4. Manager Self Service 
 
 Leave Requests versus Absences 
The following points should be taken into consideration regarding Leave Requests and Absences: 
• A Leave Request is submitted by an employee, for manager approval.  Before it may proceed 
as an official absence, a Leave Request must be actioned by a manager , to either approve or

2.2. Managing Balance Assignments 
 Balances Overview 
When assigning a new balance, only fields applicable to the balance selected are displayed . The table 
below provides explanations for each field: 
Field Explanation 
Reserved entitlement 
Refers to the portion of your entitlement that must be taken on certain days. 
You cannot choose when to take it.  For example, a factory shutting down 
for two weeks in July. 
Floating entitlement 
Portion of your entitlement tha t you are free to take anytime  (subject to 
approval and outage periods) i.e. you get an entitlement at the start of the 
year and you can take the leave any time (you don’t have to wait until you  
have worked it up). 
Accrued entitlement 
Used for certain employees (casual employees, or employees worki ng 
variable hours) . T hey accrue their entitlements to leave ov er time  (as 
opposed to getting their full entitlement at the start of the leave period). 
Allowance This is Reserved + Floating + Accrued 
Carried Forward 
This holds the days/hours that were automatically carried forward from the 
previous period into this period. Managers/Admins can manually adjust this 
also. The Carried Over + Entitlement values = Balances. 
Taken 
These hours are calculated to the employee’s  T&A record b ased on 
Booked Absences or Approved Requests. (This can be overridden). 
Booked This is leave requested that has been approved but not taken. 
Requested 
This is leave requested that hasn’t been approved regardless of whether it 
is in the future or not. 
Remaining This is the remaining balance. This does not include requested leave.

up as a Personal Calendar Balance.

Background
New functionality providing the ability to delete an employee’s appointment when processed in error either by way of replacing contract (transfer) or as a new additional contract. In addition, the ability to delete the latest appointment sequence if processed in error.
The delete contract functionality can be used for the following process scenarios:
Replacement Contract has been processed – Delete replacement and reinstate previous post
To be eligible for deletion a new replacement contract/appointment can either be appointed or commenced, but only where the new post has not been paid. Where a post has already been paid, a message is displayed stating that contract can’t be deleted.
Where the new replacement contract/appointment has already been ended, it can’t be deleted. 
For replacement contracts, all previous post data will be reactivated. Appointment status is reversed and salary and cost allocation set as active.
The new replacement contract will be deleted, including salary, allowances, pensions, UDF’s.
Alternative Outcome
If the contract is the employee’s first and only substantive appointment the button to delete the contract will instead go through the screens for switching the appointment for a different one. This process allows the employee to keep their current appointment ID however, the post number and post sequence changes to the post that have been switched to. The posts available for selection need to be authorised in advance of selection. 

Additional Contract has been processed – Delete additional contract
To be elegible for deletion the new additional contract can be either appointed or commenced, but only where the new post has not been paid. If the additional post has been paid, a message is displayed stating that contract can’t be deleted. 
If the new additional contract/appointment has already been ended, it can’t be deleted. 
For additional contracts, when the delete contract function is triggered the contract will be deleted, including salary, allowances, pensions, UDF’s. 

Contract Amendment has been processed – Delete latest appointment sequence
The latest appointment sequence is deleted and previous sequence reactivated. No impact on salary etc.

How to Delete a Contract
System process steps for deleting contracts.
Go to the Command Centre tab on the People Management dashboard.
Click the View button on the Employee section.
Search for the employee in question that is due to be deleted.
On the HR Employee Dashboard, go to the Contracts section
Click on the ellipsis button on the Summary section.
The Delete Contract button is available to use.

After clicking on Delete Contract a confirmation message is displayed, noting the Appointment ID and confirming any additional linked items that will also be deleted, for example Salary. Click OK to proceed.

Alternatively, if the contract is the employee’s first and only substantive appointment the button to delete the contract will instead go through the screens for switching the appointment for a different one. This process allows the employee to keep their current appointment ID however, the post number and post sequence changes to the post that have been switched to. The posts available for selection need to be authorised in advance of selection. 

How to Delete a Contract Amendment
System process steps for deleting contracts.
Go to the Command Centre tab on the People Management dashboard.
Click the View button on the Employee section.
Search for the employee in question.
On the HR Employee Dashboard, go to the Contracts section of the employee record.
Select the Amendment that is required to be deleted, i.e. appointment sequence and click on the View button. 
Within the View Contract screen, click on the Delete button.

After clicking on Delete Contract a confirmation message is displayed. 

Click Yes to continue. 

Additional Information
To assist with investigative purposes the following information has been provided to advise the relation with applicants and the audit report used by HR Systems when the delete functionality is used.
Applicant impact
Scenario: An applicant who is already an existing employee has been appointed via the replace contract process, and then the new replacement appointment is deleted. In this situation, the applicant remains listed against the vacancy but the post appointment is removed from the offer details screen. 
The new post is still shown linked to the original vacancy, but would not be available to reselect in order to record an offer for another candidate or process as a direct appoint. A new planned appointment would be required in that circumstance. 
HR Audit Report
Where a contract has been deleted details of the post appointment are still present on the audit report, but show ‘delete’ within the audit type and field name columns.

There are two options available when enabling Employee Onboarding: 
• Enable - Suitable if you are setting up onboarding for the first time on PeopleXD OR you 
do not intend to import checklists created for pre-v27 Onboarding Checklists on PeopleXD. 
• Import Before Enabling - Suitable if you are already using an earlier version (pre-v27) of 
Onboarding Checklists in PeopleXD. Jump straight to 3.2 Import Before Enabling if you 
wish to use this option, as it must be completed before Employee Onboarding is enabled. 
 
 
 
3.1. Enable 
To enable Employee Onboarding: 
1. Navigate to the Social Hub Configuration widget. 
 
2. Click View on the Activate option. 
3. Click the Enable tile under the Onboarding section. 
4. Enter the Start Date.  
5. Click Enable. 
 
On completion, employee onboarding is now enabled for users. 
 
 Note:  
• If Employee Onboarding is not enabled, then the existing Onboarding Checklists module 
(pre-v27) will be available to users within the Classic UI. 
• If Employee Onboarding is enabled, then this means the pre-v27 onboarding dashboard 
available to new starters will not be there anymore and instead Employee Onboarding 
will be made available for employees to complete their tasks i.e. the Social Hub. 
• Employee Onboarding is not available in the Classic UI.

Background
The Access Group has released new functionality providing the ability to delete an employee/person record, which can be used where the employee record was added in error. 
There are limitations, which prevent a person record from being deleted, these are:
An employee record cannot be deleted if their salary has been paid. In this instance, an error will be displayed stating, “This person record cannot be deleted as they have already been processed by payroll.

An employee record cannot be deleted if WFM transactions exist on their record, such as Timesheet hours. In this instance, an error will be displayed stating, “This person record cannot be deleted as WFM Transactions have already been entered against it”.

Where the employee has hours recorded against a Timesheet, which has not been paid, these can be removed. Please see further guidance under section How to Remove WFM Timesheet Transactions Preventing Person Deletion.

The TIMDEP01 report will show timesheet claims and status.

How to Delete a Person
System process steps for deleting a person record.
Go to the Command Centre tab on the People Management dashboard.
Click the View button on the Employee section.
Search for the employee in question that is due to be deleted.
Click on the ACTIONS button, which is located in the top right hand corner of the screen.
Select the Delete Person option from the actions list. 

After clicking on Delete Person, a confirmation message is displayed. Click Yes to proceed.

After clicking Yes to proceed the following confirmation action message is displayed:

Once returned back to the employee record the person status has updated from Active to Deleting. The person is not deleted immediately, a status of ‘Deleting’ will display and an overnight job will then delete the employee. There will still be an option to select Undo Delete under the Actions menu should you need to reverse these step, see next section for details. 

Once the overnight job has completed to delete the person record the post record is still available, however the post appointment will have been deleted as part of this process. If creating a new post appointment, the same sequence number will be allocated. 
The same employee number will not be re issued when setting up a new employee. 

How to Undo Scheduled Delete Person
If the system delete has not yet happened, the user will be able to undo the pending delete. System process steps to undo a scheduled person delete.
Go to the Command Centre tab on the People Management dashboard.
Click the View button on the Employee section.
Search for the employee in question that is due to be deleted.
Click on the ACTIONS button, which is located in the top right hand corner of the screen.
Select the Undo Delete Person option from the actions list. 

After clicking on Undo Delete Person a confirmation message is displayed. Click Yes to proceed.

After clicking on Yes to proceed with the Undo Delete Person the following confirmation action message is displayed:

Once returned back to the employee record the person status has updated from Deleting to Active once again. The scheduled overnight deletion job has been cancelled. 

Reporting Against Scheduled Delete Person
It is still possible to report against the person scheduled to be deleted whilst they have the ‘Deleting’ person status and before the overnight process to delete the person record completes. 
Whilst the employee has the ‘deleting’ person status the PERSUP17 HR Audit report will detail the pending delete action from the HR_PERSON table with the field name DELETE_IND. 

After the overnight job has run and the person has been fully deleted it is no longer possible to report against their person record using the PERSUP17 HR Audit report. 
This will have no impact on payroll reporting as any employee already paid cannot be deleted by this process, as noted in the background section of this document. 

How to Remove WFM Timesheet Transactions Preventing Person Deletion
Where Timesheet transactions exist in WFM and you are unable to delete person owing to error “This person record cannot be deleted as WFM Transactions have already been recorded against it”, you can remove the transactions by following these steps.
Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.
Select WFM Person Maintenance.
Query the employee.
Click the ellipsis and select Timesheet.

Navigate to the relevant week.
Click the ellipsis and select Delete.

SAVE.
You can then go ahead and delete the person record.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Employee Onboarding functionality 
in People Management and how this is used. This includes: 
• What is Employee Onboarding and when it used by employees? 
• The difference between ‘new starter onboarding’ and ‘existing employee cross-boarding’. 
• An overview of the Social Hub dashboard. 
• Detailed guidance on the main elements of the Social Hub dashboard and how they may 
be used. 
• Tracking employee onboarding progress as a manager or hr administrator. 
 
Employee Onboarding is highly configurable to ensure that every organisation can manage the 
onboarding and cross-boarding experience based on their own requirements. This document does 
not cover configuration guidance. For full training on how to set up and configure each element of 
Employee Onboarding, see the Employee Onboarding v28: How to Configure - User Guide. 
 
1.2. What is Employee Onboarding? 
Employee Onboarding  is a platform that supports onboarding guidance for new joiners and re-
joiners, while also supporting continuous onboarding guidance for existing employees.  For 
example: 
• New starter onboarding for employees joining or re-joining the organisation.

3.2.1. Checklists Overview (Tasks Outstanding List) 
The checklist allows the user to complete all Checklist Items that require completion for the typical

The employee is required to complete the Checklist Items in sequence, for example, if an employee

continues in this sequence. This ensures that employees review and complete important steps

organisational policy documents before updating their bank account details.

7. Importing Pre-V27 Onboarding Checklists (Upgrades 
Only) 
Organisations who are adopting the Modern UI and have used a pre -v27 version of Onboarding 
Checklists, have the facility to import their previous Checklist Items  before enabling Employee 
Onboarding. 
• This import is not mandatory, it is recommended you opt to create the Checklist Items, and 
custom content from scratch to give an optimal experience to employees. 
• If you have imported previous Checklist Items, you can edit these items after the import 
process, as well as adding additional content. 
• If you plan to import, it is recommended to do this before creating new checklist items, as 
doing so afterwards could lead to duplication. 
 
 
 
For full training on how to import existing checklists, see the Employee Onboarding v28: How to 
Configure User Guide. 
 
 
 Note: It is important to note that, i f an organisation has multiple checklist profiles in the 
old onboarding solution, then these default checklist items are imported as global items. 
• If these items are left as ‘global’, the items display for all employees even though they 
may have completed onboarding already  via another non-default checklist profile, or 
as part of their own profile. 
• It is recommended  to create new checklist items for Employee Onboarding  and not 
import old checklist items. 
• If you decide to import, to prevent this scenario from occurring after import, you must 
review all default checklist items that have been created as global. It is then possible to 
action the following, as necessary: 
o Restrict the items 
o Make the items inactive 
o Delete the items. However, if employees have completed a default profile pre-
upgrade this might be an issue.

1. Overview 
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how User Defined Fields (UDFs) are 
configured. 
 
This includes UDFs that are stored against: 
• Employees 
• Posts 
• Contracts 
 
This document will provide instruction on how to: 
• Create & edit UDFs. 
• Make UDF items available on People Management. 
• Make UDF items available to managers to view or update. 
• Make UDF items available to employees to view or update. 
 
 
1.2. What are User Defined Fields? 
1.2.1. UDFs Explained 
User Defined Fields (UDFs) are used to hold data  where the system doesn’t provide this as 
standard. These would typically be items that are specific to an individual organisation and  will 
differ from company to company. 
 
For example, a company may wish to store a record of standard company equipment that has 
been given to an employee. This can be cap tured in a UDF that is configured to display the exact 
equipment list specific to that company. 
 
UDFs can be created against: 
• An employee 
• A post 
• A contract 
XD People Management: User Defined Field (UDF) Configuration – User Guide

UDFs may be configured using the following elements: 
• Up to 12 standard fields: 
o Text 
o Number 
o List 
o Date 
o Text Area 
• Start Date & End Date 
 
There is no limit to the amount of UDFs that can be configured. 
 
1.2.2. Access to UDFs 
UDFs are configured via the People Management dashboard. UDFs are available as standard to all 
HR administrators via People Management. However, for each UDF created, it is possible to define 
if managers and employees should also see it. 
 
It is also possible to identify UDFs that contain particularly sensitive d ata, to apply an additional 
level of security for HR administrators to access it.  
 
1.2.3. Reporting on UDF Data 
All UDF data is full reportable XD Insight.

Overview
Reference data is held in a number of different locations within the system. 
Some Recruitment reference data is held within Personnel.

For detailed information on how the Core Reference fields have been utilised please refer to the following documents:
Reference Data Master (RDM)
For details on how to maintain the org structure reference data including Department, Management Units, Cost Centres etc please refer to: 
HOW TO View and Maintain Org Structure

The steps below explain how to add, amend or delete the different types of reference data contained in the system. 

NB: All changes described are subject to the agreed Change Control process. Refer to the knowledge article before making any changes.

Most Reference data tables are of a similar format. Each data item comprises a Code and Description and in some cases Analysis Codes may be used for reporting purposes. Variations are explained in detail in later sections of this document.

Navigation
Most People Management reference data items can now be found in the Portal: 
Core|Portal>People Management>Data Centre>Reference Data
Available items are listed in alphabetical order. If you cannot find the item you need here check the back office:
Core Personnel > Reference > then choose from ……..

Reference A - C
Reference D - J
Reference K - P
Reference Q - Z

If you still can’t find the entry you want try Reference Q –Z > Other References. 
Some Recruitment reference data is also found here, otherwise go to 

Personnel > Recruitment > Recruitment Reference
Even though Recruitment has been migrated to the portal most of the reference data is still configured in the back office. However if you can't find what you're looking for try - 
Core|Portal>People Management>Data Centre>Reference Data
Viewing reference data in the Portal
Most screens will look like the below with a filter to ‘search’ for a specific item, a slider to scroll up and down, and an ellipses (…) which may give you edit options if applicable.

Some include toggle buttons

Adding or amending reference data in the portal
Add new entry
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 

Click on Add at the bottom of the screen to insert a new row

Enter the Code and Description and SAVE

NB: The code and description values should have been agreed as part of the change control process.

Use the breadcrumb trail to exit the screen.
Amend a Description
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 

Search for the data item to be amended and click into the Description field. A blue border will appear.

Amend as required and SAVE.
Use the breadcrumb trail to exit the screen.

Deleting a data item

NB: Reference data items can only be removed if they are not being used in the database. In the portal some items can be marked as inactive. They remain on the data tables but are not available for users to select.
To check if an item is in use anywhere in the database tables run or create a Discoverer report. If the item is not in use then you can proceed to remove the entry. 
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 
Click on the item to select it (highlighted in blue).
If the system detects that the item is still in use then an error message will appear. 

Removing a data item from use
If the item is in use and the database records are not going to be updated then rename the entry to reflect the fact that it should no longer be used.
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 
Click on the item to select it, then click on the Ellipses (…) and choose delete. 
This has not been tested.
If the item cannot be deleted prefix the Description with ‘Z – DO NOT USE’ and if available untick the Active box.

NB: you may need to abbreviate the original Description as there will be a character limit on the field.
Un-ticking the active flag will remove the item from some drop-down lists – but not necessarily all.
Review the actual List of Values (LoV) in the Portal to ensure your changes are as expected.
Viewing reference data in the back office
Some screens will display reference data upon opening, others open in query mode enabling you to search for the item you wish to view.
For example - to View Country Codes go to Reference A – C > Country Codes. The screen automatically opens with the Country Codes displayed.

Use the scroll bar or Page Up and Page Down arrows to move through the list. 
To search for an individual item click on the button to switch to query mode. 

NB: If the screen opens in Query Mode you can click on F8 or the Execute Query button to return all data. 
To search for a specific item enter search criteria in the relevant field using % to represent wild card if necessary e.g. %united%. Click on the Execute Query button .

Amending reference data in the back office

Amend a Description
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 
Search for and select the data item to be amended.

Click into the Description field and amend as appropriate. 

Save and Red door to exit. 
Add new entry
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 
Ensuring you are in Data Entry Mode i.e. you can see this icon at the top of the screen click into the next empty row or click on the Add icon to insert a new row.

Enter the Code and Description and if available tick the Active box. 

NB: The code and description values should have been agreed as part of the change control process.

Click on Save then Red door to exit.
Deleting a data item

NB: Reference data items can only be removed if they are not being used in the database.
To check if an item is in use anywhere in the database tables run or create a Discoverer report. If the item is not in use then you can proceed to remove the entry. 
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 
Click on the item to select it (highlighted in blue).
Click on delete the current record to delete the row.
If the system detects that the item is still in use then an error message will appear. 

Rerun the Discoverer reports taking care to include minimal filters.
Removing a data item from use
If the item is in use and the database records are not going to be updated then rename the entry to reflect the fact that it should no longer be used.
Navigate to the relevant Reference area. 
Click on the item to select it (highlighted in blue).
Prefix the Description with ‘Z – DO NOT USE’ and if available untick the Active box.

NB: you may need to abbreviate the original Description as there will be a character limit on the field.
Un-ticking the active flag will remove the item from some drop down lists – but not necessarily all.
Review the actual List of Values (LoV) in the back office to ensure your changes are displayed as expected.
Variations

Activity Codes – Back Office
Activity codes are used to categorise cost centres. 
Personnel > Reference > Reference A-C > Activity Codes
Instead of an active flag there is a Disable flag. 

NB: Check the Core manual for more information before using this option.
Address Types – Back Office
Address types are used in Recruitment and Personnel.

Personnel > Reference > Reference A-C > Address Type Codes

To view an existing address type, select the item from the LoV then click on Search.

To add a new item click on New Address Type

Enter the Address Type Code and Description.
If required tick Available on Interview Panel. 

NB: It is also possible to control which contact types are available to view and update via ESS but these are not currently in use.
Save and Red door to exit
Advertiser Details
Advertiser details are used to record the costs associated with using external advertising bodies on staff requests and/or vacancies.

Overview

The Workgroup Override allows the user to override certain workgroup settings at an employee level. 

Currently the only override setting being utilised is the Holiday Scheme. The Holiday Scheme calculates when an employee is allowed to book leave and this is derived from the workgroup as default. In certain circumstances where multiple employees share the same workgroup, but have differing holiday terms, then the Holiday Scheme against the workgroup can be overridden at employee level and these are the steps covered in this guide. 

NB: To complete this process the following menu options must be enabled: 

‘WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Work Group Override’

 ‘WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Add/Update Work Group Override’.

Locate the individual employee. Where employees hold multiple appointments, ensure you select the relevant Appointment ID.

Under Work Group Setting, you will see Holiday Scheme. The default Holiday Scheme, which pulls in from the workgroup is displayed under Work Group Value. If an override has already been set, this will be displayed under Person Override Value.

Extend System Calendar
The Core|Time System Calendar must be extended each year to cover the next calendar year. Before extending the System Calendar check and make note of the following items (per T&A Company):

Year - Enter the year that you are configuring e.g. 2023

Start Date - Enter the start date in the format DD-MMM-YYY

NB: The start date must correspond to the 'Start Day' configured for the Company. For example, if the start day of the Company is Monday then the start date of the calendar must be a Monday. 
The start date of the new calendar year must be exactly one week after the start date of the last period of the previous year. It is important to ensure that all weeks are covered i.e. that there isn't a gap between the end of one year and the start of the next.

No. of Weeks - Specify the number of weeks in this year e.g. 52 or 53. 

SAVE

NB: The current system is configured to and including 2027.

Complete Balance Period End
At the end of the entitlement/balance year, Balance Calendars must be closed to:
•Calculate new entitlements
•Apply Length of Service adjustments.

System Calendar is up to date.
Balance Calendar exists in CoreHR
Carried Forward limits applied to Balance Calendar
Balance Calendar has been extended to at least one future Balance Period.
Entitlements, Length of Service values up to date
Balance Calendar Period end date has passed. e.g. To close the 2022-23 leave year the current date must be after 1 Nov 2023

2.3Extend Balance Calendar
Balances (e.g. Annual Leave, Study Leave) have accompanying calendars that exist independently of the System Calendar. These must be extended each year to cover the next calendar year. For example, if Annual Leave is managed in yearly blocks the Annual Leave balance calendar defines the start date and end date of each leave year (period) and specifies any carry forward rules. It is not possible to close a balance period (complete a period end) until the next period has been configured on the balance calendar.

Login to CoreTime back office

User logs on to CoreHR back office. 
1069975179070Navigate to CoreTime menu.

Extend Balance Calendar
Navigate to System Params > Balances > Calendars.
Use List of Values to select the Balance calendar to extend.
Click + to add a new row and add required details:
Period - Enter the balance period number. For yearly periods, specify '2019' for the year 2019, '2020' for the year 2020, etc. For shorter periods, specify '201901' for the first period in 2019, '201902' for the second period in 2019, etc. For example, 2019 for Annual Leave, 201901 for Time in Lieu
Start Date - Specify the start date of the period (e.g. 01 Jan 2019 or 1 April 2019)
End Date - Specify the end date of the period (e.g. 31-Dec 2019 or 31st March 2020)
End of Period Limits Days – Max - If applicable, specify maximum number of days that can be carried forward into the next balance period. Make sure the 'Carried Forward' option is selected in the 'Controls' drop down. e.g. Carry forward max 5 days

Repeat for all Balances.

Balance Calendar(s) extended. 

Complete Balance Period End
At the end of the entitlement/balance year, Balance Calendars must be closed to:
Calculate new entitlements
Apply Length of Service adjustments.
Process carried forward values

The following steps outline how to complete a Balance Period end.
Prerequisites

User must have an active CoreHR Back Office account.
System Calendar is up to date.
Balance Calendar exists in CoreHR
Carried Forward limits applied to Balance Calendar
Balance Calendar has been extended to at least one future Balance Period.
Entitlements, Length of Service values up to date
Balance Calendar Period is complete e.g. To close 2018 (1st Jan-31st Dec 2018), date must now be 2019
UOX: reports have been run by HR staff of the outstanding leave balance for individuals before the rollover begins, so that leave carry over can be calculated and input.

Data Required 

Balance to be closed

Steps to Complete – Complete Balance Period End 
Login to CoreTime back office

User logs on to CoreHR back office. 
1069975179070Navigate to CoreTime menu.

Balance Period End
Navigate to Period End > Balance Period End.
Use List of Values to select the Balance Calendar to complete.
Confirm ‘Current Period’ is as expected. 
Click ‘View Thresholds’ to ensure Carried Forward limits are as expected. Click ‘x’ to close when confirmed.

To close Current Period, click ‘Run Period End’.
Click ‘Yes’
To override Carried Forward limits per individual employee, tick ‘Ignore’. (UOX: The University of Oxford configuration is currently for all balances to have 0 days leave carried over and any agreed carry over to be input by HR teams in the new year. There should be no need to ‘ignore’ any of the carried forward limits at this stage, this would be to allow a different (higher or lower) carry over limit for an individual than the limit set on the balance).
Exit to complete Balance Period End.

UOX: Navigate to CoreTime/CoreRoster > Time Mgt > Balances > Balance Recalculation

UOX: The From Period will auto-populate with the rolled over period and the relevant dates will display
UOX: Select the “All” radio button at the bottom of the form
UOX: Click “OK”
UOX: The system will re-calculate all balances for the balance code selected. Do this for all balances which have been rolled over.

Balance Period end has been completed.
New Balance Entitlements assigned to employees.
Carried Forward values updated for employee Balances.

Background
All time (hours & minutes) needs to be recorded against a valid Pay Code. Pay Codes originate in CorePay, but require specific configuration within Core Time to function properly with Timesheets and/or Leave/Absence.
For full guidance on configuring pay codes for WFM refer to the Pay Codes guide
Time & Pay Codes
WFM Admin Dashboard > Settings > Reference Data > Pay Codes
Pay codes only need to be activated in Time Management if they are required for leave & absence or timesheets. 

There are 14 screens of parameters for each pay code. Rather than attempting to detail all of these options, pay codes can be grouped based on their behaviour. 

Pay Code Types
Pay codes can be broken into two categories:-
Leave & Absence – codes which record time away from work 
Timesheets – codes which record hours worked and result in payment to workers

How to access the Company and Calendar Configuration Screen 
Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard. 
Click on WFM Configuration. 
Search for and select Company and Calendar Config. 

The Company configuration screen shows any existing companies which have been configured on the system.

From here you can: 
Search for a specific company, using the search bar or filter. 
Access the configuration screens via the relevant 3-dot menu. 
Set Auto Advance Periods.
Add a new company. 
How to Add a New Company
To add a new company, complete the following steps:
Click Add New Company.
Fill in the Mandatory fields and enable the Active toggle, then click OK.
The 3 Step System Calendar Wizard will open, where you can configure your company.
In Step 1, Calendar Year, select the System Calendar Year, Start Date of the Company, and the number of weeks in the year. This may vary in a leap year.
Click Next.
A message regarding auto generating periods will appear:
Click Yes if you wish the weeks to autogenerate for you.
Click No if you wish to do so manually.
In Step 2, Calendar Period, you can configure the auto rostered weeks for your company. Use the dropdown menu to select the current period, this is the year and week, for example 202320.
On complete, click Next.
In Step 3, Company Parameters use the dropdown menus to populate the Mandatory fields. For example, Late Pay Code, Unapproved Absence Pay Code.
Once you have completed, click Save.
Your company will now be listed on the Company and Calendar Config screen.

How to Auto Advance Periods
To setup an auto advance for system calendars, complete the following steps:
Click Auto Advance Periods.
On the Auto Advance Periods screen, click Add.
Select the Day of Week and Time for the System Calendars to move forward one period.
Click OK.
A routine will run that checks if any of your system calendars are in the past. If they are then they will automatically advance one period. This will ensure that your calendars do not fall too far behind the actual date.

The Auto Advance Periods screen contains the following fields:

FIELD
DETAILS
Schedule Auto Advance
This displays the Auto Advance schedule setup and when the next run date will take place.

Use the Delete button to remove a schedule. 

Auto Historical Balance Recalc
By default, the toggle is off, enabling this toggle will recalculate all historical balances at period end. This can add a substantial time overhead to the process and is only advised if there is a specific reason to enable this.

Company Calendars
This lists all Company Calendars(s)

User Defined Calendar Periods
This displays the User Defined Calendars.

Active the Auto Advance toggle for the User Defined Calendar to advance when the Company Calendar, it is attached to, advances.

Configuration
Once the company has been set up, you can access it via the Company and Calendar Config screen. Click the 3-dot menu to View/Edit your selected company.

If for any reason you haven’t completed the company setup, on the 3-dot menu it will state Complete Company Setup. You will need to follow and complete the steps How to add a new company, before it can be used.

Summary Tab
The Summary Screen holds all the main information of the company which you have just created.

The Summary screen contains the following fields:
FIELD
DETAILS
Name
Name of the company being set up

Start Day
Choose a day of the week for the work pattern to start on, i.e. Monday

Start Date
Start date of the period.

End Date
End date of the period.

Label
You can add a label for the company to be more easily searchable.

User Calendars Assigned
When enabled employees are assigned to a calendar.

Active
When the active indicator is enabled, the company will appear.

Approved Status
This indicator is display only and will automatically insert ‘AP’ into the database as the Approved Status code when hours have been approved through the Maintain Exceptions forms.

Confirmed Status
This indicator is display only and will automatically insert ‘CF’ into the database as the Confirmed Status code when hours have been signed off through the Sign Off Hours form.

Use Hire & leave Dates for Calculation
This indicator, when selected, will use Hire & Leave Dates when calculating hours to prevent any unnecessary unapproved absence from being generated for employees.

User Personal Alternates
This indicator, when selected, will allow employees to change from one work pattern to another for a specific day in the View Work Schedule in the Time Record form, without having to modify the employees shift type.

Leaver Code
This specifies what Employee Status Code, or Personnel Type should be used to indicate an individual who has left the company e.g., LEAVER.

When Processed
Choose between Weekly or Monthly.

Team Schedule Timesheet Template
Input which timesheet template you wish to use, i.e. Manager Timesheet Summary. 

Calculate to
Choose between Today, Yesterday and End of Input Period.

MGR Rollback Weeks for Data Entry
Controls the number of weeks back from current period that a manager is permitted to enter data, i.e. 15. 

EMP Rollback Weeks for Data Entry
Controls the number of weeks back from current period that an employee is permitted to enter data, i.e. 15. 

Admin Timesheet Template
By default, administrators inherit the same timesheet templates as managers. Where required an administrator template can be assigned at the WFM Company level or Username Level which override the default setting when viewing the ‘Timesheet Input’.
Entry of the Admin Timesheet Template at the username level overrides the WFM Company Level supporting admin staff to have bespoke templates if required.
If the user also has Managers access assigned, on connection to the Managers Dashboards the manager screens continue to use the managers’ template.

Company Calendar Years Tab
The Company Calendar Years Screen shows the current and previous years of the company and details the start date of the year as well as the number of periods.

The Company Calendar Years screen contains the following fields:
FIELD
DETAILS
Year
Company calendar year.

Start Date
Start date of the calendar.

Periods
The number of weeks within the calendar year. This may vary depending on whether leap year.

You also have access to the Generate Period & Add buttons. These can be used to:
Generate Period: The Generate Period button allows you to set up a period by selecting the specific year and setting the fortnightly and monthly starting period.
Add: This allows you to add a new calendar year to your company.

Background
Pay Codes drive PeopleXD Time functionality as all time (hours & minutes) needs to be recorded against a Pay Code. Pay Codes originate in CorePay, but require specific configuration within Time to function properly with Timesheets or Leave/Absence.
Time & Pay Codes
CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Pay Codes
Pay codes only need to be activated in Time Management if they are relevant to the leave & absence or timesheet processes. 

There are 14 screens of parameters for each pay code. Rather than attempting to detail all of these options, pay codes can be grouped based on their behaviour. 

Pay Code Types
Pay codes can be broken into two categories:-
Leave & Absence – codes which record time away from work 
Timesheets – codes which record hours worked and result in payment to workers

Overview
The Shift Type configuration screen is available via Portal on the WFM Admin Dashboard. 

The following menu profile should be assigned in order to gain access to the steps below.
WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES
A shift type determines the hours an employee is contracted to work. Departmental HR Administrators assign the appropriate shift types to appointments via People Management > Work Schedule, but can only assign shift types that have been created by HR Systems.
Shift Types and Daily Work Patterns
Shift Types are formed by assigning a work pattern to each day of the week. A work pattern is the number of hours worked in a day, the start and end times are irrelevant, so an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 08:00AM would require the same work pattern as an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 11:00AM. 
Work patterns are broken into 3 minute intervals (the lowest number that can be accurately decimalised). The largest work pattern available is a 13 hour day.
On days when employees are not required to work the ‘REST’ work pattern is used. 
Rotating/flexible shift patterns
Most employees follow the same pattern each week. If an employee varies between different patterns each week see part B. 
If an employee has a flexi-time arrangement, where there is no predefined pattern, they should be assigned one of the standard shifts based on their average daily hours. For example, if someone works 25 hours across 5 days, they should be assigned a shift type with a 5 hour work pattern on each day, Monday-Friday. 
Departmental HR should request a new shift type via OSM service request and provide a copy of the Shift Code Generator for the shift type required. 
Generating a shift type code
Each shift type has a unique code and a name (description). The codes for weekly shift patterns are generated using the Shift Type Code Generator, with each code represents a unique combination of daily work patterns. This prevents multiple shift types being created with the same pattern. Codes for Rotating shift types are linked to the employee appointments. 
Creating a new weekly shift Pattern

System Admin - Creating new Shift Types/Work Schedules
These steps are followed by HR Systems when creating new shift types 
Introduction
A shift type determines the hours an employee is contracted to work. Departmental HR Administrators assign the appropriate shift types to appointments via People Management > Work Schedule, but can only assign shift types that have been created by HR Systems.
Shift Types and Daily Work Patterns
Shift Types are formed by assigning a work pattern to each day of the week. A work pattern is the number of hours worked in a day, the start and end times are irrelevant, so an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 08:00AM would require the same work pattern as an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 11:00AM. 
Work patterns are broken into 3 minute intervals (the lowest number that can be accurately decimalised) The largest work pattern available is a 13 hour day.
On days when employees are not required to work the ‘REST’ work pattern is used. 
Rotating/flexible shift patterns
Most employees follow the same pattern each week. If an employee varies between different patterns each week, including see part B
If an employee has a flexi-time arrangement, where there is no predefined pattern, they should be assigned one of the standard shifts based on their average daily hours. For example, if someone works 25 hours across 5 days, they should be assigned a shift type with a 5 hour work pattern on each day, Monday-Friday. 
Generating a shift type code
Each shift type has a unique code and a short name (description). The codes for weekly shift patterns are generated using the Shift Type Code Generator, with each code represents a unique combination of daily work patterns. This prevents multiple shift types being created with the same pattern. Codes for Rotating shift types are linked to the employee appointments.

What are Work Patterns
Work Patterns define a daily work schedule. They identify the different work durations that exist within the organisation and capture the expected working hours for an employee. Selected work patterns are then used to configure an employee’s shift type. Work patterns are an integral part of the system linking to multiple areas. 
Accessing the Work Patterns screen
The Work Pattern screen is where administrators can manage work patterns for their organisation. The screen lists all Work Patterns created and shows if they are active or not. This screen can be used to create new work patterns, copy existing work patterns and further configure patterns to organisational requirements.
To access the Work Patterns screen, navigate via
WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > select Work Patterns.
The following Work Patterns screen displays. 

There is a search and filter option available on the Work Patterns screen, allowing you to search for a specific work pattern or filter by Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Active or Label. 
The screen contains the following fields:
Option 
Details 
Pattern Code 
The Code given to the Work Pattern. 
Description 
The Work Pattern description. 
Default Pay Code 
The pay code assigned to the work pattern. 
Extra Hours Worked 
The pay code assigned to extra hours worked on the work pattern. 
Default Hours 
Number of hours of the work pattern. 
Default Start Time 
The start time of the work pattern. 
Default End Time 
The end time of the work pattern. 
Label 
The label added to the work pattern to make it easily searchable. 
Calculation Method 
The calculation method of the work pattern. For example, Standard, Roster or Rest Pattern. 
Active Indicator 
When the active indicator is enabled the work pattern is available to be added to a Shift Type. 
How to Add a new Work Pattern
To add a new work pattern, complete the following steps:

1. Click Add at the top of the screen. 
2. Fill in the mandatory fields Pattern Code, Description, Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Default Hours, Default Start Time, Default End Time, Earliest Start Time.
3. Click OK. 
4. Your new Work Pattern will open for you to further configure, using the tabs on the left-hand side. For example, add Standard Hours and Breaks. 
5. Once your Work Pattern is fully configured, click Save. 
6. Your Work Pattern is now ready to be added to a Shift Type. 

How to Copy a Work Pattern
To copy a work pattern, complete the following steps:

1. Select Copy from the 3-dot menu of the work pattern you wish to copy. 
2. Fill in the Pattern Code. 
3. Fill in the Description. 
4. Click OK. 
5. Your copied Work Pattern will open for you to further configure. 

Configuration of a Work Pattern
The configuration screens allow you to customise and configure work patterns and can be accessed through the Work Patterns screen by selecting the 3-dot ellipses and selecting View/Edit Work Pattern.

General Parameters
At the current time only the General Parameters screen is utilised, however as further functionality such as Rostering is introduced the other areas are likely to require configuration. 
The General Parameters screen contains the main information pertaining to the Work Pattern and allows to configure for example, default hours as well as start and end time. As with all of the other screens, the Start Time, End Time and Default Hours are displayed at the top of the screen. 

The General Params screen contains the following fields:
Field 
Details 
Description 
This allows you to choose the specific work pattern. 
Default Start Time 
This is the start time which the system defaults to. 
Default End Time 
This is the end time which the system defaults to. 
Default Hours 
These are the hours which will be filled in automatically. 
Earliest Start Time 
You can choose the earliest time that the work pattern can start. 
Overtime Override 
If you wish to override the default hours in the case of over time you can do so here. 
Short Name 
You can give the pattern a short two letter abbreviation. 
Fill Basic Hours 
When this toggle is enabled, basic hours can be filled. 
Fill Basic Before Threshold 
When the toggle is enabled, basic hours can be filled up to the specific threshold. 
Rest Pattern 
When the toggle is enabled, the hours are put on a rest pattern. 
Split Default Hours 
When enabled this will split the default hours. 
Roster Calculation 
When the toggle is enabled the menu and options are only the ones for a roster (previously known as retail) calculation. 
Standard Calculation 
When enabled the hours are calculated as standard hours. 
Default Pay Code 
You can set a pay code for the system to default to. This is a mandatory field. 
Extra Hours Worked 
You can choose the pay code for any extra hours worked. 
Label 
It is advisable to label the pattern with a short name to increase searchability.
