Background
The SSRS reports developed by the Functional Analysis and HR Analytics teams are stored in the various HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE), where end-users may execute them as necessary. Two levels of security apply to every report: PeopleXD’s database security and HR Reporting’s “folder-based” security. 

This how-to guide only addresses how to manage security within the HR Reporting environments. A brief note on PeopleXD’s database security is included for context. 

PeopleXD’s database security
When a report query is executed, PeopleXD’s native security model is applied to the data within each .RDL file. This means that a given end-user will only be able to retrieve results which they have permission to view, based on the roles assigned to them within PeopleXD’s Security module. Security can apply to areas of the business, such as departments and divisions, or specific types of data, such as salary information. 

Example: A user with permission to view all data in their current department runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for their own department. 

Example: A user with permission to view data for Pay Group 20 (but not Pay Group 21) runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for Pay Group 20, and not Pay Group 21. 

NB: Questions about Core’s database security must be handled by the HRIS Functional and Configuration Analyst (Michael O’Sullivan), who can confirm the security in place for individual users and amend it if required.
HR Reporting’s folder-based security
A second level of security has been imposed in the HR Reporting environments themselves, to ensure that users only see reports which are relevant to their line of work – for instance, a departmental user has no need to view Payroll or Pensions reports, but a Payroll user may need to view departmental reports.

This second level of security is “folder-based”. All the .RDL files in the HR Reporting environments are stored within a folder hierarchy, and each level of the folder hierarchy is shared with certain groups of users, depending on their reporting requirements. These user groups are managed via the Active Directory, and are therefore known as “AD Groups”. An AD group’s access to any level of the folder hierarchy is dependent upon the folders within that level being shared with the AD group. 

Some contextual information about AD groups and the reporting folder hierarchy is given below. 
The reporting folder hierarchy

The folder hierarchy is generically illustrated here:

Level 0 – Home: A user must have access to the Home folder of the reports server in order to access any of the folders or files located on the server. Access to the Home folder is assigned on the folder’s security profile. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to the Home folder, then that user will be able to access the reports server. Their access to the folders and files within the reports server depends on whether an AD group of which they are a member has been assigned to a given folder/file. 

Access to the Home folder is like having the key to the front door of a building. All the rooms in the building are locked and require their own keys, but a user must be able to get into the building itself before they can access individual rooms within it. 

Level 1 – Navigation Folders: Once a user has accessed the Home folder, they can navigate to the reports they need via the Navigation folders. The Navigation folders contain broad groupings of reports according to their main audience and/or purpose, e.g. “Payroll” or “Recruitment”. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Navigation folder, then that user will be able to see the Navigation folder listed within the Home folder, and will be able to enter the Navigation folder to view its contents. 

Level 2 – Subfolders: Once a user has entered a Navigation folder, the report they need may be present in a Report folder, or in a Subfolder. Subfolders are used to split very broad groups of reports into more granular categories; for instance Level 1 Personnel folder has three Level 2 subfolders: Current Reports, Monthly Reports, and Tracking Reports. 

Not every Navigation folder has Subfolders; however, where Subfolders exist, the same rules of access apply. To wit, if a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Subfolder, then that user will be able to see the Subfolder listed within the Navigation folder, and will be able to enter the Subfolder to view its contents.

Level 3 – Report Folders: Once a user has accessed a Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), they must select the report they wish to run by going to the appropriate Report folder. The Report folder contains the .RDL files which make up a report; a report may be comprised of one or many .RDL files. So long as a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Report folder, then that user will be able to see the Report folder listed within the Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), and will be able to enter the Report folder and access the .RDL files within it. 

Note: Security is not applied at the level of individual .RDL files. If a user has access to a Report folder, they have access to all the .RDL files within that folder. 

Active Directory (“AD”) groups
An AD group is simply a collection of CONNECT accounts belonging to individual users. Each group is given a semi-descriptive name indicating its membership. Some examples of AD groups include:

Group
Members
HRIS-RR-PAYMREP
Managers of the Payroll team
HRIS-RR-EDU_TEAM
The Equality & Diversity team
HRIS-RR-SUP_REP 
The HR Systems Support team

Individuals are added to AD groups via the Active Roles web interface, and AD groups are then assigned to folders within the HR Reporting environments. When an AD group is assigned to a folder, all the individual members of that AD group will be able to access the folder and all of its contents. 

Most AD groups are only assigned to a handful of folders – for example, the EDU_TEAM group only has access to folders which contain equality & diversity-related reports. Some AD groups, however, are assigned by default to every folder within the folder hierarchy. These groups are known as the “reporting super-groups”, and they are as follows:

Super-Group
Members
HRIS-RS-PowerBI Report Writers - Production
People with read/write access to the entire LIVE environment
HRIS-RS-PowerBI Reporting Support - Production
People with read-only access to the entire LIVE environment
HRIS-RS-PowerBI Report Writers - Non Production
People with read/write access to the QA, TEST and DEV environments
HRIS-RS-PowerBI Reporting Support - Non Production
People with read-only access to the QA, TEST and DEV environments
HRIS-RS-PowerBI Reporting Administrators - Non Production
IT staff who can manage the HR Reporting environments

The super-groups have full access to the HR Reporting environments (either LIVE or non-LIVE, as shown above). Membership of these groups is managed by the Microsoft Platform Services Team.

Processes

Managing AD groups
Since access to levels of the reporting folder hierarchy is managed through AD groups, you may need to review the membership of an AD group, add new members, remove existing members, or even request the creation of a new AD group entirely. 
To do any of these things, you will need to access the Active Roles web interface. 

Note: Only the HRIS Functional Analysis team should have read-write access to the Active Roles web interface; this is to ensure the careful management of access to the HR Reporting environments. 
AD group membership
To view the members of an AD group, navigate to the Active Roles web interface. On the landing screen, select Search.

Background
The SSRS reports developed by the Functional Analysis and HR Analytics teams are stored in the various HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE), where end-users may execute them as necessary. Two levels of security apply to every report: PeopleXD’s database security and HR Reporting’s “folder-based” security. 

This how-to guide only addresses how to manage security within the HR Reporting environments. A brief note on PeopleXD’s database security is included for context. 

PeopleXD’s database security
When a report query is executed, PeopleXD’s native security model is applied to the data within each .RDL file. This means that a given end-user will only be able to retrieve results which they have permission to view, based on the roles assigned to them within PeopleXD’s Security module. Security can apply to areas of the business, such as departments and divisions, or specific types of data, such as salary information. 

Example: A user with permission to view all data in their current department runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for their own department. 

Example: A user with permission to view data for Pay Group 20 (but not Pay Group 21) runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for Pay Group 20, and not Pay Group 21. 

NB: Questions about Core’s database security must be handled by the HRIS Functional and Configuration Analyst (Michael O’Sullivan), who can confirm the security in place for individual users and amend it if required.
HR Reporting’s folder-based security
A second level of security has been imposed in the HR Reporting environments themselves, to ensure that users only see reports which are relevant to their line of work – for instance, a departmental user has no need to view Payroll or Pensions reports, but a Payroll user may need to view departmental reports.

This second level of security is “folder-based”. All the .RDL files in the HR Reporting environments are stored within a folder hierarchy, and each level of the folder hierarchy is shared with certain groups of users, depending on their reporting requirements. These user groups are managed via the Active Directory, and are therefore known as “AD Groups”. An AD group’s access to any level of the folder hierarchy is dependent upon the folders within that level being shared with the AD group. 

Some contextual information about AD groups and the reporting folder hierarchy is given below. 
The reporting folder hierarchy

The folder hierarchy is generically illustrated here:

Level 0 – Home: A user must have access to the Home folder of the reports server in order to access any of the folders or files located on the server. Access to the Home folder is assigned on the folder’s security profile. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to the Home folder, then that user will be able to access the reports server. Their access to the folders and files within the reports server depends on whether an AD group of which they are a member has been assigned to a given folder/file. 

Access to the Home folder is like having the key to the front door of a building. All the rooms in the building are locked and require their own keys, but a user must be able to get into the building itself before they can access individual rooms within it. 

Level 1 – Navigation Folders: Once a user has accessed the Home folder, they can navigate to the reports they need via the Navigation folders. The Navigation folders contain broad groupings of reports according to their main audience and/or purpose, e.g. “Payroll” or “Recruitment”. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Navigation folder, then that user will be able to see the Navigation folder listed within the Home folder, and will be able to enter the Navigation folder to view its contents. 

Level 2 – Subfolders: Once a user has entered a Navigation folder, the report they need may be present in a Report folder, or in a Subfolder. Subfolders are used to split very broad groups of reports into more granular categories; for instance Level 1 Personnel folder has three Level 2 subfolders: Current Reports, Monthly Reports, and Tracking Reports. 

Not every Navigation folder has Subfolders; however, where Subfolders exist, the same rules of access apply. To wit, if a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Subfolder, then that user will be able to see the Subfolder listed within the Navigation folder, and will be able to enter the Subfolder to view its contents.

Level 3 – Report Folders: Once a user has accessed a Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), they must select the report they wish to run by going to the appropriate Report folder. The Report folder contains the .RDL files which make up a report; a report may be comprised of one or many .RDL files. So long as a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Report folder, then that user will be able to see the Report folder listed within the Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), and will be able to enter the Report folder and access the .RDL files within it. 

Note: Security is not applied at the level of individual .RDL files. If a user has access to a Report folder, they have access to all the .RDL files within that folder.

Membership of these groups is managed by the Microsoft Platform Services Team – they are not visible in the Active Roles web interface, so if you need to make any changes to super-group membership, you will have to raise a task to MPST on OSM, specifying which group you want to change and which members should be added to / removed from the group. 

Note: Because the super-groups have total access to all reports, membership must be managed extremely carefully to prevent possible data breaches. 

All changes related to super-group membership must be approved in writing by Simon Burford, Athena Artuso, or Mandy Zaccheo, prior to being raised as Minor Changes in OSM, where they will be subject to formal approval by the Head of HR Systems. 
Managing folder security
Access to the different levels of the reporting folder hierarchy is controlled by assigning AD groups to each level. 
Some AD groups have broad access, e.g. the PAYMREP (Payroll Managers) group can view the Payroll, Pensions, and Personnel Navigation-level folders, and all of their contents. 
Most AD groups have very limited access, e.g. the PERDREP (Personnel administrators) group can only view the Personnel Navigation-level folder and its contents. 
You can review and amend the AD groups assigned to any level of the reporting folder hierarchy by following the steps below.

Note: Access to a folder’s contents must be tightly controlled to prevent possible data breaches. Any change to folder security must be managed as a Minor Change on OSM and formally approved by the Head of HR Systems. 
Viewing folder security
Navigate to: Folder > Manage Folder > Security

From the HR Reporting environment’s Home page, navigate to the folder whose security you wish to review. In the menu bar at the top of the page, click “Manage folder”:

You will be taken to another screen. In the left-hand menu pane, select “Security” to view the security in place for the current folder:

A list of the AD groups which have access to the folder will be displayed:

The “Roles” column indicates the level of access each AD group has to the contents of the folder. 
Role
Level
Description
Browser
Read-only
May view folders and reports and subscribe to reports.
Content Manager
Read/write (full server)
May manage content in the Report Server. This includes folders, reports and resources.
My Reports
Read/write (restricted area of server)
May publish reports and linked reports; manage folders, reports and resources in a user’s My Reports folder.
Publisher
Read/write (full server)
May publish reports and linked reports to the Report Server.
Report Builder
Read-only 
May view report definitions.

Note: AD groups should only ever be assigned the Browser role (read-only). Users who need read/write access must be added to special “super-groups” by the HR Functional Analysis team. See the linked Knowledge Article for details. 
Editing folder security
Navigate to: Folder > Manage Folder > Security
Adding a new AD group
To add a new AD group to a folder within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, navigate to the folder’s security screen and click the “+Add group or user” button at the top of the screen:

The New Role Assignment screen will open. Enter the name of the AD group you wish to add to the folder, and select the “Browser” role: 

Click OK to save your changes and be taken back to the main security screen. The AD group you have just added will appear in the list of groups which have access to the folder:

Note: You must ensure that your new AD group is added to every level of the folder hierarchy, or members of the AD group will not be able to access the folder! 

Home
> The appropriate Navigation folder
> > The appropriate Subfolder (if applicable)
> > > The appropriate Report folder.
Removing an AD group
To remove an AD group from a folder within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, navigate to the folder’s security screen and select the group you wish to remove. Click the “Delete” button at the top of the screen:

A warning message will pop up; click OK to confirm your changes. 

The screen will refresh and the AD group you have deleted will no longer appear in the list of groups with access to the folder. 

Note: Depending on how far you need to restrict access, you may need to remove the AD group in multiple levels of the hierarchy. 
For instance, if an AD group had access to Home > Navigation > Subfolder > Report, and should no longer have access to Navigation > Subfolder > Report, you will need to remove it from the Navigation folder and the Subfolder, as well as the Report folder. 
Folder security for subscription-based reports
A tiny number of reports within the HR Reporting environments are run on a “subscription” model, in which a report user “subscribes” to a report and the report is run automatically on the user’s behalf by the REPORT_POWERBI Service Account. 
The Service Account has unlimited user sessions and unrestricted access to PeopleXD’s database, so it must be kept highly secure to prevent unwanted data breaches. This means that it will only be used to run reports in exceptional circumstances – namely, when a report consistently times out or fails to complete when run by an ordinary user. 
An explanation of the special security measures for subscription-based reports is given below.
The Subscriptions folder
Navigate to: Home > Subscriptions
All subscription-based reports must be filed in a special Navigation folder called (unsurprisingly) “Subscriptions”. Access to this folder is tightly controlled to prevent unauthorised users from viewing any subscription-based reports. Only the HR Reporting “super-groups” and subscription-specific AD groups should be assigned to the Subscriptions folder. 
If you have created a new subscription-based report, you must create a Report folder for it within the Subscriptions folder; for example Home > Subscriptions > PAYPAY25 National Minimum Wage Check: 

Each Report folder within Subscriptions must only be shared with a single AD group, comprised of the user or users who have subscribed to that particular report. 
Subscription-specific AD groups
Whenever you set up a subscription-based report, you will need to create a new AD group for the subscribers. As noted above, requests for the creation of new AD groups must be raised on OSM as Minor Changes and a task must be assigned to MPST with details of the new group. These details must include:
Group name – this must be in the format “HRIS-RR-SERVICE_[Report prefix]
Example: HRIS-RR-SERVICE_PERX14
Description – this must always be “Report run by the Service Account”.

MPST will create the group profile, and the HRIS Functional Analysis team can then add individual staff members. 

Note: To prevent the possibility of data breaches, you must ensure that only those staff members who have subscribed to the report are added to the new AD group. 
Once the new subscription-specific AD group has been created and you have added the necessary members to it, you can add the AD group to the following folders:
Home
Subscriptions
Report folder within Subscriptions

Overview
The HR Reporting solution is a Microsoft-based user interface which allows users to run reports from the PeopleXD database within their web browsers. There are four environments (servers) for the HR Reporting solution, all of which are owned by the Microsoft Platform Services Team (MPST). MPST are responsible for any technical faults that arise in the environments, and for making any changes required to maintain the overall HR Reporting solution’s VPN connection to the PeopleXD database.

The day-to-day management of these environments is largely handled by the HRIS Analysis team, who own the report files, data sources, and datasets which are stored in each environment. This document focuses on the work carried out by the HRIS Analysis team.

NB: Software Solutions and Microsoft Platform Services manage a separate aspect of reporting via SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS); their processes are not detailed in this document. It’s important to note, however, that the password for the PeopleXD database service account is controlled solely by the HR Functional Analysis team, so if the SSIS connection to PeopleXD needs to be updated, the HR Functional Analysts are responsible for updating the service account password within SSIS. 

HR Reporting Environments
The four HR Reporting environments are listed below. 
HR Reporting LIVE

Database
Accessible to… 
UOXP
End-users (Departments and Central teams)
Super-users (report writers)
Microsoft Platform Services

The LIVE environment holds the current version of every active report and shared dataset. It is the primary environment of the HR Reporting solution. Changes to the LIVE environment will impact all report users, and must be handled very carefully. 

HR Reporting QA

Database
Accessible to… 
UOXP
Super-users (report writers)
Microsoft Platform Services
End-users (ad hoc for testing purposes)

The QA environment is a copy of the LIVE environment and likewise holds the current version of every active report and shared dataset. It is also, as the name suggests, the Quality Assurance environment, where new or amended reports can be run against the UOXP database for final checks before being published to the LIVE environment. 

The QA environment is restricted to super-users and MPST, but permission is granted to end-users on an ad hoc basis to enable them to test and sign off on any new/amended reports before those reports are made live. End-user access permissions must always be removed as soon as QA testing is complete. 

HR Reporting TEST

Database
Accessible to… 
UOXU, UOXC, or UOXZ (can be switched) 
Super-users (report writers)
Microsoft Platform Services
Project testing teams (ad hoc)

The TEST environment is used for running reports against the non-production databases (UOXU/UOXC/UOXZ), which is an essential component of testing PeopleXD system upgrades. TEST is not visible to end-users, however access can be granted to project testing teams as required. 

The TEST environment’s data source connection strings can be updated to point at UOXU, UOXC or UOXZ, depending on which database a given project team wants to test. 

HR Reporting DEV 

Database
Accessible to… 
UOXC, UOXU, or UOXZ (can be switched)
Super-users (report writers)
Microsoft Platform Services

The DEV environment is a development sandbox for report writers, where multiple iterations of a report may be stored and compared to one another throughout the report writing process. New and amended reports must be promoted through the four report environments from DEV > TEST > QA > LIVE as part of the change management process. 

Data Sources
Every HR Reporting environment relies on its data sources in order to connect to the appropriate PeopleXD database for report queries. The LIVE and QA environments look at the UOXP database, while the DEV and TEST environments can be configured to look at UOXU, UOXC, or UOXZ. 

NB: Only super-users and MPST are able to view/amend data sources in any of the HR Reporting environments. If you want to know the properties of a data source, or to change those properties in some way, you must contact the HR Systems Support team at hr.systems@admin.ox.ac.uk with your request. 

Viewing a data source 
Navigate to: Home > Data Sources
In any HR Reporting environment, the data sources are stored in a folder called “Data Sources”, which exists at the top level of the folder hierarchy. Navigate to this folder to view the data sources which have been set up for your environment. 
Every environment must have the two following data sources:

Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount: this data source is used by the shared datasets to provide lists of values for parameters. 

Oracle_DS_UserCredentials: this data source is used by the individual report datasets to run the report queries. It relies on people’s unique PeopleXD login credentials to retrieve information from PeopleXD’s database
Here is how the data sources appear within the “Data Sources” folder:

To view the details of a data source, click on its name. You will be taken to the Data Source Properties page. 
Every data source has the following properties:
Property
Comments
Name 
Name of the data source, e.g. Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount
Description
Used in the TEST & DEV environments to indicate whether the data source is currently looking at UOXU, UOXC or UOXZ. 
Enable this data source (flag)
Indicates whether the data source is currently enabled in the environment – this flag should normally be ticked.

Property
Comments
Connection type
This will always be “Oracle Database”, because PeopleXD is Oracle-based software. 
Connection string
This is the most important property. It tells the data source which PeopleXD database to connect to, e.g. UOXP, UOXU, UOXC, or UOXZ.

Property
Comments
Log into the data source…
This will be one of four options:
As the user viewing the report. (This option is never selected.)
Using the following credentials (username and password supplied) – this is only used for the Service Account data source.
By prompting the user viewing the report for credentials (user prompted to supply their own username/password when accessing the report) – this is only used for the User Credentials data source.
Without any credentials. (This option is never selected.)
Type of credentials
This will always be “Database username and password”.
Prompt
Whatever text should appear above the login fields for users. This value should not be changed without good reason, because whatever you enter here will appear in every report!

Here is what the prompt text looks like on a report:

Amending the User Credentials data source

NB: You must never change any of a data source’s properties unless absolutely necessary, because doing so risks disabling the data source.
Navigate to: Home > Data Sources
If you have the necessary permissions to amend data sources within the HR Reporting environments, you can do so by navigating to the “Data Sources” folder and selecting the Oracle_DS_UserCredentials data source: 

You will be taken to the Data Source Properties page. Make the changes you require, then click “Apply” to save the changes:

If you’ve altered the data source connection string to point to a different PeopleXD database, you can check that your changes will work before you apply them. Change the credentials to “Using the following credentials” and enter your own HR Reporting username and password:

 
Now click “Test connection” at the bottom of the page:

The report server will check that the credentials you have provided are able to connect to the PeopleXD database you have specified in the connection string. After a minute or two, you should get a status message: 

NB: If your connection test fails, check that you have entered the right login credentials. If your credentials are correct, it’s possible that the PeopleXD database is temporarily unreachable – the best advice here is to wait half an hour and try again.
Once you’re happy that your new connection string is working, you must change the credentials property back to “By prompting the user viewing the report for credentials”:

Click “Apply” to save your changes:

Amending the Service Account data source
The Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount data source connects to PeopleXD’s databases to retrieve the information which populates the shared datasets in each environment.

NB: The ServiceAccount data source is also used in exceptional circumstances to retrieve data for reports which time out when using the UserCredentials data source. Only a tiny number of reports use the ServiceAccount data source and the reasons for linking these reports to the ServiceAccount data source have been fully justified in each case in a formal OSM Change Request. 
The Service Account has unlimited user sessions and unrestricted access to Core’s database, so it must be kept highly secure to prevent unwanted data breaches. Only a subset of reporting super-users know the login credentials for the Service Account data source, and they must periodically update these login credentials to keep the account secure. 
The Service Account username is REPORT_POWERBI. This is static across all HR Reporting environments and must never be changed. 
The Service Account password, on the other hand, must be updated annually. It must also be updated whenever a person with knowledge of the current password leaves the HR Functional Analysis team – this is to ensure that the password remains secure. 
When the Service Account password changes, it must be updated in the following places:
The HR Reporting environments
HR Reporting LIVE
HR Reporting QA
HR Reporting TEST
HR Reporting DEV

The HR Reporting.sln files within Microsoft Visual Studio 
HR Reporting_LIVE.sln
HR Reporting_QA.sln
HR Reporting_TEST.sln
HR Reporting_DEV.sln

The components of the SSIS package managed by Software Solutions
PeopleXD.sln within Microsoft Visual Studio
PeopleXD.conmgr within Connection Manager
The environment profiles within SQL Server Management Studio
LIVE server: BI-SQLINT04.CONNECT.ox.ac.uk
UAT (QA) server: BI-SQLINT03-QA.CONNECT.ox.ac.uk
TEST server: BI-SQLINT02-T.CONNECT.ox.ac.uk
DEV server: BI-SQLINT01-D.CONNECT.ox.ac.uk 
Updating the HR Reporting environments
To update the Service Account password in the HR Reporting environments, navigate to the Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount data source in each environment and go to its Properties page. Overwrite the existing password and then click the “Test Connection” button to ensure the Service Account can connect to PeopleXD using its new credentials:

If the test is successful, click “Apply” to save your changes:

Repeat for all four HR Reporting environments. 
Updating the Visual Studio solution files
To update the Service Account password in the Microsoft Visual Studio solution (.sln) files, launch each solution in Visual Studio. Click on the Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount data source within the Solution Explorer pane under the “Shared Data Sources” heading:

The Shared Data Source Properties window will pop up. Click the “Build…” button next to the Connection String field:

The Connection Properties sub-window will pop up. Overwrite the existing password and then click the “Test Connection” button to ensure the Service Account can connect to PeopleXD using its new credentials:

NB: Ensure the “Save my password” flag is enabled for the Service Account data source!
If the test is successful, click “OK” twice to save your changes and exit back to the Shared Data Source Properties window. Click “OK” again to close that window. 

Now click the “Save All” icon in the menu bar (or hit Ctrl+Shift+S) to commit your changes to the solution file:

Repeat for all four HR Reporting solution files (.sln) in Visual Studio. 
Updating the SSIS package components
 
The SSIS package and its components are owned and managed by the Software Solutions team (DEV and TEST) and the Microsoft Platform Services Team (UAT/QA and LIVE). 
As of January 2021, we have the following contacts in both teams:
Software Solutions
Ewan Kilgour, the Head of Data Reporting, Architecture and Modelling
Louise Brotchie, the Software Solutions Business Integrations & Technologies (SSM-BITe) team leader. 
MPST
Neil Smart, MS SQL Server Database Administrator
Saffron Greenwood, Team Leader Microsoft Platform Services
In order to update the SSIS package components with a new password for the PeopleXD service account, it is necessary to arrange a video call via Microsoft Teams with a member of either Software Solutions or MPST, depending on which environment you are editing. 
Within the video call, the Software Solutions or MPST person will need to take the following actions to enable you to update the Service Account password in all the necessary locations:
They must launch Visual Studio and open the PeopleXD.sln file. Within the .sln file, they must open the Connection Manager pane – this is where the password can be updated.

They must open SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and open the environment profiles. Within each profile, they must open the Environment Variables section – this is where the password can be updated. Remember to contact the correct team depending on which environment profile you are updating:
DEV – owned by Software Solutions
TEST – owned by Software Solutions
UAT (QA) – owned by MPST
LIVE – owned by MPST

The person you are meeting will need to share their screen with you in Teams so that you can see the fields where the Service Account password must be updated. You will then have to request control of the screen. Click the button at the top of the video window to request control of your partner’s screen: 

Once they have granted control, you will be able to click on and manipulate items on the shared screen as if they were on your own screen. 

NB: Taking control of a shared screen often causes a lag between your actions and the changes onscreen. Your mouse may move slowly, and data you key in may take a moment to appear. This is normal.
Amend the password in the PeopleXD.sln file and within the SSMS environment profiles and save your changes. You can then give back control of the MS Teams screen to your meeting partner. Your meeting partner should perform a connection test to ensure that the new password is working correctly. Once they have confirmed this, you can end the meeting.

Context
Shared datasets are SQL queries which are available to re-use across multiple report (.RDL) files. In HR Reporting, shared datasets are used to retrieve reference data from PeopleXD, in order to populate drop-down lists for report parameters. 

Example: Many reports have a “Department” parameter, which allows users to specify which department(s) they want to see returned in the report results. It looks like this:

The shared dataset LOV_Optional_Department.rsd is the source of information for the “Department” parameter’s drop-down list. The shared dataset queries PeopleXD’s database and returns a list of all active departments. This list is then attached to the “Department” parameter, so that users can select the departments in which they are interested. 
Because LOV_Optional_Department.rsd is a shared dataset, it can be attached to any report which has a “Department” parameter. 

Shared datasets are managed in two places: Visual Studio, where they are created and amended, and the HR Reporting environments, where they are deployed to run alongside reports. See below for detailed guidance.

A note on naming conventions
All shared datasets are prefixed with the phrase “LOV_Optional”, because shared datasets return lists of values (LOVs) from which users can select the options in which they are interested. Shared datasets must adhere to the following naming conventions to make it easy to identify what sort of data a given dataset might return. 
If the dataset returns reference codes, the convention is: 
LOV_Optional + Reference item_Code
If the dataset returns reference descriptions, the convention is: 
LOV_Optional_Reference item
If the dataset returns reference codes and descriptions, the convention is:
LOV_Optional + Reference item +_and_Description

Some examples are given here. 
What is retrieved?
Shared dataset name
List of department codes
LOV_Optional_Department_Code
List of department names
LOV_Optional_Department
List of department codes + names
LOV_Optional_Department_and_Description
List of absence reason codes
LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason_Code
List of absence reasons
LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason
List of absence reason codes + descriptions
LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason_and_Description
Viewing a shared dataset
Visual Studio
Shared datasets are created and amended in Visual Studio, where they are saved with file extension .RSD. You can view a complete list of the shared dataset files in your current Visual Studio solution (.sln) by going to the Solution Explorer pane and expanding the Shared Datasets folder: 

The data a shared dataset retrieves from PeopleXD is defined within the SQL query of that dataset. You can view the SQL query at any time by opening the .RSD file, either by double-clicking it, or right-clicking and selecting Open from the menu:

The Shared Dataset Properties window will open. 

All shared datasets have the following properties:

Name – the name of the dataset .RSD file (this must follow the naming conventions outlined above).
Data source – the shared data source for the dataset. This should always be Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount.
Query type – this should always be “Text”.
Query – this is where the SQL query for the dataset is stored. The query code defines what information the shared dataset will retrieve from PeopleXD.

The Query pane is displayed in the lower half of the Shared Dataset Properties window: 

You can preview the data a shared dataset will retrieve by clicking “Query Designer…” at the bottom of the Query pane:

The Query Designer window will open. Click the “Run” button (!) at the top of the screen to preview the shared dataset – this triggers the SQL query to contact the PeopleXD database and retrieve information: 

The SQL query will run and the results will be displayed in the lower half of the Query Designer window:

HR Reporting environments
A shared dataset (.RSD) is like a report (.RDL): both run SQL code which queries the PeopleXD database to retrieve information. Just like reports, shared datasets need to be deployed from Visual Studio to the HR Reporting environments so that users can run the queries. 

NB: Always remember to deploy your shared datasets to the HR Reporting environments!

If a shared dataset does not exist in an HR Reporting environment, it won’t be able to populate drop-down lists for any report parameters which depend on that dataset. 

For example, if a report has a parameter for “Department Code”, the shared dataset which retrieves the list of department codes from PeopleXD must exist in the HR Reporting environment, or the parameter will not work. 

You can view a complete list of the shared datasets in any HR Reporting environment by navigating to Home → Datasets (MASTER) within the environment:

Datasets (MASTER) is a hidden folder in the HR Reporting environments. You may need to tick the “Show hidden items” option on the Home screen before you’ll see it!

Click on a shared dataset to be taken to its Properties page. Here, you can view the dataset’s name and data source, the security applied to the dataset, and (most importantly) which reports depend on the dataset. 
Reports which are linked to a shared dataset are called that dataset’s “dependent items”. Click the Dependent items link in the properties menu to see a full list of all the reports which rely on the shared dataset. In this example, you can see that the shared dataset has 337 dependent items: 

Any changes to this shared dataset will affect all 337 dependent items. Information about how to update a shared dataset within the HR Reporting environments is provided below. 
Creating a new shared dataset
Create the .RSD file
To create a new shared dataset, go to the Solution Explorer pane and right-click the Shared Datasets folder and select “Add New Dataset”: 

The Shared Dataset Properties window will open. You must now set the following properties for your new dataset:
Name – LOV_Optional_... (see the note on naming conventions)
Data source – Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount
Query type – Text
Query – this is where you must paste the SQL query for your shared dataset. 

You can preview your new dataset by clicking “Query Designer…” to open the Query Designer window:

Click the “Run” button (!) at the top of the screen to preview the dataset results. To save your new dataset, enter CTRL + S. The new dataset will be saved to your current Visual Studio solution, and you can now add it to report .RDL files to populate LOV parameters.
Attach the dataset to an .RDL
Once you’ve created the .RSD file, you will need to attach it to the relevant report .RDL file(s). 
Example: Your report .RDL file has a parameter for “Employee Status” and you want it to display a list of all Employee Status values, so that when a user runs the report, they can choose which employee statuses they want to filter the report for (e.g. only PERMANENT and FIXED TERM employees). 

You have created a new shared dataset called LOV_Optional_EmployeeStatus.rsd to query PeopleXD’s database and return a list of all active employee statuses. You now need to attach the LOV_Optional_EmployeeStatus.rsd to your report .RDL file to populate the drop-down list for the “Employee Status” parameter. 
Open the .RDL file to which you want to attach your new dataset. In the Report Data pane, right-click the Datasets folder and select “Add Dataset…”:

The Dataset Properties window will open. Enter the dataset’s name and select the option to “Use a shared dataset”, then choose your newly-created shared dataset from the list of shared datasets in the lower half of the window: 

When adding a shared dataset to an .RDL file, you don’t need to enter the full formal LOV_Optional… name of the dataset (although you can if you prefer!) Instead, you can just enter a short name for the dataset which refers to the data it is returning, e.g. “EmpStatus” for the LOV_Optional_EmployeeStatus dataset.
Click OK to close the Dataset Properties window. Your new dataset will now appear in the Datasets folder of the Report Pane. Enter CTRL+S to save your changes to the .RDL file. 
Attach the dataset to a parameter
Now that your shared dataset is attached to the .RDL file, you must attach it to the specific report parameter which relies on the dataset to populate its drop-down list of values. 
In the Report Data pane, expand the Parameters folder. All the parameters contained within the report’s SQL query should be listed here. Select the parameter to which you want to attach your new shared dataset:

Double-click to open the Report Parameter Properties window. Click into the “Available Values” tab and select the option to “Get values from a query”:

In the lower half of the screen, use the drop-down menus as indicated.
Dataset: choose your shared dataset. 
The name displayed here will be whatever you put in the Dataset Properties window from the previous step.
Value field: select ‘VALUE_FIELD’.
Label field: select ‘LABEL_FIELD’. 

Click OK to close the Report Parameter Properties window, and enter CTRL+S to save your changes to the .RDL file. 
Deploy the new dataset
Now that your new shared dataset is attached to the appropriate parameter(s) within the relevant .RDL file(s), you need to deploy the dataset to the HR Reporting environments. 

Always deploy new shared datasets to all four HR Reporting environments: DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE. This ensures that each environment has all the same shared datasets. 

Why is this important? 
The QA and LIVE environments must be kept in sync, because QA is a mirror of LIVE, so anything you deploy to LIVE must also go into QA.

The DEV and TEST environments are used for developing and testing reports, so it’s important that they have all the same shared datasets as the LIVE environment, to facilitate testing and development. 
To deploy a dataset, go to the Solution Explorer pane and expand the Shared Datasets folder. Right-click on the dataset you need to deploy and select “Deploy”: 

You can see the progress of the deployment in the Output pane at the bottom of the screen:

Editing a shared dataset
Generally speaking, you shouldn’t need to make changes to shared datasets, because they are set up to return data from reference tables within the database – this means that any changes made in the database should automatically be reflected in the shared dataset. 

Example: The LOV_Optional_Department dataset is programmed to return a list of all department names from PeopleXD. Whenever a new department is added to PeopleXD, it automatically appears in the shared dataset – you don’t need to do anything to make this happen. 

Some shared datasets, however, have hard-coded values or filtered results which may need occasional tweaking. 

Example: The LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason dataset is programmed to return a list of absence-related appointment reasons from PeopleXD. The SQL query for this dataset specifies that only appointment reasons which meet certain conditions should be returned, e.g. when the reason includes the term ‘ADOPTION’ or ‘SICKNESS’. If a new absence-related appointment reason is added to PeopleXD, you will need to hard-code it into the shared dataset! 

If you do need to edit a shared dataset, you’ll have to do three things:

Raise a Change Request on OSM to cover the changes you’re making.
Amend the .RSD file in Visual Studio with the updated SQL code. 
Update the dataset’s properties within the HR Reporting environments. 

See below for guidance.

Amend the .RSD file
Open the relevant solution file in Visual Studio, go to the Solution Explorer pane and expand the Shared Datasets folder. Select the dataset you need to edit, and double-click to open the Shared Dataset Properties window. 

Edit the SQL code for the dataset in the Query pane, then click “Query Designer…” at the bottom of the pane to preview your changes: 

The Query Designer window will open. Click the “Run” button (!) at the top of the screen to preview the shared dataset:

Once you’re happy with your edits, enter CTRL+S to save your changes to the .RSD file. 

Update the dataset properties
Once you’ve saved your changes to your amended .RSD file, you are ready to update the shared dataset in the HR Reporting environments. 

NB: Do not deploy the amended .RSD file to the HR Reporting environments! This will overwrite the existing shared dataset, and break the link between the shared dataset and all of its “dependent items” (linked reports).

Follow the guidance below for information on how to update the HR Reporting environments so that they use the amended shared dataset. 
First, while still within Visual Studio, go to the Solution Explorer pane and expanding the Shared Datasets folder. Click on your amended .RSD file in the list of shared datasets, then go to the Properties pane (beneath the Solution Explorer pane) and copy the “Full Path” field:

Now navigate to the Home → Datasets (MASTER) within the HR Reporting environment where you want to update the shared dataset:

Click on the name of your shared dataset to be taken to its Properties page. At the top of the screen, click the “Replace” button:

A pop-up window will open. In the “File name” field, enter the full path that you copied from Visual Studio:

Click “Open” to load the .RSD file into the HR Reporting environment directly from the Visual Studio solution folder. A little pop-up will appear saying “Upload complete”. You may need to click “Apply” at the bottom of the Properties screen to save your changes.

To test that your updated dataset is working correctly, click the Dependent items link in the properties menu to see a full list of all the reports which rely on the shared dataset. Open one of the reports and go to the parameter within that report which uses the shared dataset to check that the parameter displays the correct list of values, and performs appropriately within the context of the report. 

Example: If you have updated LOV_Optional_EmployeeStatus.rsd, click on any of the reports listed on the Dependent items screen:

Within the report, go to the Employee Status parameter and check the list of values in the drop-down menu. Check that the LOV displays the correct values, based on the update you just made:

Select some values from the parameter and run the report query. Check that the report returns the correct results based on the parameters you’ve set. 

Make sure you’re satisfied that the updated dataset is performing correctly before closing any OSM change record related to the update. 

Retiring a shared dataset

It is very, very unlikely that you will ever need to retire a shared dataset, so carefully consider whether this is the correct course of action before you proceed. 
If you do need to retire a shared dataset, you will need to do a few things:
Remove the dataset from the HR Reporting environments. 
Remove the dataset from every .RDL file to which it is currently attached.
Republish the amended .RDL files without the shared dataset.

Make a note of Dependent Items
Navigate to the Home → Datasets (MASTER) within the HR Reporting environment from which you want to remove the shared dataset:

Click on the name of your shared dataset to be taken to its Properties page. Click the Dependent items link in the properties menu to see a full list of all the reports which rely on the shared dataset. 

You will need to note each of these reports down in a list so that you know which .RDL files you will need to edit within Visual Studio.
Remove the dataset from an .RDL
Open the relevant Visual Studio solution (e.g. if you are removing a dataset from the DEV environment, open the HR Reporting_DEV.sln). Go to the Solution Explorer pane and locate the .RDL you wish to edit in the Reports folder. 
Open the .RDL file. In the Report Data pane, open the Datasets folder and select the dataset you want to remove. Right-click it and select “Delete” to remove it from the .RDL file:

A warning message will pop up. Click “OK”.

The dataset will be deleted from the .RDL file. 
Remove the dataset from a parameter
Now that your shared dataset has been removed from the .RDL file, you must remove it from the specific report parameter which relied on the dataset to populate its drop-down list of values. 
In the Report Data pane, expand the Parameters folder. All the parameters contained within the report’s SQL query should be listed here. Select the parameter from which you want to remove your retired dataset:

Double-click to open the Report Parameter Properties window. Click into the “Available Values” tab and select the option to “Get values from a query”:

In the lower half of the screen, check that the drop-down menus are blank (i.e. they don’t refer to any dataset).

You now have two options: to attach a new dataset to this parameter, or to delete the parameter entirely.
If you plan to attach a new dataset to this parameter, follow the steps provided above. 
If you plan to delete the parameter, follow the guidance in the how-to manage parameters document (tbc).
Close the Report Parameter Properties window when you are finished and enter CTRL+S to save your changes to the .RDL file. 

You will need to repeat this process for every “Dependent Item” linked to the shared dataset you are retiring. Every .RDL file which you amend will need to be republished with a new version number following the steps in the HOW TO - Manage Reports - Release and Deployment.docx
Remove the dataset from HR Reporting
Go back to the Home → Datasets (MASTER) within the HR Reporting environment from which you want to remove the shared dataset. Select your dataset to be taken to its Properties page, and at the top of the screen, click the “Delete” button:

A warning message will pop-up. Click “Delete”.

Your screen will refresh and you will be returned to the Datasets (MASTER) folder.

Additional guidance: How to amend reports in Visual Studio
Additional guidance: How to manage reports on the HR Reporting servers

This document details the process for rendering a report’s raw SQL code into a Visual Studio .RDL file which can be deployed to the HR Reporting environments. 

Visual Studio Basics
This section provides some background information that you will need when working in Visual Studio.

Commonly-used terms
There are a number of commonly-used terms that appear throughout this document. A brief explanation of each is given here.

Term
Notes
Example
Dataset
A dataset is the SQL code which queries the PeopleXD database and returns results. It can be embedded (unique to a single .RDL file) or shared (available to re-use across multiple .RDL files). 
“DataSet1” within any .RDL file contains the report SQL code.
Dataset (Embedded)
An embedded dataset is a SQL query which is unique to a single .RDL file. 
All report queries are “embedded” datasets.
Dataset (Shared)
Shared datasets are SQL queries which are available to re-use across multiple .RDL files. We use shared datasets to return Lists of Values (LOVs) which power parameter drop-down lists. 
LOV_Optional_DepartmentCode
Data source
A data source is a connection to a PeopleXD database (UOXC, UOXP, etc.). 
Oracle_DS_UserCredentials

Deployment
The act of publishing a report (.RDL file) or a shared dataset to one of the HR Reporting environments.

Project
A project is a “sub-container” within a solution. The project is where your data sources, datasets, and reports are saved. A solution can contain multiple projects, but for HR Reporting, we have a strict 1-to-1 relationship between solutions and projects, such that each solution only contains a single project. 
HR Reporting QA.sln contains project “HR Reporting QA”, which holds the data sources, shared datasets, and reports for the HR Reporting QA environment. 
Report
A report within Visual Studio is an individual .RDL file. 
PERDEP01 Full Data Set.RDL
Report suite
A report suite is a group of .RDL files which all belong to the same “report”. 
Every PERDEP01… .RDL which comprises PERDEP01 Staff in Post.
Service Account
The Service Account is a data source that has complete access to the PeopleXD databases, and which is allow unlimited connections to those databases. It is used to retrieve the LOVs for the shared datasets. 
Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount
Solution
A solution (.sln) is simply a container Visual Studio uses to organize one or more related projects. When you open a solution, Visual Studio automatically loads all the projects that the solution contains.
HR Reporting QA.sln

Launching the app
Before you can create or edit reports, you will need to launch the Visual Studio application and select the solution file (.sln) that you want to work in. 

Launch Visual Studio from your Start menu and enter your CONNECT login details when prompted, in order to access the CONNECT Remote Desktop:

After a short wait, the splash screen will appear, followed by a sign-in window. Click the “Not now, maybe later” link at the bottom of the sign-in window: 

You’ll then be asked for your display preferences. Select Development Settings: General and click Start Visual Studio to complete the app launch. 

After a short wait (occasionally as long as a minute or two), Visual Studio will open and you will see the Home screen:

Opening a solution file
Report files in Visual Studio are grouped into larger files called “solutions”. Each solution has its own data sources, datasets, and report files. There are four solutions for you to choose from in Visual Studio:
Solution
Data source
Notes
HR Reporting DEV
Non-production (generally UOXC)
This is a sandpit environment for creating new reports. 
HR Reporting TEST
Non-production (generally UOXU)
This is a test environment, mainly for use by project teams
HR Reporting QA
Production
This is the UAT environment, where reports are deployed for testing by end-users. It is also where old versions of reports are archived. 
HR Reporting LIVE
Production
This is the live environment, where final, approved drafts of reports are stored and published to the live server. 
Which solution you open will depend on what you need to do in Visual Studio. 

To open a solution, go to File > Open > Project / Solution:

A warning message will appear; just click OK to dismiss it:

The Open Project file browser will open. You need to navigate to I:\OUIT\CoreHR Reports. This is a secure network drive owned by Microsoft Platform Services and used for storing all HR Reporting files: 

Choose the solution you wish to work in, and double-click the corresponding folder icon. Within the folder, select the solution file and double-click to open: 

Another warning message will pop up; simply click OK to dismiss it:

The solution file will load. You can always check which solution you have open by looking at the title bar or within the Solution Explorer pane:

NB: It is not possible to have more than one solution file open at a time. If you want to do some work in HR Reporting DEV and HR Reporting QA, for example, you will need to exit one solution before you can open the other. 

Creating a New Report

Create a draft in DEV
If you are creating a new report (rather than amending an existing one), you must always begin in the HR Reporting DEV solution. 
Copy the MASTER Report Template 
Launch Visual Studio and open the HR Reporting DEV solution. Within the Solution Explorer pane, expand the Reports list and select the MASTER Report Template file. 

Raise a change request in OSM
The New Change window will pop up. Complete the header fields as follows:
Field
Comment
Coordinator
Enter your name. 
Service Line
Professional Services and University Admin
Service
HRIS
Category
SSRS
Approval Expiry Date
Set the deadline by which you require change approval. 

NB: You must not implement your change in the LIVE environment until you have received change approval. If your change is time-sensitive (e.g. you need to implement it before next Friday), you should set an Approval Expiry Date which will ensure that you receive approval in time to implement your change before the deadline. 

In the Classification section, complete the fields as follows:
Field
Comment
Status
Logged (this field is pre-populated)
Type
Minor (this field is pre-populated)
Justification
Report

In the Schedule Detail section, confirm when you intend to implement your change, and how long you expect implementation to take:

NB: Your Implementation Start/End Dates must come after the Approval Expiry Date. If you have a sense of how long it will take to complete a change, you can be precise about the time-stamps, but it’s not necessary to be exact, here. 
Fill in Change Detail section
The Change Detail section is where you must record exactly what you are changing, why you are changing it, and what the potential impact(s) of your change may be. 
In the “Summary” field, enter the phrase REPORT CHANGE: [Name of the report you are changing]:

In the “Description” field, complete the 14-part questionnaire as follows:
Question
Answer
Details - What is changing?
Provide a brief explanation of what you are changing, and if possible, include the current SQL code and the new (amended) SQL code. 

If you have made extensive changes to the SQL, it’s helpful to attach two .TXT files to your change: one containing the unchanged SQL, and one containing the amended SQL. If you do this, you should say “Refer to attachments” in your change description, rather than providing the SQL code inline. 
Justification - Why is the change necessary?
Changes to reports are usually required to fix problems, e.g. error messages or a failure to return all the expected data – in those cases, the justification is “To resolve [brief description of problem]”. If there is a linked Incident, refer to it by number, i.e. “See linked Incident #X for details.”

If the request is for an enhancement rather than a “break-fix” request, then the justification should be provided on the Enhancement Form that users are required to submit.
Related Changes - Are there dependent changes?
If there are related changes, list them here by Change ID number; otherwise, put “No dependent changes”.
Impact on dependent services? What is the impact on connected or downstream services or components?
If changing a report will have an impact on downstream services such as system integrations or HR processes (e.g. Payroll things), it’s worth detailing the impact here. Normally, however, you can just put “No impact on services”. 
Impact - Specify downtime or at risk period
No downtime or at-risk period is entailed by a change to a report, so you can put “N/A”. 
Impact - Effect of not applying the change?
Explain the problem which led to the report change, e.g. “Users will be unable to run the report successfully” or “Report will not return Fixed Term employees”. 
Risk Assessment - What are the risks to the services?
It is very unlikely that a report change will ever pose a risk to services, so you can normally just put “N/A” here. 
Testing - Who will test it and how?
The HRIS Functional Analyst / Senior HR Analyst will make the change outlined above in the HR Reporting QA solution and deploy the amended .RDL file to the HR Reporting QA server. 

The change requestor [normally whoever raised the incident] will be given a link to the amended .RDL in the QA server and asked to confirm whether they are now seeing the expected results.
Implementation Plan - Who will implement it and how?
Once testing is successfully completed, the HRIS Functional Analyst / Senior HR Analyst will deploy the amended .RDL file to the HR Reporting LIVE server and archive the old version in the _Back-up Versions folder on that server.
 Communications Plan – Who needs to know and how?
In most cases, only the person who asked for the change will need to know when the change has been implemented. However, for very large or widely-used reports, e.g. PERDEP01 or HRINFO01, it’s very important to communicate the changes more widely. Speak to the HR Systems Business Change Analyst (Tonya Iasisen-Kandola) if you’re ever unsure about how a change should be communicated – if necessary, she can ensure comms are sent out to anyone who needs to know. 
Business Owner/Approver
Jenny Lister (Head of HR Systems)
What is the potential security impact of the change?
None. 
How will the security impact be tested?
N/A
Back Out Plan - How will it be backed out in the event of the change failing?
The previous version of the report can be restored from the _Back-up Versions folder on the LIVE server.
When you have completed the Change Details section, click the “Save” button at the bottom of the New Change window to make your change live:

The screen will refresh, and the New Change window will close. Your change request will appear as shown below, with an official request number. Click “Go to” to be taken to your change request: 

Add tasks
Go to your change request and select Task from the ribbon. Click “New Task” to create a new task:

The New Task window will pop up. Complete the fields as shown below:
Field
Comment
Team
Select your team from the drop-down.
Owner
Enter your name.
Service Line
Professional Services and University Admin
Service
HRIS
Category
SSRS
In the “Summary” field, enter the task summary. You will need to raise three standard tasks for any report change. Template text (including task summaries) is provided below; modify this as required for each task. 
QA: Update the .RDL file(s)
Amend [REPORT TABS] as detailed in the change summary and save all the files in the [REPORT NAME] suite as a new major version (#.0). Deploy the new _v# versions of the .RDLs to the HR Reporting QA server.
QA: Archive old versions
Archive the old (version #.0) copies of the [REPORT NAME] .RDL files in the _Back-up Versions folder of the HR Reporting QA server, and make a note on each .RDL indicating when it was archived.
LIVE: Update the .RDL file(s)
Once change approval has been granted, deploy all the updated (version #.0) .RDL files to the HR Reporting LIVE server to replace the existing version of the [REPORT NAME] .RDLs. Move the new versions into the [REPORT NAME] folder and delete the old versions from the HR Reporting LIVE server.

Your task pane for the change should now look something like this:

Implementing a Change in QA
After you’ve raised the change in OSM, you should make any amendments required to the report .RDL files in Visual Studio (see linked guide tbc). 
Test the amended .RDL files yourself to check that they are working as expected, and deploy them to the HR Reporting QA server. This is where the end-user who requested the change will perform user acceptance testing (UAT), and confirm whether or not the amended files are ready to be published to the HR Reporting LIVE server. 

NB: If the amended .RDL files fail UAT, you must work with the end-user to modify the .RDLs until such time as the files return the results the end-user is expecting. Do not complete your tasks until the end-user has confirmed that the .RDLs have passed UAT. 
Once the amended .RDL files have passed UAT, you can complete the tasks on your change request, as shown below. 
Complete the QA tasks
As you complete each task on the change, you must mark it “Complete” and add a note indicating what action you took to complete the task. Select the task you wish to mark “Complete” and click the Complete button:

A small window will pop up where you can enter the details of the actions you took to complete the task. 

Click OK to save your changes. The task will now appear in the task pane with the status “Completed”:

NB: You can’t modify a task once you have marked it “Complete”! 
Template text for each task completion is provided below; modify this as required for each task as you complete it. 

QA: Update the .RDL file(s)
The amendments described in the change summary have been made to the relevant .RDL files in the [REPORT NAME] suite, and all the .RDL files have been saved as "_v#" and deployed to the HR Reporting QA server.
QA: Archive old versions
The old "_v#" .RDL files have been archived in the _Back-Up Versions folder on the HR Reporting QA server.

STOP: You must now submit the change for formal approval. Do not take any further action until approval has been granted.
Obtain change approval
Once your amended .RDL files have passed UAT and you have completed the QA tasks on your change request, you must obtain formal change approval. This is an essential part of change management – you should never make changes to the HR Reporting LIVE server without first getting formal approval for those changes. 
Follow the steps below to prepare your change request for approval. 

Assign a Service Approver
Go to your change request. At the top of the screen, select the button to Add Approver:
 
A pop-up box will open where you can enter the name of the Service Approver whose approval you require for your change (for reporting changes, the service owner – and therefore the service approver – is always the Head of HR Systems, Jenny Lister):

Click OK to assign the approver. At the top of the screen, you will need to click Save to commit your changes. 

Check Approval Expiry Date
In Section 1.1., you set an Approval Expiry Date for your change – this is the deadline by which you require change approval. Report changes can sometimes require a lot of development, and the original Approval Expiry Date you set for your change may no longer be valid. 

Once your amended .RDL files have passed UAT and you are ready to request change approval, double-check your Approval Expiry Date and amend it if necessary. 

If you’ve made any changes, you will need to click Save at the top of the screen to commit them. 

Check Implementation Dates
In Section 1.1., you set Implementation Dates for your change, indicating when you intended to implement your change, and how long you expected implementation to take. As noted above, report changes can sometimes require a lot of development, so you may need to edit your original Implementation Start and End Dates to reflect when you will actually be implementing your change in the HR Reporting LIVE environment. 

If you need to edit your Implementation Dates, go to the Schedule Detail section on the Change Summary and make the necessary changes:

If you’ve made any changes, you will need to click Save at the top of the screen to commit them. 

Submit change for approval
If you’re satisfied that the Approval Expiry Date and the Implementation Dates are correct, you are ready to submit your change for formal approval. To do this, simply amend the change’s Status to “Pending Approval” in the Classification section:

An email will be sent to the Service Approver asking for them to formally approve the change. 
When the Service Approver approves your change request, you will receive an email notification of the approval. Approving the change automatically updates the change’s status from “Pending Approval” to “Scheduled”, so you should receive an email notification for the approval and the change of status:

On OSM you will see the Status now appears as “Scheduled”:

Implementing a Change in LIVE
Once you have received formal change approval and your change’s status is “Scheduled”, you are ready to implement your change in the HR Reporting LIVE environment. 
Deploy the amended .RDL files to the HR Reporting LIVE server and move them into the appropriate report folder. You will need to delete the previous versions of the .RDLs from the server once the amended versions are in place (see linked guidance tbc).
Complete the LIVE task
Select the relevant task from your task pane and click “Complete”: 

A small window will pop up where you can enter the details of the actions you took to complete the task. 

Click OK to save your changes. 
Template text for the LIVE task completion is provided below; modify this as required for your task as you complete it. 
LIVE: Update the .RDL file(s)
The amendments described in the change summary have been made to [REPORT TABS] and all the .RDL files in the [REPORT NAME] suite have been saved as "_v#" and deployed to the HR Reporting LIVE server.

Update the change status
After completing the final task on your change, you need to update the change Status twice: first, to “Implemented”, and second, to “Closed”. 
In the Classification section of the change summary, amend the change’s Status from “Scheduled” to “Implemented”:

The screen will refresh. Now update the change’s Status from “Implemented” to “Closed”:
INSERT IMAGE
The change is now closed. 

NB: You can’t modify a change once you have marked it “Closed”! Be very sure that you don’t need to take any further action! 
Complete the linked incident
Go to the Incident tab on the ribbon and select the incident which you used as the basis for your change request. Click “Go To” to be taken to the Incident record:

Go to the task pane on the Incident record, select the task, and click “Complete”:

A small window will pop up where you can enter the details of the actions you took to complete the task. 

NB: You can complete the Incident task with the same text you used to complete the LIVE task on your change request. Just mention the change request ID number as well, as this is useful for future reference.

Click OK to save your changes. 
Your change request for a report change is now complete!

Requests for New Reports

The change management process for requests for new SSRS reports is largely the same as the change management process for amendments to existing SSRS reports, but there are a few differences, which have been captured here. 

Requesting a New Report

Fill in form fields

The guidance here is identical to the guidance for Section 1.1.

Fill in Change Detail section

The Change Detail section is where you must record exactly what you are changing, why you are changing it, and what the potential impact(s) of your change may be. For a new report, you aren’t actually “changing” anything; you are simply adding a new report to the existing report catalogue. The information you provide in the Change Detail section will therefore be different to the information you would provide for a change to an existing report.
In the “Summary” field, enter the phrase NEW REPORT: [Name of the report you are creating]:

In the “Description” field, complete the 14-part questionnaire as follows:

Question
Answer
Details - What is changing?
Provide the name and a brief description of the new report you are creating. 
Justification - Why is the change necessary?
New reports are usually created to facilitate system processes, particularly newer processes such as those introduced by projects or changes to legislation. Refer to the role of the requestor here, e.g. “Requested by Payroll Manager”, and copy the requestor’s comments from their request – they will normally have provided the justification within the comments. If there is a linked Incident, refer to it by number, i.e. “See linked Incident #X for details.”
Related Changes - Are there dependent changes?
If there are related changes, list them here by Change ID number; otherwise, put “No dependent changes”.
Impact on dependent services? What is the impact on connected or downstream services or components?
If the new report is intended to have an impact on downstream services such as system integrations or HR processes (e.g. Payroll things), it’s worth detailing the impact here. Normally, however, you can just put “No impact on services”. 
Impact - Specify downtime or at risk period
No downtime or at-risk period is entailed creating a new report, so you can put “N/A”. 
Impact - Effect of not applying the change?
This is the reason the new report is required, e.g. “Payroll will be unable to report on data for furloughed workers without the new report”.
Risk Assessment - What are the risks to the services?
It is very unlikely that creating a report will ever pose a risk to services, so you can normally just put “N/A” here. 
Testing - Who will test it and how?
The HRIS Functional Analyst / Senior HR Analyst will create the new report outlined above in the HR Reporting QA solution and deploy the .RDL files to the HR Reporting QA server so that they may be tested.

The change requestor [normally whoever raised the incident] will be given a link to the new report in the QA server and asked to confirm whether they are happy with the report or if it requires further development before it can be published to the LIVE server.
Implementation Plan - Who will implement it and how?
