Context
This document outlines the release and deployment processes for reports in the HR Reporting catalogue. These processes were designed to support robust version control of all the report suites which comprise the HR Reporting catalogue, to ensure that:

users have access only to the most recent version of any report suite
there is only a single “active” version of any given report suite at any given time
previous versions of amended or retired report suites (where applicable) are available in case they need to be viewed or restored to active use

NB: The most important aspect of version control for the HR Reporting catalogue is this: versioning is done at the report suite-level, not the .RDL level. 

This means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite. 
For example, say you are making a change to the report suite PERDEP01 Staff in Post. This report suite consists of 13 separate .RDL files. Even if you are only making a change to one of those 13 .RDLs, you must update the version number on all 13 .RDLs – that is, if you update e.g. the Full Data Set.RDL and promote it from Version 6.0 to Version 7.0, you must also promote the version numbers for the rest of the .RDL files within the report suite to the new version number. 

Report suite
.RDL file
Previous version
New version
PERDEP01 Staff in Post
Full Data Set – the one you’re changing
6.0
7.0

Full Data Set with Cost Allocation
6.0
7.0

Full Data Set with Allowances
6.0
7.0

Limited Data Set
6.0
7.0

…etc…
…
…

By updating the version numbers for each .RDL within a report suite, you ensure that the entire report suite is promoted from one version to the next. This prevents complications like having Full Data Set (Version 6.0) in the same report as Limited Data Set (Version 2.0). 

Version control for HR Reporting is managed in multiple places:
The “Report Summary” header of the SQL query for each .RDL file
The Visual Studio HR Reporting_LIVE.sln and HR Reporting_QA.sln
The HR Reporting LIVE and QA environments
The Live Reports Tracker document

As a rule, the LIVE environment and Visual Studio solution only contain the most recent published version of each .RDL file. 
The QA environment and Visual Studio solution will contain both the most recent published version of an .RDL, as well as any previous versions of that .RDL (stored in a separate folder to the current versions).
For more information about different report servers please refer to the HR Reporting environments section.

See below for further information about each of these areas.

Report Summary headers
The SQL query for every .RDL file contains a “Report Summary” header. This header identifies the following attributes of the .RDL file:

Attribute
Meaning
Name
The name of the report suite
Tab name
The name of the individual .RDL file
Version
The major version of the report suite to which this SQL query belongs
Last updated
Month and year of most recent update to report suite
Change ID
OSM Change Request number
NB
Specific notes about the latest version of the report.

A completed example is shown here: 

/*************** REPORT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes
** Tab name: Appointment Changes
** Version: 5.0 
** Last updated: JULY 2021
** Change ID: 20012493 
***************************************************/

Whenever you update the version number of a report suite, you must update the Report Summary header for every .RDL file within that report suite to reflect the new version number, the month & year the report suite was updated, and the OSM Change Request number relating to the update. 

What if you haven’t actually changed every .RDL file?
Generally speaking, when you update a report suite that contains multiple .RDL files, you will only be changing the SQL code in a few of those .RDLs, not all of them. If you’ve got some .RDL files in your report suite which have not been edited, use this Report Summary Header instead – it’ll make it obvious to anyone who opens the file that the code for this particular .RDL wasn’t updated when the report suite version changed:
/*************** REPORT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes
** Tab name: New Starters
** Version: 5.0 
** Last updated: JULY 2021
** Change ID: 20012493 
** NB: This code has not been edited; this was a version change only.
***************************************************/

Providing these details in the Report Summary header enables any user reviewing the SQL query to quickly determine which version of the query they are looking at and when it was last updated. Most importantly, users can also search for the Change ID on OSM and find the full details of and justification for the update – this is a major time-saver when reviewing SQL queries!

Note that for new reports, you will still need to include these details in the Report Summary header. The version will be “1.0” and the change request should detail both the function of the new report and the justification for creating it.

Visual Studio solutions
There are four HR Reporting solutions (.sln files) in Visual Studio: DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE. The DEV solution is used for creating and testing brand-new reports, while the TEST solution is mainly restricted to project testing and testing updated reports against specific data in test environments. Version control in Visual Studio is managed in the HR Reporting_QA.sln and the HR Reporting_LIVE.sln. 

Solution
Description
Stores archived copies?
HR Reporting_DEV
This solution is a sandpit for development, and is primarily used as a place to create and unit test new reports. 
No – DEV holds no .RDL files for either active or archived report suites.
HR Reporting_TEST
This environment is used to test new and updated versions of reports against a non-production environment where testing is taking place. This would normally happen within the context of a project but may be used to test reports which support new processes being tested in non-production such as those introduced as part of Year End or POG work. It can also be used to regression test the impact of changes to PeopleXD on the existing HR Reporting Catalogue. 
No – TEST holds no .RDL files for either active or archived report suites, except for short periods of time when project teams require the reports for testing. 
HR Reporting_QA
This solution holds the most recent published versions of all the active reports in the HR Reporting catalogue, as well as back-up copies of the previous versions of each report suite (where previous versions exist) in an archive folder. 
Yes – previous versions of the .RDL files for each report suite are held in the Archive folder in the QA solution. The previous versions can be opened in Visual Studio from this Archive folder. 
HR Reporting_LIVE
This solution holds the most recent published versions of all the report suites in the HR Reporting catalogue. 
No – only the most recent versions of the .RDL files for each report suite are stored in the LIVE solution.

Whether you are creating a new report, amending an existing report, or retiring an existing report, you will need to follow the release and deployment processes for both the HR Reporting_QA and HR Reporting_LIVE solution files at a minimum. 

In the QA solution…
All .RDL files in the new or amended report suite must be saved to the HR Reporting_QA solution with the new version number as a filename suffix on each .RDL, e.g. PERDEP01 Full Data Set_v4 for Version 4.0.
Optional: It is helpful to periodically move any .RDL files from previous/retired versions of reports from the I:\OUIT\CoreHR Reports\HR Reporting_QA folder to the I:\OUIT\CoreHR Reports\HR Reporting_QA\HR Reporting_QA\Archive subfolder – it keeps the QA solution from getting too cluttered with older versions!

In the LIVE solution…
Any .RDL files from previous/retired versions of the report suite must be deleted from the LIVE solution.
All .RDL files in the new or amended report suite must be copied to the LIVE solution from the QA solution.
The version number suffix on the .RDL filenames (e.g. PERDEP01 Full Data Set_v4) must be removed from the .RDL files in the LIVE solution before the files are deployed to the LIVE report environment. 

Version numbers are explicitly listed in filenames in the QA solution and environment, so that users can instantly see which version of a report suite they are accessing. 

Version numbers are not included in the filenames of the LIVE solution or environment, for two reasons: 
their presence may confuse users, and 
the LIVE solution and environment should only ever hold the most recent version of any report suite, so it is not necessary to state the version numbers in the filenames of the .RDLs.

HR Reporting environments
The HR Reporting environments follow broadly the same format as the Visual Studio solutions detailed above. There are four HR Reporting environments: DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE. The DEV environment is used for creating and testing brand-new reports, while the TEST environment is mainly restricted to project testing. Version control is managed in the HR Reporting QA environment and the HR Reporting LIVE environment. 

As with the Visual Studio solutions, only the HR Reporting QA environment stores archived copies of report suites. 

Whether you are creating a new report, amending an existing report, or retiring an existing report, you will need to follow the release and deployment processes for both the HR Reporting_QA and HR Reporting_LIVE environments.

In the QA environment…
All .RDL files in the new or amended report suite must be deployed to the QA environment and filed in the appropriate report folder on the server.
The version number of the new/amended report suite should be recorded or updated in the report folder’s Description field. 
Any previous/retired versions of the .RDL file(s) must be removed from their current report folder and filed in the _Back-Up Versions folder.

In the LIVE environment…
Any previous/retired versions of the .RDL file(s) must be deleted from the LIVE environment.
All .RDL files in the new/amended report suite must be deployed to the LIVE environment and filed in the appropriate report folder on the server.

Live Reports Tracker 
The Live Reports Tracker is a spreadsheet which contains details of all active reports in the HR Reporting catalogue, including each report’s name, where it is filed in the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, and which AD groups it is shared with. 

Version control is not managed as such in the Live Reports Tracker, however this document must be updated whenever you create a new report, retire an existing report, or amend any of the following aspects of an existing report:

The report’s prefix (e.g. PERDEP01) 
The report’s name (e.g. Staff in Post)
The report’s location within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy (e.g. Home > Personnel > Current Reports)
The AD groups which have permission to view the report in the HR Reporting_LIVE environment (e.g. HRIS-RR-PERDREP – Personnel). 

Refer to the process below for further information on when and how to update the Live Reports Tracker.
General Processes
It’s important to note that the fundamental steps for releasing and deploying new/amended reports are nearly identical, so they have been included at the top of the Processes section for easy reference. These steps are: 

Preparing the .RDL files in Visual Studio 
Moving the prepared .RDLs into the appropriate Visual Studio solutions 
Deploying the .RDLs to the appropriate HR Reporting environments. 
Using the HR Reporting folder hierarchy

Retired reports are managed differently, so if you are retiring a report, you may wish to skip to that section. 

4445-11620500
STOP: All changes to the HR Reporting catalogue (new reports, amended reports, retired reports) must be recorded in detail in OSM via a formal change request. Each of the steps listed in the guidance below should have a corresponding task on an OSM change. 
Do not proceed until you have raised a change request in OSM and assigned yourself the relevant tasks!
See: HOW TO - Manage Reports - Change Processes in OSM.docx

Preparing .RDL files in Visual Studio
Before you can release and deploy a new or amended report, you will need to have the necessary .RDL files in place in Visual Studio. Both new and amended reports are created by copying existing .RDL files and editing them as required, depending on what you are trying to achieve. 

Never, ever make changes to an existing .RDL file. Always make a copy and edit that instead. 

To copy an .RDL file, go into the Visual Studio solution which contains the .RDL. Expand the Reports list within the Solution Explorer to view all the .RDL files available within your current solution. 

Select the .RDL file you wish to copy. 
If you are amending a report, the file you need to copy is the current version of the .RDL you want to modify. 
Example: if you are creating version 2.0 (_v2) of RECSUP01 Applicant Detail Per Vacancy, you should copy the .RDL file RECSUP01 Applicant Detail Per Vacancy_v1. 

If you are creating a new report, the .RDL file you need to copy is the MASTER Report Template.rdl in the HR Reporting_DEV solution. This template .RDL file contains all of the necessary formatting in the report Tablix, so that you don’t have to add it in when you render your new report: 

Once you’ve selected the .RDL you wish to copy, enter CTRL+C to copy the file, then enter CTRL+V to paste the copied file into the Reports list. The copied file will appear at the bottom of the Reports list, with the prefix “Copy of…”:

Right-click your “Copy of…” .RDL file and select “Rename”:

Amend the name of the .RDL file as necessary, being sure to add the new version number to the end of the filename. Hit ENTER to save your changes. 

What about new reports?
If you are creating a brand-new report, you should rename the .RDL file with the prefix of your new report suite and the name you have chosen for the .RDL file. Remember that the version number for new reports is always _v1:

Example: TIMDEP40 Sickness Absences over Time_v1.RDL 

Once you have created a copy of the .RDL file you wish to modify, you can make your changes to the copy. See the guide for rendering reports in Visual Studio if you need help. 

Save your changes when you are finished. Your new .RDL file is now ready for the release and deployment process. 

Remember: versioning is done at the report suite-level, not the .RDL level. If you are amending a report suite that contains multiple .RDLs, you will need to create new copies of every .RDL file in the report suite, make the necessary amendments, and save your changes before you can begin the release and deployment process for your amended report. 

Moving .RDL files in Visual Studio 
A key aspect of the release and deployment process is moving .RDL files from one HR Reporting solution to another in Visual Studio. 

When you develop a new report, you will need to move the new report’s .RDL file(s) across three solutions:
HR Reporting_DEV HR Reporting_QA HR Reporting_LIVE
When you amend an existing report, you will need to move the amended report’s .RDL file(s) across two solutions:
HR Reporting_QA HR Reporting_LIVE1

To move an .RDL file from one solution to another, open the solution you want to add the .RDL to – for example if you are moving an .RDL from HR Reporting_DEV to HR Reporting_QA, you should open the QA solution.

Go to the Solution Explorer, then select the Reports folder and right-click it to open the sub-menu. Select Add > Existing Item… (or type Shift + Alt + A):

The solution folder on I:\OUIT\CoreHR Reports\ will open. This folder contains all the files which belong to your current HR Reporting solution: 

If you want to add an .RDL file from a different solution, navigate back to the main I:\OUIT\CoreHR Reports folder and select the solution folder you want to open. 

In this example, you can see from the title bar and the file path that you are selecting files from the DEV solution to add them to the QA solution:

Scroll through the solution folder until you find the file you want to add to your current solution, then select it and click Add:

The file you have added will now appear at the bottom of the Reports list within the Solution Explorer of your current solution: 

You can move multiple .RDL files to your current solution simultaneously – simply select all the files you wish to move before you click Add. All files you have added will appear at the bottom of the Reports list within the Solution Explorer of your current solution.

Deploying .RDL files from Visual Studio
Once you have prepared your new/amended .RDL files and ensured that they are present in the appropriate Visual Studio solution, you are ready to deploy the .RDLs to the HR Reporting environments. 

The .RDL files should only ever be deployed in the following order:

(Optional) Deploy into the DEV or TEST environments. This is only required if you are testing a newly-developed report or if you need to test a report against a specific non-production Reporting environment (TEST can be configured to “point at” UOXZ, UOXC and UOXU, as required). 
Deploy into HR Reporting QA environment. This is where end-users can perform UAT and confirm if they are happy for your new/amended report suite to be published. 
Deploy into HR Reporting LIVE environment. Only do this after receiving formal change approval in OSM. 

The deployment process is the same across all HR Reporting solutions and environments, and the steps are outlined below. 

To deploy an .RDL file, select it in the Solution Explorer pane and right-click. Select “Deploy” from the right-click menu:

The progress of the deployment will display in the Output pane at the bottom of your screen. Look at the final message to see whether your deployment has succeeded or failed:

You can deploy multiple .RDL files simultaneously – simply select all the files you wish to deploy before you select “Deploy” from the right-click menu. Each file will be deployed individually by Visual Studio, and the results of your deployment will be displayed in the Output pane at the bottom of your screen: 

If your deployment has succeeded, the file will be available in the HR Reporting environment’s Home _Deployment folder.

What if your deployment fails? 
Sometimes, Visual Studio will be unable to deploy your .RDL file. This can be because…

There is something wrong with the format of the .RDL file itself.
The .RDL file refers to a shared dataset which doesn’t exist in the HR Reporting environment you’re deploying to. 
The HR Reporting environment is temporarily unavailable, so Visual Studio can’t contact it. 

If your deployment has failed, you will see an Error List pane with a description of the reason for the failure; for example: 

Refer to the guidance for troubleshooting common errors to resolve the problem, and click “Deploy” when you are ready to retry deployment. 

Using the HR Reporting folder hierarchy
Once you have successfully deployed the .RDL file(s) for your new/amended report suite, you must move the file(s) to the appropriate location within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy. 

NB: Review the HOW TO - Manage Reports - Access Permissions within HR Reporting.docx for further information on what the reporting folder hierarchy is and how it is used. 

If you’ve created a new report, you’ll have to set up a new folder within the folder hierarchy before you can move your .RDL files. If you’ve amended an existing report, you’ll need to archive the previous version of the report suite before you can move your .RDL files. 

Moving .RDL files within the folder hierarchy
To move .RDL files from one folder to another within an HR Reporting environment, go to the folder in which the .RDL files are currently located and click the tick-box next to each .RDL you wish to move:

At the top of the screen, click “Move”:

The Select folder window will open. From here, you can navigate to the appropriate navigation folder subfolder report folder where your .RDL file(s) should be sent. 

Click the appropriate report folder, then click “Select”. The screen will refresh and the Select folder window will close. The .RDL files you’ve moved will disappear from your current folder, so you should navigate to the folder you just selected to check that the .RDLs you’ve moved are appearing correctly there:

Creating new report folders
Before you can file the .RDLs for your new report, you’ll need to ensure you’ve actually got a report folder in place for them. Follow this process to create a new report folder in any HR Reporting environment. 

Please ensure that you are fully familiar with the use of folder access permissions within HR Reporting before you create a new folder. This is essential in order to avoid data breaches.

Where should your new report folder go? 
Some aspects of creating a new report folder are common sense – payroll reports will go in the Payroll folder, personnel reports will go in the Personnel folder, etc. But if your navigation folder contains subfolders, which subfolder should you choose? 

Subfolders often have names that are meaningful to the main users of the reports located within them, e.g. “Relocation” within the Payroll folder, or “Athena SWAN Reports” within the HR Analytics folder. If you are unsure of where to file your new report, speak to the end-user who requested it – they may be able to suggest a logical subfolder.

If the end-user can’t advise you, or you are still unsure, speak to the HR Functional Analysis team for guidance. 

Navigate to the appropriate navigation folder or subfolder to which your new report belongs. At the top of the screen, click “New” and select “Folder” from the drop-down menu:

A pop-up will open, prompting you for the folder name. Enter the prefix and name of your new report suite:

Click “Create” to create the report folder. It will appear in the folder list:

Now that your folder exists, you need to apply the appropriate user access permissions. Click the ellipsis (…) symbol next to the report folder’s name and select “Manage”: 

Select the Security tab from the left-hand side of the screen:

A list of all the users and AD groups which have access to your new report folder will be displayed. This list is inherited from the navigation folder or subfolder in which your new report folder sits, so the first thing you need to do is to customise your report folder’s security. 

Note: Customising your report folder’s security breaks the link between the report folder and its navigation folder/subfolder. This means that you can make changes to the access permissions of the navigation folder/subfolder and those changes will not automatically be reproduced for your report folder. Updating the Live Reports Tracker
The Live Reports Tracker is a spreadsheet maintained by the HR Functional Analysis team. It is used to allocate prefixes to new or renamed reports (e.g. TIMDEP01), and to record the location of each report suite within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy. 

These steps are essential for all new report suites, but are rarely required for amended reports unless certain conditions are met. 
New reports
If you have created a new report, you will need to assign it an appropriate prefix and determine where it will be filed in the HR Reporting folder hierarchy. 
Assign a prefix
Report names are all prefixed with an alphanumeric code in the form “XXXYYY##”. This code contains the following information: 

The “XXX” segment of the code indicates the report’s primary data source – for example, a personnel report will draw the majority of its data from the Personnel tables in the PeopleXD database, while a payroll report will draw the majority of its data from the Payroll tables in the PeopleXD database. 
The “YYY” segment of the code indicates the report’s primary audience – for example, a personnel report will be mainly run by departments, while a pensions report will be mainly run by the Pensions Office. 
The “##” segment of the code indicates the type of data the report contains: 
Current data: data from the database as it is today (e.g. “PERDEP01 Staff in Post”)
Monthly reporting data: data from a given point in time, or from a certain date range (e.g. “PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes”)
Tracking data: data that is used to monitor various processes across the University (e.g. “PERDEP41 Immigration and Right to Work”)

Context
This document details the formal change management process in OSM which must be used for implementing changes to SSRS reports and shared datasets (including the creation & deployment of new SSRS reports and shared datasets). Please refer to the Knowledge Article for additional details on who must be consulted and informed about such changes, and what downstream processes/services a report change may impact. 

Changes to Existing Reports/Shared Datasets

The processes below refer to reports (.RDL files), but are the same for any changes to shared datasets (.RSD files). If you are amending a shared dataset, you should edit the text of the change request and linked tasks as follows:

All references to “report” should be amended to “shared dataset”.
All references to “.RDL file(s)” should be amended to “.RSD file(s)”.
All references to [REPORT NAME] or [REPORT TAB] should be amended to the name of the shared dataset (e.g. LOV_Optional_EmployeeStatus.rsd).

Footnotes have been added throughout the guidance to remind you of when such amendments may be required.

Raising a Change Request
Fill in form fields

Context
This document contains a list of error messages commonly encountered when writing reports in SQL Developer and rendering them in Visual Studio. An explanation of each error is provided, and where a resolution exists, this has been provided as well. 
Any new error messages encountered by report writers should ideally be captured in this document so that resolutions, when identified, may be added here. 

SQL errors 

Enter substitution variable

This window pops up in SQL Developer if there is an ampersand (&) anywhere in the report code. Replace the ampersand with the word “and”. 

Alternatively state the command SET DEFINE OFF at the top of your code before the SELECT statement, and highlight it before pressing the “Run” button:

The SET DEFINE OFF command tells SQL Developer to ignore variables within the SELECT statement.
ORA-00904: Invalid Identifier

This error occurs when your code references an ITEM or VIEW which does not exist. 

Check that the item and/or view in the error line referenced by the error message isn’t misspelled (e.g. PESRON_REFERENCE instead of PERSON_REFERENCE, PRBI_H_PERSON_MASTER instead of PRBI_HR_PERSON_MASTER). 
If your code has multiple layers (Base Query, Subquery / Subqueries, Main Display Layer), make sure that the view references are not included beyond the Base Query unless they are explicitly stated in the FROM statement:
Incorrect
Correct
===MAIN (DISPLAY) LAYER===

SELECT
View.Item

FROM

===BASE QUERY===

(SELECT
View.Item

FROM
Database.View)
===MAIN (DISPLAY) LAYER===

SELECT
Item

FROM

===BASE QUERY===

(SELECT
View.Item

FROM
Database.View)
In the example screenshot above, the report code has a Base Query and a Main Display Layer. The Main Display Layer is selecting the item PERSON_REFERENCE from the Base Query, rather than directly from the COREHR database, so it does not need to refer to the view PRBI_HR_PERSON_MASTER. The reference to the view needs to be removed from the error line in order to resolve this error.

ORA-00918: Column ambiguously defined

This error occurs when your code references the same item more than once in a single SELECT statement, e.g.:
SELECT
View.Item1,
View.Item2,
View.Item3,
View.Item1 – duplicate reference

FROM
Database.View

The code cannot be executed because it’s attempting to pick up the same item multiple times. You can either remove the duplicate reference, or use aliases to give the item different labels, e.g.:
SELECT
View.Item1 as “Personnel Number”,
View.Item2 as “Forename”,
View.Item3 as “Surname”,
View.Item1 as “Employee Lookup Value”

FROM
Database.View

The code can now be executed because it has given the duplicate items two separate aliases, so it can differentiate between them. 

ORA-00932: inconsistent datatypes: expected DATE got NUMBER

This error occurs if your SQL query is attempting to compare two dates within a calculation or a WHERE condition, and one of the dates is not in “Date” format.
Check for any TRUNC() functions wrapped around dates. The TRUNC() function attempts to read anything within the brackets as if it is in date format. If you feed a non-date variable into a TRUNC() function, such as a text string or an integer, TRUNC() can’t understand what you’re asking it to do. 
ORA-01790: expression must have same datatype as corresponding expression

This error occurs if you are attempting to UNION two (or more) queries and the column ordering is not identical across the queries. A UNION statement tells SQL to append the results of Query 2 to the results of Query 1, like so:
Query 1
Q1 Name
Q1 Date of birth
Q1 NI Number
Q1 Email
Query 2
Q2 Name
Q2 Date of birth
Q2 NI Number
Q2 Email
UNION table:
Q1 Name
Q1 Date of birth
Q1 NI Number
Q1 Email
Q2 Name
Q2 Date of birth
Q2 NI Number
Q2 Email
The error occurs if the columns are out of sync when SQL tries to join the two queries:
Q1 Name
Q1 Date of birth
Q1 NI Number
Q1 Email
Q2 Name
Q2 NI Number
Q2 Date of birth
Q2 Email
Check the column order in the queries you are attempting to UNION to ensure they are identical. Move columns around as necessary in your SELECT statements until your queries have the same columns in the same order, and try again. This should resolve the error. 

Visual Studio errors

BC30203 Identifier Expected
 
You may see this error when attempting to preview a report within Visual Studio. Check the Expression value for the Parameters textbox within your report:

The VBA expression in this textbox is what generates the parameter statement at the top of a finished report, confirming what parameters were selected:

Make sure that every parameter field is identified as a .VALUE or a .LABEL item within the VBA expression code. If the .VALUE or .LABEL identification is missing from the parameter string, you need to add it back in, or the VBA expression will be invalid:

This document provides information that you will need when working in Visual Studio. This is not a process document so much as a “contextual information” document. 

Commonly-used terms
There are a number of commonly-used terms that appear throughout this document. A brief explanation of each is given here.

Term
Notes
Example
Dataset
A dataset is the SQL code which queries the PeopleXD database and returns results. It can be embedded (unique to a single .RDL file) or shared (available to re-use across multiple .RDL files). 
“DataSet1” within any .RDL file contains the report SQL code.
Dataset (Embedded)
An embedded dataset is a SQL query which is unique to a single .RDL file. 
All report queries are “embedded” datasets.
Dataset (Shared)
Shared datasets are SQL queries which are available to re-use across multiple .RDL files. We use shared datasets to return Lists of Values (LOVs) which power parameter drop-down lists. 
LOV_Optional_DepartmentCode
Data source
A data source is a connection to a PeopleXD database (UOXC, UOXP, etc.). 
Oracle_DS_UserCredentials

Deployment
The act of publishing a report (.RDL file) or a shared dataset to one of the HR Reporting environments.

Design pane
The area of Visual Studio where you render the .RDL file.

Project
A project is a “sub-container” within a solution. The project is where your data sources, datasets, and reports are saved. A solution can contain multiple projects, but for HR Reporting, we have a strict 1-to-1 relationship between solutions and projects, such that each solution only contains a single project. 
HR Reporting QA.sln contains project “HR Reporting QA”, which holds the data sources, shared datasets, and reports for the HR Reporting QA environment. 
.RDL file
An .RDL file is a report; the terms are interchangeable.

Report

Solution
A solution (.sln) is simply a container Visual Studio uses to organize one or more related projects. When you open a solution, Visual Studio automatically loads all the projects that the solution contains.

Launching the app
Before you can create or edit reports, you will need to launch the Visual Studio application and select the solution file (.sln) that you want to work in. 

Launch Visual Studio from your Start menu and enter your CONNECT login details when prompted, in order to access the CONNECT Remote Desktop:

After a short wait, the splash screen will appear, followed by a sign-in window. Click the “Not now, maybe later” link at the bottom of the sign-in window: 

You’ll then be asked for your display preferences. Select Development Settings: General and click Start Visual Studio to complete the app launch. 

After a short wait (occasionally as long as a minute or two), Visual Studio will open and you will see the Home screen:

Opening a solution file (.SLN)
Report files in Visual Studio are grouped into larger files called “solutions” (file extension .sln). Each solution has its own data sources, datasets, and report files. There are four solutions for you to choose from in Visual Studio:
Solution
Data source
Notes
HR Reporting DEV
Non-production (generally UOXC)
This is a sandpit environment for creating new reports. 
HR Reporting TEST
Non-production (generally UOXU)
This is a test environment, mainly for use by project teams
HR Reporting QA
Production
This is the UAT environment, where reports are deployed for testing by end-users. It is also where old versions of reports are archived. 
HR Reporting LIVE
Production
This is the live environment, where final, approved drafts of reports are stored and published to the live server. 
Which solution you open will depend on what you need to do in Visual Studio. 

To open a solution, go to File > Open > Project / Solution:

A warning message will appear; just click OK to dismiss it (there is no way to prevent this pop-up, but it has no impact on your ability to use Visual Studio): 

The Open Project file browser will open. You need to navigate to I:\OUIT\CoreHR Reports. This is a secure network drive owned by Microsoft Platform Services and used for storing all HR Reporting files: 

Choose the solution you wish to work in, and double-click the corresponding folder icon. Within the folder, select the solution file and double-click to open: 

Another warning message will pop up; simply click OK to dismiss it:

As with the previous pop-up, there is no way to prevent this message from appearing every time you use Visual Studio, but it won’t impact your ability to use the application. 

After a moment, the solution file will load. You can always check which solution you have open by looking at the title bar or within the Solution Explorer pane:

Once you’ve opened a solution, you can open any of the files contained within it. These include:

Shared data sources
Shared datasets
Reports

To open any of these files, go to the Solution Explorer pane on the right side of the screen and expand the folder which contains the file(s) in which you are interested. Double-click the file to open it. 

NB: It is not possible to have more than one solution file open at a time. If you want to do some work in HR Reporting DEV and HR Reporting QA, for example, you will need to exit one solution before you can open the other. 

Viewing a report file (.RDL)

Open the .RDL
To open a report file, go to the Solution Explorer pane and expand the Reports folder. You will be presented with a list of all the report files currently available to open within the solution.

To open one, you can either double-click it, or right-click and select Open from the menu:

The .RDL file will load and the Design pane will be displayed:

The Design pane
All .RDL files within Visual Studio have a Design pane, where you can format the data from your SQL query into a user-friendly report. The Design pane for every report in the HR Reporting catalogue must contain the following elements:
Title textbox 
This textbox appears at the top of the report and contains the title of the .RDL file, in the format [Report prefix] + [.RDL name], e.g. PERDEP01 Limited Data Set. 

Parameters textbox 
This textbox appears underneath the Title, and contains a VBA expression which will display the parameters selected each time the report is run. In the Design pane, it looks like this:

When a report has been run, the Parameters textbox looks like this:

NB: Full details on how to edit the VBA expression used in the Parameters textbox are provided in the HOW TO guide (link required). 
Report Tablix
The “Tablix” (a Microsoft term) displays report data from a data set in cells that are organized into rows and columns. This is where your report fields are arranged and formatted, and where your results appear when you run the report query. A Tablix can be formatted as a simple table or as a matrix. 

Footer textbox
This textbox appears at the bottom of the screen, and contains a standard VBA expression which will display a message whenever the report is run. The message states the name of the .RDL file, the SSO of the username who ran the report, as well as the date and time of the report run. In the Design pane, it looks like this:

When a report has been run, the Footer textbox looks like this:

NB: Do not edit the VBA expression for the Footer textbox; the message displayed must remain standard across the entire HR Reporting catalogue. 

The Preview pane
All .RDL files within Visual Studio also have a Preview pane, where you can run your report query and check your results and your formatting without needing to deploy the report to the HR Reporting environments. 

To open the Preview pane, simply click the tab at the top of the .RDL file. If your report has parameters, you will be prompted to fill them in, exactly as a report user would be on the HR Reporting environments:

Enter the parameters you wish to use (or none if you don’t want to restrict your results), and click View Report to run the report query. The SQL code of your report will query the PeopleXD database to which your solution is connected, and the “Loading…” message will display while the query runs:

When the query is complete, the report results will load in the Preview pane. The page numbers at the top of the report indicate how many pages of results have been retrieved. 

NB: The parameter prompts at the top of the screen can be edited if you want to re-run the report with new parameters – simply change the parameter values and click View Report to re-run your query.

You can export your results by clicking the Save icon and choosing the export file format: 

To exit the Preview pane, simply click back into the Design tab at the top of the .RDL file. 

The Report Data pane
The Report Data pane is where you configure the individual elements of your .RDL file: its data sources, datasets, and parameters. The Report Data pane is located on the left side of the screen:

Expand any of the folders to view their contents. A brief description of each is given below.

NB: The Built-in Fields are essential components of all .RDL files, and are included as standard in every report. We don’t ever edit these values. We also don’t use the Images functionality within Visual Studio, so this folder can be ignored. 

Parameters 
The Parameters folder lists each parameter present in your report. 

A parameter must exist in multiple locations within every .RDL file:
The SQL code of your report query: essential
The Parameters folder of the Report Data pane: essential 
The Parameters textbox: optional (if you want the parameter values displayed on the report each time it is run)
You can add new parameters to the Report Data pane by right-clicking the Parameters folder and selecting Add Parameter…. 

NB: Never add a parameter within the Report Data pane without also adding it to the SQL code of your query. Parameters must exist within your SQL code or they will not work!
You can click into each parameter to view or edit its properties. Double-clicking a parameter will open the Report Parameter Properties window for that specific parameter.

There are three main sections to any parameter which you must configure.
General
The General properties of a parameter include:
Property
Values
Notes
Name
Name of the parameter
This must exactly match the name of the parameter within the report SQL code; e.g. if your parameter is called PersonRef within the SQL code, it must be called PersonRef within the properties screen. 
Prompt
The user prompt
This can be whatever you like (although there are naming standards); e.g. the PersonRef parameter can have the prompt value of “Personnel number”. 
Data type
Text, Boolean, Date/Time, Integer, Float
The only values used within HR Reporting .RDL files are Text (for alphanumeric fields) and Date/Time for date parameters. 
Visibility
Visible, Hidden, Internal
All parameters are Visible by default, except the Username parameter, which is Hidden. 
Available Values
If your parameter is powered by a drop-down list of values (LOV), you can either define the LOV here or select a shared dataset from which to derive the values. 
Default Values
If you want a default value for your parameter, you can define it here. 
Data Sources
The Data Sources folder lists each data source present in your report. All reports must contain the two standard shared data sources:
Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount: the service account is used to run the queries for shared datasets, e.g. to retrieve all department codes for use in a parameter’s drop-down list. 
Oracle_DS_UserCredentials: the user account is used to run the main report SQL code – it’s each report user’s individual reporting login credentials. By passing these credentials to PeopleXD, the database can automatically detect and apply the correct security when retrieving report results; e.g. a user who is only allowed to see Pay Group 20 will only see results for Pay Group 20. 

If you are missing either data source (for instance, if you are creating a new report), simply right-click the Data Sources folder and select Add Data Source…. 

Datasets
The Datasets folder lists each dataset present in your .RDL file. This includes the main report query, as well as any additional datasets which are used to power your parameters. 

NB: The main report query should always be named “DataSet1”, while any parameter-related datasets should have descriptive names linking them to their parameters, e.g. Department for a dataset which provides a list of departments for the Department parameter. 
Double-click any dataset to open the Dataset Properties window. 

If you are looking at an embedded dataset, you can view the raw SQL code of the dataset in the Query pane:

If you are looking at a shared dataset, you will be able to see the full name of the shared dataset – this will enable you to select the shared dataset from the Solution Explorer pane to view the SQL code for that dataset. 

Viewing a shared dataset (.RSD)
To open a shared dataset, go to the Solution Explorer pane and expand the Shared Datasets folder. You will be presented with a list of all the shared dataset files currently available to open within the solution. 

To open one, you can either double-click it, or right-click and select Open from the menu:

The Shared Dataset Properties window will open and the Query screen will be displayed. The Query screen holds the SQL code for the dataset, enabling you to see what information the dataset is retrieving from PeopleXD. 

NB: Never amend a shared dataset without speaking to Athena Artuso. Shared datasets are used by multiple reports across the HR Reporting catalogue, and any changes to a shared dataset will impact all its dependent reports. 

Viewing a shared data source
Open the data source
To open a shared data source, go to the Solution Explorer pane and expand the Shared Data Sources folder. You will be presented with a list of all the shared data sources currently available to open within the solution.

To open one, you can either double-click it, or right-click and select Open from the menu: 

The Shared Data Source Properties window will open and the General screen will be displayed. The Connection String field will show you which PeopleXD database the current Visual Studio solution is connected to:

NB: Do not change the Connection String for a shared data source without first speaking to Athena Artuso or Simon Burford. 

Never update the Connection String in the HR Reporting LIVE solution; this must always be connected to UOXP. 

View the connection credentials
Each data source connects to PeopleXD by logging into the PeopleXD database specified in the Connection String. This means that login credentials must be supplied to the data source. 
To check the login credentials on any data source, click Build… next to the Connection String field:

The Connection Properties window will pop up. This window will confirm which PeopleXD database you are using, and will display the login credentials being used to access that database. 
UserCredentials data source
For the Oracle_DS_UserCredentials data source, the login credentials can be set to your personal reporting login details – this will enable you to run your report in the Preview pane without having to provide your username and password every time you way to run your query. Just enter your login details in the Connection Properties window and select “Save my password” to store your password for the duration of your Visual Studio session. If you want to check that you’re able to log into the PeopleXD database, click Test Connection:

Visual Studio will check your credentials and confirm whether the database is accessible: 

ServiceAccount data source
For the Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount data source, the login credentials are the same across all environments. Click Build… to view the login credentials and click Test Connection to ping the PeopleXD database and confirm whether it is accessible. 

NB: The Service Account has unlimited user sessions and unrestricted access to PeopleXD’s databases, so it must be kept highly secure to prevent unwanted data breaches. Only a subset of reporting super-users (Athena Artuso and Simon Burford) know the login credentials for the Service Account data source, and they must periodically update these login credentials to keep the account secure. 

The Service Account username is REPORT_POWERBI. This is static across all HR Reporting environments and must never be changed.

Deploying files to HR Reporting servers
If you want to make a Visual Studio file available on one of the HR Reporting servers, you must deploy that file to the server in question. You can deploy:

Shared data sources
Shared datasets
Report (.RDL) files

The name of the solution file within Visual Studio confirms which HR Reporting server your files will be deployed to, e.g. if you are using HR Reporting DEV.sln, any files you deploy from Visual Studio will be published to the HR Reporting DEV environment. 

NB: There is a 1-to-1 relationship between a Visual Studio solution and its corresponding HR Reporting server; this is defined at the solution level and applies to all files within that solution. 

HR Reporting DEV.sln deploys to HR Reporting DEV
HR Reporting TEST.sln deploys to HR Reporting TEST
HR Reporting QA.sln deploys to HR Reporting QA
HR Reporting LIVE.sln deploys to HR Reporting LIVE

To deploy a file, select it in the Solution Explorer pane and right-click. Select Deploy from the right-click menu:

The deployment progress will display in the Output pane at the bottom of your screen. Look at the final message to see whether your deployment has succeeded or failed:

If your deployment has succeeded, the file will be available on the relevant HR Reporting server. If your deployment has failed, you will see an Error List pane with a description of the reason for the failure:

Macros
Macros have been added to each word template to carry out the following:

Add Departmental header and footer from another document. 

Enable automatic display of Fill-in prompts to the end user (e.g. to enable the population of certain fields within the letter).

Allow the user to create a standard text document from the template letter, which can then edited (see below for more detailed information on each Macro). 

Macros can be found in the following folder O:\PS\HRIS\Core correspondence templates\v20\Macros\New Macros from 30OCT15. 

NB. During the first run of this macro, a variable named “macruncorexx” is created and set with a value of 1. Variables are set against a Word document, so once set will remain each time the document is opened. This stops the macro running if the document is re-opened; this will allow users to edit and save changes to the document. 

When the macro is run it carries out the following:
Opens the first page header and copies the header information from the area bookmarked “header1” from a letterhead document held in C:\Coreapps\Letter_head.docx on the user’s PC (see section on Department Letterheads).

Copies the footer information from the area bookmarked “foot3” from the same document.
 
Selects the entire document and performs a Ctrl+A, then F9 keyboard action; this causes the Fill-in prompts to be displayed for the user to complete.

Selects all text and removes all mail merge fields (e.g. ifs and fill-ins etc.) to leave only plain text in the document. 
The Macro is named AutoOpen in each template. Macros can be accessed in Word from View>Macros button>Edit macro.

There are two macros to choose from depending on whether a Departmental letterhead is required: one pulls through the letter head/footer information and the Fill-in prompts and the other only enables the Fill-in prompts. The name of the Macro should always be AutoOpen.

New Macro Fill-ins only – this macro is used if the template is NOT output on departmental letterhead stationery:

Sub AutoOpen()
'''Sub AutoOpen() is the name of any macro that runs when a word document opens. 
'''All macro information needs to be entered between Sub AutoOpen() and End Sub
Dim strVal as Long
'''The above just tells word that strVal is a number, as opposed to text.
'''during the first run of this macro a variable called macruncorexx is created and set with a value of 1
'''variables are set against a word document so once set will remain each time the document is opened
'''the existence of macruncorexx and value of macruncorexx is checked by the first piece of code in the macro to establish if the macro has been run before
'''the following code sets strVal as the value of macruncorexx if it exists
'''if macruncorexx does not yet exist then strVal is set as 0 to tell word that the macro has not yet been run
On Error Resume Next
strVal = ActiveDocument.Variables("macruncorexx").Value
 If Err.Number <> 0 Then
 strVal = 0
 End If
On Error GoTo 0 ' reset error handler

'''the macro then only continues if the strVal (taken from the value of macruncorexx if it exists) is not 1
If strVal <> 1 Then

'''you must then add any specific macro within this space
'''select all of the document of forces the prompts to be displayed
 Selection.WholeStory
 
 Selection.Fields.Update
 Selection.MoveUp Unit:=wdLine, Count:=1

'''end specific macro space

'''after any specific macro has been run the following code will set macruncorexx as 1 to tell the macro not to run again next time
ActiveDocument.Variables.Add Name:="macruncorexx", Value:=1
'''the following three rows of code removes all mail merge fields (e.g. ifs and fill-ins etc.) to leave only plain text in the document
Selection.WholeStory
 Selection.Fields.Unlink
 Selection.HomeKey Unit:=wdStory
'''the end if below indicates the end of all of the things the macro should do the first time it is run
End If
 
end sub

How to make the answer to a FILLIN prompt repeat elsewhere in the document, without needing to repeat the FILLIN prompt itself.

The FILLIN prompt needs to be wrapped in another set of brackets with the words ‘SET’ and the reference of your choice given after for the prompt/answer, e.g.

{ SET TheName { FILLIN “Please write your name” } } 

In order for the answer to then appear in the text, simply insert { TheName } wherever you wish the answer to this prompt to appear.

The letter templates can be quite difficult to work with and the slightest change can affect the output of the letter and how the merge fields, fill-ins and ASK fields function.

Formatting can be affected by things outside our control such as local PC settings, versions of Microsoft and the departmental header being used.

In the event of a macro not working as expected on one document which is working correctly on another document, compare the two documents and check for extra or missing characters, spaces, and punctuation in the macro code.
Department header appearing on every page

Does page 2 onwards have a page number in the top left of the page? If No – copy from another template. Save and test.

Check the formatting of the header. Go to Page Layout>Page Setup>Layout. Check that the ‘Different first page’ box is ticked. 

Extra spacing between rows or paragraphs
Formatting in MS Word is often determined by local settings on your PC. Regardless of the settings applied to a document these can be overridden by the default settings on a user’s PC. Formatting is based on best endeavours and there is an expectation that departments will need to check and amend formatting on documents produced from the system.

Check the paragraph settings on the Page Layout tab. If document has spacing set after the line this may be the cause. Try removing it and running the letter again. Ensure that Spacing After is set to 12pts.

Check how many carriage returns there are between the rows/paragraphs. Adjust as required.

If it’s a merge field, check the actual data that is being merged. If the field allows manual entry (e.g. the Job Text field), then it could be an extra space or return in that particular field on the record you are running the letter for.

No spacing between paragraphs

Check the paragraph settings on the Page Layout tab. Ensure that ‘Spacing_After:’ is set to 12pts.

Avoid using carriage returns to create spaces between paragraphs, as this can affect the Widow/Orphan control and may result in a heading being on a different page from the rest of the text.

Department header not appearing
The macros that control the inclusion of headers and footers is based on whether there is anything in the field already. Documents that have the University Logo in the header e.g. contracts will not also pull in the departmental header.

Check whether there is a space or carriage return in the document header. If yes – remove it and test again. If no – check that the correct macro is saved against the document. See Section 2.2 for guidance on the macros for Headers and Footers.

Ask fields

The Ask field code prompts you to enter information and assigns your response to a bookmark. For the information to appear in the document, you must insert a Ref field that refers to the bookmark. Word prompts you for a response each time you update the Ask field, such as when you press F9 or step through the records in a mail merge. 
You can use the Ask field in a document or as part of a mail merge. 
To display the response in the content of the document, you must insert a Ref field after the Ask field.
Adding an ASK field 
On the Insert tab, in the Text group, click Quick Parts, and then click Field.

In the Field names list, select Ask.

In the Prompt box, type the question that you want answered.

In the Bookmark name box, type a name for the bookmark that will store the response to the prompt.
If you want a predefined response, select the Default response to prompt check box, and type the text.

If you want the same response to apply to all the records in a mail merge, select the Prompt before merging bookmark text check box. Otherwise, Word will prompt you for a response with each record.

Click OK
Example

To use the Ask field as part of a mail merge, do the following while you are setting up the mail merge:
On the Mailings tab, in the Write & Insert Fields group, click Rules, and then click Ask.

In the Bookmark box, type a name for the bookmark that will store the response to the prompt.
In the Prompt box, type the question you want answered.
If you want a predefined response, type the response in the Default bookmark text box.
If you want the same response to apply to all the records in the merge, select the Ask once check box. Otherwise, Word will prompt you for a response with each record.
Syntax
When you view the Ask field code in your document, the syntax looks like this:
{ ASK Bookmark"Prompt" [Optional switches ] }
Note:  A field code tells the field what to show. Field results are what is shown in the document after having evaluated the field code. To toggle between viewing the field code and the field code results, press Alt+F9.

Instructions

Bookmark
The bookmark name assigned to the response to the prompt, for example, ClientName.
"Prompt"
Prompt text, which is displayed in a dialog box — for example, "Enter the client's name."

Optional switches
\d "Default "
Specifies a default response if you don't type a response in the prompt dialog box. For example, the field
{ ASK Typist "Enter typist's initials:" \d "tds" } assigns "tds" to the bookmark Typist if you don't enter a response. 
If you don't specify a default response, Word uses the last response that was entered. To specify a blank entry as the default, type empty quotation marks after the switch. For example, type \d "" . 
\o

When used in a mail merge main document, displays the prompt one time instead of each time you merge a new data record. The same response is inserted in each resulting merged document.

Example

An Ask field with a bookmark of MonthReport and prompt of What month is this report for? has been inserted near the beginning of the document.
The month name occurs several places in the document. A Ref field that specifies the MonthReport bookmark has been inserted in each of these places.
If you perform a mail merge or press F9 while the Ask field is selected, Word displays the prompt. In this example, the user typed August in response to the prompt.
Each of the REF fields is updated with the content of the MonthReport bookmark: in this example, August.
Fill-In field
The Fill-In field prompts you to enter text. Your response is printed in place of the field. 
Note: To insert your response in more than one location, use an Ask field.
Word prompts you for a response each time you update the Fill-In field, such as when you press F9 or step through the records in a mail merge. When you create a new document that is based on a template (a .dotm or .dotx file) and that contains Fill-In fields, Word prompts you for a response at each Fill-In field.
You can use the Fill-In field in a document or as part of a mail merge.
To use the Fill-In field in a document
On the Insert tab, in the Text group, click Quick Parts, and then click Field.

In the Field names list, select Fill-in.
In the Prompt box, type the question you want answered.
If you want a predefined response, select the Default response to prompt check box, and type the text.
If you want the same response to apply to all the records in a mail merge, select the Prompt before merging bookmark text check box. Otherwise, Word will prompt you for a response with each record.
Click OK.
To use the Fill-In field as part of a mail merge
While you are setting up the mail merge, do the following:
On the Mailings tab, in the Write & Insert Fields group, click Rules, and then click Fill-in. 
In the Prompt box, type the question you want answered.
If you want a predefined response, type the response in the Default fill-in text box.
If you want the same response to apply to all the records in the merge, select the Ask once check box. Otherwise, Word will prompt you for a response with each record.
Syntax
When you view the Fill-In field code in your document, the syntax looks like this:
{ FILLIN ["Prompt "] [Optional switches ] }

Note: A field code tells the field what to show. Field results are what is shown in the document after having evaluated the field code. To toggle between viewing the field code and the field code results, press Alt+F9.
Instructions
"Prompt"
Text that is displayed in the dialog box — for example, "Enter the client's name:"
Optional switches
\d "Default"
Specifies a default response if you type nothing in the prompt dialog box. The field { FILLIN "Enter typist's initials:" \d "tds" } inserts "tds" if no response is entered.
If you don't specify a default response, Word uses the last response that was entered. To specify a blank entry as the default, type empty quotation marks after the switch. For example, type \d "".
\o
Prompts just one time during a mail merge instead of each time a new data record is merged. The same response is inserted in each resulting merged document.
Example

1. The document includes a postscript that consists of a Fill-In field. The prompt for the Fill-In field is Type a personal message here.
2. The Fill-In field is updated with the text that the user typed in response to the prompt.
IF field
 
The If field compares two values and then inserts the text appropriate to the result of the comparison. When used in a mail merge main document, the If field can examine information in the merged data records, such as postal codes or account numbers. For example, you can send letters to only those clients located in a particular city.
You can use the If field in a document, or you can use the If field as part of an If-Then-Else rule in a mail merge.
To use the If field in a document, do the following:
On the Insert tab, in the Text group, click Quick Parts, and then click Field.
 
In the Field names list, select If.
 
In the Field codes box, type the expressions, operator, true text, and false text, following the syntax shown above.
 
Click OK.
 
To use the If field as part of a mail merge, do the following while you are setting up the mail merge:
1.On the Mailings tab, in the Write & Insert Fields group, click Rules, and then click If...Then...Else.
 
2.In the Field name list, select the name of a merge field, such as City.
 
3.In the Comparison list, select the operator that you want. For example, to single out recipients in a particular city, select Equal to.
 
4.In the Compare to box, type the value that you want to use. For example, to single out recipients in Tokyo, type Tokyo.
Note: If you selected is blank or is not blank in the Comparison list, leave the Compare to box empty.
 
5.In the Insert this text box, type the text that you want to appear in the document when the condition that you specified is true. For example, to customize the text for recipients in Tokyo, you can type especially for your Tokyo neighborhood.
 
6.In the Otherwise insert this text box, type the text that you want to appear in the document when the condition that you specified is not true. For example, to provide generic text for recipients who are not in Tokyo, you can type especially for your surrounding neighborhood.
 

Syntax
When you view the If field code in your document, the syntax looks like this:
{ IF Expression1OperatorExpression2TrueTextFalseText}
Note: A field code tells the field what to show. Field results are what is shown in the document after having evaluated the field code. To toggle between viewing the field code and the field code results, press Alt+F9.
Instructions
Expression1, Expression2
Values that you want to compare. These expressions can be merge field data, bookmark names, strings of characters, numbers, nested fields that return a value, or mathematical formulas. If an expression contains spaces, enclose the expression in quotation marks.
Notes: 
Expression2 must be enclosed in quotation marks so that it is compared as a character string. 
If the operator is = or <>, Expression2 can contain a question mark (?) to represent any single character or an asterisk (*) to represent any string of characters.
If you use an asterisk in Expression2, the portion of Expression1 that corresponds to the asterisk and any remaining characters in Expression2 cannot exceed 128 characters.
Operator
Comparison operator. Insert a space before and after the operator.
Operator 
Description 
= 
Equal to
<> 
Not equal to
>
Greater than
<
Less than
>=
Greater than or equal to
<=
Less than or equal to
TrueText, FalseText
Text that results when the comparison is true (TrueText) or false (FalseText). If FalseText isn't specified and the comparison is false, the IF field has no result. Each string containing multiple words must be enclosed in quotation marks.
 
Example
The following example specifies that if the customer order is greater than or equal to 100 units, the text "Thanks" appears in the document. If the customer order is fewer than 100 units, the text "The minimum order is 100 units" appears in the document.
{IF order>=100 "Thanks" "The minimum order is 100 units"}

Word tips Keep text together.docx:
Keep text together
You can often improve the look of your document by keeping certain words and paragraphs together on the page or across page breaks. Also, you can use hyphenation to improve overall readability.
Word automatically breaks the text at a space or a hyphen at the end of a line. To keep two words or a hyphenated word together on one line, you can use a nonbreaking space or nonbreaking hyphen instead of a regular space or hyphen.
Click where you want to insert the nonbreaking space.
On the Insert tab, in the Symbols group, click Symbol.

In the box that opens, click More Symbols.

In the Symbol dialog box, on the Special Characters tab, click the Nonbreaking Space row to highlight it, and then click Insert.

Click Close.
Tip: You can also use the keyboard shortcut. Click where you want to insert the nonbreaking space, and press Ctrl+Shift+Spacebar.
Sometimes you want a hyphenated word to stay together on one line, without it breaking across lines. 
Click where you want to insert the nonbreaking hyphen. 
On the Insert tab, in the Symbols group, click Symbol. 

In the box that opens, click More Symbols.

In the Symbol dialog box, on the Special Characters tab, click the Nonbreaking Hyphen row to highlight it, and then click Insert.

Click Close.
Tip:  You can also use the keyboard shortcut. Click where you want to insert the nonbreaking hyphen, and press Ctrl+Shift+Minus Sign.
Word automatically breaks paragraphs at the end of a page, so a paragraph that started on one page continues on to the next page. To keep the whole paragraph on the same page, follow these steps.
Right-click the paragraph that you want to keep together. In the box that opens, select Paragraph.

In the Paragraph dialog box, click the Line and Page Breaks tab.
In the Pagination section, select the Keep lines together check box, and click OK.
If two consecutive paragraphs or a subhead and a paragraph are closely related, you might want to keep them on the same page.
Right-click the paragraph or subhead that you want to keep with the content that follows it. In the box that opens, select Paragraph.

In the Paragraph dialog box, click the Line and Page Breaks tab.
In the Pagination section, select the Keep lines together check box, and click OK.
Tip: It’s best not to add additional line breaks between your paragraphs because Word interprets each line break as a beginning of a new paragraph, and page breaks might not occur properly. If you want spaces between paragraphs, use the Paragraph Spacing controls. For more information, see Change spacing between paragraphs.
If a paragraph has a page break in the middle so that only the last line appears at the top of the following page, this lonely line is called a “widow.” If, on the other hand, a paragraph has a page break in the middle so that only the first line appears at the bottom of a page while the rest of the paragraph appears on the next page, this lonely line is called an “orphan.”
If you want to avoid widow and orphan lines in your document, follow these steps.
Right-click the paragraph in which you want to avoid widows and orphans. In the box that opens, select Paragraph.
Click the Line and page breaks tab.
In the Pagination section, select the Widow/Orphan control check box.
Click OK.

Background
Each vacancy can include a Grade and Salary field. This is generally used to share salary/pay related information when the vacancy is advertised. 
The Pay Scale Band functionality allows for the Grade and Salary to be automatically updated to reflect a salary range, based on the Pay Scale selected, i.e. once the Pay Scale is set on the vacancy e.g. “Grade 1” then the Grade and Salary is automatically updated to the corresponding salary range for that grade e.g. “£25,000 - £35,000”. 
Configuration
Menu Options
The following menu options are required for a user to access the Pay Scale Bands options on the Recruitment Toolbox:
Coreportal Recruitment - Pay Scale Bands Edit
Coreportal Recruitment - Pay Scale Bands View
Both menu options must be added to the relevant menu profile to allow system administrators to view and edit the Pay Scale Bands screen.
Activate Pay Scale Bands
The Pay Scale Bands feature must be switched on in order for the Grade and Salary to be auto-populated based on the configured ranges. Navigate via: 
Administrator Dashboard > Admin Settings
Search for parameter “cp_erc_auto_bands”.
Click on Edit and set Current Value to Y to activate.

Define the Bands for a Pay Scale
Navigate via:
Recruitment > Toolbox > Pay Scale Bands
Once on the Pay Scale Bands screen all active pay scale bands will be displayed.

Adding a new Pay Scale Band
On the Pay Scale Bands screen, click the “Add” button at the top right. A new field will open:

Select the Pay Scale code from the drop down list, or type in (e.g. “03F”):

When a code is selected, the description will default into the Description field:

In the Min Rate and Max Rate fields, enter the minimum salary and the maximum non-discretionary salary for the pay scale:

Set Mid-Point to None.
Click SAVE at the bottom of the screen to save the new Pay Scale Band.

Amending an existing Pay Scale Band
Navigate via:
Recruitment > Toolbox > Pay Scale Bands
Select the pay scale band you wish to edit. Click into the Min Rate and Max Rate fields to amend them as required; then click “Save” at the bottom of the screen to save your changes. 
If updating the Pay Scale Bands after a Pay Uplift, it is recommended to run report PAYSUP02 Non-Discretionary Salary Ranges after the rates have been updated so that rates above the incremental bar are not included in the Pay Scale Band rage. 

Deleting a Pay Scale Band
Select the pay scale band you wish to delete. Click “Remove” to delete it from the screen; then click “Save” at the bottom of the screen to save your changes.

HOW TO - Manually Update the Job Seekers:
Contents
 TOC \o "1-3" \h \z \u 1.Introduction PAGEREF _Toc40447551 \h 1
2.Adding an employee PAGEREF _Toc40447552 \h 1

Introduction

CoreHR have a piece of functionality called the Job Seekers Register (“JSR”), which can be used to identify employees whose contracts are ending and who should be considered for redeployment within their companies. 

The JSR is, in essence, just a register – adding an employee’s contract to it does not automate any kind of employment processes. However, the existence of a central register of “job seekers” may support the Senior Appointments team’s with the Priority Candidate Support Scheme (“PCSS”). 

There are two ways to use the JSR:

Automatically – system rules can be configured to automatically identify employee contracts which are due to end and add them to the JSR.** 
Manually – a flag called “JSR Override” can be used to manually add an employee’s contracts to and remove them from the JSR. 

**The automatic process requires a lot of careful thought about what types of contracts should be considered “eligible” for addition to the JSR. Rules can be configured based on organisational hierarchy and appointment details – e.g. all fixed-term contracts at Standard Grade 7 within a given department, or all contracts of any kind on the Marie Curie Student pay grade. These rules must be configured and thoroughly tested to ensure that they are working as desired. In the interests of speed, the Senior Appointments Team have opted not to adopt the automatic JSR process at this time. 

The manual process for using the JSR is outlined below. 

Adding an employee’s contract to the JSR

NB: The JSR functionality exists within CoreHR’s back-office. To access it, you must launch the back-office from CorePortal.
Navigate to: CorePersonnel > Employee Search > Person Profile
On the Employee Search screen, enter the name or personnel number of the employee you wish to add to the JSR. Double-click their record to enter the Person Profile screen. 

In the upper right corner of the screen, go to the Select Detail menu and choose the option “Job Seekers”: 

You will be taken to the Job Seekers Register screen. 

NB: This is not the JSR itself, it’s just the area where you can add/remove a single employee.
In the lower half of the screen, you will see a list of the employee’s current appointments. Two fields are of interest here (circled in red):

JSR – this flag indicates whether the contract is already on the Job Seekers Register. It will be ticked once the record has been added by the overnight database job. This flag cannot be updated by users; it is a system-only flag. 
JSR Override – This field determines whether the automatic or manual process will be used to add a contract to the JSR. 
JSR Override has three options: 
Calculate – use the eligibility rules configured in the system to determine whether the contract in question is eligible to be added to the JSR. 
Yes – add the contract to the JSR manually, ignoring any eligibility criteria which may exist in the system.
No – never add the contract to the JSR, regardless of whether it meets any eligibility criteria. 
To add a contract to the JSR, change the JSR Override field to “Yes”.

A warning message will appear. Click “Yes” to dismiss it:

Save your changes. 
An overnight process (PERS_JOB_SEEKERS_REGISTER_PROC.PROCESS_J) will run in CoreHR, which will pick up the record you have amended and added it to the JSR. 
The following day, if you return to the employee record, you will see the JSR flag is now ticked:

Removing an employee’s contract
If, for whatever reason, an employee no longer needs to be on the Job Seekers Register, it’s simple to remove them. 
Navigate to: CorePersonnel > Employee Search > Person Profile
Go back to the employee record and choose “Job Seekers” from the Select Detail menu. On the Job Seekers Register screen, change the JSR Override field from “Yes” to “Calculate”:

The warning message will appear asking you to confirm you wish to make this change. Click “Yes” and save your changes. The overnight database job will run again and remove the employee contract from the JSR. 
The following day, if you return to the employee record, you will see the JSR flag is no longer ticked.

1. Overview  
1.1. Purpose of the Guide 
This document outlines how to use and manage the Applicant side of PeopleXD Recruitment. It 
provides guidance on the Applicant Details that are created as part of an applicant’s registration 
and application process on the Careers Website. 
 
This guide includes how to navigate and use the dashboards and widgets available to PeopleXD 
users for the Recruitment product. 
 
 
 
  
 Note:  This guide does not include: 
• Steps on how to create a Vacancy within the Recruitment platform. 
• Steps on how to manage the Careers Website.

2. Applicant Detail  
2.1. Applicant Detail 
2.1.1. Overview  
Once a vacancy has been created, you are able to view applicants that have applied for the vacancy 
or manually add an applicant to the vacancy (bypassing applications  from the Careers Website ). 
The applicant record on PeopleXD Recruitment holds the following details: 
 
• Applicant’s personal detail • Vacancy & Application Detail 
• Correspondence • References 
• Events • Documents 
• Diversity Details • Other Information (User Defined 
Fields) 
 
 
 
2.1.2. Creating an Applicant Manually  
There is an option for you to create an applicant manually on behalf of a user that may not have 
the access to login to PeopleXD as an internal applicant or register as an external applicant via the 
recruitment website.  
 
To do this: 
1. Navigate to the Recruitment dashboard. 
2. Navigate to the Applicants widget on the Applicants tab. 
3. Click Add Applicant. 
 
 Note: Access to the Applicant Details is controlled by menu options. For detail on how to 
configure these screens and menu options, see the XD Recruitment: Configuration Guide.

6. Applicant Right To Be Forgotten Requests  
6.1. Overview 
GDPR gives individuals the right to ask organisations to delete their personal data. In the 
scenario where a candidate has registered on an organisation’s website e.g. Careers Portal, or 
has submitted an application but been unsuccessful, they may request the right to be forgotten.  
The Right To Be Forgotten feature in PeopleXD Recruitment allows users to action this request by 
deleting any candidate information retained with PeopleXD. 
 
6.2. Process Candidate Right to be Forgotten Requests 
To process a request, follow the below steps:  
1. Navigate to the My Recruit Toolbox widget on the Recruitment Dashboard. 
2. Click Open on Right To Be Forgotten. 
3. Search for the applicant to be deleted using their name, applicant number, or email 
address. Alternatively, click OK to view all available candidates. 
 
4. Click Delete on the relevant row. 
5. Click Yes to confirm the deletion. 
 

XD Recruitment: Applicant Management - User Guide            
Access Limited Distribution Page 35 of 35 
 
 
6.3. What Candidate Data is Deleted 
The following are all deleted when a Right to be Forgotten request has been processed:  
• All Candidate Data held within the PeopleXD ATS i.e. Portal View of PeopleXD Recruitment 
• Generated PDF View of Candidate Application 
• Candidate Data held within eRecruitment website 
 
The following candidate data is not deleted:  
• Candidate Data held within the new Careers Website (powered by Volcanic). However, 
customers have a self-serve facility to delete this data.  
• Merged PDF Packs of Candidates (multiple candidates merged into the one PDF 
document). These merged documents can be deleted manually by users, or as part of a 
process when closing the vacancy. These documents can also be deleted as part of the 
automated Applicant Cleardown process subject to the vacancy and candidate being 
eligible for cleardown. See the user guide for further information.
