Introduction

There is a piece of functionality within PeopleXD called the Job Seekers Register (“JSR”), which can be used to identify employees whose contracts are ending and who should be considered for redeployment within their companies. 

The JSR is, in essence, just a register – adding an employee’s contract to it does not automate any kind of employment processes. However, the existence of a central register of “job seekers” may support the Senior Appointments team’s with the Priority Candidate Support Scheme (“PCSS”). 

There are two ways to use the JSR:

Automatically – system rules can be configured to automatically identify employee contracts which are due to end and add them to the JSR.** 
Manually – a flag called “JSR Override” can be used to manually add an employee’s contracts to and remove them from the JSR. 

**The automatic process requires a lot of careful thought about what types of contracts should be considered “eligible” for addition to the JSR. Rules can be configured based on organisational hierarchy and appointment details – e.g. all fixed-term contracts at Standard Grade 7 within a given department, or all contracts of any kind on the Marie Curie Student pay grade. These rules must be configured and thoroughly tested to ensure that they are working as desired. In the interests of speed, the Senior Appointments Team have opted not to adopt the automatic JSR process at this time. 

The manual process for using the JSR is outlined below. 

Adding an employee’s contract to the JSR
Navigate to: People Management > Employees > View > Key Information > Job Seekers Register
On the Employee Search screen, enter the name or personnel number of the employee you wish to add to the JSR. Click “View” to open the record: 

On the Key Information tab, click the button for “Job Seekers Register” at the bottom of the screen:

You will be taken to the Job Seekers Register screen. 

NB: This is not the JSR itself, it’s just the area where you can add/remove a single employee.
In the lower half of the screen, you will see a list of the employee’s current appointments. Two fields are of interest here (circled in red):

JSR – this flag indicates whether the contract is already on the Job Seekers Register. It will be ticked once the record has been added by the overnight database job. This flag cannot be updated by users; it is a system-only flag. 
JSR Override – This field determines whether the automatic or manual process will be used to add a contract to the JSR. 
JSR Override has three options: 
Calculate – use the eligibility rules configured in the system to determine whether the contract in question is eligible to be added to the JSR. 
Yes – add the contract to the JSR manually, ignoring any eligibility criteria which may exist in the system.
No – never add the contract to the JSR, regardless of whether it meets any eligibility criteria. 
To add a contract to the JSR, change the JSR Override field to “Yes”.

A warning message will appear. Click “Yes” to dismiss it:

Your changes will be saved automatically. 
A process in PeopleXD (PERS_JOB_SEEKERS_REGISTER_PROC.PROCESS_J) will run overnight to pick up the record you have amended and add it to the JSR. 

The following day, if you return to the employee record, you will see the JSR flag is now ticked:

Removing an employee’s contract from the JSR
If, for whatever reason, an employee no longer needs to be on the Job Seekers Register, it’s simple to remove them. 
Navigate to: People Management > Employees > View > Key Information > Job Seekers Register
Go back to the employee record and choose “Job Seekers Register” from the Key Information tab. On the Job Seekers Register screen, change the JSR Override field from “Yes” to “Calculate”:

The warning message will appear asking you to confirm you wish to make this change. Click “Yes” and save your changes. The overnight database job will run again and remove the employee contract from the JSR. 
The following day, if you return to the employee record, you will see the JSR flag is no longer ticked.

Process steps
Preparation

Create a new folder under P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Applicant Clear down\Annual clear down and name it to show the year being cleared e.g 2010/11.

Open the bulk applicant clear down checklist and save a copy in the folder you have created adding the same dates to the file name.

Running the report
In Discoverer run report RECEUP01_Bulk applicant clear down control and enter the relevant parameters:

Date FROM = 1 Aug 20xx
Date TO = 31 Jul 20xx

Do not enter anything into the remaining fields.

 

NB: the clear down process does not include the date entered in the End Date field in the clear down applicants screen. However when running the Discoverer report the date entered in the Status date TO: field is included. 

Export the entire workbook into the folder you have created.

Pivot the data from the Applicant Detail per Vacancy tab as follows:

Rows:
Applicant status
Applicant status description

Data:
Count of Applicant status

If required edit the pivot table to remove the sub totals.

In column D add a sum to show the number of pages that will be returned in the preview report. (Total by status/38)
Clearing down by applicant status

Before you begin you must discuss and agree timescales with the Head of HRIS.
Navigate to Recruitment>Recruitment Maintenance>Applicant Clear Down

The ‘Clear Down Applicants’ window opens:

Enter date range

Start date = 1 Aug 20xx
End date = 1 Aug 20xx

NB: The clear down process does not include the date entered in the End Date field. Therefore to include applicants with a status date of 31 July in a particular year you need to enter 1 Aug for that year in the End Date field.

NB: Once a date range has been entered it will remain on the screen until you red door back to the main menu.

Enter applicant status (code) in the Applicant Status field or select from the LoV, ensuring your cursor is in the Applicant Status field.

To preview the list of applicants that meet the selection criteria, ensure the Mode Indicator is set to ‘Preview’ and click on .

The preview report will open in a new window (sorted in first name order):

NB: there is no applicant count or total on this report so if there are multiple pages there is no easy way of checking the number matches the report. Refer to the pivot table you created to see the approx. number of pages

To close the preview report, close the viewing tab/window.

 
To clear down applicants that meet your selection criteria, change the Mode Indicator to ‘Update’ and click on again. A warning message will appear: 

Click OK. 

A new report will open in a new window (sorted in first name order) confirming the records that have been cleared down:

NB: If there are no applicants for your chosen status, a blank report will open.

Repeat steps 3.3 to 3.6 for each applicant status.

Post clear down checks
Once the clear down process is completed you should carry out a few simple checks.

Re-run Discoverer report ‘Bulk applicant clear down control’ for date range and check that nothing is returned.

NB: If anything is returned in the report, export it to the folder for the year being cleared and investigate further. 

View a sample of applicants (Approx. 10) from the Applicant Detail per Vacancy tab in the exported report.

Review 1% of vacancies from the Applicant summary by vacancy tab in the exported report where the value in the ‘difference’ column is 0. Check that there are no applicants remaining on the vacancy.

Review 1% of vacancies from the Applicant summary by vacancy tab in the exported report where the value in the ‘difference’ column is greater than 0. Check that the number of applicants remaining matches the number of applicants in the difference column.

Removing the merged PDF packs

NB: This needs to be completed by CoreHR.

Copy the list of vacancies (column A) from the Applicant summary by vacancy tab in the original report and paste into a blank worksheet. Save the new file in the folder you created with the file name ‘List of vacancies for Core to delete merged pack’. (NB: All vacancies should be included even if some applicants remain.)

Raise a case with CoreHR and attach the list of vacancies to the case. 

Enter the case number and date submitted on the checklist.

Once CoreHR confirm that they have deleted all of the merged PDF packs, note the date on the checklist.

Deleting an applicant account from the applicant portal where no applications have been submitted

Restrictions
There is a limit to what we are able to clear down. Applications must be retained for a period of six months after an appointment has been confirmed or it has been confirmed that no appointment has been/will be made for that vacancy. These timescales have been confirmed by Anne Harkness.

If an application cannot be cleared down because it is less than six months from the final status date of the vacancy the HRIS Support Centre have a standard email to send to the applicant. For further details refer to the related Knowledge Article.

Process steps

Check vacancies applied for

Navigate to Recruitment > Recruitment Enquiries > Applicant Detail

For each vacancy that the applicant has applied for you must check that all applicant statuses are in a “final state” (i.e. one of the ‘Rejected’ statuses, one of the ‘Successful’ statuses or ‘Offer Refused ‘, ‘Withdrawn’, ‘Standby’ etc) and that the date of the final applicant status is at least 6 months prior to today’s date. 

The only exception to this is if the vacancy is in TSS. In this case you must check that the status for the applicant you are clearing down is at least 6 months before today’s date.

Search for and open the applicant record.

Click on Vacancy Detail from the select detail menu. 

The Applicant Maintenance window opens: 

Make a note of the all the vacancies that the individual has applied for.

Navigate to Recruitment > Recruitment Enquiries > Vacancy Detail

Go the Applicant Status screen and check the status of ALL applicants on each vacancy (excluding TSS vacancies).
If any of the applicants have a status that is not a “final” status (e.g. ‘Applied’, ‘Shortlisted’, ‘Invited to Interview 1’, ‘Offer Made’, ‘Preferred Candidate’, ‘Request References’ etc) go to section 4:

If ALL applicants have one of the following statuses, ‘Rejected’ statuses, one of the ‘Successful’ statuses or ‘Offer Refused ‘, ‘Withdrawn’, ‘Standby’ etc. continue to section 2. 

Updating the applicant status

Navigate to Recruitment > Recruitment Maintenance > Vacancy Detail

In order to be able to run the clear down process you first need to change the applicant status to ‘Z-HRIS Support Centre Use Only’. 

You must also delete the merged pack on each vacancy as it will contain the application submitted by the applicant you are clearing down.

For each vacancy that the applicant has applied for, follow the steps below:

Open the vacancy and go to the Applicant status screen. 

Check the latest “status date” of all applicants. 

If the latest applicant status date is less than six months ago, make a diary note to revisit the vacancy after 6 months have elapsed. 

If the latest applicant status date is more than six months ago, continue from step 2.3 onwards.

Click on the Applicant ID or Name to select the applicant you want to update. 

From the drop down list under ‘Applicant status’ choose “Z-HRIS Support Centre Use Only” and SAVE.
 

The Applicant Status and Status Date are now updated. Click on the Generate Applications button. The ‘Generate Applications’ window opens:

Click on the Delete Merged Application button.

Clearing down the applicant record(s)

Once the steps in Section 2 have been completed for all applicable vacancies, navigate to: 

Recruitment > Recruitment Maintenance > Applicant Clear Down

Enter the date/s that you changed the Applicant Status(es) into the Start Date and End Date fields. 

NB: if you made the changes over two or more days, enter the earliest date into the Start Date field and the latest date in the End Date field.

Enter/select ZSUP in the “Applicant Status” field:

Ensure that the Mode Indicator is set to Preview and click the “Submit Clear Down Applicants Report” button.

The Preview report will open in a new window showing the applicant(s) that will be cleared down and the vacancy ID/s. Note that the Mode of Operation = Preview

Check that the correct applicant(s) and vacancy(ies) are returned in the report.

If the expected details are shown in the report, change the mode indicator to Update and click the Submit Clear Down Applicants Report button.

A new report will open in a new window showing the applicant records that have been cleared down. Note that the Mode of Operation = Update:

Vacancies where the applicant statuses are not complete

If the applicant statuses on any of the vacancies are not complete the HRIS Support Centre will need to contact the recruiting Department(s). 

NB: If the applicant statuses on any of the vacancies are not complete the HRIS Support Centre will need to contact the Department(s). 

If the recruitment process is complete, the department(s) must update the applicant statuses for the vacancy(ies) to their final statuses as defined in section 1.4. 

If the department confirms that the recruitment process is still underway for the vacancy(ies) you will need to wait until the applicant statuses have all been update to a final statuses as defined in section 1.4. 

NB: In both cases you must wait for six months after the final “status date” to remove the application for that vacancy.

Clearing an applicant portal account where no applications have been submitted.

It is not currently possible to clear down an applicant account in the Portal if they have not submitted any applications. We have raised this with Core but they also are unable to action this.
A workaround has therefore been agreed that the 1st line support centre will carry out.

Background
The PAYDEP01 Payroll Costings Report is run each month after the final monthly payroll run. It returns the complete pay history for all active staff (casuals and employees) in a given payroll period, e.g. January 2023. We share this data with departments so that they can check their monthly costings. 

PAYDEP01 is a large dataset and can easily run to more than 140,000 rows of data. Before we share it with departments, we must “condense” the data into as few rows as possible. To do this, we use a tool called the Payroll Condenser. This is a macro-enabled Excel spreadsheet which condenses the raw data from PAYDEP01 so that there is one only row of data per Employee + Appointment ID + Pay Element combination.

How it works
There are two types of transaction recorded in the PAYDEP01 Payroll Costings Report:

Elements the University pays to the employee directly (salaries, allowances, hourly rates for casual workers).
Elements the University pays to other parties which form part of the total cost of employment (National Insurance, the apprentice levy, and any employer contributions to pensions). 

The Payroll Condenser looks at all the Elements attached to Employee “ABC” + Appointment ID “123” and condenses the lines for EMPLOYERS NI, APPRENTICE LEVY and any Employer Pension contributions into the lines for salaries & allowances.

Payroll Condenser Errors
The final step in the Payroll Condenser process involves an automatic comparison of the Original payroll data to the Condensed data, to check that the values match between both datasets. The results of this automatic comparison are output to a worksheet called Final Check Figures. If there are any mismatches in the data, they will appear as errors in the Final Check Figures worksheet:

The total number of error records is shown in the lower half of the worksheet:

You will need to fix these errors before the Condensed payroll data can be forwarded on to departments. 

Identifying Error Records
Begin by identifying the error records, as outlined below. 

Unhide EmployeeCheck sheet
Right-click on any worksheet and select “Unhide…”. In the pop-up window, unhide the EmployeeCheck sheet:

Check the “Difference” columns
Within the EmployeeCheck sheet, you will see a list of personnel numbers alongside columns comparing the Original data to the Condensed data for each personnel record. There is a “Difference” column beside each comparison:

Apply a filter to the worksheet and filter the first “Difference” column (next to the “Gross Original” and “Gross Condensed columns) for non-zero values by unticking the “0” value: 

The non-zero values in the “Difference” columns indicate mismatches between the Original and Condensed data. The personnel numbers in your filtered dataset are the error records you need to correct.

Preparing the Data
Get the Condensed data
Once you’ve got the error records in the EmployeeCheck worksheet, go to the Condensed worksheet and search for the first personnel number in your list of error records. The Condensed payroll costings data for that employee will be displayed, grouped by Appointment ID. In the example below, the employee only has one row appearing in the Condensed worksheet: 

According to the EmployeeCheck worksheet, the Condensed data doesn’t 
match what’s in the Original Data worksheet, so you must get the Original data in order to do a comparison. 

Copy the Original data
Go to the Original Data worksheet and search for the same personnel number. The Original payroll costings data for that employee will be displayed, grouped by Appointment ID. In the example below, the employee has six rows appearing in the Original Data worksheet:

Select the rows and enter CTRL+C to copy them. Be sure to select every column from A (Tax Year) to AH (Total by Cost Centre). 
Paste the Original data below the Condensed data
Go back to the Condensed worksheet (which should still be filtered for the error record you’re investigating). Enter CTRL+V to paste the Original data rows into the worksheet, below the Condensed data rows:

NB: always leave a blank row or two between the Condensed data (at the top) and the Original data (beneath). This will ensure that you don’t confuse the two sets of records!

Fixing Error Records
You are now ready to do a visual comparison of the Condensed data to the Original data for each error record, to see where the mismatch has occurred. 

Generally speaking, errors occur because the Payroll Condenser has “skipped” records when condensing the payroll data for an employee. You must therefore check whether the Condensed data rows contain the same information as the Original data rows in the following columns:
Appointment ID
The Original data may contain more Appointment IDs than the Condensed data. If this is the case, you’ll need to add the rows for the missing Appointment IDs to the Condensed data to resolve the error. 

Element
The Original data may contain more pay elements than the Condensed data. If this is the case, you’ll need to add the rows for the missing Elements to the Condensed data to resolve the error. 
 
Check for missing Appointment IDs
Compare your Original and Condensed data. Are there any Appointment ID values in your Original data that don’t appear in your Condensed data? 
Example 1: no errors. The same Appointment ID appears in both Condensed data (above) and Original data (below). If this is the case for your current record, move on to check for missing Elements. 

Example 2: errors. There is an appointment ID present in the Original data (below) which is missing from the Condensed data (above). If this is the case for your current record, continue to follow the process below. 

Prepare the Original data
In your copy-pasted rows of Original data, remove any non-error rows – you only want to keep the rows for the missing Appointment ID:

Condense the data

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
The Reward Team and HR Analytics Team are responsible for producing and confirming the rates for existing grades. Requests for the creation of any new grades should be raised through these teams, or via the HRSEG on which these teams are represented.

To set up a new grade, the following items must be confirmed by the Reward and HR Analytics Teams:

Grade Code (e.g. 02S)
Grade Description (e.g. STANDARD GRADE 2)
The number of Scale Points on the grade (e.g. 9)
The full Scale Narrative of each point on the scale (e.g. POINT 1 NSP6)
Any Bar Points on the scale (e.g. points 7-9 are discretionary points)
The Yearly Full Time Rates (e.g. Point 1 - £15,765.00)
The Full Time Hours for the grade (e.g. 36.5)
Whether the grade should be available to select on new Staff Requests
Whether the grade will be subject to Cost of Living awards
The Effective Date of the new grade (likely to be the normal pay uplift date for the grade – e.g. 01-Aug-2021)

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?
Requests for new grades and changes to existing grades should come from and be discussed with the Reward, HR Analytics, and Payroll teams. Grade-related requests will usually be discussed and agreed at HRSEG (Human Resources Systems Evaluation Group). However, if the changes requested must be implemented urgently, they may be agreed by another means e.g. email.

New Grades
Pensions should be consulted, as they will need to confirm which Pension Scheme should be assigned to the new grade. 

Payroll should be consulted, as they will need to if they want to publish the grade to the web (see the Affected Reports section below).

The X5 team will need to be informed of the new grade as soon as possible, so that they can check whether any staff who will be on the grade are likely to be involved in research – if so, the new grade will need to be set up in X5 by their system support team. (X5 provides administrators and principal investigators (PIs) with a tool for costing research grant applications.) 

Changes to existing grades or rates
Changes to existing grades or rates may result in employee records being updated, e.g. where a scale point is being removed. The HR Analytics team should therefore be consulted as the changes to employee records may need to be undertaken by the Data Service Team. The X5 team have asked for as much notice as possible in terms of rate changes. Ideally when these are being tested in the non-prod environment but certainly ahead of the update into production. 

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 
The change process applicable at the time of the change should be followed. The current process is to create a change request in OSM which is approved by the relevant approver. Ideally, the change should be approved prior to being put into QA testing. 

The HRIS Functional Analysis Team are responsible for setting up new grades & points and amending existing grades & points. 

If a new grade is being created and the Full Time Hours value for the grade is not present in the list of ‘FTE Hours’ in the database, a new value will need to be created. This can either be done via a separate change or added as a separate element to the current change. For information on how to add a new FTE Hours value, refer to the document How To – View and Maintain Reference Data.

Note that, in some cases, it may be necessary to move employees onto a new grade or point. For example, the lowest scale point (4) was removed from Apprentice Grade 01A in Feb 2018 as it fell below the minimum Living Wage. Employees who were appointed to this grade/scale therefore needed to be moved onto the next highest scale point (5).

Changes to employee records are usually carried out by the HRIS Data Service Administrator. In this case it may be necessary to contact the individual departments to notify them about/discuss the proposed changes.

Expense Codes Background
Expense Codes are used to summarise transactions into groups of expenses/costs and liabilities, so they can be posted GL in the form of Debits and Credits. The following points should be taken into consideration regarding Expense Codes:
An Expense Code is not associated with an employee. Its possible to have a different expense Code for every element of pay an employee receives. 
Expense Codes are used in conjunction with the Cost Centres, i.e. one Expense Code may be used in many different Cost Centres.
The Expense Code is normally derived based on the type of employee and the type of pat that the employee receives.
An Expense Code is an 8-digit number field. Data mapping can be used to ensure the Expense Code output by PeopleXD matches the Expense Code in the Financial Management System (FMS).
The requirement for a new Expense Code would ordinarily be made via the Payroll Operations Manager and usually combined with a new Pay Code/Allowance request. The Expense Code once setup would be added to the Pay Code on the third tab titled General Ledger and should only be input if provided by Payroll, otherwise left blank. For further information about Pay Codes refer to the “How To Manage Pay Codes in the Portal” guidance at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\How to guides. 
View existing Expense Codes
To view existing Expense Codes, navigate via:
People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Expense Codes

Create new Expense Codes
Expense Codes are not interfaced into PeopleXD from the FMS so there is a requirement to manually create new codes when requested by the Payroll Operations Manager
Navigate to People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Expense Codes
The Expense Codes screen opens:

To add a new Expense Code, click on Add.
Enter the Expense Code - This will be the new Expense Code provided by Payroll.
Enter a Description for the Expense Code as provided by Payroll.
Ensure the Active indicator updates automatically. 
Click Save. 

Expense Codes can also be created via the Payroll Dashboard in the same way, navigating to Payroll Dashboard > Settings > General Ledger Costing > Expense GL Codes

Data Talk
Mapped values may be added to the Journal File definition. This is used when the Reference Data item within the FMS does not match the Reference Data item within PeopleXD. An example of this is where the GL/Account codes in the FMS are alphanumeric, whereas the expense Codes in PeopleXD are numeric.
The below steps are used to map elements from the Journal File for output to the FMS.
Navigate to Payroll Dashboard > Settings > General Ledger Costings > General Rules & Settings
The Maintain GL Parameters screen opens.

On the Employee Self Service landing page the next Pay Day is displayed under ‘Important Dates’. This relies on Payroll calendars held in the Portal for each pay group paid through the Payroll module. 

In December each year new calendars must be created for the following year. It is not possible to overwrite an existing calendar with dates for the following year so new calendars must be created. It now seems to be possible to have more than one calendar for each pay group.

Depending on when Pay Day falls in December there are two options for updating the calendars.

Option 1 - (Recommended to give you time to create the new calendars for the forthcoming year.) 
In December create a new calendar for each pay group for the following year and add the January pay date only following the steps in Section 1 - Creating a new calendar.

In January, before the January Pay Date, update the calendars for the whole year following the steps in Section 2 – Editing an existing Calendar. 

You can then delete the calendars for the previous year following the steps in Section 3 - Deleting a Calendar.

Option 2 – The day after December’s pay day, create new calendars for the forthcoming year following the steps in Section 1 - Creating a new calendar, then delete the calendars for the outgoing year following the steps in Section 3 - Deleting a Calendar. NB: The Next Pay Date section in the Portal will be blank until the new calendars have been created.

Background

The External Users widget is a widget within the CorePortal Security Dashboard. Enabling this widget will allow us to create Portal accounts for users who do not have an employee record in CoreHR. Specifically, it will allow us to provide members of the Access Group with Portal accounts, so that they can provide better support to the University with incidents, problems and projects.

Enabling the External Users widget
Navigate to: CorePortal > Security > Menu Profiles
From the Search bar at the top of the screen, navigate to the Security dashboard, and select the Menu Profiles tab from the sidebar menu: 

Search for the menu profile “COREPORTAL_SUPPORT”. When it appears, click the three dots on the right and select “Manage Menu Options”:

The Menu Options screen will open. Search for keyword “External” and enable the following options:
Create External
Delete External
External User Creation
Get External

Changes are saved automatically. 

Creating an External User

Navigate to: CorePortal > Security > User Management

From the Search bar at the top of the screen, navigate to the Security dashboard, and select the User Management tab from the sidebar menu. Scroll down the screen to the External Users widget and click “Create External User”:

The Add External User window will pop up. Complete all the fields provided, and note that you will have choose the username and password yourself.

NB: The Access Group (previously CoreHR) have historically had usernames prefixed with “C##”, so maintain this naming convention for any external accounts you create for Access Group representatives. 

Click “OK” to save your changes. The newly-created user will appear in the External Users widget:

Managing an External User
Navigate to: CorePortal > Security > User Management

From the Search bar at the top of the screen, navigate to the Security dashboard, and select the User Management tab from the sidebar menu. Scroll down the screen to the System Users widget and search for the username of the external user you wish to manage:

NB: External users are automatically granted employee numbers linked to their usernames. External user employee records are all prefixed with “EXT”, as in the image above (EXT00000001, EXT00000002, etc.). If you know your external user’s EXT number, you can search for that instead of the username.
Select the user record and click the three dots on the right to open the sub-menu. Select “Manage Account”:

The Manage Portal Account screen will open. Here, the external user account can be managed in the same way as any other Portal account. 

Set Authentication Type
Select the General tab from the sidebar menu. Under the Security heading, click Authentication Type and select “LDAP - Active Directory Authentication” from the drop-down menu. This will allow the external user to access CorePortal via the SSO WebAuth login screen:

Assign Menu Profiles
Select the Menu Security tab from the sidebar menu. A list of available menu profiles will appear. You can search for a specific profile, or choose to see only Active or Inactive profiles using the drop-down list next to the Search box:

To assign a menu profile to a user, or to remove a menu profile which is currently assigned to a user, simply toggle the Active indicator on the profile record. An active profile has a blue indicator, while an inactive profile has a pale white indicator:

Your changes will be saved automatically and a message will appear on the screen confirming this:

Deleting an External User

Navigate to: CorePortal > Security > User Management

From the Search bar at the top of the screen, navigate to the Security dashboard, and select the User Management tab from the sidebar menu. Scroll down the screen to the External Users widget. 
Select the external user you wish to delete and click the three dots on the right to open the sub-menu. Select “Drop/Delete Account”:

A warning message will appear. If you are certain you wish to delete the account, click “Yes”:

The screen will refresh and the external user will disappear from the External Users widget. Their username and EXT number have both now been deleted from the database.

IMPORTANT READ THIS FIRST

Your upload file must contain all of the columns shown on the template document even if they contain no data. The upload template will include a column for each possible data item so for a UDF, 12 fields can be added so there will be 12 columns in addition to the required fields.

Once you have save your upload file as a .CSV, DO NOT SAVE again when exiting as the formatting you have just completed will change back to the defaults.

Date format – Date formats are not always translated into the required format for the field they are being uploaded to. E.g in a UDF the Date From field will appear in the correct format DD-MMM-YYYY but any dates contained within the body of a UDF will not. You must therefore format these dates in the upload file first.

Preparing the data to upload

Navigate to : CorePortal > Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration

In the Data Migration Templates Widget search for the relevant template. 

Click on the Ellipses against the file you need. Download the Template AND the Helper.

The template shows the fields required, format and other related information. 

The example below is from the template for a UDF:

Format your file so that the columns correspond to the template and all fields are formatted as text (ensuring dates include the 0 at the beginning e.g. 01 not 1).

From within your upload file, open the template file. In step 1 of the import wizard, choose Delimited (default) and tick if your data has headers. Click NEXT.

In step 2 of the wizard leave Tab selected then select either Comma or Other – and enter a pipe (|) as applicable. Click NEXT.

In step 3 keep the default settings and click FINISH.

A blank file will open (the example below is for uploading UDF data). Copy and paste your data into this file (with or without the header row as applicable).

You may find it helpful to apply a colour to the columns that will be uploaded, especially if you have blanks columns at the end of your data that will be included in the upload.

Save as a CSV (comma delimited) file. 

Open your file in NOTEPAD++ to check that the formatting has been preserved and that there are no odd characters or errors before you attempt to upload it.

Uploading the data

Navigate to : CorePortal > Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration

In the Data Migration Options widget click on LOAD FILE.

Browse to find your file then click OK. 

Wait for the progress bar to stop and (Upload Complete) to appear. Click OK. 

Your file now appears in the list with the status READY

Click on the ellipses and choose Edit to review the records. 

Check that the data looks as expected. 

If required you can process a single record to check the details: 

Click on any row, the PROCESS RECORD button will appear. Click to process the chosen record.

To update all records click on PROCESS ALL RECORDS. 

NB: The status will show as PROCESSING until all records have been updated.

When the file has been fully processed the status will show COMPLETE.

If the file has failed validation the status will shows FAILED. The number of records failed will show in the File Summary column.

Click on the ellipses and choose Edit to view the failed records.

Correct your file as required and follow steps 1 to 8 again.

Quick steps for preparing and uploading a file

Check that the data on the upload file matches the upload template
From within the file to be uploaded, open the Core upload file
Copy and paste the data into the new file
Update any dates to the correct format. NB the TO/FROM date format in UDFs is not the same as other date fields.
Save as a .csv file and Close without saving
Open Notepad ++ and open the csv file you just saved.
Check the formatting, spacing and date format.
Remove special characters such as ; : 
Upload the .csv file in the Data Migration tool

HOW TO - Add a Formatting Switch to a Fi:
Add a formatting switch to a field code 
Right-click the field, and then click Edit Field.
Do one of the following: 
If Field properties and Field options are displayed, select the formatting options that you want. 
If only the field code is displayed, click Options, and then select the formatting options that you want. 
If the Options button appears dimmed, additional formatting options may not be available.
You can use three formatting switches to format field results: 
Format switch (\*) 
Numeric format switch (\#) 
Date-Time format switch (\@) 

Format switch(\*) 
The Format field switch (\*) defines how to display field results. The format instructions determine the following: 
The use of uppercase and lowercase letters
Number formats — for example, whether 9 is displayed as ix (roman numerals) or ninth (ordinal text)
character formats
Format switches also retain a field result's formatting when the field is updated.
Capitalization formats: 
The following is a list of switches and the items that they capitalize:
\* Caps    This switch capitalizes the first letter of each word. For example, { FILLIN "Type your name:" \* Caps } displays Luis Alverca even if the name is typed in lowercase letters.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click Title case.
\* FirstCap    This switch capitalizes the first letter of the first word. For example, { COMMENTS \* FirstCap } displays Weekly report on sales.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click First capital.
\* Upper    This switch capitalizes all letters. For example, { QUOTE "word" \* Upper } displays WORD.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click Uppercase.
\* Lower    This switch capitalizes none of the result; all letters are lowercase. For example, { FILENAME \* Lower } displays weekly sales report.doc. 
This switch has no effect if the entire field that contains the switch is formatted as small capital letters.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click Lowercase.
Number formats: 
The following is a list of number switches and their results:
\*alphabetic    This switch displays results as alphabetic characters. The result has the same case as the word "alphabetic" in the field code. For example, { SEQ appendix \* ALPHABETIC } displays B (instead of 2), and { SEQ appendix \* alphabetic } displays b.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click a, b, c,.
\*Arabic    This switch displays results as Arabic cardinal numerals. For example, { PAGE \* Arabic } displays 31.
Notes: 
If the Number format setting in the Page Number Format dialog box is not Arabic, this switch overrides the Number format setting.
For page numbers only, there is also an ArabicDash format, which displays results as Arabic cardinal numbers surrounded by hyphen characters. For example, { PAGE \* ArabicDash } displays - 31 -.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click 1, 2, ,3, ....
\*CardText    This switch displays results as cardinal text. The result is formatted in lowercase letters unless you add a format switch to specify a different capitalization. For example, { = SUM(A1:B2) \* CardText } displays seven hundred ninety, and { = SUM(A1:B2) \* CardText \* Caps } displays Seven Hundred Ninety.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click One, Two, Three.
\*DollarText    This switch displays results as cardinal text. Word inserts and at the decimal place and displays the first two decimals (rounded) as Arabic numerators over 100. The result is formatted in lowercase letters unless you add a format switch to specify a different capitalization. For example, { = 9.20 + 5.35 \* DollarText \* Upper } displays FOURTEEN AND 55/100.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click Dollar Text.
\*Hex    This switch displays results as hexadecimal numbers. For example, { QUOTE "458" \* Hex } displays 1CA.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click hex ....
\*OrdText    This switch displays results as ordinal text. The result is formatted in lowercase letters unless you add a format switch to specify a different capitalization. For example, { DATE \@ "d" \* OrdText } displays twenty-first, and { DATE \@ "d" \* OrdText \* FirstCap } displays Twenty-first.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click First, Second, Third, ....
\*Ordinal    This switch displays results as ordinal Arabic numerals. For example, { DATE \@ "d" \* Ordinal } displays 30th.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click 1st, 2nd, 3rd.
\*Roman    This switch displays results as Roman numerals. The result has the same case as the word "roman" in the field code. For example, { SEQ CHAPTER \* roman } displays xi, and { SEQ CHAPTER \* ROMAN } displays XI.
To select this option in the Field Options dialog box, click I, II, III,.

Character formats and protecting previously applied formats: 
The following are character formatting switches and their results:
\*Charformat    This switch applies the formatting of the first letter of the field name to the entire result. The result of the following example has bold formatting because the R in REF is bold. 
{ REF chapter2_title \* Charformat } displays Whales of the Pacific in bold text.
To add this switch, type it in the field code or in the Field codes box in the Field dialog box.
\*MERGEFORMAT    This switch applies the formatting of the previous result to the new result. For example, if you select the name displayed by the field { AUTHOR \* MERGEFORMAT } and apply bold formatting, Word retains the bold formatting when the field is updated to display a new author name.
When you insert fields by using the Field dialog box , the \*MERGEFORMAT switch is included by default. You can turn this option off by clearing the Preserve formatting during updates check box in the Field dialog box.
Back to formatting switches 

Numeric format switch (\#) 
The Numeric format switch (\#) specifies the display of a numeric result.
For example, the switch \# $#,##0.00 in { = SUM(ABOVE) \# $#,##0.00 } displays a result such as "$4,455.70." If the result of a field is not a number, this switch has no effect.
Note: Quotation marks are not required around simple numeric formats that do not include spaces — for example, { MarchSales \# $#,##0.00 }. For more complex numeric formats and those that include text or spaces, enclose the numeric format in quotation marks, as shown in the following examples. Word adds quotation marks to numeric format switches if you insert a field by using the Field dialog box or the Formula command in the Data group of the Layout tab (Table Tools contextual tab).
Combine the following format items to build a numeric format switch:
0 (zero)    This format item specifies the requisite numeric places to display in the result. If the result does not include a digit in that place, Word displays a 0 (zero). For example, { = 4 + 5 \# 00.00 } displays 09.00.
#    This format item specifies the requisite numeric places to display in the result. If the result does not include a digit in that place, Word displays a space. For example, { = 9 + 6 \# $### } displays $ 15.
x    This format item drops digits to the left of the "x" placeholder. If the placeholder is to the right of the decimal point, Word rounds the result to that place. For example:
{ = 111053 + 111439 \# x## } displays 492.
{ = 1/8 \# 0.00x } displays 0.125.
{ = 3/4 \# .x } displays .8.
. (decimal point)    This format item determines the decimal point position. For example, { = SUM(ABOVE) \# $###.00 } displays $495.47. 
Use the decimal symbol that is specified as part of the regional settings in Control Panel.
, (digit grouping symbol)    This format item separates a series of three digits. For example, { = NetProfit \# $#,###,### } displays $2,456,800. 
Use the digit grouping symbol that is specified as part of the regional settings in Control Panel.
- (minus sign)    This format item adds a minus sign to a negative result or adds a space if the result is positive or 0 (zero). For example, { = 10 - 90 \# -## } displays -80.
+ (plus sign)    This format item adds a plus sign to a positive result, a minus sign to a negative result, or a space if the result is 0 (zero). For example, { = 100 - 90 \# +## } displays +10, and { = 90 - 100 \# +## } displays -10.
%, $, *, and so on    This format item includes the specified character in the result. For example, { = netprofit \# "##%" } displays 33%.
"example formatting for positive; negative"    This format item specifies different number formats for positive and negative results, separated by a semicolon. For example, if the bookmark Sales95 is a positive value, the field { Sales95 \# "$#,##0.00;-$#,##0.00" } displays the value with regular formatting — for example, "$1,245.65". A negative value is displayed with bold formatting and a minus sign — for example, -$ 345.56.
"example formatting for positive; negative; zero"    This format item specifies different number formats for a positive result, a negative result, and a 0 (zero) result, separated by semicolons. For example, depending on the value of the Sales95 bookmark, { Sales95 \# "$#,##0.00;($#,##0.00);$0" } displays positive, negative, and 0 (zero) values as follows: $1,245.65, ($ 345.56), $0.
'text'    This format item adds text to the result. Enclose the text in single quotation marks. For example, { = { Price } *8.1% \# "$##0.00 'is sales tax' " } displays $347.44 is sales tax.
`numbereditem`    This format item displays the number of the preceding item that you numbered by using the Caption command (References tab, Captions group) or by inserting a SEQ field. Enclose the item identifier, such as "table" or "figure," in grave accents (`). The sequential number is displayed in Arabic numerals. For example, { = SUM(A1:D4) \# "##0.00 'is the total of Table' `table`" } displays 456.34 is the total of Table 2.
Back to formatting switches 

Date-Time format switch (\@) 
The Date-Time format switch (\@) specifies the display of a date or time.
For example, the switch \@ "dddd, MMMM d, yyyy" in the field { DATE \@ "dddd, MMMM d, yyyy" } displays "Friday, November 23, 2007." Combine the following date and time instructions — day (d), month (M), and year (y); hours (h) and minutes (m) — to build a date-time format. You can also include text, punctuation, and spaces.
Date instructions: 
Month (M) 
The letter M must be uppercase to distinguish months from minutes.
M    This format item displays the month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit months. For example, July is 7.
MM    This format item displays the month as a number with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit months. For example, July is 07.
MMM    This format item displays the month as a three-letter abbreviation. For example, July is Jul.
MMMM    This format item displays the month as its full name.
Day (d) 
The letter d displays the day of the month or the day of the week. The letter d can be either uppercase or lowercase.
d    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 6.
dd    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a number with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 06.
ddd    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a three-letter abbreviation. For example, Tuesday is displayed as Tue.
dddd    This format item displays the day of the week as its full name.
Year (y) 
The letter y displays the year as two or four digits. The letter y can be either uppercase or lowercase.
yy    This format item displays the year as two digits with a leading 0 (zero) for years 01 through 09. For example, 1999 is displayed as 99, and 2006 is displayed as 06.
yyyy    This format item displays the year as four digits.
Time instructions: 
Hours (h) 
A lowercase h bases time on the 12-hour clock. An uppercase H bases time on the 24-hour, or military, clock; for example, 5 P.M. is displayed as 17.
h or H    This format item displays the hour without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 9.
hh or HH    This format item displays the hour with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 09.
Minutes (m) 
The letter m must be lowercase to distinguish minutes from months.
m    This format item displays minutes without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit minutes. For example, { TIME \@ "m" } displays 2.
mm    This format item displays minutes with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit minutes. For example, { TIME \@ "mm" } displays 02.
Seconds (s) 
s    This format item displays seconds without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit seconds. For example { TIME \@ “s” displays 5.
ss    This format item displays seconds with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit seconds For example { TIME \@ “ss” displays 05.
A.M. and P.M. (AM/PM) 
This displays A.M. and P.M. To change the A.M. and P.M. symbols for Microsoft Windows, change the regional settings in Control Panel.
am/pm or AM/PM    This format item displays A.M. and P.M. as uppercase. For example, { TIME \@ "h AM/PM" } and { TIME \@ "h am/pm" } display 9 AM or 5 PM.

HOW TO - Manage Training Events v1.0.doc:
Core allows users to configure system events by specifying what occurrence or action will “trigger” an event and what action or output the event should produce. 

There are many different Event Categories, and within each Category, there are many different Event Types. 
This guide covers the category of Training Events, and takes you through the following processes: 
 TOC \o "1-2" \h \z \u Creating a new event PAGEREF _Toc442711694 \h 1

Creating a new event
Navigate to: CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration
Open CoreHR and in the toolbar, go to CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration

Select “Training – Employee Courses” from the drop-down menu. All the available Training event types will now appear on the screen. 

The Active Indicator flag shows there are three active event types: “Request Date”, “Start Date”, and “Training Status”. Select the event type for which you want to create a new event, and click “Edit”. 

A pop-up window will open. In the lower half of the window, you can see every event attached to the event type you selected. To view an existing event, select it and click “Edit”. To add a new event, click “Add New Notification”:

Select the “Notification Type” that the event should trigger. 

Choose from the following options:

Field Name
Description
Email
Sends event notification to a specified email address
Employee
Sends event notification to all employees registered for a training course
Organisation Role
Sends event notification to employees who hold a specific role, e.g. “Pay Approver”
Person
Sends event notification to a specified Personnel Number
Process
Not in use
Reports to Manager
Not in use
Username
Not in use
Tell the system how many days Before or After the event to generate the notification:

Set the Conditions which will trigger this event (these should have been provided by the person who requested the new event). 

Note: If your event is triggered by a PROVIDER_CODE, be sure to check that the code has been set up by navigating to CorePersonnel > Training > Training Maintenance > Course Providers. The PROVIDER_CODE should appear on the screen. 

If the PROVIDER_CODE you need isn’t present, you will need to create it by clicking “Add New” and following the on-screen instructions. 

After setting your Conditions, click to save your changes. You must do this before you can configure the Subject and Message text of your event notification.

Click “Configure Subject” to add the notification subject line, and in the pop-up window, select the data source PERS_TRAINING_LOG_VIEW:

Add your “Subject Text” in the field provided and click “Save”. 

Click “Configure Message” to add the notification message text. Once again, select the data source PERS_TRAINING_LOG_VIEW:

Add your “Message Text” in the field provided and click “Save”. 

Make the event active by ticking the “Active Indicator” flag.

Note: Ticking the “Active Indicator” means that any notifications created for this event will be sent by email to the users specified in the “Notification Type” field.

If you want to test event notifications without sending emails, untick the “Active Indicator” and tick the “Test Mode Indicator” instead. 

Click to save your changes. The event will now appear on the main Event Notifications screen. 

Editing an existing event

Open CoreHR and in the toolbar, go to CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration

Select “Training – Employee Courses” from the drop-down menu. All the available Training event types will now appear on the screen. 

Select the Event Type which contains the event you want to edit, and click “Edit”.

A pop-up window will open. In the lower half of the window, you can see every event attached to the Event Type you selected. Select the event you wish to edit and click “Edit”.

The event will open in a separate pop-up window. Edit the event settings as required. Remember that to change the subject or message text, you will need to click “Configure Subject” / “Configure Message” to make the text editable.

Click to save your changes and exit to the home screen. 

Deactivating an existing event
If you wish to deactivate an event, open CoreHR and in the toolbar, go to CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration

Select “Training – Employee Courses” from the drop-down menu. All the available Training event types will now appear on the screen. 

The Active Indicator flag shows there are three active event types: “Request Date”, “Start Date”, and “Training Status”. Select the event type for which you want to deactivate an event, and click “Edit”. 

A pop-up window will open. In the lower half of the window, you can see every event attached to the event type you selected. To deactivate an existing event, select it and click “Edit”:

Untick the “Active Indicator” flag and click “Save Changes”. 

The event will no longer be flagged “active” on the Event Notifications screen.

In April 2021, we discovered that some users were unable to run reports on the HR Reporting servers unless they took the steps outlined below – see OSM Problem Record #40002259 for full details.

These steps may prove useful for other browser-related issues. 

If a user is experiencing problems with a browser-based process, e.g. running reports or doing work in the Portal, there are some common troubleshooting techniques you can employ to try to resolve the issue. This document explains how to: run an incognito browsing session, clear browsing history, and disable extensions on all common PC browsers. 

Incognito browsing

If a user is having problems with a process and you suspect their browser may be to blame, it is useful to try running the process in an “incognito” browser session before you clear their history or disable their extensions. 
An incognito session is a temporary browser session that is isolated from the browser's main session and user data – that is, it is “unaware of” any of the cached data or extensions that are normally present when the browser is running. 
To open an incognito browser session in any browser, follow the instructions below.

Browser
Directions
Google Chrome
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N
From the menu: Select “New incognito window”
Mozilla Firefox
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P
From the menu: Select “New Private Window”
Microsoft Edge
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N
From the menu: Select “New InPrivate window”
Microsoft Internet Explorer
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P
From the menu: Select “Safety” and then “InPrivate browsing” 

The browser session may open in a new tab or a new window, depending on the browser you are using. 

If your user is able to run their process successfully in an incognito browsing session, that indicates that you will need to clear their browser history and disable their extensions to allow the user to run their process in a normal browser session. Information on how to clear history and disable extensions in each browser is presented below.

Clearing browser history
Google Chrome

Search bar link: chrome://settings/clearBrowserData
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + Delete
From the menu: Select “More tools” and “Clear browsing data”:

Any of these methods will take you to the chrome://settings/clearBrowserData screen, where a floating window labelled “Clear browsing data” appears. Go to the Advanced tab of this window and select all items: 
Browsing history
Download history
Cookies and other site data
Cached images and files
Passwords and other sign-in data
Auto-fill form data
Site settings
Hosted app data
Set the Time range to “All time” and click Clear data:

The screen will refresh itself briefly and the “Clear browsing data” window will disappear once the data has been cleared.
Mozilla Firefox
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + Delete 

The keyboard shortcut is the fastest way to manage browser history in Firefox, although distinct types of browser history (e.g. cookies or auto-fill form data) can be managed individually by going to the search bar link: about:preferences#privacy 

After entering Ctrl + Shift + Delete, the “Clear All History” window will pop up. Select all items in the History and Data sections:
Browsing & Download History
Active Logins
Form & Search History
Cookies
Cache
Site Preferences
Offline Website Data
Set the Time range to clear to “Everything” and click OK:

The screen will refresh itself briefly and the “Clear All History” window will disappear once the data has been cleared. 
Microsoft Edge
Search bar link: edge://settings/clearBrowserData
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + Delete
From the menu: Select “Settings” to be taken to the Settings page. Click on “Privacy, search, and services” in the left-hand menu bar: 

Scroll to the section titled “Clear browsing data” and click the button labelled “Choose what to clear”:

Any of these methods will take you to the edge://settings/clearBrowserData screen, where a floating window labelled “Clear browsing data” appears. Select all items: 
Browsing history
Download history
Cookies and other site data
Cached images and files
Passwords
Autofill form data (includes forms and cards)
Site permissions
All data from the previous version of Microsoft Edge

Set the Time range to “All time” and click “Clear now”. 

The screen will refresh itself briefly and the “Clear browsing data” window will disappear once the data has been cleared.
Microsoft Internet Explorer

Search bar link: n/a for Explorer
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + Delete
From the menu: Select “Safety” and “Delete browsing history”: 

Either of these methods will open a pop-up window labelled “Delete Browsing History”. Deselect the first item:
Preserve Favourites website data 
Now select all the remaining items: 
Temporary Internet files and website files
Cookies and website data
History
Download History
Form data
Passwords
Tracking Protection, ActiveX Filtering, and Do Not Track

Click “Delete”. The screen will refresh itself briefly and the “Delete Browsing History” window will disappear once the data has been cleared. 
Disabling extensions

NB: It is only necessary to disable all extensions if you are unsure which extension is causing the problem. You can isolate the problematic extension by re-enabling extensions one-by-one and testing your process (e.g. running a report). 
If you are able to run your process successfully, the re-enabled extension can remain enabled. 
Once you have isolated the problematic extension, you can either leave it permanently disabled, or advise the user to perform their process in another browser which does not have this extension attached. 
Google Chrome
Search bar link: chrome://extensions/
From the menu: Select “More tools” and “Extensions”:

The Extensions page will open, and any browser extensions which have been installed for a user’s Google Chrome browser will be displayed. You can see from the toggle on each extension icon whether an extension is enabled or disabled.

Background
The GDPR Request Centre can be made available to users to complete the following employee requests:
Subject Access Requests – Any employee has the right to request a copy of the personal data the organisation has stored about them in a “structured commonly used and machine-readable format”. The GDPR Request Centre provides this data in both a CSV file and a machine-readable JSON file. 
JSON – JavaScript Object Notation is an open-standard file format that uses human-readable text to transmit data objects consisting of attribute-value pairs and array data types. JSON is a language-independent data format. 
Right to be Forgotten Requests – Any employee has the right to be forgotten as per GDPR guidelines. It is the responsibility of the organisation to carry out any due diligence and internal processes in relation to this request.
Configuration
A combination of user security requirements are needed, this includes a menu profile and an organisation role. 
Menu Profile
Within the Security module, create a new Menu Profile.
Navigate via Security > Menu Profiles > click the Create new Profile button.
Add the Code and Description and click Add Profile to save
Code = GDPR

Users require a menu option to see the GDPR Requests in the Dashboard and to see the Core GDPR business area in Insight:

Organisational Role
A user needs to be assigned an Organisational Role in order to be able to see employee records on the GDPR Request Centre and within the Insight Reports. 
There is a standard Org Role provided by The Access Group ‘GDPR Organisational Role’ and this needs to be assigned at Company access level.
Firstly, the Org Role needs to be activated. Navigate via People Management > Data Centre > References Data > Open> Organisational Role Types> filter by the GDPR role type and enable the active indicator. 

You then need to define the org group that access is aligned to. This will either be at Company or Department level. It is only possible to define one level in PeopleXD by which employees will be grouped e.g. If set to Department, each department needs to be assigned to a user to ensure that all employees can be managed in the GDPR Request Centre. A mix of levels is not possible. 
Navigate to Administrator Dashboard > Admin > Admin Settings > search for the following parameter: gdpr_org_group.

Click on the Edit button and set the required Org Level by entering the required code e.g. ORGZ (Company level). Click Save.

GDPR Control Parameters
GDPR Statutory Years for Deletion
When a deletion request is being processed, there is validation to prevent this occurring if the employee’s leave date is less than a specified number of years. This is defaulted to 7 years; however, this is configurable.
To manage the setting navigate via
Administrator Dashboard > Admin > Admin Settings > search for parameter gdpr_statutory_years.
Click on the Edit button and enter the required number of years. Click Save. 

Cleardown Days for GDPR Requests
GDPR request history for ‘query’ requests is automatically cleared down on the GDPR Request Centre after a specified number of days. This is defaulted to 30 days; however, this is configurable. 
To manage the setting navigate via
Administrator Dashboard > Admin > Admin Settings > search for parameter gdpr_cleardown_days.
Click on the edit button and enter the required number of days. Click Save.

Create a Subject Access Request
The Subject Access Request is managed via the GDPR Requests Centre.
Navigate via Administration Dashboard > Admin > GDPR Requests > Open:

Click on the New Requests button, to open the ‘Create New Request’ screen

To create the Subject Access Request complete the fields as follows:
Request Type
Data Provision
Data Subject
Search for the employee by forename, surname or employee number. 
Filter Setting – Ordinary
On by default.
This is standard personal information data e.g. employee number, name, address etc.
Filter Setting - Sensitive
On by default.
This refers to special categories of personal data e.g. ethnic backg4round, sexual orientation etc.
Filter Setting - Financial
Off by default.
This is the data subjects financial information e.g. payroll history. 

Click OK.
The following confirmation message is displayed. Click Yes to fully submit the request. If you click No the request is not submitted. 

Once a request has been successfully submitted, it is listed on the GDPR Requests screen with a status of “OPEN” and a request type of “QUERY”. 

The request can take some time to process depending on the record and is based on the range of data and volume recorded for that employee on PeopleXD. 
When the processing begins, the status updates on the GDPR Requests screen to “PROCESSING”. 
The status updates to “CLOSED” once fully completed. The information requested for the data subject is now available to download.
Download Subject Access Request Files
To download the Subject Access Request output files for the employee navigate to the GDPR Request Centre via Administration Dashboard > Admin > GDPR Requests > Open. 
The completed Subject Access Request will be displayed on this screen. You can use the search requests facility where multiple exist.
Click on the Ellipses button and select the option Documents.

The GDPR Documents screen opens and all of the files produced as part of this request are listed on screen. The same report is available in two formats a csv and a json file.
Click the Ellipses button for the required file and select Download.

If there are any files for the employee on PeopleXD, these are listed on this GDPR Documents screen. These can be differentiated from the GDPR report files as these include a source name. 
Process a Right to be Forgotten request
The Right to be Forgotten request is managed via the GDPR Requests Centre.
Navigate via Administration Dashboard > Admin > GDPR Requests > Open:

Click on the New Requests button, to process the Delete Request. 

 
Complete the fields as follows:
Request Type
Data Deletion
Data Subject
Search for the employee by forename, surname or employee number.

Click OK. Three warning messages are then displayed in turn which need to be responded to fully submit the deletion request.
First warning:

Second warning:

Third warning:

If No is selected for any of the warning messages the request is not submitted.
Once Yes is selected for all three warnings the request is fully submitted.
Once a request is successfully submitted, it is listed on the GDPR Requests screen with a status of “OPEN” and request type “DELETE”.

Request Failure
The request is listed on the GDPR Requests screen with a status of “DELETE NOT ALLOWED”.
An employee record may only be deleted if:
The employee is a leaver
Their leave date is more than 7 years ago. 
The employee record is not deleted for a request with this status. 

Request Success
The time taken for the request to be processed depends on the range and volume of data recorded for that employee. When the processing begins, the status updated to “PROCESSING!. Once the delete request finishes processing the request is immediately deleted from the GDPR Requests screen. 
All traces of the deletion request are removed from PeopleXD and are not retrievable visa the GDPR request Centre. This is completed in accordance with the GDPR regulations. The request may be reported on via Insight, with the employee details redacted. 
Deleting GDPR Requests
Subject Access Requests and failed Deletion requests will remain on the GDPR Requests screen for reference, until cleared down manually or automatically. Automatic clear down is carried out after 30 days, but this is configurable.
Successful deletion requests are immediately deleted from the GDPR Requests screen. 
To manually delete a request click on the ellipses button and select Delete.

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?

The requirement for a UDF will often come from a Business requirement, so the Business Process Advisor within the HRIS Support Centre will usually lead on gathering requirements for a new UDF.

A “MASTER UDF Template” excel file is stored in the following folder which should be completed, usually by or with assistance from an HRIS Analyst, outlining how the UDF should be set up within the system:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\UDFs

Completed UDF templates should be saved within a sub-folder named to reflect the UDF to be set up. Any changes to the template during the process (see Change Management section) should be saved within this sub-folder.

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

New UDFs and changes to existing UDFs are generally requested by the relevant business area, often within Personnel Services. The HRIS Business Process Adviser will usually lead on/be involved in the consultation and gathering requirements for both new UDFs and changes to existing UDFs.

The Change Request will be approved by the relevant approver in OSM – usually the Head of HRIS or their nominated deputy.

You must give early notification of the intention to change a UDF or create a new UDF to the HR Analytics team, or HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, to consider the impact on the data warehouse.

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 

New UDFs and changes to existing UDFs should be managed via the Change Request process in OSM.

New UDFs could be a candidate for a Standard Change but this needs to be discussed and agreed.

If during the course of the build or testing process any requirement for changes to the UDF are identified, the template should be amended and saved (with a new version number) in the UDF folder. Only the latest version of the UDF Template should be attached to the Change Record, so previous versions may need to be removed (if possible).

How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
Adding a new UDF

UDFs are ‘forms’ that can be used to store additional information which cannot be recorded anywhere else in the Personnel module. There is a standard template that cannot be altered although the field descriptions and content can be configured.

UDFs can be held at Appointment, Person (employee) or Recruitment level. This is determined via the Advanced settings when creating a UDF.

Person and Appointment level UDFs are accessed within the employee record in People Management in the User Defined Field section. Recruitment UDFs are less common and relate to additional sections added to the online Application Forms. The Application Form with inbuilt supporting statement has one UDF and the Apprenticeship Application form has three. These provide additional sections that could not be included any other way.

Each UDF is assigned a Reference Code and Description when it is first created. 

The reference code is restricted to 6 characters (alpha). It is used for reporting purposes to identify the relevant data items. It is not displayed in the UDF. 

The Description is displayed within the UDF in the Select Detail or Selection menus as applicable. There is a 40 character limit for the Description.

There are 12 Fields available. Each field can be configured as a List item (LoV), Text (free text field), or Date. (There are other options but we don’t use them.)

UDFs are configured in the Portal via People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects.

The User Description (Data Label) is displayed against each input field in the UDF and appears in the UDF as shown below:

Data Type determines what can be entered into that field. E.g Date, text, list item

List items form a drop-down list that can be selected within a field in the UDF. 

The data items are stored in the database table under the Item number and not the field description/label. For example ‘Inducted By’ will be stored under Item 3 in the database. This causes issues when User Descriptions or Field Items need to be amended.

Full details on creating a new UDF can be found in the How To guide. 

Changing a UDF

Making amendments to UDFs is technically straight forward; However, great care must be taken as existing data will not automatically feed through to the data which has already been entered. This is because data is entered against an Item Number generic across all UDFs rather than against a field specific to that UDF. Please read the information below before proceeding.

Adding a new List Item to an existing list
Adding a new List Item to an existing list will not have any impact on existing data. 
You can also amend the order in which the list items are displayed by re-entering the entire list or swapping items around. 

Editing existing List Items:
Any changes made will apply to all existing records where the edited field(s) have previously been selected. However the UDF itself will not update automatically on the individual records and an error message will be displayed whenever the UDF is opened. To correct this the individual UDF records must be updated to re-select the edited item. This is a manual process as each UDF needs to be opened within every affected employee record, the updated field(s) reselected and the changes saved. 

For this reason changes can only be made with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the employee records.

List Items - The preferred approach is to add a new list item, update the affected records to select the ‘new’ list item and then untick the active indicator against the ‘old’ list item.

Example:
Right to Work List item ‘EEA Family Permit’ was changed to ‘EEA Family Permit (6 months)’ in Jan18. A new list item was added for the new description, the affected employee records were updated to select the ‘new’ description and the ‘old’ list item showing the previous description was made inactive.

Editing existing Field items:
Any changes to the Description will apply to all existing records where the edited field(s) have previously been selected. Unlike the List items the Field items will update automatically and no changes will be required to the individual records. However, any reports containing the edited UDF will need to be updated as the column headers will refer to the previous Field Item Description.

Removing Field Items or changing the order in which they are displayed
Due to the way in which the items are stored in the database i.e. against the item number not the User Description, this is not a straightforward change and has the similar limitations to editing field items. 

Depending upon the number of changes and the number of affected records you may need to consider creating a new UDF and migrating the data via the Data Upload tool available in the Core Portal. 

For this reason changes can only be made with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the employee records.

Removing List Items 
You can remove items from the list of values by making them inactive, or by deleting the item and if necessary re-ordering the list. However, any user data which has already been entered using the deleted list item will not be correct but will not display an error message. 

For this reason list items can only be deleted with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the affected employee records.

Changing where the UDF appears
If you need to change where the UDF is displayed (i.e. from Appointment to Person) it is possible to simply change the tick box under the Advanced tab. However any new records created after the change will appear in a different table so any user data entered against the previous position will not be visible in the new position. The historic information will not be lost but you will be unable to view it in the back office unless you keep the old “position” ticked, which will cause confusion.

Therefore, depending on the change required, it may be better to set up a new “replacement” UDF in the new position and then remove the old UDF from use (following the “Removing a UDF” steps). 

If you need to transfer historic data from the old version of the UDF into the new version this can be done via the Data Upload tool in the Core Portal – refer to HOW TO Prepare Data for the Data Migration Tool

Removing a UDF

If no user data has been entered against a UDF you are able to delete the row from the User Defined Fields screen.
