Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?

Normally the HRIS Business Analyst or HRIS Process Team would undertake user acceptance/functional testing, although this may also be done by end users depending on which groups of users will be expected to use the report.

Communications
Who needs to be informed (but not consulted) about this change? Detail when they should be informed (before or after the change).

The Right to Work UDF is used in an interface so the ‘SSM – Business Integration Technologies Team’ within Software Solutions will need to be informed of any potential changes to this UDF ahead of any work being done – see Downstream Systems & Processes.

It is likely that user communication will be required, particularly with a new UDF, depending on who the target audience of the UDF will be. As UDFs are normally raised through the Process Team or Business Analyst, training guidance and communication will normally be considered and taken care of.

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.

Data Warehouse
Most UDFs are migrated into the Data Warehouse and split out into individual tables according to their code. There are then views built which translate the underlying columns (text1, text2 etc) into their actual headings. If you are changing the structure of a UDF (introducing a new field, changing the heading) there will be changes required to the warehouse. If you are replacing a UDF with a new version with a new name then all of the tables in the warehouse will need to be rebuilt. You must inform the HR Analytics Team, or the HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, of the changes being made.

Interfaces
UDFs are rarely used within interface files but information in the Right to Work UDF is taken by the following interfaces:
CoreHR to Access Databases ‘staff including casuals’ interface (Interface Staging PROGID_170), which sends email to HRIS Support with subject lines following this pattern: Interface Staging: req=hris/pcapps/staff ref=%ID% status=SUCCESS. 
CoreHR to EAP interface (Interface Staging PROGID to be confirmed), which sends Right to Work data for all staff to the Examiner Appointments and Payments system, transforming the CoreHR data into “Right to Work = TRUE/FALSE” values. 

NB!! Rules have been built into these interfaces to extract the data from the RTW2 UDF. Any proposed changes to the UDF or the description of the data labels within it will need to be fed back to the SSM-BITE team before the changes are made, so that the interfaces can be modified as necessary to continue picking up the required RTW information. 

This is particularly important as UDFs are set up against generic Name/Description/Types, e.g. Reference Code, Item1, User Field1. Changes to the structure of a specific UDF need to be explicitly communicated to the SSM-BITE team so that they can ensure that the necessary parameters are in place in the interface to pick up the data from the modified UDF. 

Affected Reports
Are there any standard reports which may need to be updated following this change?

There will almost always be reports affected by a change to a UDF as there is normally at least one accompanying report with that UDF. However this would depend on the UDF being updated as there is not one “UDF” report, rather they are reported on separately using the UDF “Reference Code” to only return data of a specific UDF type within any given report.

Any changes to UDFs (including moving from one UDF to another for the same purpose – e.g. ‘RTW’ to ‘RTW2’) will need to be reflected in the report. In a similar way to interfaces, the reports will still run but the data they return is likely to be out of sequence or not make sense if a report is not updated, and will therefore return inaccurate information.

Background
A decision was made to configure Insight to report on onboarding surveys as it is the only way to extract the answers given in the surveys – AG confirmed that the system was configured to create a new view for each survey created that would only be available in Insight.
Two reports were configured – a standalone report to return employees who had outstanding tasks to complete and a multi tabbed report to display the answers given by employees when completing the relevant tasks. 
The reports contain filters (some hard coded and some with user defined parameters), calculations and sort orders.
Currently the reports are shared with individual users but they can also be shared with User Role/s (not tested). They were initially shared with a Pilot group in February 2023.
Naming convention
A naming convention has been agreed as follows:
Reports will be suffixed with INS followed by the relevant number and prefixed with the abbreviation of the module they relate to e.g. PER for People Management and REC for Recruitment. So the onboarding reports begin PERINS01 and PERINS02.

PERINS02 Incomplete Onboarding checklist items

Unshare the report with all users except support.

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
The Active Roles Web Interface is used by HR Systems to manage access to the HR Reporting environments. Individuals are added to Active Directory (“AD”) groups, and the groups are granted read-only access to folders and sub-folders within the HR Reporting environments. Which AD groups are granted access to which folders/sub-folders is determined by consultation, usually within the Functional Analysis or HR Analytics teams, but often with input from the HR Systems business change advisors. 
Note: all users must login to the HR Reporting environments via CONNECT. Users with CONNECT managed desktops will be logged in automatically, but those without CONNECT managed desktops must be set up with a “Global” CONNECT account. The Functional Analysis team are responsible for the creation of these accounts for users of HR Reporting. 
Only a small number of people within HR Systems have access to the Active Roles Web Interface to view and manage the AD groups; the site itself is managed by the Microsoft Platform Services Team (“MPST”). MPST are the owners of the Active Roles Web Interface and they can grant or remove access to the site upon request. 
There are two different types of AD groups: normal groups, and “super-groups” which are for use solely by report writers and support teams. You can tell which is which by looking at the group name prefix. 
HRIS-RR-… : this is a normal AD group which can be maintained by the Functional Analysis team. Requests for changes to existing AD groups must be raised on OSM as Minor Changes and implemented by the Functional Analysis team.
HRIS-RS-…: this is a “super-group”. Members of reporting super-groups have total access to the HR Reporting environments, and members of “Report Writers” super-groups are able to publish content to the HR Reporting environments. Super-groups can only be maintained by Microsoft Platform Services, and all changes related to super-group membership must be approved in writing by Simon Burford, Athena Artuso, or Mandy Zaccheo. 
Requests for creation of new normal AD groups must be raised on OSM as Minor Changes and a task must be assigned to MPST with details of the new group. These must include:
Group name – this must be in the format “HRIS-RR-[short descriptive group name]” . 
Example: HRIS-RR-FINANCE_BFT
Description – a description of the group you wish to create. 
Example: Finance Budgeting & Forecasting Team
MPST will create the group profile, and the Functional Analysis team can then add individual staff members. 
Requests for creation of new super-groups must be raised on OSM as Minor Changes, but only after written approval has been granted by Simon Burford, Athena Artuso, or Mandy Zaccheo. A task must be assigned to MPST with details of the new group. These must include:
Group name – this must be in the format “HRIS-RS-[short descriptive group name]” 
Example: HRIS-RS-PowerBI Report Writers – Project Teams
Members – a list of the individuals (fullname + SSO) whom you wish to be added to the new super-group. 
Example: Athena Artuso (admn4134)
If someone is requesting access to the Active Roles Web Interface itself to view or manage the information there, an OSM Minor Change request must be raised and a task sent to the Microsoft Platform Services Team (“MPST”). Only MPST are able to manage access to the Active Roles Web Interface. 
Note: Only the Functional Analysis team should have read-write access to the Active Roles Web Interface; this is to ensure the careful management of access to the HR Reporting environments. Members of other teams such as the HRIS Support Centre may require read-only access to the Active Roles Web Interface to help them investigate customer queries, but they should not be given read-write access.

Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

Mandy Zaccheo for read-only access requests

Change Management

How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
A very basic guide to managing existing AD groups is provided here; a separate how-to can be created if required. A guide to creating Global CONNECT accounts is also needed. 
Adding a new member to an AD group
Navigate to: https://activeroles.it.ox.ac.uk/Service/default.aspx 
On the landing screen, select Search. 

Search for the name of the AD group you wish to modify. Select the group and in the right-hand menu bar, select “Members”:

The screen will refresh and a list of the group’s members will be displayed. To add a new member (or members), click the “Add…” button:

Search for the name you wish to add and select the relevant record(s); then click OK at the bottom of the screen to commit your changes:

Removing a member from an AD group
Navigate to: https://activeroles.it.ox.ac.uk/Service/default.aspx
Search for and select the AD group in question and open the “Members” screen, as detailed above. Select the member(s) you wish to remove and click the “Remove…” button.

A warning message will pop up. Click “Yes” to commit your changes.

Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?
The Active Roles Web Interface is a live system; there is no method for testing the changes made within it before they are implemented. However, it is best practice to ask individuals who have been added to AD groups to confirm that they can access the relevant areas of the HR Reporting environments (what is relevant will depend on which AD group they belong to; e.g. adding someone to the Payroll team group should grant them access to the Payroll folder and all subfolders, as well as many Pensions reports). 
Individuals who have been set up with Global CONNECT accounts must check and confirm whether they are able to log into the HR Reporting environment via their new accounts. 
If someone has been granted access to the Active Roles Web Interface, they will need to check and confirm that they are able to access the site and read its contents. Users with read-write access should check that they have the ability to add and remove individuals from existing AD groups.

Communications
Who needs to be informed (but not consulted) about this change? Detail when they should be informed (before or after the change).
Whoever has requested addition to or removal from an existing AD group (whether for themselves or, as is more likely, on behalf of another user) should be informed once the change has been implemented. Similarly, whoever has requested creation of a new AD group should be informed once the group has been created and members added. 
Finally, whoever has requested access (read-only or read-write) to the Active Roles Web Interface should be informed once MPST have granted that access.

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.
Both the creation of Global CONNECT accounts and changes to existing AD groups within the Active Roles Web Interface directly impact user access to the HR Reporting environments, and as such must be handled very carefully to prevent users from accessing report data unnecessarily.
Changes to user access to the Active Roles Web Interface have a secondary impact on management of existing AD groups. Only members of the Functional Analysis team should have read-write access to the Active Roles Web Interface for creation of Global CONNECT accounts and management of AD groups, to ensure that reporting access is tightly controlled.

HOW TO – Manage Balances in CoreTime
HOW TO – Maintain Pay Codes for Time Management
HOW TO – Update Holiday Schemes

Balances Overview
Within Time Management each appointment requires an associated Balance which determines how the annual leave for the appointment will be calculated. The Balance can draw on a range of parameters, dependent on the settings, including: Holiday Schemes, Long Service Schemes, timesheet hours and the current appointment.
Departments are responsible for assigning the appropriate Balance to each appointment via People Management, but cannot view the underlying Balance settings. It is therefore important that the Balances are correctly configured and appropriately named, so that HR administrators can easily identify the correct option and audit their appointments for errors.
Before further balances are created, it is recommended that the new setting providing the option to connect the balance to the appointment FTE Hours is explored. If Balances no longer need to be specific to appointments sharing the same FTE Hours value, the total number of Balances could be significantly reduced and HR Admins would be able to apply the same Balance to support staff and academic-related staff.

New Balance Settings = Advanced parameters > Company Holiday Entitlement 
Fields: Link ‘Default Hours to Personnel’ & ‘Personnel Default Hours Divisor

Tweaking of the Entitlements per Balance is also required when these settings are in use, so that one Balance can be linked to multiple Long Service Schemes. 

Identifying when a new Balance is required
To reduce the risk of departments assigning the wrong Balance and to minimise the central overhead of maintaining PeopleXD-Time, new Balances (and any associated config items) should only be created when necessary. 
To determine if a new Balance and/or associated config items are required, follow the Balance decision tree. 
Before creating a new Balance, assess the net benefits. Is the balance likely to be required long-term and used by multiple employees and does it warrant the additional maintenance overhead or complexity? Some exceptions may be better suited to management by departmental HR through manual balance adjustments. 
If bespoke Balances or Holiday Schemes covering only a small number of appointments are frequently requested, it may become necessary to apply some sort of threshold. Similarly, if a department has inconsistent or unpredictable closure patterns, it may benefit Departmental HR to adopt a self-book approach to closure days (Balances with no Holiday Scheme)

Accrual Balances - Background
It is anticipated that the two Accrual Balances set up during the initial configuration, codes CASUAL and VARI will be appropriate for all use by all University departments. New Accrual Balances should only be required when expanding use of People XD time to new staff types, such as TSS workers. 
Accrual Balances are not linked with Holiday Schemes and the calculations are not impacted by the appointment FTE hours setting, so the key factors to consider are:

The rate (%) at which holiday is accrued
Whether this rate is impacted by long service
The type of leave year followed (a personal leave year or a universal leave year), and where a universal leave year is followed, the leave year start/end dates
The Holiday Pay Code(s) which will affect the balance

Only Accrual Balances which follow a universal leave year can be linked to a Long Service Scheme, but the Long Service Scheme must be specifically configured for use with an Accrual Balance (do not link to the Long Service schemes configured for Entitlement Balances)

Universal leave year Vs Personal leave year
Accrual Balances can be configured in two ways to cater for the common annual leave arrangements used by paid as claimed-style appointments:

Universal leave year – linked to a set leave year, such as the University standard leave year which runs 1st October – 30th September.
Personal Leave Year – Leave year determined per appointment, e.g. using the appointment start date as the leave year start. 

Accrual Balances & Pay Codes
Leave which is accrued is managed through timesheets. For the balance to function correctly and to allow staff to record leave taken, Pay Codes need to be correctly configured. Unlike Entitlement Balances, which share pay codes, it is likely each Accrual Balance will require its own set of Pay Codes including:
At least one Accrual Pay Code which accrues leave e.g. 107 PAID AS CLAIMED PAYMENT
At least one Holiday Pay Code which records leave taken e.g. 4231 CAS HOLIDAY PAY (HRS) 
Pay Codes should be created before attempting to configure an Accrual Balance. Bespoke Pay Code Access Groups will be required to enable the appropriate staff to record time against these pay codes. 

Long Service Scheme (for Accrual Balances)
A Long Service Scheme can be linked to an Accrual Balance, but this is optional and Accrual Balances will function without a scheme. 
Long Service schemes should only be linked to Accrual Balances that follow a universal leave year, they cannot not be used with Accrual Balances that follow a personal calendar. 

Entitlement Balances - Background
An entitlement Balance provides the employee with an annual leave allowance to use during their leave year. The amount of entitlement the system issues is calculated by drawing on several factors: the settings within the Balance itself, certain appointment settings and where applicable, the associated configuration items (e.g. Holiday Scheme).

The appointment settings impacting the entitlement are:
Contracted hours/multiplier – part-timers get a pro rata entitlement
Start /end date – e.g. those starting mid leave year get a pro rata entitlement 
Continuous service start date – factored into the long service entitlement (if applicable)

Balances are assigned in days for full time staff and hours for part time staff. In this context full time staff means staff who work the standard days every week, according to their grade e.g. 7.5 hours per day for Grade 6 and above. If an employee works different hours each day then the annual leave balance should be assigned in hours. In this scenario public holidays and fixed closure days will be assigned the actual hours due to be worked on those days. 

Most balance settings will be the same across all entitlement Balances, the settings which differ are:
The FTE Hours - the default weekly hours, e.g. 37.5 for academic related (May not be applicable if the ‘Link Default Hours to Personnel’ setting is in use)
Base Entitlement – for a full time staff member before any pro rata calculations or long service days, e.g. 38 days or equivalent in hours
The leave year start and end dates – e.g. running 1st Oct-30th Sept

The associated items affecting the entitlement (where applicable) are:
Holiday Schemes
Long Service Schemes

Follow the New Balance Decision Tree to determine when a new Balance is required, and when it can be linked to existing Holiday and Long Service schemes.

Standard University Annual Leave Entitlement
It is expected that most appointments will follow the standard University leave arrangements. I.e. A base entitlement of 38 days’ leave pro rata and a leave year running 1st Oct - 30th Sept. 

Preparation
Before you begin creating a Balance, ensure you have determined:
A name for the balance (see relevant section for guidance) 
The baseline entitlement, e.g. 38 days pro rata 
The holiday year start/end dates
The full-time equivalent hours (FTE hours), e.g. 37.5 hours for Grade 6+
Plus, where applicable:
The Holiday Scheme the Balance will follow, or where a new scheme is required, the precise list of closure dates (public holidays and fixed closure days) 
The Long Service Scheme, or where a new scheme is required, the rules of the scheme

Long Service Increments
Each increment represents a stage in the long service scheme. The value recorded in the ‘Floating Entitlement’ column is the number of additional days that will automatically awarded at that stage, based on that employee’s length of service. The days are cumulative, so each increment only needs to display the number of additional days awarded at that stage. 
By default, the leave is awarded at the start of the leave year during which the employee crosses the threshold (anniversary year). To award the additional leave at the start of the following leave year, you need to increase the months by 12. 

In the above example, an employee is entitled to an additional day of leave at the start of the leave year following their 5th anniversary.
The system would not award any additional leave until the start of the leave year during which the employee’s continuous service is scheduled to exceed 72 months (6 years).

Balance calendar
Each Balance has its own Balance Calendar, which determines the start and end dates of the leave year (periods), and the rules for carrying forward leave from one leave year to the next. 

These must be extended each year to cover the next calendar year. For example, if Annual Leave is managed in yearly blocks the Annual Leave balance calendar defines the start date and end date of each leave year (period) and specifies any carry forward rules. It is not possible to close a balance period (complete a period end) until the next period has been configured on the balance calendar.
You may find it useful to refer to the guides - HOW TO - Update Holiday Schemes v1.1.docx and HOW TO – Maintain calendars in WFM

Balance entitlements
Each Balance needs its own set of Balance Entitlements. The Balance Entitlements determine amount of annual leave that a full-time employee receives to take on dates of their choosing (Personal Leave). In PeopleXD, this is categorised as Floating leave. For every leave year (period) a Balance Entitlement must be set. 

Calculating Floating leave days/hours
If a Holiday Scheme has been linked to the Balance, the Balance entitlement must offset the number of closure days in the Holiday Scheme. The number of closure dates can vary year on year, so the floating leave values may need to fluctuate to reflect these changes. To determine the number of floating days needed in any specific year, use the following formula:
Floating days + Closure days = Base entitlement 

Note: If the Holiday Scheme includes closure day(s) which are awarded on top of the base entitlement, such as discretionary additional leave days awarded by the VC in certain years, and you do not want these days to reduce the amount of Personal Leave the employee has, ensure you either increase the base entitlement value (e.g. to 39) or ignore the leave in the closure days value

The Casual Payment Submission spreadsheet was created as a direct result of the project ‘Ensuring legal compliance for casual workers’ in 2016. 

Responsibility for creating casual worker records was devolved to departments and introduced the mandatory use of an Excel spreadsheet to submit worker payments to Payroll. The spreadsheet supports the capture of weekly working hours for Tier 4 workers. The removal of paper and the submission of encrypted timesheets electronically will lead to improved efficiency and information security.

The spreadsheet was developed by Software Solutions (David Hickman) and contains validation rules to ensure data is entered correctly and macros to convert the data entered into a format that can be loaded directly into the payroll module. 

The workbook contains hidden sheets, rows and columns and is protected to prevent the validation rules and macros from being changed or deleted accidentally. 

Full instructions on how to edit the spreadsheet can be found in the Technical specification document. 

There are two versions of the spreadsheet:

Casual Payment Submission Spreadsheet Department use – for all departments except TSS. This version of the spreadsheet contains all relevant pay codes for departmental use and validates entries against the CASUAL and CASTCH bucket posts.

Casual Payment Submission Spreadsheet TSS. 
This version of the spreadsheet contains the pay codes applicable to TSS and validates entries against the specific TSS bucket posts.

All other validation rules and macros are the same. 

In 2022 online time sheeting is being piloted. One workgroup in the Physics department are submitting timesheets online. It is hoped that this will be implemented across the whole University in time thus removing the need for the Submission spreadsheet.

Automated email notifications are generated from CoreHR based on specific Events created in the system. The settings within the event determine when the emails are triggered. An event can have a single or multiple emails linked to it.

The default mailbox is HRIS.MAILRETURN@IT.OX.AC.UK from which the automated emails are sent.

Details of the events and automated emails can be found in the Events and Notifications log here. Refer to the ‘Full Details’ tab or ‘Applicant Notifications’ tab.

Further information about EMS settings in test environments can be found in the Email and Event Configuration following a clone document.

To view the individual events and notifications in the back office see the ‘How To..’ section above.

(NB this article does not include emails that can be generated manually by departments e.g. when communicating with applicants about a specific vacancy)

Email types

Applicants

Emails are automatically generated to applicants and potential applicants under the following circumstances:

When changes are made to an applicant (portal) account
When a new password is requested
When an application has been submitted for a vacancy
When an application for a vacancy has been unsubmitted by a department

Applicant Portal Users

When vacancies meeting specified criteria are opened for advertising. 

This job is slightly different as the emails are sent once a day rather than immediately after it has been triggered by the event. A job runs at regular intervals through the day to generate the emails which are then stored to be sent later. A creation job runs to gather all of the emails to be sent and then the send job runs to send the emails.

These jobs often fail, especially after the system has been taken down for patching or upgrades. We have experimented with various timings of these jobs and at the present time there is a 2 hour delay between the creation and send jobs. The job names are as follows:

pers_applicant_notify_pack.create_notifications 
pers_applicant_notify_pack.send_emails

 If the jobs fail there are some actions that our DBAs can take:

- break the current two jobs 
- disable the notifications on the DB tables
- kill any running process of the creation or sending
- recreate the two jobs to run at separate hours
- remove the pre-existing DBA jobs

Job Name
Purpose

EMS_MAILER_Q.GENERATE_EMAIL

Every 10 mins
pers_applicant_notify_pack.create_notifications

Daily
pers_applicant_notify_pack.send_emails
Send collated notification
Daily

If this does not work then the issue should be raised with Core. There are multiple Core Cases that can be reviewed and referenced if required. 

There is also an open Problem Record - 40000869.

Vacancy Notifications. 

Emails are automatically generated to departmental users for the following reasons:
When applicant packs are generated for a vacancy (job completed)
When merged packs are generated for a vacancy (job completed)

Staff Request notifications

Emails are automatically generated to departmental users for the following reasons:
When a staff request has been submitted for approval (to relevant approvers)
When a staff requested has been processed to completion by the Reward Team
 

Auto-Enrolment

The auto enrolment routine runs once a month after the final payroll run has been completed. There are pre-set criteria within the auto-enrolment process, details of which can be found in the auto-enrolment configuration document here.

Emails will be sent to individuals for the following reasons:
When an employee has been Assessed But Postponed (possibly because their earnings on the relevant appointment have not yet reached the minimum contribution value)
When an employee has been Auto Enrolled
When an individual’s appointment is not eligible 
When an employee has chosen to opt out

PeopleXD holds rules which determine whether or not a given appointment is eligible to be counted towards an employee’s Continuous Service. Those rules must be aligned with the University’s policy around Continuous Service and should be updated whenever this policy changes or any aspect used within the configuration is added to. 
The configuration has been set up so that there shouldn’t need to be any reconfiguration required when new departments are raised within the main University structure. However, any new "Societies" will need business change to consult on whether the department qualifies for continuous service. If the new department code qualifies this will require a change to the continuous service configuration.
There may be a need to review the configuration if any of the related items have a new reference data added, such as Employee Status, Sub Division or the Marie Curie Student pay scale. Pay Code Knowledge Article
Background

By default, all Pay Codes are returned to employees in the Timesheet Entry and Absence Entry screens. Pay Code Groups can be used to tailor the list of pay codes returned to employee and managers when inputting and viewing data.
Pay Code Groups can be assigned to the employee and/or their appointment. 

Pay code groups are assigned to Managers either by System users or Work Groups. In these cases, the system user level configuration takes precedence over the work groups level.
The default manager configuration is:

No Pay Code Grouping applied

In this case there are no limits applied and all pay codes are returned.

System User Level/Organisational Role

Pay Code groups which are assigned at System User/Organisational roles level take precedence over the Work Groups.
Within site settings, the Manager Before Org Roles Access decides if an Organisation role or Username take precedence.

3. Employees Work Group

The personalised groups assigned to an employee’s work group dictates codes. As an example, If a manager has employees in various work groups, the list of pay codes available will also vary.

Manager and Administrator input applies to the following screens: 

Timesheet Input 
Absence Details 
Time Exceptions 
Record Absence Details (back-office) 
Maintain hours (back-office) 

Pay Code Access Groups are required for Accrual Balances to enable staff to record time against specific pay codes. 

Formatting of the Group Codes and Descriptions
There is a standard format for Access Group Codes and Descriptions:-
For Employees the Code is Prefixed with 'EM' and the Description with 'Employee' followed by further details e.g. Code = EMFX6+, Description = Employee (Grade 6 & above)

For casual workers the code is prefixed with 'CAS' and the Description with 'Casual' followed by further details e.g. Code = CASBGL, Description = Casual Bar Work - General Ledger

Viewing and Maintaining the Reference Data

For details on how to create and update the data refer to the HOW TO guide.

Company – linked with payroll and should not be edited without referring to the payroll system owner. Any additions or changes to this area are likely to be discussed and agreed by all affected parties.

Division – Divisions must be linked to a specific company code. They can be hidden from Staff Requests. 

Sub-Division (User Field 1) – Linked to a Division; the code is generally derived from the divisional code e.g. SD20 is the sub-division under division 2, SD30 is under division 3 etc. There are some exceptions as mentioned above.

Level 4 – this is an additional level with the HR System only. Generally the code is derived from the Management Unit code with 01 at the end. E.g. NDM Management Unit = 2B02, Level 4 code = 2B0201

Management Unit – Use of this varies according to how flat the department structure is within the Division. For example the management units in GLAM differentiate between the libraries, museums and gardens.

Pay Administered By – makes the distinction between support and senior/academic roles where the latter are processed at divisional level. Access to salary approvals is controlled by this field.
Codes will begin with the two character department code followed by DEP (pay will be administered by the department) or DIV (pay will be administered by the divisional office). The description will usually be the department name or the division. 
E.g. Department AB - Pitt Rivers has two options for Pay Administered by; ABDEP - Pitt Rivers Museum and ABDIV - GLAM (the short name for the division). 

Some departments within UAS do not have a Pay Admin by DIV as UAS does not operate in the same way as the Academic Divisions. Most of the processing is done by the central UAS Personnel (divisional) team.
 
Cost Centres - Within the hierarchy the default GL code should be used by the department – usually the two character department code followed by 11 0’s. All cost centre and project codes are refreshed overnight by an interface from Oracle Financials. The interface sets an activity code to reflect if this is a General Ledger Cost Centre or a Project Code. 

Location – Used for payslip distribution. It is also linked to the Depts. Database maintained by the Data Service team. 
The code is numerical and the description consists of the two character department code and the department name e.g. AC – Geography. NB: there is a character limit so some names may be shortened.
Most departments have a single location but some have two or more. Additional location codes follow the same format but a sequential number is added after the department code, e.g. AC1 - Geography. 

See HOW TO Create a New Location Code v2.0.docx for more information on Location Codes.

College Association – is used for joint appointments with a college. 
The colleges are included in the department list. ‘Default/Not Applicable’ is used for all post/appointments that are not joint appointments with a college.
‘Not Yet Known’ is used when setting up a joint appointment before the college of association is known. It can be amended later on before the appointment is finalised.

Sensitive Departments

An optional field in the Maintain Department codes screen allows us to further restrict access to ‘sensitive departments’. Access to sensitive departments has to be explicitly requested and granted. 

Employees in sensitive departments do not appear in the cross company search screen when appointing new staff.

The restructure tool
The Post Restructuring Tool is software within Core Personnel which enables us to move high volumes of employees between different areas of the Organisational hierarchy. 

Organisational hierarchy changes currently occur annually (PRAS organisation changes). However minor departmental restructures can occur at any time and often Data Services assist with these changes.

The tool automates a number of tasks that would otherwise need to be completed manually. The tool can be run in two modes;

Update Existing Contracts: – agreed method since 2017. 
Retains existing Appointment ID and creates a new post and sequence. 
 

Create New Contracts: – no longer used.
Creates a new Appointment id, post and sequence 
It can be run at Employee, Post or Organisational level which means longer term there is the potential to use the tool for correcting errors on individual employee post/appt records. Potentially eliminating the need for users a having to create Staff Requests to correct hierarchy details on post/appt.

Percentage allowances

For v26+ of the software, percentage allowances must all have two retro codes: one which is used by the system to record £0 rows against it, and one which the Payroll team can use to manually record retro payments against the pay code. The following should be noted when setting up percentage allowance retro codes:
The system retro code should start with a 9 and should be prefixed with “SYS –“ (e.g. 9408 | SYS - BAND 1B % ARR). The system retro code (9XXX) must be set up with a multiplier of 0 to ensure that any system-generated arrears are calculated at £0. 
This is to work around an issue discovered in v26 upgrade testing where percentage allowances are calculated at the PAY290 stage. This will need to be revisited if the calculation of percentage allowances is moved to the standard PAY140 stage.
The manual retro code should start with a 2 and be prefixed with “Z –“, e.g. 2408 | Z - BAND 1B % ARR

All percentage allowance retro codes should be set up as value allowances. It is no longer possible to copy the percentage allowance pay code to create the retro as the Payment Type and Subset Type cannot be edited.

Pay codes cannot be removed once they have been used, but they can be disabled.

There are two options for disabling pay codes. 
A pay code can be disabled completely, which means that it is not available to enter or select in the Allowances screen in People Management and cannot be entered onto timesheets in CorePay. 
Alternatively a pay code can be disabled in People Management only, which means that it can still be entered onto timesheets manually or via the External Takeon process. A number of pay codes have been identified as being required only in CorePay and these have the rule ‘Enable/Disable for Allowances/Deductions’ set to Disable.

Issue with minor 20.0.23: Scaled Allowances not calculating using Allowance Multiplier
Detailed Description

Hello,

We have recently had the minor release 20.0.23 put into our HRISTEST environment. We have noticed a massive difference in how scaled allowances are paying in this version which I have separately mentioned in case 00058665 but I thought it would be much better to raise a separate case for this issue to make tracking easier.

Please see attached a document showing two examples of where scaled allowances are paying differently in version 20.0.23 than they were in 20.0.19. We believe that we paid when we first went live with Core Pay to have scaled allowances work in the way that they do so we're not happy with the way they are calculating in 20.0.23. There is a £9,920.90 difference in scaled allowances alone between the two versions, plus this increase is also taken into percentage allowances which are based on these scaled allowances which results in a larger increase, not to mention employer pension, NI etc. This is obviously a blocker for us going live with any later version than we're currently on.

As far as I can tell, the only release note in any of the versions between 20.0.19 and 20.0.23 is JIRA DS-13839, which states:
"Issue: Where a pay code is a scaled allowance the pay multiplier should only be used where the indicator "Clinical APA" is ticked on. Currently the system allowed the pay multiplier to be applied to all allowance types. Resolution: If an allowance was not using the Clinical APA indicator then the pay multiplier should be 1. Where the Clinical APA indicator is ticked, the pay multiplier can be less than 1."

This doesn't explain perfectly what I'm seeing, particularly (as Daniel Whelan explained in case 00058665) we don't seem to have the "Clinical APA" indicator in our environment, so I'm not sure if this JIRA is definitely the cause of the issues I'm seeing or not, but I can see nothing else in the release notes that would point to the problem. The only other changes to scaled allowances are changes to the retro process for scaled allowances, but I would have thought that this would be a change in a different process.

We cannot afford another large delay on investigating a blocker for the minor release so if this could be investigated urgently I would very much appreciate it.

Many thanks,
Simon

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
The Payroll team is responsible for informing the HR Functional Analysis team of any changes to the Payroll Officer calculations used across the catalogue of reports. A member of Payroll (normally the Payroll Systems Administrator, Tracy Roberts) will raise an incident with the HRIS Support Centre detailing the changes to be made to the different calculation variants (New Starter, Leaver, Pay Audit, and Casual Worker). HR Functional Analysis will then raise a change request based on the incident, detailing the changes to be made to each calculation variant, and the affected reports to amend. 

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?
The Payroll team is the owner of the Payroll Officer calculations. They are solely responsible for determining which departments and divisions each member of the Payroll team oversees, and how these are reflected in the Payroll Officer calculation variants. 
Changes to the Payroll Officer calculations must originate with the Payroll team, and the amended reports containing the changed calculations must be tested and signed off by the Payroll team (again, this is normally Tracy Roberts) before they can be implemented in the HR Reporting LIVE server. 

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 
Changes to the Payroll Officer calculations are Minor Changes within OSM. The environment owner for the HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE) is the Head of HR Systems, Jenny Lister, and she must provide change approval before any changes are implemented. 
The HR Functional Analysis team are the owners of the report catalogue* and are therefore responsible for making the changes to the Payroll Officer calculations within the affected reports, testing those changes, obtaining QA sign-off from the Payroll team, and implementing the changes by deploying the amended reports to the HR Reporting LIVE server once the Head of HR Systems has approved the OSM change request. 
*excluding reports owned by HR Analytics

How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
View the Payroll Officer calculations
All Payroll Officer calculations are clearly identified within the SQL queries of the affected reports. Open the .RDL files within Visual Studio to view and amend the calculations.
To jump directly to the calculations within the SQL, open the main report dataset for your .RDL and search for the text payroll_officer within the SQL code. You will be taken to a subquery within the report. The header specifies what variant of the Payroll Officer calculation the report contains, when the calculation was last updated, and the OSM Change ID of the most recent change. An example is shown below. 
NB!! Only the section of the calculation highlighted yellow is editable; the rest of the calculation must not be changed. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------------------- PAYROLL OFFICER QUERY BEGINS ---------------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
/*************** PAYROLL OFFICER CALCULATION *******************
** This report contains a payroll_officer calculation. 
** Variant: NEW STARTERS
** Last updated: OCTOBER 2020
** Change ID: 20011795
***************************************************************/

(SELECT
USER_FIELD5,

…..The editable portion of the calculation appears here, it will begin with CASE WHEN…..

END AS officer
FROM COREHR.PRBI_USER_FIELD5_LOV
ORDER BY USER_FIELD5, OFFICER) payroll_officer
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------------------- PAYROLL OFFICER QUERY ENDS -----------------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

Change a Payroll Officer calculation
The Payroll team will provide you with the updated calculations and will clearly indicate the different variants (New Starters, Leavers, Pay Audit, and Casual Workers). 
To amend a Payroll Officer calculation, first ensure you have the code for the appropriate calculation variant; e.g. do not update a New Starters calculation with code for the Leavers variant. 
Jump to the calculation within the report’s SQL code. Paste the updated calculation provided by Payroll over the segment of the calculation beginning CASE WHEN – this is the logic which specifies which payroll officers are responsible for which departments/divisions. An example is shown below:
(SELECT
USER_FIELD5,

CASE WHEN USER_FIELD5 IN( 'AJDEP', 'AUDEP', 'AWDEP', 'AYDEP', 'B6DEP', 'B9DEP', 'BHDEP', 'BSDEP', 'CCDEP', 'CFDEP', 'CMDEP', 'CQDEP' ........) 
THEN 'Jo' 
WHEN USER_FIELD5 IN( 'ACDIV', 'AEDEP', 'AEDIV', 'AFDIV', 'ATDEP', 'BADIV', 'BZDEP', 'CTDEP', 'CTDIV', 'CUDIV', 'CVDEP', 'CVDIV', 'CXDIV', 'CYDIV', 'CZDIV', 'D3DEP', 'D3DIV', 'DBDEP', 'DCDEP', 'DKDEP', 'DLDEP', 'DRDEP', 'DTDEP'........ ) 
THEN 'Diane'
WHEN
[.... the calculation will continue here.... ]

END AS officer
FROM COREHR.PRBI_USER_FIELD5_LOV
ORDER BY USER_FIELD5, OFFICER) payroll_officer

Save your changes to the .RDL file within Visual Studio and deploy it to the HR Reporting QA server so that the Payroll team can test the amended calculation. Once they confirm they are happy with the updated report, seek change approval for the OSM change and implement the changes on the HR Reporting LIVE server.

Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?
The Payroll team (normally the Payroll Systems Administrator, Tracy Roberts) are responsible for testing the changes to the Payroll Officer calculations once the affected reports have been updated with the amended calculations. Tracy must run the affected reports on the HR Reporting QA server and verify that the correct payroll officer is being returned for each department and division. 

Communications
Who needs to be informed (but not consulted) about this change? Detail when they should be informed (before or after the change).
Only the Payroll team are affected by changes to the Payroll Officer calculations, so it is sufficient to keep the change requestor (normally Tracy Roberts) informed of progress in implementing changes. 

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.
The output of the Payroll Officer calculation should be reflected in the shared data sets “LOV_Optional_PayrollOfficers” and “LOV_Optional_PayrollOfficers_CASUAL”. The list of UK bank sort codes is periodically updated by external companies, and we must incorporate these updates into our list of sort codes within CoreHR’s reference library. 

We periodically receive a link to the updated list of UK sort codes in an email from helpdesk@mailservice.sortingcodeselectronic.co.uk. This email is sent to InternalServices@it.ox.ac.uk; it is then logged as an Incident in HEAT and assigned to the HRIS Analysis team for processing.

Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

The HRIS Analysis team “owns” this information, insofar as they are responsible for keeping it up to date within Core. 

It is not necessary to keep the bank sort code list up to date every time an updated list is published as it is quite rare that a sort code is required which does not already exist within the system (and it is easy to add a new sort code manually) so approval to proceed with the change to sort codes is dependent upon resource availability within the HRIS Analyst team.

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in PeopleXD?

The standard process for creating or amending a location code is for the request to be made via an Incident that will be assigned to the Functional Analysis team within OSM. It should be clear from the Incident if the request is for a new location or an amendment to an existing location. Full address details should be provided in order to determine the requirements of the change. The address and area code may be detailed in one of the tasks within OSM if it is not within the main details section. The Functional Analysis will raise a standard change (see Change Management below).

If a change to the details of a code is required, you should remember that any changes to the reference data will affect all employees with the location code. You will therefore need to check that every employee with that location code is covered by this change. If not, you may need to create a new location code, or shift some employees on to a different code before you begin.

The format of the location description should ideally be a 2 digit alpha-numeric code followed by a <space>, a <hyphen>, and then a <space>. The description should be a maximum of 34 characters after the 2 digits and <hyphen>, example AL – BIOCHEMISTRY. It usually represents the dept. code followed by the description. This format is required because of a downstream interface. If multiple locations exist for one department code, then you may add a numeric digit e.g. AL1.

NB: The location description on the payslip is limited to 25 characters (including spaces), even though the field in the back office allows 40 characters to be entered.

The area code is the messenger code which is kept on the Access database which Data Services are currently responsible for. Data Services should be able to advise what the messenger code is for the building / post code which is being set up, as there is normally already another address at that location. 

If the location is changing it is worth bearing in mind that the area (messenger) code may also need to change. You can also check which locations fall under which messenger/area code by running the PERSUP06 report, or checking the export saved in the following folder:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\Locations

If the location you are setting up does not already exist on the system or the depts. database you will need to find the closest location and use the same messenger code as this location. Data Services Team will be able to assist with this as they will need to do the same on the Departments Database. 

NB: The Area Code is what is known in colloquial terms as the ‘Beat Bike’ number and is used for the University messengers who deliver the internal post.

The Online Application Form Profile is maintained via the Staff Portal. 

In order for applicants to be able to apply for a vacancy online, the following must be true:
•The vacancy must be set up in the CoreHR Back Office
•The vacancy ‘publish external’ dates must be ‘current’
•The vacancy must be authorised
•The vacancy must be set up to include a link to an active application form profile

•The online application form which is configured in the Portal
•The ‘Additional Questions’ section which is configured in the Back Office.

The online form consists of the Form Type and the Form Profile. The Form Type is the same for all versions of the application form. The Form Profiles are linked to a Form Type but each is individually configured to cater for the different types of roles recruited for and the requirements for those roles.

Understanding the form configuration
Each section and each item within the section has its own settings. To expand and view a section click on the symbol.

A tick in the ‘Include’ checkbox means that the section or item within a section is active and will appear in the Online Application Form Profile. 

The Short Description is displayed in the section heading, and the Detailed Description appears beneath the heading – see the example below.

Short Hint – if used, this will show text alongside or under the field label and is visible to the applicant. Space is limited so take care not to overlay any of the existing text or drop down boxes.

Help Text - this is additional information accessed via the to help applicants complete a field.
Standard Additional Questions section

The standard Additional Questions section is partially controlled via the Staff Portal and partially in the Back Office. 

The current questions and change history can be found in the Questionnaire Setup document under P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\Application Form Profile Maintenance\Application Form Profile - Questionnaire Section.

Within the portal, the configuration settings determine whether this section is active and included, and whether the section as a whole is mandatory for completion. The remainder of the settings, i.e. the question wording, question section headers, question type (free text, date, yes/no, numeric etc) and whether the question is mandatory/not mandatory are maintained via the CoreHR Back Office.

It is also possible to exclude this section from an application form and if required replace it with a new set of questions via a UDF created in the back office; see the section on non-standard additional questions.

All changes should be made in a test environment in the first instance. 

NB: It is not possible to amend or delete questions within a Question Category if it is linked to a vacancy. You will need to recreate a Question Category in order to amend or reorder the sequence questions.

The ‘Template Detail’ tab of the spreadsheet lists all sections that are controlled individually per Online Application Form Profile. Approved process for raising

Requests for Job Titles or Post Titles can be made by any user of Core or consumer of its information. 

It should ideally be requested with the following information although my not be dependent upon the individual raising:
Job Title Description (mandatory)
Job Title Code (max 6 chars – alpha numeric)
Is the Job Title to be active on Staff Requests?
Is the job title to be used for casuals or non-employees?

When this request has been received by the HRIS Support Centre a check should be made against existing Job Titles to ensure a similar code does not already exist.

Job title is not supposed to reflect seniority or other distinctions that can be differentiated by grade. If the “Job Title Description” includes grade or seniority then it should be rejected based on these grounds (see Additional Information section).

It is very likely that new job titles will be set to be available on staff requests. The only exceptions is job titles to be used for bucket posts (casual/non-employee posts) or job titles held for historic reasons.

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

All new requests for Job Titles should be run past the HRSEG group. Liz Mitchell or a representative of the HR Information Team should provide their approval to proceed with the change although all HRSEG members must be happy with the addition / change / removal of a Job Title.

The Reward Team must make a final decision as to whether the job title should be active for use in staff requests.

There may be cases where the HRSEG panel might want to see a job description or have further info such as Core Sub Category code and Category code, so an action in that case would be for HRIS Support to obtain the required information from the requestor and a follow up with relevant members of HRSEG in order to assess and obtain approval. This may need to be progressed outside of a formal HRSEG if the request is urgent.

If the Job Title needs to be set up in a rush you may use the HRSEG to achieve quick consultation and approval for the new code.

Should a request for a job title be rejected by HRSEG, Liz Mitchell is often happy to feed the reasoning back to the requestor.

Susanne Hemmerich (Head of HRIS Support Centre) to approve the change in HEAT. This is a standard change request and does not need to go via an enhancement request.

Added information regarding the VPN firewall to the BI layer

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?

There are two methods of restricting IP addresses covered in this article:
IP Restriction on accessing the CorePortal
Firewall restrictions on the VPN tunnel to the BI layer
IP Restriction on accessing the CorePortal
Changes to access to the CorePortal is likely to come via incident management but may come in the form of a new public subnet being created within the University Network. 

We will also need to review the configuration of the IP filtering when any new modules go live, plus we will need to periodically review the configuration in case Access Group alter the way IP filtering works or they include new options for filtering (which as standard are likely to come with no filtering).

Firewall restrictions on the VPN tunnel to the BI layer
There are two services which might require a change to the VPN tunnel firewall. These are the HR Reporting solution and SSIS Interfaces controlled by Software Solutions.

The IP addresses for the connect servers which the SQL servers sit on, plus SQL Developer, Visual Studio etc, are already whitelisted, but potentially they may move their subnet and need th IP addresses changed, or potentially further IP addresses could be created if they expanded the solution, but this should in theory be very stable. Any request for change would be initiated by MPST.

Similarly we have a solution for integration SSIS / SQL servers to sit on IP range 129.67.224.192/27, which has been added to the firewall IP range to allow the interfaces SQL server to connect to the PeopleXD BI layer.

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

The HRIS Service Manager will need to approve any expansion of the range of IP addresses able to access any part of the HRIS service. It is possible that a decision may need to be discussed with software solutions and MPST, or other IT Services teams (infosec) to confirm that the request is valid and to assess any risk involved.

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 

Standard change management applies, although the infosec team may need to be contacted to assess the security risks involved and for suggested testing which may include pen testing (although this is costly and is unlikely to be justified unless there is a large security risk).

Change requests will often be raised and coordinated by the team who requires the IP restriction to be added and will be signed off by the service owner for HR Systems. This may be the HR Systems Functional Analyst team but may be Software Solutions or MPST teams.

How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
Adding a new IP range to the portal access

For how to add IP ranges to be able to access the Core Portal in any environment please follow the instructions here:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\IP Filtering\How to apply IP filtering to CorePortal.docx

To open an IP Range to Discoverer you will need to raise a ticket with CoreHR and request that BT add the IP range to the firewall so that we can connect to Discoverer via that IP range. For an example of this see case #00147410 on the Core Community Portal.

Adding a new IP range to the portal access

To add new IP addresses to connect to the BI layer there are two steps:
Raise a request to Access Group to request that the IP address / range be added to the VPN firewall rules. The update will need to be made to both CW (Citywest Production data centre) and PW (Penrose Wharf our UAT data centre) firewall rules. 
This is done by raising a case with Access Group and providing an updated change request form listing the additional IP address range required. 
The change request forms are stored in the following location and must be updated when a new request is raised: P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Infrastructure\VPN Tunnels (BT)\Requests for Change
Request that MPST makes the same change at our end of the VPN tunnel. 
This is done via a task in OSM against the change request.

Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?

To test that it works you will need to ensure you are connected to the network in the IP range and that you can connect to a test environment which has the new IP filtering applied.

Communications

From MPST: 
There will be at least one fairly brief interruption in connectivity (most likely when each end is changed) notification should be given to HR Reporting users and anyone who relies on UPST's Interface Staging infrastructure.

N/A

Additional Background Information
Any other relevant information, links to supporting documentation etc.

Note that there is no IP filtering restrictions on e-Recruitment so it should be possible to access this from anywhere. 

Currently there is no difference in the restrictions between different environments but this may be something we wish to consider going forward.

Anyone who is connected to a local private VPN, Eduroam or OWL are not going to be able to connect directly to the University Network. This is an infosec requirement (details below) so anyone on these networks must VPN into the Oxford Network in order to access CoreHR.

You can identify which network or subnet someone is connected to by looking at their IP address against the list here: 
https://networks.it.ox.ac.uk/itss/netblocks/subnets

The following email is from Robin Stevens in InfoSec regarding the risks of opening up new networks and the importance of keeping OWL and Eduroam access limited:

The University has thirty /24 allocations under 192.76, many of which date back to the earliest days of IP networking in the University. In general these can treated the same way as IP addresses under 163.1.0.0/16 or 129.67.0.0/16. They are part of the University backbone network and subject to the same policies and monitoring, so from a security perspective I see no problem.

The only exceptions I'd suggest considering would be for OWL Visitor (intended for use only by non-members of the University) and Eduroam (which may be used by non-members; University members can use VPN for access to restricted resources). Other than for self-service and e-recruitment I suspect the need for wireless access to CoreHR is limited.

Further details are given on <https://help.it.ox.ac.uk/network/addresses/ipv4>.

I hope this helps, but let me know if you have any further questions.

Best wishes,

 Robin

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
The Reward Team and HR Analytics Team are responsible for producing and confirming the rates for existing grades. Requests for the creation of any new grades should be raised through these teams, or via the HRSEG on which these teams are represented.

To set up a new grade, the following items must be confirmed by the Reward and HR Analytics Teams:

Grade Code (e.g. 02S)
Grade Description (e.g. STANDARD GRADE 2)
The number of Scale Points on the grade (e.g. 9)
The full Scale Narrative of each point on the scale (e.g. POINT 1 NSP6)
Any Bar Points on the scale (e.g. points 7-9 are discretionary points)
The Yearly Full Time Rates (e.g. Point 1 - £15,765.00)
The Full Time Hours for the grade (e.g. 36.5)
Whether the grade should be available to select on new Staff Requests
Whether the grade will be subject to Cost of Living awards
The Effective Date of the new grade (likely to be the normal pay uplift date for the grade – e.g. 01-Aug-2021)

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?
Requests for new grades and changes to existing grades should come from and be discussed with the Reward, HR Analytics, and Payroll teams. Grade-related requests will usually be discussed and agreed at HRSEG (Human Resources Systems Evaluation Group). However, if the changes requested must be implemented urgently, they may be agreed by another means e.g. email.

New Grades
Pensions should be consulted, as they will need to confirm which Pension Scheme should be assigned to the new grade. 

Payroll should be consulted, as they will need to if they want to publish the grade to the web (see the Affected Reports section below).

The X5 team will need to be informed of the new grade as soon as possible, so that they can check whether any staff who will be on the grade are likely to be involved in research – if so, the new grade will need to be set up in X5 by their system support team. (X5 provides administrators and principal investigators (PIs) with a tool for costing research grant applications.) 

Changes to existing grades or rates
Changes to existing grades or rates may result in employee records being updated, e.g. where a scale point is being removed. The HR Analytics team should therefore be consulted as the changes to employee records may need to be undertaken by the Data Service Team. The X5 team have asked for as much notice as possible in terms of rate changes. Ideally when these are being tested in the non-prod environment but certainly ahead of the update into production. 

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 
The change process applicable at the time of the change should be followed. The current process is to create a change request in OSM which is approved by the relevant approver. Ideally, the change should be approved prior to being put into QA testing. 

The HRIS Functional Analysis Team are responsible for setting up new grades & points and amending existing grades & points. 

If a new grade is being created and the Full Time Hours value for the grade is not present in the list of ‘FTE Hours’ in the database, a new value will need to be created. This can either be done via a separate change or added as a separate element to the current change. For information on how to add a new FTE Hours value, refer to the document How To – View and Maintain Reference Data.

Note that, in some cases, it may be necessary to move employees onto a new grade or point. For example, the lowest scale point (4) was removed from Apprentice Grade 01A in Feb 2018 as it fell below the minimum Living Wage. Employees who were appointed to this grade/scale therefore needed to be moved onto the next highest scale point (5).

Changes to employee records are usually carried out by the HRIS Data Service Administrator. In this case it may be necessary to contact the individual departments to notify them about/discuss the proposed changes. 

Template for raising a Change in OSM – NEW GRADES/RATES

Reference data items can only be removed if they are not being used in the database. 

If the change request specifies to remove an item then first ensure the value is not in use anywhere in the database. Run or create a Discoverer report to check whether the data item is present anywhere in the database tables.

Most reference table maintenance screens check for referential integrity, but not all. If the item is in use an error message will appear if you attempt to delete it.

If the item is in use, then it will need to be established whether the relevant records are to be updated to remove these entries. Depending on the data item, this may already have been discussed as part of the change request process and a plan put in place. If not, you should check with the person requesting the change what the plans are for updating the affected records before you proceed.

If the item is in use and the database records are not going to be updated then it is accepted practice to rename the entry to reflect the fact that it should no longer be used e.g. Prefix the description with ‘Z – DO NOT USE.’ followed by the original description or an abbreviated version.

Some data items also have an Active flag. If an item cannot be deleted from the database un-ticking the active flag will normally cause it to be removed from some drop down lists – but not necessarily all.

Different FTE Hours

Different leave years
Different Base Entitlement

Mandatory holiday dates (e.g. public holiday and fixed closure dates)

The requirement for a UDF will often come from a Business requirement, so the Business Process Advisor within the HRIS Support Centre will usually lead on gathering requirements for a new UDF.

A “MASTER UDF Template” excel file is stored in the following folder which should be completed, usually by or with assistance from an HRIS Analyst, outlining how the UDF should be set up within the system:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\UDFs

Completed UDF templates should be saved within a sub-folder named to reflect the UDF to be set up. Any changes to the template during the process (see Change Management section) should be saved within this sub-folder.

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

New UDFs and changes to existing UDFs are generally requested by the relevant business area, often within Personnel Services. The HRIS Business Process Adviser will usually lead on/be involved in the consultation and gathering requirements for both new UDFs and changes to existing UDFs.

The Change Request will be approved by the relevant approver in OSM – usually the Head of HRIS or their nominated deputy.

You must give early notification of the intention to change a UDF or create a new UDF to the HR Analytics team, or HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, to consider the impact on the data warehouse.

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 

New UDFs and changes to existing UDFs should be managed via the Change Request process in OSM.

New UDFs could be a candidate for a Standard Change but this needs to be discussed and agreed.

If during the course of the build or testing process any requirement for changes to the UDF are identified, the template should be amended and saved (with a new version number) in the UDF folder. Only the latest version of the UDF Template should be attached to the Change Record, so previous versions may need to be removed (if possible).

How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
Adding a new UDF

UDFs are ‘forms’ that can be used to store additional information which cannot be recorded anywhere else in the Personnel module. There is a standard template that cannot be altered although the field descriptions and content can be configured.

UDFs can be held at Appointment, Person (employee) or Recruitment level. This is determined via the Advanced settings when creating a UDF.

Person and Appointment level UDFs are accessed within the employee record in People Management in the User Defined Field section. Recruitment UDFs are less common and relate to additional sections added to the online Application Forms. The Application Form with inbuilt supporting statement has one UDF and the Apprenticeship Application form has three. These provide additional sections that could not be included any other way.

Each UDF is assigned a Reference Code and Description when it is first created. 

The reference code is restricted to 6 characters (alpha). It is used for reporting purposes to identify the relevant data items. It is not displayed in the UDF. 

The Description is displayed within the UDF in the Select Detail or Selection menus as applicable. There is a 40 character limit for the Description.

There are 12 Fields available. Each field can be configured as a List item (LoV), Text (free text field), or Date. (There are other options but we don’t use them.)

UDFs are configured in the Portal via People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects.

The User Description (Data Label) is displayed against each input field in the UDF and appears in the UDF as shown below:

Data Type determines what can be entered into that field. E.g Date, text, list item

List items form a drop-down list that can be selected within a field in the UDF. 

The data items are stored in the database table under the Item number and not the field description/label. For example ‘Inducted By’ will be stored under Item 3 in the database. This causes issues when User Descriptions or Field Items need to be amended.

Full details on creating a new UDF can be found in the How To guide. 

Changing a UDF

Making amendments to UDFs is technically straight forward; However, great care must be taken as existing data will not automatically feed through to the data which has already been entered. This is because data is entered against an Item Number generic across all UDFs rather than against a field specific to that UDF. Please read the information below before proceeding.

Adding a new List Item to an existing list
Adding a new List Item to an existing list will not have any impact on existing data. 
You can also amend the order in which the list items are displayed by re-entering the entire list or swapping items around. 

Editing existing List Items:
Any changes made will apply to all existing records where the edited field(s) have previously been selected. However the UDF itself will not update automatically on the individual records and an error message will be displayed whenever the UDF is opened. To correct this the individual UDF records must be updated to re-select the edited item. This is a manual process as each UDF needs to be opened within every affected employee record, the updated field(s) reselected and the changes saved. 

For this reason changes can only be made with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the employee records.

List Items - The preferred approach is to add a new list item, update the affected records to select the ‘new’ list item and then untick the active indicator against the ‘old’ list item.

Example:
Right to Work List item ‘EEA Family Permit’ was changed to ‘EEA Family Permit (6 months)’ in Jan18. A new list item was added for the new description, the affected employee records were updated to select the ‘new’ description and the ‘old’ list item showing the previous description was made inactive.

Editing existing Field items:
Any changes to the Description will apply to all existing records where the edited field(s) have previously been selected. Unlike the List items the Field items will update automatically and no changes will be required to the individual records. However, any reports containing the edited UDF will need to be updated as the column headers will refer to the previous Field Item Description.

Removing Field Items or changing the order in which they are displayed
Due to the way in which the items are stored in the database i.e. against the item number not the User Description, this is not a straightforward change and has the similar limitations to editing field items. 

Depending upon the number of changes and the number of affected records you may need to consider creating a new UDF and migrating the data via the Data Upload tool available in the Core Portal. 

For this reason changes can only be made with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the employee records.

Removing List Items 
You can remove items from the list of values by making them inactive, or by deleting the item and if necessary re-ordering the list. However, any user data which has already been entered using the deleted list item will not be correct but will not display an error message. 

For this reason list items can only be deleted with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the affected employee records.

Changing where the UDF appears
If you need to change where the UDF is displayed (i.e. from Appointment to Person) it is possible to simply change the tick box under the Advanced tab. However any new records created after the change will appear in a different table so any user data entered against the previous position will not be visible in the new position. The historic information will not be lost but you will be unable to view it in the back office unless you keep the old “position” ticked, which will cause confusion.

Therefore, depending on the change required, it may be better to set up a new “replacement” UDF in the new position and then remove the old UDF from use (following the “Removing a UDF” steps). 

If you need to transfer historic data from the old version of the UDF into the new version this can be done via the Data Upload tool in the Core Portal – refer to HOW TO Prepare Data for the Data Migration Tool

Removing a UDF

Removing a UDF with no user data entered
If no user data has been entered against a UDF you are able to delete the row from the User Defined Fields screen.

Navigate to: People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects.
