Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?

Normally the HRIS Business Analyst or HRIS Process Team would undertake user acceptance/functional testing, although this may also be done by end users depending on which groups of users will be expected to use the report.

Communications
Who needs to be informed (but not consulted) about this change? Detail when they should be informed (before or after the change).

The Right to Work UDF is used in an interface so the ‘SSM – Business Integration Technologies Team’ within Software Solutions will need to be informed of any potential changes to this UDF ahead of any work being done – see Downstream Systems & Processes.

It is likely that user communication will be required, particularly with a new UDF, depending on who the target audience of the UDF will be. As UDFs are normally raised through the Process Team or Business Analyst, training guidance and communication will normally be considered and taken care of.

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.

Data Warehouse
Most UDFs are migrated into the Data Warehouse and split out into individual tables according to their code. There are then views built which translate the underlying columns (text1, text2 etc) into their actual headings. If you are changing the structure of a UDF (introducing a new field, changing the heading) there will be changes required to the warehouse. If you are replacing a UDF with a new version with a new name then all of the tables in the warehouse will need to be rebuilt. You must inform the HR Analytics Team, or the HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, of the changes being made.

Interfaces
UDFs are rarely used within interface files but information in the Right to Work UDF is taken by the following interfaces:
CoreHR to Access Databases ‘staff including casuals’ interface (Interface Staging PROGID_170), which sends email to HRIS Support with subject lines following this pattern: Interface Staging: req=hris/pcapps/staff ref=%ID% status=SUCCESS. 
CoreHR to EAP interface (Interface Staging PROGID to be confirmed), which sends Right to Work data for all staff to the Examiner Appointments and Payments system, transforming the CoreHR data into “Right to Work = TRUE/FALSE” values. 

NB!! Rules have been built into these interfaces to extract the data from the RTW2 UDF. Any proposed changes to the UDF or the description of the data labels within it will need to be fed back to the SSM-BITE team before the changes are made, so that the interfaces can be modified as necessary to continue picking up the required RTW information. 

This is particularly important as UDFs are set up against generic Name/Description/Types, e.g. Reference Code, Item1, User Field1. Changes to the structure of a specific UDF need to be explicitly communicated to the SSM-BITE team so that they can ensure that the necessary parameters are in place in the interface to pick up the data from the modified UDF. 

Affected Reports
Are there any standard reports which may need to be updated following this change?

There will almost always be reports affected by a change to a UDF as there is normally at least one accompanying report with that UDF. However this would depend on the UDF being updated as there is not one “UDF” report, rather they are reported on separately using the UDF “Reference Code” to only return data of a specific UDF type within any given report.

Any changes to UDFs (including moving from one UDF to another for the same purpose – e.g. ‘RTW’ to ‘RTW2’) will need to be reflected in the report. In a similar way to interfaces, the reports will still run but the data they return is likely to be out of sequence or not make sense if a report is not updated, and will therefore return inaccurate information.

Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
New Pension Schemes
The Payroll and Pensions teams are responsible for requesting the creation of new pension schemes. 

Pensions should discuss the requirements for the new pension scheme with Payroll. Payroll must then complete a Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet and send it through to the HRIS Support Centre, together with details of any new or amended pay codes which are required to support the new scheme. The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request for a new pension scheme as a change within OSM. 

The Pensions team will likely give a few months of advance warning when a new scheme needs to be set up, so that there is sufficient time to set it up in a test environment and check that the payroll and reporting outputs for the new scheme are all correct. 

Changes to Existing Schemes
The Pensions team is responsible for requesting changes to existing pension schemes. 

Pensions must raise a support-desk call to the Functional Analysis team and provide details of the changes to be made. If the changes are for contribution rates, Pensions must supply the official “schedule of contributions” from the scheme provider showing the new rates and their effective date. 

The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with Payroll and Pensions to test the changes before making them live. 

Changes to the State Pension Age (SPA)
The Pensions team is responsible for requesting changes to the State Pension Age. 

The State Pension Age (also called the “State Retirement Age”) is the age at which an individual can begin claiming their state pension, based on their gender and date of birth. It is set by the UK government, and is periodically revised. 

The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with Pensions to test the updated State Pension Age parameters before making them live. 

Changes to Auto-Enrolment
The Pensions team is responsible for requesting any changes to the Auto-Enrolment functionality, including:
The parameters for auto-enrolment (e.g. earnings thresholds) 
The default pension schemes for auto-enrolment
The notifications (emails and letters) sent to employees
Pensions must raise a support-desk call to the HRIS Functional Analysis team and provide details of the changes to be made, including updated text and PDF attachments for the notifications (where applicable). 

The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with the Pensions team to test the changes before they are made live. 

Changes to Pensions Reports
The Pensions team is responsible for requesting changes to any of the reports they use, and for requesting the creation of new reports. 

Pensions must raise a support-desk call to the HRIS Functional Analysis team and provide either:
Details of the changes to be made to the existing report(s)
Details of the new report(s) they would like to be created
Justification for the changes/new report(s)
The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with the Pensions team to test the changed/new report before it is made live. 

Changes to the Profund Interface
The Pensions team is responsible for confirming whether a new pension scheme or Additional Voluntary Contribution (AVC) scheme must be added to the Profund Interface Report (PERPEN26). 

Pensions must confirm the report field in which the new pension scheme should appear. Note that a new AVC must be mapped to both the related pension scheme (e.g. OSPS) and the relevant pay codes for the AVC.

The Access Group are responsible for supporting the Profund Interface report, so the HRIS Functional Analysis team must raise a case on the The Access Group Community service desk, providing details of the new scheme/AVC to be added to PERPEN26, and the relevant report fields and pay code mappings. Once The Access Group have made the necessary changes, HRIS Functional Analysis must liaise with Pensions to test the report before asking Core to make it live. 

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?
The Pensions team is the business owner of all pensions-related information. They are responsible for ensuring that new pension schemes are created, as necessary, and that all existing pension schemes are kept up-to-date with the latest scheme-provider regulations. 

Pensions must consult with the Payroll team before any pension scheme is created or changed, and Payroll need to sign off on all changes/new schemes before they can be made live. 

The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process all requests for changes to pension schemes and/or creation of new pension schemes as changes within OSM. The Head of HR Systems must approve the changes before they can be implemented in the live environment. 

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 
Requests to create new pension schemes, amend existing pension schemes, update Auto-Enrolment configuration, or change/create reports for the Pensions team, should all be processed as Minor Changes in OSM. These changes require consultation with and approval from the following stakeholders:
Payroll
Pensions
Head of HR Systems
The HRIS Functional Analysis team is responsible for implementing the changes and working with Payroll and Pensions to test that new schemes/reports are working as expected, and that changes to existing schemes/reports work correctly without negatively impacting existing functionality. 

The following tasks may be appropriate to add to OSM changes for Pensions requests. Not all of them will be applicable in every case, but it is worth considering whether they are necessary. 

New Pension Schemes
Create the new pay codes for the pension scheme
Create the new pension scheme codes
Update the Auto-Enrolment rules (where applicable)
Update the Auto-Enrolment notifications (where applicable) 
Update the PERPEN26_Profund Interface report
Add the new pay codes to the Linacre College payroll reports
Changes to Existing Schemes [tasks depend on the kind of change requested]
Update the EE or ER contribution rates
Update the EE or ER Deduction pay codes on the scheme
Update to the VSC contribution rates on the scheme (USS only)
Update any other details on the scheme
Update the Auto-Enrolment rules 
Update the Auto-Enrolment notifications 

Changes to the State Pension Age (SPA)
Update the State Pension Ages table in Core|Portal > CorePay > Payroll Dashboard > UK Tax Rates > General
Update any reports which reference the SPA
Changes to Auto-Enrolment
Update the parameters for auto-enrolment
Update the default pension schemes for auto-enrolment
Update the notifications sent to employees
Update the attachments included with the notifications
Changes to Pensions Reports
Update the conditions and/or calculations to refer to new/changed schemes
Update the conditions and/or calculations to refer to new/changed pay codes
Update the report specification document
Changes to the Profund Interface
Confirm PERPEN26 report field for new pension scheme
Confirm pay code mappings for new AVC
Raise call with The Access Group to add new scheme/AVC to PERPEN26
How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
Adding a new pension scheme

Note: The Payroll team must provide a completed Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet, containing the details of the new scheme, before the scheme can be created. 

New pension schemes are created at Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme. 

Full details can be found in the document HOW TO – Maintain Pension Schemes. 

Editing an existing pension scheme
The amount employees (“EEs”) and employers (“ERs”) must contribute to a pension scheme (the “contribution rate”) is liable to change periodically. The scheme provider will supply an updated “Schedule of Contributions” detailing the rate changes and the date the changes will go into effect. The Pensions team must pass this information to the HRIS Functional Analysis team for processing.

Likewise, the pay codes attached to a pension scheme may change, although this is very rare once a pension scheme is in place. 

Changes to pension schemes at Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme. 

Note: Any change to contribution rates may require an update to the Auto-Enrolment notifications to reflect the new rates. This should be specified by the Pensions team, who must provide the new text for the notifications as well as the new PDF attachments.

Full details about how to amend existing pension schemes can be found in the document HOW TO – Maintain Pension Schemes. 
Removing a Pension Scheme
Pension schemes are not deleted when they fall out of use; instead, they are renamed with the prefix “~ZZ - “. 

Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?
The Payroll and Pensions teams are responsible for testing new pension schemes and any changes to existing pension schemes, to ensure the contributions are correctly calculated and appear correctly on reports and payroll outputs. 
Pensions and HRIS Functional Analysis are responsible for testing changes to the pension reports, and to the Auto-Enrolment functionality, to ensure any new/changed reports work as expected, and that any updates to the Auto-Enrolment functionality are working correctly. 

Communications
Who needs to be informed (but not consulted) about this change? Detail when they should be informed (before or after the change).

The Auto-Enrolment communications (both letters and emails) need to be updated with the new pension contribution rates whenever these change for a given scheme, so that newly-enrolled members of the scheme are aware of the current rates. 

The latest version of the Auto Enrolment PDF, which includes rates, can be found at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Auto Enrolment\Letters for email notifications. Liaise with the Pension Administration Specialist (Linda Howse) for any updates or a new version or be provided. 

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.
USS Interface
New USS pension schemes will need to be configured in the USS Interface configuration screen. Pensions will need to confirm which columns need to be ticked against the new pension scheme, they can do this using the “USS Mapping CDD” in the following folder:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Pensions\USS Interface

There is also a user guide within the folder which explains where to navigate to complete the configuration.

Profund Interface
New schemes will have an effect on the Profund Interface. Any changes will need to be communicated to Core to amend the report – see the “Consultation & Approval” section for more information.

In addition, any changes to the Pay Codes attached to a pension scheme will need to be fed back to Core as they are likely to require amendments to the report. 

Pay Scales Interface
The Pay Scales Interface (Finance and X5 teams) is likely to be affected by changes to Pension Rates. You can email the X5 team with the new rates and the Payroll team will run a report to get the new rates for the finance website. Please see the “Affected Reports” section for further information.

Affected Reports
Are there any standard reports which may need to be updated following this change?
Payroll & Pensions Reports
The NHS Pension Scheme Rate is hard coded into the PAYPEN02 report; these must be updated whenever there is a change to the NHS Pension Scheme rates. You may need to code something yourself if a new scheme is set up.

Pay Scales Interface
The following reports need to be run and checked when there is any change to pension rates:
PERSUP14 - Pay scale interface to X5
PERSUP15 - Pay scale interface to finance website

These reports are built to pick up the most recent rates within the system for NI and Pensions so once the new rates have all been loaded the payroll team can run the PERSUP15 report from HR Reporting and the Functional Analysis Team can run the PERSUP14 report using SQL Developer and pass it to the X5 team. 

Please note, depending on the amount of changes occurring, the X5 team do not necessarily need to have the file sent, you can just email them with the updated rate and they can update a file manually (see the Additional Background Information section), but you should still ensure that the report is working as expected so that if you do send a file (when there’s an increase to salary or NI rates) then the pension aspect is taken into consideration. 

The PERSUP14 SQL files for use in SQL Developer are stored in the following depository:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reports\SQL and RDL Library\Functional Analyst SQL Depository

Please see the Statement of Work document in the following folder for further information on how to run and distribute the reports: P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Interfaces\Pay400 (Grades Interface to X5 Finance Web)\

Additional Background Information
Any other relevant information, links to supporting documentation etc.

OSM Incident #10204821: The X5 team confirmed they do not require a copy of the PERPSUP14 report after a change to pension rates; it is sufficient just to email x5helpdesk@it.ox.ac.uk with details of the new rates.

The Pensions team is responsible for requesting changes to any of the reports they use, and for requesting the creation of new reports. 

Pensions must raise a support-desk call to the HRIS Functional Analysis team and provide either:
Details of the changes to be made to the existing report(s)
Details of the new report(s) they would like to be created
Justification for the changes/new report(s)
The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with the Pensions team to test the changed/new report before it is made live. 

Changes to the Profund Interface
The Pensions team is responsible for confirming whether a new pension scheme or Additional Voluntary Contribution (AVC) scheme must be added to the Profund Interface Report (PERPEN26). 

Pensions must confirm the report field in which the new pension scheme should appear. Note that a new AVC must be mapped to both the related pension scheme (e.g. OSPS) and the relevant pay codes for the AVC.

The Access Group are responsible for supporting the Profund Interface report, so the HRIS Functional Analysis team must raise a case on the The Access Group Community service desk, providing details of the new scheme/AVC to be added to PERPEN26, and the relevant report fields and pay code mappings. Once The Access Group have made the necessary changes, HRIS Functional Analysis must liaise with Pensions to test the report before asking Core to make it live. 

Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?
The Pensions team is the business owner of all pensions-related information. They are responsible for ensuring that new pension schemes are created, as necessary, and that all existing pension schemes are kept up-to-date with the latest scheme-provider regulations. 

Pensions must consult with the Payroll team before any pension scheme is created or changed, and Payroll need to sign off on all changes/new schemes before they can be made live. 

The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process all requests for changes to pension schemes and/or creation of new pension schemes as changes within OSM. The Head of HR Systems must approve the changes before they can be implemented in the live environment. 

Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 
Requests to create new pension schemes, amend existing pension schemes, update Auto-Enrolment configuration, or change/create reports for the Pensions team, should all be processed as Minor Changes in OSM. These changes require consultation with and approval from the following stakeholders:
Payroll
Pensions
Head of HR Systems
The HRIS Functional Analysis team is responsible for implementing the changes and working with Payroll and Pensions to test that new schemes/reports are working as expected, and that changes to existing schemes/reports work correctly without negatively impacting existing functionality. 

The following tasks may be appropriate to add to OSM changes for Pensions requests. Not all of them will be applicable in every case, but it is worth considering whether they are necessary. 

New Pension Schemes
Create the new pay codes for the pension scheme
Create the new pension scheme codes
Update the Auto-Enrolment rules (where applicable)
Update the Auto-Enrolment notifications (where applicable) 
Update the PERPEN26_Profund Interface report
Add the new pay codes to the Linacre College payroll reports
Changes to Existing Schemes [tasks depend on the kind of change requested]
Update the EE or ER contribution rates
Update the EE or ER Deduction pay codes on the scheme
Update to the VSC contribution rates on the scheme (USS only)
Update any other details on the scheme
Update the Auto-Enrolment rules 
Update the Auto-Enrolment notifications 

Changes to the State Pension Age (SPA)
Update the State Pension Ages table in Core|Portal > CorePay > Payroll Dashboard > UK Tax Rates > General
Update any reports which reference the SPA
Changes to Auto-Enrolment
Update the parameters for auto-enrolment
Update the default pension schemes for auto-enrolment
Update the notifications sent to employees
Update the attachments included with the notifications
Changes to Pensions Reports
Update the conditions and/or calculations to refer to new/changed schemes
Update the conditions and/or calculations to refer to new/changed pay codes
Update the report specification document
Changes to the Profund Interface
Confirm PERPEN26 report field for new pension scheme
Confirm pay code mappings for new AVC
Raise call with The Access Group to add new scheme/AVC to PERPEN26
How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
Adding a new pension scheme

Note: The Payroll team must provide a completed Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet, containing the details of the new scheme, before the scheme can be created. 

New pension schemes are created at Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme. 

Full details can be found in the document HOW TO – Maintain Pension Schemes. 

Editing an existing pension scheme
The amount employees (“EEs”) and employers (“ERs”) must contribute to a pension scheme (the “contribution rate”) is liable to change periodically. The scheme provider will supply an updated “Schedule of Contributions” detailing the rate changes and the date the changes will go into effect. The Pensions team must pass this information to the HRIS Functional Analysis team for processing.

Likewise, the pay codes attached to a pension scheme may change, although this is very rare once a pension scheme is in place. 

Changes to pension schemes at Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme. 

Note: Any change to contribution rates may require an update to the Auto-Enrolment notifications to reflect the new rates. This should be specified by the Pensions team, who must provide the new text for the notifications as well as the new PDF attachments.

Full details about how to amend existing pension schemes can be found in the document HOW TO – Maintain Pension Schemes. 
Removing a Pension Scheme
Pension schemes are not deleted when they fall out of use; instead, they are renamed with the prefix “~ZZ - “. 

Testing 
Who would normally be responsible for testing? Are there standard items to test?
The Payroll and Pensions teams are responsible for testing new pension schemes and any changes to existing pension schemes, to ensure the contributions are correctly calculated and appear correctly on reports and payroll outputs. 
Pensions and HRIS Functional Analysis are responsible for testing changes to the pension reports, and to the Auto-Enrolment functionality, to ensure any new/changed reports work as expected, and that any updates to the Auto-Enrolment functionality are working correctly. 

Communications
Who needs to be informed (but not consulted) about this change? Detail when they should be informed (before or after the change).

Where changes are made to Pension Schemes, particularly in the structure of how a pension scheme is configured, the HR Analytics team will need to be informed of the change being made. This is required so that the team can understand changes to pension payments over time when analysing payroll data for financial statements etc.

The Auto-Enrolment communications (both letters and emails) need to be updated with the new pension contribution rates whenever these change for a given scheme, so that newly-enrolled members of the scheme are aware of the current rates. 

The latest version of the Auto Enrolment PDF, which includes rates, can be found at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Auto Enrolment\Letters for email notifications. Liaise with the Pension Administration Specialist (Linda Howse) for any updates or a new version or be provided. 

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.
USS Interface
New USS pension schemes will need to be configured in the USS Interface configuration screen. Pensions will need to confirm which columns need to be ticked against the new pension scheme, they can do this using the “USS Mapping CDD” in the following folder:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Pensions\USS Interface

There is also a user guide within the folder which explains where to navigate to complete the configuration.

Profund Interface
New schemes will have an effect on the Profund Interface. Any changes will need to be communicated to Core to amend the report – see the “Consultation & Approval” section for more information.

In addition, any changes to the Pay Codes attached to a pension scheme will need to be fed back to Core as they are likely to require amendments to the report. 

Pay Scales Interface
The Pay Scales Interface (Finance and X5 teams) is likely to be affected by changes to Pension Rates. You can email the X5 team with the new rates and the Payroll team will run a report to get the new rates for the finance website. Please see the “Affected Reports” section for further information.

Affected Reports
Are there any standard reports which may need to be updated following this change?
Payroll & Pensions Reports
The NHS Pension Scheme Rate is hard coded into the PAYPEN02 report; these must be updated whenever there is a change to the NHS Pension Scheme rates. You may need to code something yourself if a new scheme is set up.

Pay Scales Interface
The following reports need to be run and checked when there is any change to pension rates:
PERSUP14 - Pay scale interface to X5
PERSUP15 - Pay scale interface to finance website

These reports are built to pick up the most recent rates within the system for NI and Pensions so once the new rates have all been loaded the payroll team can run the PERSUP15 report from HR Reporting and the Functional Analysis Team can run the PERSUP14 report using SQL Developer and pass it to the X5 team. 

Please note, depending on the amount of changes occurring, the X5 team do not necessarily need to have the file sent, you can just email them with the updated rate and they can update a file manually (see the Additional Background Information section), but you should still ensure that the report is working as expected so that if you do send a file (when there’s an increase to salary or NI rates) then the pension aspect is taken into consideration. 

The PERSUP14 SQL files for use in SQL Developer are stored in the following depository:
P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reports\SQL and RDL Library\Functional Analyst SQL Depository

Please see the Statement of Work document in the following folder for further information on how to run and distribute the reports: P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Interfaces\Pay400 (Grades Interface to X5 Finance Web)\

Additional Background Information
Any other relevant information, links to supporting documentation etc.

OSM Incident #10204821: The X5 team confirmed they do not require a copy of the PERPSUP14 report after a change to pension rates; it is sufficient just to email x5helpdesk@it.ox.ac.uk with details of the new rates. 
OSM Incident #11464475: The X5 team have asked to receive as much notice as possible in terms of changes. Ideally when these are being tested in the non-prod environment, but certainly ahead of the update into production.

Background
The onboarding checklist is based on the items gathered in the paper New Starter Data Collection form and is intended to replace this form, providing a more secure and efficient method for gathering the information.

On/Offboarding checklists are configured via the Social Hub configuration widget which has been added to the Administrator Dashboard.

Following a successful pilot the onboarding checklist was launched to the whole University from 1 November 2023. Through the use of Staff Groups the checklist was released to New Starters, Rehires and New Appointments (NAA, NAT, NC, CIGI, CIGD) and applied to appointments which started on or after 1 November 2023.

Checklists are made up of a variety of different items configured to form tasks. These include:

Input items – standard items – e.g. Bank details
UDFs – Person level UDFs can be added to the checklist for completion by the employee. In all cases a new UDF is created. NB: Appointment level UDFs are not available but we have raised this with Access Group
Surveys – these are ‘questionnaires’ specifically configured by us mostly to gather data required for Appointment UDFs
Custom Forms – provide information e.g. A welcome message from the Pro VC/HR Director and links to staff handbooks
 
Onboarding tasks apply to all appointments that meet the criteria specified in the staff groups where the start date is on or after the activation date. 

Exceptions
When an appointment is commenced on or after 1 November 2023, onboarding tasks will be assigned even if the effective date of the appointment is before the activation date. Raised with Access Group case # 64406103.
Where tasks have previously been assigned and completed, a further qualifying appointment may not result in the tasks being assigned again. However, any tasks that were not previously assigned and completed will be created and assigned to the employee. E.g. an individual moving from a non clincial to a clincal role will be assigned the tasks required for clinical appointments.

When activating onboarding, the system will create and assign tasks for all active employees that meet the criteria specified in the staff groups. It will then mark all tasks as completed where the appointment start date is before the activation date.

Exceptions 
When onboarding was re-set a few examples were identified where the tasks has been automatically completed incorrectly. Raised with Access Group case # 64406103.

Staff Grouping
Staff groups control (restrict) which questions are presented to each employee. There are a large number of criteria to choose from when creating Staff Groups including, Category and Sub Category, Appointment Reason, Department and Division. In preparation for the wider roll out new staff groups were created to cater for Casual workers and TSS workers plus the New appointment reason codes. 

The full details of Staff Groups can be found in the Configuration document.

Multiple staff group restrictions can be applied to a task. Each task on the checklist has at least one staff group restriction assigned.

A matrix showing the allocation of questions per staff group can be found here.

Automatic notifications
Automatic notifications have been enabled as part of the wider roll out. 

The notifications are generated once a week on Sunday and sent to every employee with outstanding task/s to remind them to log in and complete them. 

A separate notification can also be sent to employees whose appointment start date is within the two-week period following the notification date (not activated). 

Apart from configuring the email there is no flexibility within the automated notifications and there is no way to specify/restrict who receives a notification. 
Social Activity
Social activity is optional for departments to use. This section only appears in the Social Hub if an HR admin has added a message to the employee via the employee record.

Tiles
On the landing page there are a number of images (tiles) that contain links to other pages on the University website. These are created as Custom pages and then added to the Landing Page

Security
The onboarding and offboarding checklists are accessed via the Social Hub. Access to onboarding has been included in the following menu profiles:

COREPORTAL_HR_ADMIN_WEB
COREPORTAL_HR_ADMIN_WEB_RO
COREPORTAL_HR_DATA_SERVICES
COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE

A new org role has been created to enable the Insight reports to be shared with a group rather than on an individual user basis:

ONB - Onboarding Administrator

For configuring the checklist and reports the following menu profiles are required:
SOCIAL_ONBOARD_ADMIN
AG_INSIGHT

Auditing
Auditing has been switched on for the following views:
ONBOARDING_PERS_COMPLETE_ITEMS
ONBOARDING_ASSIGNED_ITEMS

Insight reports
Departments can monitor progress of checklist items for employees in their department via the Onboarding screen accessed from the Command centre. However, Insight reports have also been created as follows:–

PERINS02 - Incomplete Onboarding checklist items – shows outstanding tasks per employee/department

PERINS01 - Completed Onboarding checklist items CLINICAL – returns all of the data entered into the individual tasks that are not automatically updated on the employee record e.g. surveys. Includes Clinical details and NHS Pension details.

PERINS01 - Completed Onboarding checklist items NON CLINICAL – returns all of the data entered into the individual tasks that are not automatically updated on the employee record e.g. surveys. Excludes Clinical details and NHS Pension details.

Resetting onboarding
If onboarding is reset at any time Access Group have confirmed that the following items are deleted as part of the reset:

It should also be noted that although surveys are not deleted there can be an issue with reporting if the same surveys are added into the new checklist. To avoid confusion, where existing surveys need to be updated, they should be deleted and a new survey created. Deleting a survey will also delete the Insight view.
Things to note
There is a character limit for field/column names in the reports. This does not correspond to the character limit on the checklist fields. 

Take care with field names when creating surveys. Ensure that every field name is clearly defined and not repeated so that when adding the item to a report it's clear which field you are adding. e.g. when adding dates specify what date - Date started, date checklist completed etc....

Each report includes standard fields plus the additional items required for that report.
Th
Survey views must join to HR Person Master so you need at least one field from that view in a report.

When adding filters, the operator 'between' does not include the dates entered in the start and end date fields

The social onboarding view is taking appointment ID from HR POST PERSON which returns the substantive appointment

Downstream Systems & Processes
Details of any processes which are affected or need to be carried out following, or as part of, the change. Please detail any triggers, actions required and when the actions should be carried out.

USS Pensions interface: This system belongs to the USS pension provider, and the Pensions team uploads reports to this system on a regular basis. Personal titles in CoreHR must be mapped to the equivalent title codes for USS at CoreHR > Core DataTalk > Data Mapping: USSTTL. Any time a new personal title is added or an existing one is modified, you will need to ask the Pensions team to check what the corresponding USS Mapped Code should be, and set up a mapping if appropriate within the Data Mapping setup.

UNICARD: CoreHR sends employee data, including personal titles, to a middleware system called Interface Staging. The Card Office database, UNICARD, has a system integration (#167) to import the personal titles from Interface Staging to add to their staff records. Any time a new personal title is added or an existing one is modified, you will need to liaise with the SSM-Business Integration & Technology (BITE) team to inform them of the change, as they will need to modify the integration from Interface Staging to UNICARD to ensure the new/modified title is included.
Note: The Card Office will only display professional titles, e.g. “Doctor”/“Professor”, on staff ID cards, therefore non-professional titles such as “Mr” and “Ms” must be suppressed by the integration rather than imported into UNICARD. The interface checks all titles from CoreHR against a mapping table called gen_lookup_values to determine whether to import the titles into UNICARD or to map them to NULL values (which effectively suppresses them). 
If you have added a new title to CoreHR, you must assign a task in OSM to the SSM-BITE team, and ask them to add the new title to the gen_lookup_values table. Check with the Card office whether they want the title to display or be suppressed, and advise the SSM-BITE team accordingly. 

SAP Concur: CoreHR sends employee data, including personal titles to a middleware system called Interface Staging. Interface Staging passes some employee data to a second middleware system called BizTalk, which distributes the data to various “receiving” systems. SAP Concur is one of these systems, so any changes to personal titles must be communicated to the Finance team so that they can update any title data mappings within SAP Concur as necessary. 

The X5 system also receives titles in the feed from CoreXD (INT.027), they should be notified in case of any system impact, although this is lower risk as currently a new title will not cause a change to be made in the X5 system.

The list of titles held in Core has to be manually entered each time Core release a new version (minor or major), so the list of titles must always be checked after the environment has been handed back. Approved process for raising 
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?

There are two main uses of the applicant clear down:

Applicant Requests Data Removed From System, referred to hereon as the “Applicant Request Process”
Periodic clear down of data to comply with Data Protection laws, referred to hereon as the “Bulk Clear down Process”

The first, where an applicant requests that their details are removed from our system, will be raised via an incident. 

The second, where the HRIS Support Centre needs to fulfil its legal obligation to clear down applicant data periodically, will be managed annually and scheduled to coincide with the start of the new HESA year.
Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?

Applicant Request Process

We would always accept an applicant’s request to delete their e-Recruitment profile, however we are legally obliged to retain any recruitment data for six months following the date after an appointment has been confirmed (or it has been confirmed that no appointment has been/will be made for that vacancy). The full process is outlined in the “Applicant clear down process at request of applicant” document in the following folder: P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Applicant Cleardown.

Bulk Cleardown Process

The HRIS Service Manager needs to request/approve this process to be run and the timeframes involved. 
Change Management
What type of change is this? When should approval be sought and from whom (internal to team or change manager)? Who would normally be responsible for implementing? 

Once the historic data has been cleared down this exercise will be managed as an annual BAU exercise and will not require a change request in HEAT. 

The timing should be agreed with the Heads of HRIS Support and HR Information.

The clear down is expected to be carried out by the HRIS support centre 1st line support team lead.
How to
Technically how to process the change in the system
Applicant Request Process
Full details can be found in:
HOW TO – Clear down applications at the request of an applicant: 

There is a limit to what we are able to clear down. Applications must be retained for a period of six months after an appointment has been confirmed or it has been confirmed that no appointment has been/will be made for that vacancy. This has been confirmed by Anne Harkness.

If an application cannot be cleared down because it is less than six months from the final status date of the vacancy the HRIS Support Centre have a standard email to send to the applicant, as below:

Dear 
 
Thank you for your email request for the deletion of your University of Oxford e-Recruitment on-line account.  
 
Due to requirements placed upon us by the ‘fair recruitment’ process, we are able to action your request incrementally over time, rather than being able to fully action it now.  We are required to retain all applications against vacancies for a period of six months following the date after an appointment has been confirmed (or it has been confirmed that no appointment has been/will be made for that vacancy). Challenges to recruitment outcomes could be received for any vacancies within these timeframes, and would require access to full application data received against any such vacancies.  Full deletion of your account can follow as soon as all of your past applications have been deleted.
 

In terms of the vacancies you have applied for, we can confirm that a number of your applications fall outside the period we are required to retain, and we therefore can delete them straight away.
 
For each application within the six month period, we will identify the date on which we can delete the application and schedule a task to do this.  We can offer to update you on each occasion to confirm this to you for each application removed, or we can update you once all applications have been removed, unless any subsequent applications are received.  Please do feel free to let us know your preference with regard to this. Once all individual applications have been deleted you applicant account will automatically be deleted also.
 
In the meantime Personal information provided to the University of Oxford is held in accordance with the provisions of the Data Protection Act 1998. The University’s Policy on Data Protection may be viewed at:
http://www.admin.ox.ac.uk/councilsec/dp/policy.html.

Bulk clear down process

Based on the latest (current) applicant status date.

The bulk clear down would usually be carried out for a one year period (HESA year) beginning on 1 August. 

Applications should be retained for the current year plus the previous year. I.e. in the HESA year 2016/17, applications where the latest status date falls in the previous HESA year (2015/16) will be retained in addition to the current year. 

As soon as possible after 1 Aug 2017 applicants from the 2015/16 HESA year should be cleared and so on…….

Note: 14/12/2016 A change from three month to six month retention period was made to this process as per discussion with Susanne Hemmerich.

Outstanding questions about the process

What happens if an in-progress (unsubmitted) application exists for an applicant with previous submitted applications that we do delete? Would the record still be deleted?

What happens if an applicant has submitted their application but the department has not pulled it through from the ‘submit web applicants’ area and therefore has no applicant status assigned?
Decisions
A change from three month to six month retention period was made to this process as per discussion with Susanne Hemmerich [14/12/2016].

It is not necessary to retain a record of the clear down (i.e. the PDF output from Core)

It is not necessary to inform departments when we clear down an applicant record unless the application status codes have not been updated, in which case First Line will contact the Department to update them.

It is not necessary to re-run the applicant packs for each vacancy after running the clear down process. 

It is not necessary to raise a change each time we run this process. 

This should be treated as a standard process and does not need to be tested. 

It is not necessary to clear the data from QA20 and TEST; this can wait until the next clone. 

Bulk applicant clear down - Points to note
The character limit in the applicant status description is greater than on the applicant clear down preview report. Applicant status REJE – Rejected – Ext Applicant Int Vacancy needs to be reduced. Suggest Rejected - Ext App Int Vacancy. (Raised with Core who are referring it for a bug fix Case #00065693). Core have recognised this as a bug and it will be fixed in v20.0.24. JIRA number DS-16619. The description field on the report will be increased to 40 characters.
NB: In the meantime the status description will need to be amended as above in PRD.

The actual ‘END DATE’ entered in the applicant clear down screen is not included in the clear down process. In order to clear down applicants to and including 31 Jul XX the END DATE needs to be 1 Aug XX (Confirmed by CoreHR via Case #00068425). I have tested this and attached screenshots to the Change request 20005862. 

Applicant events are not cleared down as part of the process. (Raised with Core Case # 00064641). Core have responded to say that although there are no plans to include events in the clear down process, the error message is being removed in v22.

The clear down process follows standard security i.e. users can only clear down applicants against vacancies in departments that they have access to

Questions/decisions
Merged pack removal. What happens when the applicant statuses on a vacancy span two HESA years? E.g. some applicants are cleared down in year 1 but the remaining applicants won’t be cleared down until year 2. When do we ask Core to delete the merged pack? 
Option 1 – remove PDF pack after initial applicants are removed. This will ensure that all details relating to the applicants that have been cleared are removed from the vacancy. It is unlikely that the department will want access to the original merged pack.
Option 2 – remove PDF pack when ALL applicants are cleared from the vacancy. Applications for cleared applicants will remain after the individual applications have been removed. 

ANSWER/DECISION: Option 1. Raise a case with CoreHR to clear down merged packs after initial applicant statuses are cleared down.

Can we ask Core to add an applicant count to the preview report so that we can check that the numbers returned on the preview match our own reports? Where I was able to check the number of applicants in the preview report against the Discoverer report the number always matched exactly.

CASE #00065305 raised with CoreHR. 
Response from Core – “Unfortunately this report is not editable. We could pass this ticket to our colleagues in CRM to see if edits can be made to this. However, I am unsure if updates are possible as it is a standard report. If you would like for me to pass this ticket to CRM, I can request this.” The only other option would be to draw and calculate this message via BI Reporting. This would not be a CoreHR standard report so I would not be able to assist in creation of such a report. 

COMMENT:
In order to validate the numbers where volumes are high, a simple check is to divide the number of applicants by the number returned on a full page of the preview report (38 applicants). I tested this method and in my view it gives an acceptable result. 

ANSWER/DECISION:
I have responded to Core and asked if this can be considered for future development.

How will we know whether an applicant has applied for more than one vacancy i.e. whether their account should be closed after the clear down is complete? 

ANSWER/DECISION: The functionality has been extensively tested and we are confident that an applicant account will be deleted once the last application has been cleared down.

How does user access affect the reports and ability to clear down applicants? Can analysts only view and clear down applicants for departments included in their access? 

ANSWER/DECISION: Testing shows that a user’s access determines what applicants will be cleared down i.e. only applicants against vacancies in departments the user has access to will be cleared down. Need to ensure that anyone clearing down applicants has access to ALL department codes unless otherwise agreed.
What if anything should we do with OPEN vacancies that have been cleared? In the period 2010/11 there are 20 vacancies with the status = OPEN plus 1 with the status = HOLD.

ANSWER/DECISION: TBD but nothing in the short term. The HR Information Team are also concerned with vacancies that remain OPEN after recruitment is complete.

Relates to question 2. What if anything do we want to do to validate that the Discoverer reports and actual applicants cleared down correspond?

ANSWER/DECISION:
Testing has shown that where possible to check, the numbers matched. In order to validate the numbers where volumes are high, divide the number of applicants by the number returned on a full page of the preview report (38 applicants). This will give the number of pages to expect.

Have we received confirmation from Liz that they have all the data they need?

ANSWER/DECISION: YES see email dated 3 Jan 2017
We need an explanation of exactly what the script is returning and whether the clear down script will have an effect on any transfers. Taken from App clear down test 3 v2. See testing V4 after clear down under 12:Support>Change control>Testing>Applicants clear down

What happens when an applicant has submitted an application but the department have not pulled their application through from the ‘Submit Web Applicants’ screen?
ANSWER/DECISION: 
Testing has shown that the application will remain in the ‘Submit Web Applicants’ screen. Where all other applications have been cleared the applicant account will still be closed in both the back office and the applicant portal. However when the department pull the applicant through to the vacancy (status = applied), the applicant account in the back office is recreated under the same applicant ID. However the online applicant account is not recreated and the applicant will need to create a new account if they wish to apply again in the future. Additional Background Information

Employee Self Service and Manager Self Service were implemented following a year-long project in 2018. ESS is available to all employees with a CMS University contract of employment; MSS is available to all designated Self-Service Managers. 

Users can access HR Self-Service from anywhere with an internet connection from any device via the University’s VPN (Virtual Private Network). 

In the first phase of the project employees were given access to view current contract and pay information, view and update some personal details and view payslips and P60s. A welcome email is sent to new users by the Systems Administrator when their account is created.

The ability to update bank details was enabled but removed quite soon after implementation following concerns about validating the changes made. It is intended that this will be made available in a later phase.

Managers can view a list of the employees in their team, their contract details and some personal details.

Text in the Self-Service Portal can be edited in the Language pack – See How To above…….

Automated emails are configured e.g. when an employee changes their bank details. Navigate to People Management > Data Centre > HR Admin Setup Settings > Event Configuration. For full details refer to the Events and Email Notifications Knowledge Article.

Workgroups
Manager Self Service is reliant on work groups being created to which managers and employees are assigned. Each work group should have a manager assigned to it. Managers are assigned to work groups via People Management > Employee Administration > Maintain Organisation Roles

Employees are assigned to a Work Group for each appointment (excludes Casuals). The Work Group field in the Organisation Hierarchy has been enabled and appears after Location (see below).
 

Workgroups are created and managed by the Systems (Security) Administrator.

Payroll calendar
On the Employee Self Service landing page, the date of the next Pay Day and the number of days to go is displayed in the ‘Important Dates’ section (see below). 

On the actual Pay Day, the legend says ‘today’. The day after Pay Day the next date is displayed.

A separate calendar is required for the calendar year for each Pay Group paid through payroll. At the present time we have calendars for pay groups 20 and 21.

In December each year new calendars will need to be created for the following year. It is not possible to overwrite an existing calendar to add dates for the following year so new calendars must be created. There does not appear to be any way to ‘direct’ the Pay Day view to a specific calendar, it seems to rely on the year in the SYSDATE matching the year on the Calendar. Thorough testing has been carried out on the process, the results of which can be viewed here.

Depending on when the December Pay Day falls there are two options for updating the calendars.

Option 1 (recommended) – add the January pay date for the forthcoming year to the current year’s calendars as a 13th Pay Date. This will allow plenty of time to create new calendars for the forthcoming year.

Option 2 – The day after December’s pay day, create new calendars for the forthcoming year and delete the calendars for the outgoing year. NB: The Next Pay Date section in the Portal will be blank until the new calendars have been created. 

For details on how to create and edit these calendars refer to the How To guide - HOW TO - Maintain Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal v 1.0.docx

Requirements

Fulfilment of the admin role on IRIS requires the following:

Guidance on the use of tickets and tasks in OSM

Queries will come to you in one of two ways:
As tasks on OSM to be investigated and actioned
Via email, either personal or Safety Office mailbox. This is not the primary way of support queries coming to the team to process and this behaviour should be discouraged for future use when it occurs. Once received via email, a ticket will need to be created on OSM and processed from there.

Investigation of Requests

Queries that come into the IRIS Support Team via tasks on OSM, may include requests that need to be verified with safety contacts throughout the University e.g. a request to create a new department in NDM would need to be checked with one of the Area Safety Officers for Medical Science if the request did not come from them.

Times when this is appropriate will be highlighted in the guidance that follows.

Escalations

There are two avenues of escalation for requests that come in via OSM:
Escalation to the IRIS Product Ownership Group (POG) for discussion and decision
Escalation to the supplier EcoOnline

In both instances, tasks that require escalation should be done so initially to the Business Change Analyst.

Reassigning Incidents from one Department to another

Reporters of incidents are asked to assign each incident they log to a Department, Faculty or School where the incident took place. This is not always a clear-cut decision due to the complex nature of the University and the buildings and spaces it occupies. There are some situations where it can be easy to assign an incident to an incorrect department to process.

A user on the system can reassign incidents between departments only if they have permissions to view incidents that take place in both of these departments i.e. if an incident was assigned to the Maths Department but should have been assigned to the Physics Department, a user could only reassign this if they had permissions to view incidents in both the Maths and Physics Departments. Search Pages Introduction
The Search Engine is accessible in each application by clicking the Search button from the 2nd menu bar. 
There are 2 sub tabs within the Search Engine – Spotlight and All Tables. 
The Spotlight tab breaks up the database into smaller ‘spotlight’ groups of tables as shown in the first image below. 

The All tables tab displays the full hierarchy of tables that are available to the user in the current application. This could be displayed as a very long page of tables for applications with a large number of data tables. 
Saved Searches will usually be displayed on the right hand side of the Spotlight search page providing easy access to re-run searches that have previously been set up and saved. 

Your Search Criteria
Select a table to begin a new search. 
Your Criteria (as shown below) will provide some fields as default options to define your required search criteria. 

Make as many selections as required – the default setting is to find records that match all of your criteria. It is possible to change this to find records that match any of your criteria by using the ‘Find records that match…’ selector from the top of the Criteria box. 
To add additional fields to the criteria area use the ‘Add custom criteria’ option. Tick as many additional fields as are required. 
Fields that are from a related table can also be used as search criteria by selecting the link at the bottom of the additional criteria pop-up below and navigating to the required table then ticking the field. 
When all required criteria has been entered, click on the Run Search button. 

Your Search Results
Your results will appear at the bottom of the page below Your criteria. 
The number of results found that match your criteria will be displayed in brackets. 
It is possible to refine your criteria further and then click ‘Re-run search’ to alter the results that are returned. 

A few key fields will be included as columns in your results by default. 
Use the ‘Add or Remove Column’s button to add additional fields into your results in the same way as adding criteria. This includes navigating to related tables. 
Use the ‘Reorder Columns’ button to change the order of the fields included in your results. 
It is possible to view a record in more detail by clicking into one of the rows from your results – an option to return to search results will be available from both the edit and summary pages. 

Download options
All searches will include the option to Print – select the ‘Print’ button from between your criteria and your results and then use the printer options to set up the page layout and other formatting options. 

The Download button will provide a choice of either PDF or CSV. 
Selecting PDF will allow for further Page Size and Orientation settings to be chosen. 

Saved Searches
All users have the ability to save searches that will be available to re-run under the users own account. 
To save a search, complete the criteria selection and update results with any additional columns and reordering that is required and then select the ‘Save search’ button from between the criteria and results area. 

Enter a name for the search and then click the Save button. 
The search will now be saved on the Spotlight search page to be re-run as required. 
The saved search will also be pinned to the application homepage by default – use the unpin option shown above to remove a saved search from the homepage quick links. 
Publishing Saved Searches
Nominated users can also have additional privileges to publish saved searches for all users to run. 
An additional tick box will be available under the Save search option providing the ability to ‘publish’ the search to the Spotlight page of saved Searches for all users of the current application. 
Permissions to be able to publish saved searches can be granted by contacting the Info Exchange Helpdesk on 01926 844211 or emailing helpdesk@alcumusgroup.com

Introduction

Exchange Administrators and other nominated key users who have been given ‘Create Reports’ access for an application are able to create and publish standard reports, aggregate the data and build a variety of graphical charts including Line, Bar, Pie using the aggregated results. 

These reports are then available for all users of the application to generate online using their own run-time criteria where applicable. 

The functionality is available on all deployments using our IE2 technology. 

Any queries relating to this functionality should be directed to the helpdesk on 01926 844211 or via e-mail helpdesk@alcumusgroup.com 

Creating a Report

All users of the Info Exchange application are able to run searches at any time using any field combinations. 

An Exchange Administrator also has the ability to create a report and edit the report to further aggregate the data and build graphical charts. 

Exchange Administrators can also allow other key users to be able to create reports without the need for full Administration access. This can be permitted on an application basis by updating the user’s profile in the appropriate application through the Administration > Applications tool. 

It is recommended that the number of users able to create reports is kept to a minimum to avoid excessive numbers of reports being created or existing reports being altered unnecessarily. 

To create a report, click the Reports tab, select the spanner icon in the top corner and choose the “Create new report” option. 

Give the report a title and select the primary table for the report and then click Continue.

Report Settings

The following settings can be applied to a report during the initial set up and then updated at any time afterwards. 

A description can be entered about the report that will appear in smaller text under the report name on the main reports page. 
Select an icon from the available options to represent the report on the main reports page.

Add the report into a group - “Other reports” is the default group.

Tick to “Ignore user’s permissions when running report” if this report contains high level data only (no specific details) and it is preferable for users to report on all records not just the ones they usually have permissions to access. 

Tick to “Show the report on the application homepage”. This will force the report name to appear on the application homepage in the Reports box as a hyperlink for all users. If this is not activated users will still have the ability to add it their homepage if they wish. 

Tick to “Show tabs in docked orientation” to present the layout of the finished report in a docked tab format of data tables and graphs rather than stacked below each other on a single page view. 

Tick the “Publish to other users” when the report is complete and is ready for other system users to access and run. 
Select the “Page size” to determine the number of records to show on each page of the report data table. 

Tick “Show Hyperlinks” to allow the first column of each record in the data table to be used as a hyperlink clicking through to the summary page of the record. 

Tick “Aggregated rows to expand” to allow reports with aggregation to display a chevron that will expand to display all individual rows that are included in the aggregated row. Please note that activating this option can increase the page load time of a report. 

Tick “Enable CSV download” to display the download csv option on a report – this will be disabled by default. 

Click Save to update the report with the chosen settings. 

Report Criteria

The Criteria tab of the report configuration is divided into 2 sections – Fixed and Runtime criteria. 

Fixed criteria can be set up by the report creator and will be locked into the report each time it is generated with only records that match the fixed criteria values being returned.

Runtime criteria are fields that can be applied to the report as an initial page for the user running the report to decide which criteria options to choose. The report will then return records that match the user’s specified criteria values. 

A combination of the 2 can be used e.g. fixed criteria of records with an “Open” Status plus a runtime criteria of a Date field so that each user running the report can vary the records retuned by the date range entered but only Open records will ever be returned in the results.

To apply either type of criteria click the “Add additional criteria” button and tick the required fields from the available fields as shown below and click Done. 

For fixed criteria, select the required values from the chosen fields and click Done. 

Note that fields from related tables can also be included as criteria – when selecting the required fields use the blue hyperlink at the bottom of the field selector box to select a field from a related table. 

An example might be to navigate up the table hierarchy to the Site table and then tick the Region field from the list of fields in the Sites. 

When all criteria have been applied, click the Save Changes button. 

Data Table – Adding & Removing Columns

The next tab in the report configuration is the Data table and this displays the columns of data for the records that are returned in the report results. 

To add or remove columns from the data table, click on the Edit Columns options on the right hand side and choose “Add or remove columns” from the menu. 

Tick or un-tick the fields that are required as columns in the data table. 

Fields from related tables can also be included by using the blue hyperlink at the bottom of the window and following the same process as described in the Criteria section to navigate to other tables and tick required fields. 

Data Table – Reorder Columns

When the required fields are displayed as columns, these can then be reordered into a preferred layout. 

Note that if aggregation is going to be applied to the data, the aggregation field must be the first column in the table. 

To reorder the fields, select the Edit Columns option again and choose the “Reorder columns” option from the menu. 

Drag and drop each field into the appropriate order and click Done when complete. 

Aggregation

To aggregate records together and produce counts of the aggregated data click the icon next to the No aggregation status on the right hand side. 

2 levels of aggregation are supported in the Data table. 

To aggregate by the field that is the first column in the data table tick the first Aggregate option. 

To aggregate at 2 levels by the fields that are the first and second columns in the data table tick the 2nd Aggregate option. 

Click Done to apply the aggregation to the data table. 

If the fields required for aggregation are not displayed as options in the Aggregation settings box, the columns in the data table need to be reordered to first and second column position. The aggregation settings box will automatically update with the new fields after the reorder has been applied. 

Selecting an aggregation option will then prompt a choice of including subtotal rows.

When aggregating by 2 fields there will be an option to include a 2nd table in the data table area that shows the total record count by the 2nd field in a separate table. 

Table aggregated by Site and then Primary Cause
11144254635500
8858251513840

Separate table aggregated just by Primary Cause

To set the aggregation values click Edit Columns on the right hand side and select “Set aggregation types” from the menu. 

Choose the appropriate option from the list available for each column in the data table. Count or Sum are the most commonly required options. Click Done to update the data table. 

Data Table - Column Visibility

Sometimes fields have to be included in the report data table as a column for purposes such as plotting the field on a graph or including the field in a report calculation but the report creator does not actually want to show this field on the data table as a column to the users running the report. 

Column visibility can be set on or off to display only the required fields on the data table. 

Click the Edit Columns button on the right hand side and select “Set column visibility” from the menu option.

Tick or un-tick the fields to set the visibility for each column and then click Done. 

Data Table – Editing Columns

Changes can be made to an individual column by clicking on a column heading to change the settings for the column. 

914400top

The label of the column name can be changed by un-ticking the Use default label box and typing a new Column Name into the box provided. 

The column can be set to visible or not by ticking or un-ticking the box.

The aggregation setting for this column can also be updated through this interface.

Click Done to apply any updates to the data table. 

Data Table – Calculations

Calculated columns can be added into the report. There are some pre-defined calculation options plus the ability to add custom calculations using any fields that are added into the data column (including non-visible fields).

To add a calculated column click the Edit Column button on the right hand side and select “Add calculated column” from the menu. 

The types of calculation available will depend on the data fields included in the report, e.g. the Year to date total will only be available if there is a date field in the report table. 

All of the options will present the user with some further options to complete before the calculated column is added to the report. The example below is the Rolling total calculation type:

The report creator must select a related field from the fields that are used in the report (including non-visible fields) to apply the calculation to and then enter the Number of months rolling. 

Click Done to update the report data table with the new calculated column. 

The option for Custom calculation is more complex are there is no pre-defined calculation that will be applied and the report creator must configure the calculation using C# language. 

The first stage of adding a custom calculation is to create a Name and Label for the calculated column and then choose the type of data that the column is going to display. 

The next stage is to declare the fields that are to be used in the calculation – these must be present in the report table but can be non-visible fields. 

The calculation expression is then entered into the Expression box in C#. 

The calculation must be tested before it can be saved. 

Click Save calculation to add the new column into the report data table. 
Graphs

Multiple graphs can be added to a report using the data available in the data table of the report. 

To add a new graph click the Add Graph option on the right hand side and type in a Graph title. 

Select the type of graph and further options will then appear depending on the type chosen.

Bar, Column & Line Graphs

The options available are very similar for bar, column and line graphs. 

Bar graphs display the bars horizontally across the page and Column graphs display the columns vertically up the page. 
 

Graph Style

The Graph Style options are Standard, Sub-divided or Stacked. 

Standard will display one bar, column or line in a single block colour. 

Sub-divided bars and columns break a single data field into different coloured segments representing the values of the field e.g. Risk field divided into High, Medium & Low. 

Stacked bars and columns stack multiple data fields onto each other in different coloured segments. 

Legend Position

Choose a legend position on the graph e.g. on the Left or Right, Top or Bottom. 

Fields 

Select the field or fields to be plotted on the graph by ticking the required boxes. 

Use the Colour column to choose a specific colour for the field. 

For Column and line reports choose whether the field should be plotted as a Column or a Line and then against which Y axis it should be displayed. 

Axis Range & Increment

Set preferences for the Axis range e.g. 0 to 100 if the data plotted is showing percentages. 

Choose a preferred Increment for the Axis e.g. increments of 100.

Column or Line graphs provide options for both Y1 and a Y2 axis. 

Target Line

Add a target line onto the graph and set the value and colour of the line. 
Multiple target lines can be added. 

Show values on graph

Tick the box to include the data values on the graph – these will appear on top of the bar or columns or at each point of the line. 

Some example bar, column and line graphs are shown on the next page.

Pie Graphs

There are fewer settings available for pie graphs as only one data field can be plotted on this type of graph. 

Legend Position

Choose a legend position on the graph e.g. on the Left or Right, Top or Bottom. 

Segments

Choose the data field that is going to be represented in the pie by a different colour segment for each data value of the chosen field. 

Segment colours

The colours of the pie graphs segments will be determined automatically by default. The report creator can choose to use a related field to determine the colours if preferred. 

Un-tick the option at the bottom to Determine colours automatically and then tick a field that should be used to colour the segments. Only fields of a “colour” data type will be available for selection and the field can be one that is non-visible on the report data table. 
Show values on graph

Tick the box to include the data values on the graph – these will in the segments of the pie. 

Results Page Layout 

The report creator can design the layout of the report results page incorporating the data table, graphs and formatted text boxes in a variety of positions on the page. 

The layout will be rendered both on screen and on the Download PDF option. 

To design the page layout, click the spanner icon on the report results page and select “Design this page” from the menu. 

The page is divided into Segments, Columns and Objects. 

Add a new segment by scrolling to the bottom of the page and clicking “Add Segment”. 

Each segment can be split into multiple columns by clicking the “Add column” button available when hovering over the right hand side of segment. 

In each column, hover over the right hand side to click the “Add object” button and then select the type of object from the options shown below. 

Drag and drop the objects to move around the page until the desired layout is achieved. 

Click the Done button at the top right of the page to save the page layout design. 

Deleting a Report

A report can be deleted by clicking the spanner icon on the report results page and select “Delete report” from the menu. 

Managing Reports List Page

Clicking on the Report button from an application takes a user to the list of reports that are available to the user. 

To manage the layout and ordering of this page, click the spanner icon from the Reports page and choose the “Design this page” option from the menu. 

Add a new Report Group by clicking the option at the bottom of page. 

Edit the name of an existing group by clicking the “Edit” button within the group. 

Reorder reports within a group by clicking the “Reorder Reports” button. 

Click Done at the top right of the page to save any changes made to the layout of the Report page.

Description of Service
Business Description
The purpose of the IRIS (Incident Reporting and Investigation System) is to ensure that the University Safety Office can adequately perform its legal obligations to report, document and analyse patterns of accidents and safety related incidents under UK safety legislation. 
Service Summary
IRIS replaces the paper based set of manual processes with a new policy and a digital processes. The Safety Office procured a health and safety management system called InfoExchange, which is produced by Alcumus Group (‘Supplier’). This system is delivered using a SaaS (Software as a Service) model.
Staff and Students will have access to IRIS to report Health, Safety and Environmental related incidents. The incident reports will be reviewed on the system by Safety Officers. Safety Officer will put an action plan together for follow up or future preventative actions. These actions will be assigned to departmental safety officers or departmental managers via email notification. 
Hours of Service
The Service is intended to be available for logging incidents 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year, from anywhere with an internet connection.
