Appendix E: Definitions
All definitions are derived from ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) publications unless otherwise stated. ITIL is best practice framework for delivering IT Services. 
Change Management:
The process responsible for controlling the lifecycle of all changes, enabling beneficial changes to be made with minimum disruption to IT Services.

Change Types:
Standard: A pre-authorised change that is low risk, relatively common and follows a procedure or work instruction – for example the provision of standard equipment to a new employee.
Normal: Normal changes follow the defined steps of the change management process. Such changes are categorised as Minor, Significant and Major.
Minor: Change is related to a single application and side-effects can be safely excluded.
Significant: Changes affecting several applications, or the whole of major application, or a change affecting fundamental parts of the IT Infrastructure supporting several applications.
Major: Change affecting a major part of the business-critical infrastructure or a change that introduces major new technologies on a considerable scale. 
Emergency Change: A change that must be introduced as soon as possible – for example, to resolve a major incident or implement a security patch.

Change Advisory Board (CAB): A group of people that support the assessment, prioritisation, authorisation and scheduling of changes. A change advisory board is usually made up of representatives from the IT Service Provider; Business Units and on occasion third parties, such as suppliers. The membership of the CAB will reflect the changes being considered.

Customer:
Someone who buys (provides the budget for) goods or Services. The Customer of an IT Service Provider is the person or group who defines and agrees to the Service Level Targets.

Data Retention:
Data retention is the continued storage of an organisation's data for compliance or business reasons. A data retention policy should be created in partnership with the service provider and business unit. It includes a set of guidelines that describes which data will be archived and how long it will be kept for. 

Disaster Recovery:
Disaster recovery (DR) is an area of security planning that aims to protect an organization from the effects of significant negative events. DR allows an organisation to maintain or quickly resume mission-critical functions following a disaster. A disaster recovery plan provides a structured approach for responding to unplanned incidents that threaten a company’s IT infrastructure, including hardware and software, networks, procedures and people.

Incident:
An unplanned interruption to an IT service or reduction in the quality of an IT Service.

IT Service:
A service provided by an IT service provider. An IT Service is made up of a combination of information technology, people and processes.

Process:
A structured set off activities designed to accomplish a specific objective. A process takes one or more defined inputs and turns them into defined outputs.

Recovery Time Objective (RTO):
The maximum time allowed for the recovery of an IT Service following an interruption. The service level to be provided may be less than normal service level targets.

Recovery Point Objective (RPO):
The maximum amount of data that may be lost when service is restored after an interruption. The recovery point objective is expressed as a length of time between the creation/modification of the data and the point of the failure. Data is recovered to the state it was in at the recovery point. Changes after that point are lost.

Request (or Service Request):
A formal request from a user for something to be provided – for example, a request for information or advice; to reset a password; or to install a computer for a new user. Service Requests are managed by the request fulfilment process, usually in conjunction with the service desk.

Service:
A means of delivering value to customers by facilitating outcomes customers want to achieve without the ownership of specific costs and risks.

Service Catalogue:
A database or structured document with information about all live IT Services. The service catalogue is part of the service portfolio and contains information about two types of IT service: customer-facing services that are visible to the business and supporting services required by the service provider to deliver customer-facing services. http://www.it.ox.ac.uk/services 

Service Desk:
The single point of contact between the service provider and the users.

Service Provider: 
An organisation supplying services to one or more internal customers or external customers.

Stakeholder:
A person who has an interest in an organisation, project or IT Service. Stakeholders may be interested in the activities, targets, resources and deliverables.

Superuser:
A user who is an expert in the business processes supported by an IT service and will provide support for minor incidents and training.

User:
Someone who uses the service.

2. Description of service 
2.1. Service summary 
 
Odyssey is a cloud-based software suite of radiation safety tools designed to assist staff members in managing their 
radiation safety program and increasing compliance. Odyssey is hosted on Amazon Web Services for data security and 
scaling and acts as a centralized location for data entry, storage, and analysis to improve efficiency and reduce cost. 
 
Odyssey software helps staff manage the University’s radiation equipment and materials, and allows for the tracking 
of storage and disposal of radioactive waste. 
 
Odyssey modules include: 
 
 Machine Management 
 Equipment Catalog 
 Inventory Tracking 
 Permits 
 Waste Management 
 Reporting 
 Forms 
 
2.2. Hours of service and support  
 
 The Service is intended to be available at all times - including evenings, weekends, bank holidays, and 
University closures. 
 
 First line and second-line support is available 9am - 5pm on normal working days. Normal working days are 
Monday – Friday, excluding bank holidays and University closures. 
 
 Third line support (via Versant) is available 13:00-21:00 GMT on normal working days (Monday – Friday). 
Versant operate a US-based support centre, in-line with US working hours. Escalations to Versant will only be 
made by members of the Safety Office / HR Systems, and Versant will not be expected to provide support 
directly to customers of the Radiation Management Service. 
 
 All other times, the service operates without technical support – however support calls may be logged out of 
hours for review the next working day. 
 
  
   
 
Service Level Agreement  5 
2.3. Maintenance schedule 
 
Versant will schedule routine maintenance of the Odyssey platform as needed. The University will be informed at a 
minimum two weeks prior to the date on which it will occur. Scheduled Downtime will not exceed 4 hours per month, 
and will occur during non-peak hours, outside of normal business days (Monday to Friday).  
 
Following notification from Versant, the Service Manager will notify customers at least 48 hours beforehand via the 
following University channels: 
 
 An update posted to the status page at https://status.ox.ac.uk/ 
Maintenance performed outside of the service window will be classified as Emergency Maintenance, and any instances 
of Emergency Maintenance will be notified directly to the Service Sponsor and Service Owner, and announced on the 
status page at https://status.ox.ac.uk as soon as possible. 
 
 
2.4. Patching policy 
 
Versant follow a continuous integration approach, and deliver updates to their Odyssey platform on a fortnightly basis. 
Atlassian ticketing is used to catalogue customer requests and feature improvements. For dedicated environments, 
updates/patches are implemented at a pre-specified interval, typically quarterly. 
 
2.5. Entitled users 
The Service is provided for use by those registered with the Safety Office as one of the following categories of user: 
 
 Radiation Worker 
 Radiation Protection Supervisor 
 Senior Radiation Protection Supervisor 
 
This Service Level Agreement does not entitle anyone else to use the Service.  
 
2.6. Access  
The Service is designed to be accessible from any modern web browser, regardless of location or time of day. The 
following browsers are tested as clients prior to any system release: 
 Microsoft Edge (latest) 
 Firefox (latest) 
 Chrome (latest) 
 
2.7. Limitations 
There are no further limitations on the provision or use of the Service, other than limitations that may arise through 
Customer responsibilities (Section 6.2)

2.8. Funding and charges 
 
The University has agreed terms with Versant for the provision of the Odyssey platform with an initial one-year 
contract. This is expected to be extended, with Versant having agreed to honour the initial price into year two. 
 
Project ITS877 has budget allocated to fund the license costs in 2023/2024 and 2024/2025. After this time, license 
renewal costs will be allocated from the Safety Office budget. 
 
2.9. Accessibility conformance 
The University’s policy for Web Accessibility is level AA of WCAG, see the University rules for websites at 
http://www.ox.ac.uk/rules-for-websites WCAG has been extended to WCAG 2.1 (June 2018). (There is a less well-
known standard, ATAG, for authoring tools.). Compliance responsibility is shared across the University by content and 
software owners. 
 
IT Services Web Strategy says all platforms, websites, intranets, and blog sites must: 
 Adopt HTTPS encryption, in line with trends in web traffic security 
 Meet conformance Level AA of the W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1, and adhere to IT Services 
accessibility guidelines  
 Meet the University information security baseline requirements, see the description at  
 Adhere to the University data protection policy and comply with GDPR, see the policy at: 
 https://compliance.admin.ox.ac.uk/data-protection-policy 
 
Versant have authored the Odyssey application to WCAG 2.0 level A. It should be noted that this of a lower level of 
compliance than level AA. Given that the Radiation Management System (Odyssey) is a specialist service, with a highly-
restricted user base, this does not present any immediate cause for concern. 
 
In the event of future accessibility requirements needing additional development work by Versant, for example in 
order to make specific features of the platform compliant with WCAG level AA – this is available to the University for 
an additional fee.

10. Appendix F: Definitions 
 
All definitions are derived from ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) publications unless otherwise 
stated.  ITIL is best practice framework for delivering IT Services.  
 
Change Enablement: 
The process responsible for controlling the lifecycle of all changes, enabling beneficial changes to be made with 
minimum disruption to IT Services. 
 
Change Types: 
Standard:  A pre-authorised change that is low risk, relatively common and follows a procedure or work instruction – 
for example the provision of standard equipment to a new employee. 
Normal: Normal changes follow the defined steps of the change management process.  Such changes are categorised 
as Minor, Significant and Major. 
Minor:  Change is related to a single application and side-effects can be safely excluded. 
Significant: Changes affecting several applications, or the whole of major application, or a change affecting 
fundamental parts of the IT Infrastructure supporting several applications. 
Major: Change affecting a major part of the business-critical infrastructure or a change that introduces major 
new technologies on a considerable scale.   
Emergency Change: A change that must be introduced as soon as possible – for example, to resolve a major incident 
or implement a security patch. 
 
Change Advisory Board (CAB):  A group of people that support the assessment, prioritisation, authorisation and 
scheduling of changes.  A change advisory board is usually made up of representatives from the IT Service Provider; 
Business Units and on occasion third parties, such as suppliers.  The membership of the CAB will reflect the changes 
being considered. 
 
Customer: 
Someone who buys (provides the budget for) goods or Services. The Customer of an IT Service Provider is the person 
or group who defines and agrees to the Service Level Targets. 
 
Data Retention: 
Data retention is the continued storage of an organisation's data for compliance or business reasons.  A data retention 
policy should be created in partnership with the service provider and business unit. It includes a set of guidelines that 
describes which data will be archived and how long it will be kept for. For a definition of data retention see  
http://searchstorage.techtarget.com/definition/data-retention 
 
Disaster Recovery: 
Disaster recovery (DR) is an area of security planning that aims to protect an organization from the effects of significant 
negative events. DR allows an organisation to maintain or quickly resume mission-critical functions following a 
disaster.  A disaster recovery plan provides a structured approach for responding to unplanned incidents that threaten 
a company’s IT infrastructure, including hardware and software, networks, procedures and people. For a definition of 
Disaster Recovery, see http://searchdisasterrecovery.techtarget.com/definition/disaster-recovery 
 
Incident: 
An unplanned interruption to an IT service or reduction in the quality of an IT Service. 
 
IT Service: 
   
 
Service Level Agreement  17 
A service provided by an IT service provider.  An IT Service is made up of a combination of information technology, 
people and processes. 
 
Process: 
A structured set off activities designed to accomplish a specific objective.  A process takes one or more defined inputs 
and turns them into defined outputs. 
 
Recovery Time Objective (RTO): 
The maximum time allowed for the recovery of an IT Service following an interruption. The service level to be provided 
may be less than normal service level targets. 
 
Recovery Point Objective (RPO): 
The maximum amount of data that may be lost when service is restored after an interruption.  The recovery point 
objective is expressed as a length of time between the creation/modification of the data and the point of the failure.  
Data is recovered to the state it was in at the recovery point.  Changes after that point are lost. 
 
Request (or Service Request): 
A formal request from a user for something to be provided – for example, a request for information or advice; to reset 
a password; or to install a computer for a new user.  Service Requests are managed by the request fulfilment process, 
usually in conjunction with the service desk. 
 
Service: 
A means of delivering value to customers by facilitating outcomes customers want to achieve without the ownership 
of specific costs and risks. 
 
Service Catalogue: 
A database or structured document with information about all live IT Services.  The service catalogue is part of the 
service portfolio and contains information about two types of IT service: customer-facing services that are visible to 
the business and supporting services required by the service provider to deliver customer-facing services.  The Service 
Catalogue is available at http://www.it.ox.ac.uk/services  
 
Service Desk: 
The single point of contact between the service provider and the users. 
 
Service Provider:   
An organisation supplying services to one or more internal customers or external customers. 
 
Stakeholder: 
A person who has an interest in an organisation, project or IT Service.  Stakeholders may be interested in the activities, 
targets, resources and deliverables. 
 
Superuser: 
A user who is an expert in the business processes supported by an IT service and will provide support for minor 
incidents and training. 
 
User: 
Someone who uses the service.

Guidance for Odyssey Radiation Management System – Version 1.0 3 of 81 
 
1.0  Introduction 
Odyssey is Oxford’s Radiation Management System. A central system to record and manage 
the University’s radiation-related data including registered workers, materials and waste, 
and machine and equipment. 
All radiation host departments will have access to the system and be required to keep their 
department records up to date. Only registered radiation workers with an Oxford Single 
Sign-On (SSO) will have access to the system.  
Note: In the first phase of implementing the system only the Safety Office Radiation Team, 
Senior Radiation Protection Supervisors (SRPS), and Radiation Protection Supervisors (RPS) 
will have access to Odyssey.  
Odyssey is a cloud-based system provided by Versant Physics, an American software 
company.  
 
  
 
Guidance for Odyssey Radiation Management System – Version 1.0 4 of 81 
 
2.0  Worker Registrations 
2.1 Registering a new radiation worker 
An online form will be used to register a new radiation worker, whether they are a student, 
staff or visitor. The form is initiated in the system and will pass through the following stages 
for completion and approval:  
Radiation Worker > RPS > SRPS > Academic Line Manager > Safety Office.  
This form should be used when a radiation worker is registering for the first time in each 
host department. For example, if a worker is already registered with Biology and is now 
registering with Oncology, this form would be used to register the worker as a new worker to 
Oncology.   
In addition, the form should also be used if a worker is registering to work at an external 
institute. 
If the worker is already registered in a Host department but wishes to be registered for a 
different work type or additional radionuclides, then the ‘Work Type Registration’ form 
should be used. (See 3.1 Adding additional work types to a radiation worker record). 
2.1.1 Registration forms have an expiry date to be completed  
When any registration form is sent from Odyssey, it defaults to have an expiration date 6 
weeks from the creation date. For example, if the form was sent to the worker on the 
01/08/2024 and the worker selected the link to complete the form after 12/09/2024 they will 
receive an error page and will not be able to complete the registration form.  
If this happens, the SRPS will need to send a new registration form to the worker. Then, the 
Safety Office will be required to Terminate the now expired work registration form.  
Safety Office users and SRPS users can check whether a registration form has been 
viewed/completed and the expiration date by navigating to the Link Management Screen; 
Odyssey > Forms > Email Forms > Manage Sent Forms. 
This is also where the Safety Office could revoke an email sent in error and then view the 
workflow to terminate it.  
 
 
 

  
 
Guidance for Odyssey Radiation Management System – Version 1.0 5 of 81 
 
2.1.2 Initiating a new registration form  
It is recommended the SRPS of the host department, for where the worker shall be working, 
should initiate the registration process. There may be circumstances in departments, 
whereby the RPS can initiate the form. This begins with sending the online form to the 
worker from Odyssey. 
If the Worker has work with different RPS, it is not possible to specify this on the form. 
Another work type form should be initiated to capture that different work with the different 
RPS in the same department.  
If you are a SRPS for more than one department ensure that the 
department that the worker will be working is selected in the top right of 
the screen. 
1. From the landing page, select the ‘Send Registration Form’ icon.  
 
2. The ‘Send Form’ page will open. 
3. Choose the ‘Select Form’ button within the ‘Published template’ section. 
 
4. Select ‘Worker Registration Form’ from the list of form templates and select the ‘Open’ 
button. 
 
Note: If you have selected the wrong form, you can choose the ‘Select Form’ button to 
select a different form.  
5. If the worker is not registered for radiation work in another department, type the 
workers Oxford email address in the ‘Recipient email’ field. 
Email address must be in the following format name.surname@dept.ox.ac.uk 
If the worker is already registered, you may find them in the ‘Recipient user’ list.

 Introduction
Odyssey is Oxford’s Radiation Management System. A central system to record and manage the University’s radiation-related data including registered workers, materials waste, machines and radiation protection instruments.
All radiation host departments will have access to the system and be required to keep their department records up to date. Only registered radiation workers with an Oxford Single Sign-On (SSO) will have access to the system. 
Note: In the first phase of implementing the system only the Safety Office Radiation Team, Senior Radiation Protection Supervisors (SRPS), and Radiation Protection Supervisors (RPS) will have access to Odyssey. 
Odyssey is a cloud-based system provided by Versant Physics, an American software company. 

 System Configuration
Departments
The EA Environment Agency
The University of Oxford is bound by legislative guidance surrounding the holdings and use of radioactive materials and waste. The legislation is directed through the Environment Agency with a set of Departments that provide the controlling limits for holdings and use of radioactive materials and waste.
The Departments are based on geographical location and are specific to a number of buildings within that location.
Each Department is tailored to the specific activities that take place.
The University of Oxford currently holds the current paper permits.
5 Unsealed Source Permits 
4 Sealed Source Permits 
1 Category 5 Permit
In addition to this the Environment Agency provide an Exemption Order which defines a set of limits for material to be held under exemption conditions. The Exemption Order is applied to each individual building, hence each building has an Exemption Order limit.
Each year, In February, the University of Oxford must provide a return to the EA that describes the full radioactive waste activity for the year. In addition to this, the EA may inspect the University of Oxford and any one of its Permitted locations at any point during the year and require evidence of holdings and use against the limits given to the department, alongside the waste activities.
To amend an EA Permit, an application must be made to the EA for a “Variation”. If successful, the Permit is updated and referenced with a reference suffix at the end of the permit number.
Each Permit is broken down into an agreed set of limits that is given to each Department. This is referred to in the Odyssey system as a “Department Limit”.
The Departments must operate within the limits given to them. Each month they will provide the Safety Office with Source Accountancy Records to confirm their holdings and waste disposal records and to confirm that they remain within their allocated limits.
The source accountancy confirmation and confirmation of waste accumulation and waste disposal to drain and to air will be in the form of a report generated for each department.
Different reports deal with different elements of this process and is further explored in the reporting section below.

Geological Specimens
As at 25/04/2025, Geological Specimens (Rocks) are no longer required to be held under Safeguards regulations.
Rocks contain naturally occurring radionuclides including (but not limited to) Uranium and Thorium. It has been agreed that the University of Oxford will maintain a detailed catalogue of these items in the Digital Asset Management application referred to as EMU. In addition to this, a limited set of data relating to each rock will be kept on the Odyssey system in order to keep track of radiological activity. The two data sets are aligned with a common ID.
Safeguards and The ONR Office for Nuclear Regulation
The ONR provides regulation in regard to nuclear material only. This regulation is referred to as Safeguards. Safeguards accountancy records must be available at any given point in time should the ONR wish to inspect the University of Oxford premises.
In addition, the regulation requires nuclear materials to be reported annually via:
PIL – Physical Inventory Listing, in regard to holdings 
MBR – Materials Balance Report in regard to movement.

Structure
Structure starts at the University of Oxford level and is based on geographical location. 
The University of Oxford has a number of Departments. 
A Department may be self-contained or may have a number of Sub-Departments. 
Each Department has one or more Buildings. 
Each Building has one or more Rooms, Labs and Waste Stores.
A Department may share a Building with another Department and maintain a set of rooms within the shared building.
A Department may share a Room, Lab or Waste Store within a shared Building with another Department.

 Site Structure

All Departments, Buildings, Rooms, Labs and Waste stores are entities referred to as “Sites”. The University of Oxford will sit at Top Level in the Site Structure and the Departments will sit in the structure underneath this. The Departments all sit as Primary Sites, with the Buildings and Rooms, Labs and Waste Stores shown underneath.
In the example below, the Worker will log into the Pathology Dunn School Department and have visibility to 4 Buildings and have access to 14 Rooms, Labs and Waste Stores.

In the case where a Building is shared, the Building will also be made a Primary Site within the system and must also be given an Association to the Building (See below). This will allow the Workers of both Departments to have visibility of Rooms, Labs and Waste stores to which they have been given access.
In the example below the Worker is located in the JR Hospital Main Building and will log in to either of the Departments RDM Cardiovascular Medicine or Surgical Sciences. This will enable to the Worker to view any of the 4 Rooms/Labs within the JR Hospital Building 622 as defined in their Department limit. 
This is enabled via 2 things.
Through the JR Hospital Main 622 Building being listed as a Primary Site, which sits as a sibling alongside the RDM Cardiovascular Medicine and Surgical Sciences Departments.
Through the creation of an “association” between the Department and the Building.

Associations
To enable visibility of a shared Room, Lab or Waste Store an “Association” needs to be created in the System between the Department and the Shared Building. This is achieved through editing the Department Site (from the Site Structure) and adding an “Association” to the shared Building. Note: please ensure that an “Association” must be created for each Department that shares a Building.
Note: please ensure that the association is created on the Department record and that it cites the Building site. Do not create an association on the Building record citing the Department as this will cause users in both Departments to be able to view the personal details of the other Department through the Worker reporting.

When the Department is created, the Department will dictate exactly what Rooms, Labs, Waste Stores should be visible when using the Department. If the “Association” has been created and the Room, Lab, Waste Store has been added to the Department, the Worker will have visibility of the Room, Lab, Waste Store when logging into the Department on the System.
Please note: 
A lab will only be visible for use with inventory, once it has been set for use with Sealed and/or Unsealed Sources.
A room will only be visible when adding a machine to the system, once it has been set for use with machines.

Logging In
When logging in to the system, please ensure that you are in the correct Department in which you wish to work. For example, if you wish to “add inventory” to the “Biochemistry Department”, please make sure that you are in the Biochemistry Department. 

To do this, click on the Department drop down which will display underneath your name on the top right-hand side of the screen when you mouse over your name.
Please note that (S)RPS’s and Workers will have only have visibility of sites for which they have permission to access.

All Departments and Buildings are visible from this drop down as all Buildings are created at “Primary” level. This has be done to facilitate the instances where multiple Departments share a Building.
A user in a Department will see only the Departments and Buildings to which they have an association.
The Safety Office and Administrators will see the entire list.

Authorised Locations
Once the Department Limit has been created, select the Authorized Labs to add the relevant rooms and labs to be used with the Departmental Limits.

Once added the rooms will all be listed as shown. Note: if the room is listed in blue, then it has been authorised for use as a lab with inventory. To authorise a location as a lab, the user must visit the LABs module and add the room to be authorised as a lab.
Select Add Authorised Location to add the authorised lab to the Department Limit. If a room is no longer required to be used against the Department Limit, click on the pencil icon to edit and delete the room.
The exact same logic applies to waste sites. A room must be authorised as a Waste Site in the Waste Management module under Sites. Once authorised, it can be added to the Department Limit as previously described by selecting Add Authorised Location.

Note: for the Exempt Limits only, the location added will be the Building i.e. not a room or lab. Select “Automatically authorise all descendant locations” with the tick.
This is to ensure that every room in the Building is covered under the one Exempt Limit. Therefore, there will only ever be one Exempt Limit per Building.
Please ensure that this field remains unticked for the Sealed and Unsealed limits.
Note: the descendant locations does not work for Waste locations that are not set up as labs. These are required to be manually added if they are required. In the University of Oxford set up, it is not required to dispose of exempt waste directly to a waste store that is not a lab. Exempt materials will be disposed of directly into a waste container within a lab.

 Inventory Management
Unsealed Sources
Unsealed sources may be held under an EA Department Limit or under the guidelines given by the Exemption Order. The Exemption Order has been defined as a series of identical limits as described in the system under the “Exempt Limit” per building.
The majority of our nuclear material is held under the Exemption Order as Uranium compounds and Thorium salts, as they are very low quantities. For example, Uranyl Acetate.

Nuclear materials, (Uranium, Plutonium and Thorium), that are held as Unsealed Sources, or Exempt Sources, will also be subject to ONR scrutiny and so will also be shown on the Safeguard reports.

Archived Inventory

Inventory is moved to an “Archived” status, once it is no longer actively held against the Department. This can be achieved through disposal of a source i.e. aqueous disposal to drain or gaseous discharge to air via fume hood or stack. System Reference ID

This is the system generated unique identifier for each piece of inventory within the system. The format is 3 digits with a suffix of 3 digits.
Where an aliquot has been made, the system will automatically generate a System Reference ID using the original number of the parent source and incrementally increasing the suffix. 

This makes it easy to trace parent and sibling inventory throughout the system. 
For example, a parent inventory item may have a System Reference ID #122-000. The subsequent aliquot will have a System Reference ID of #122-001. A further split that may be sent to waste will have a System Reference ID of #122-002. Therefore it is easy to see at a glance that the aliquots and waste items both relate to an original parent radionuclide.

Reference Date

System Calculated Fields

The system will calculate a value based on the inputs given. 2 inputs are required to calculate the 3rd variable.

Reference Activity + Reference Mass = Specific Activity
Reference Activity + Reference Volume = Activity Concentration
Reference Activity + Activity Concentration = Reference Volume
Reference Activity + Specific Activity = Reference Mass
Reference Mass + Specific Activity = Reference Activity
Reference Volume + Activity Concentration = Reference Activity

Note: it may be that only 1 variable is known, in which case other variables must be input manually when known.

Geological Specimens are held in the Museum of Natural History in the form of “Rocks”. They remain as unsealed sources given that they contain naturally occurring radionuclides for example Thorium and Uranium. They are categorized into two groups:
Group 1:   Combined β+γ dose rate at 30cm from surface less than 2.5 μSv/h
Group 2:   Combined β+γ dose rate at 30cm from surface greater than 2.5 μSv/hn 2.5 μSv/h
At the time of writing, the University of Oxford has 189 Group 2 rocks and 780 Group 1 rocks. They will be migrated into the system electronically via a spreadsheet upload. They will be added to the system using a specific “Geological Specimens” template which is relevant to this data set only.
It is likely that there will be a handful of amendments in any given year. Confirmation of the holdings will be on a monthly basis in line with all University Departments. This is achieved through the “Monthly Possession” reporting.
Create an Aliquot – Split Unsealed Source

Action:
To create an aliquot, select “Split Unsealed Source”

The system will default the action to the current date and time. If required, click into the white space by the date and time and enter an alternative date and time.
The type of aliquot (split) will default to Activity as recorded in MBq. Alternatively it is possible to split by Mass or Volume, depending on how the radionuclide was recorded in the first place. This example shows an aliquot in Activity MBq. Click the dropdown to show the alternative aliquot type. Note: the system will automatically calculate the remaining activity after the aliquot.
Click Submit and the Splitting Results will appear.

Note: a new System Reference ID is created by using the original parent System Reference with an incremental suffix number.

Click on the System Reference ID shown in blue and this will open the Source Profile page for the newly created aliquot.

The profile clearly shows the link back to the parent ID for the aliquot. Click on the Parent ID to return to the Profile page for the Parent source.

The parent source in this example was itself an aliquot of another source, so the Source Profile in this example shows both a parent and a child relationship.
All aliquots (splits) for a source are listed at the bottom of a Source Profile, with an audit trail of when and who made the aliquot, and what is the Profile ID of each aliquot made.

It is possible to create multiple aliquots at a time. Enter the detail for the first aliquot (split), and then click “Add Split”. Another Split box will appear, and the relevant detail can be added.
Note: multiple aliquots created at the same time from this page must be created using the same unit type i.e. all in Activity, Mass or Volume. The aliquots cannot be mixed. To create a subsequent aliquot in a different type, the User must create a new separate split each time.

Note: each aliquot will take identical details from the Parent source in regard to the compound, lab, owner, unique reference etc. If it is required to edit these details, please visit the Source Profile page of the aliquot taken to change the detail.
This shows the result for multiple aliquots created at the same time and that are now added to the Inventory Holdings.

This below shows the Source Profile that demonstrates Source ID 220-002 is itself an aliquot of an original source, and that it now has a relationship with 3 child sources – aliquots.

Create an Aliquot and Send to Waste

There are two types of Waste:
Accumulated Waste – where the University holds waste on the premises under certain conditions for a period of time for a limited time period as defined by the Department limits.
Waste Disposal – that is waste that is disposed of outside of the University of Oxford via a third party such as Grundons. Waste disposal activities are also governed by a set of Department limits.

A Worker may wish to create an aliquot of waste activity as a result of experimentation. 
The waste may be generated as a single activity via an aliquot and sent to a waste container. A whole item of inventory stock may also be sent to a waste container as an individual stock or alongside other whole inventory items.
Action:
To create an aliquot of waste, select “Split Unsealed Source”

Enter the relevant details and click on Submit.

The date and time can be overwritten on this screen, if the detail is being recorded a while after the event. A choice is given to split out an aliquot for waste by Activity, Mass or Volume (depending on how the radionuclide is recorded in the first place).
The system calculates the Activity, Mass or Volume at the point of split and will show the relevant values after split.
Input the value to send to waste.
Tick the check box to “Send to waste”.
Select the Container Option “Existing Container”.

 

Select the Waste Container (bin number) from the Non-Archived section.

The Non-Archived section contains all the bins that are available in the waste store for the Department. In this example, there are two options available – a Blue Solid Low Level waste bin and an Orange Organic Liquid waste bin.
The Non-Archived bins are those that are open and available for selection as storage containers.
Select the Waste type

 

There are 4 possible waste types:
Note: Organic Liquid Waste and Solid Waste will always be added to a waste container and stored in the Department as accumulated waste until a request is made to the Safety Office for it.
Gaseous Waste may be bagged and accumulated if the Department has an accumulation limit to do so. Most often, gaseous waste will be disposed of via the fume hood within the gaseous emissions limits that are set for a Department.
Aqueous Waste may be accumulated in a container and held in a metal drum, usually for a period of no longer than 3 months (or as the limits are defined for the Department). It may also be disposed of directly to drain. Each drain (sink) in a Department will have local protocols as to the type and amount of radionuclide that can be disposed of via the drain. The Department will also have an Overall Departmental limit of Aqueous Waste defined by radionuclide.
Organic Low Level Liquid Waste may be accumulated within a Department in the Orange bin. The maximum storage period of the bin is 12 months.
Solid Low Level Waste may be accumulated within a Department in a bin. The maximum storage period of the bin is 12 months.

Change of State and Dilution of Unsealed Source
It may be necessary to amend a stock through further dilution, thus reducing the activity concentration whilst retaining the reference activity, and/or to alter the state i.e. a liquid form is turned into a solid state.
The following example reviews how to change the state of a source from powder to a solution.
Identify the Inventory stock to make into a solution. 
The value will currently be recorded in grams with a compound mass.

 

In put the volume of the solution either in ml or μL and note the system will calculate the reference volume.
Click update to save the record.
Note: the record will retain the values in mass as well as the values in volume. This will allow the user to take any subsequent aliquots from this source in either mass or volume, thus allowing for calculation with multiple states as necessitates.
 
Note: the source profile will always return the units to display in summary as MBq with mg and μL. 

 Waste Management
Bin Inventory
All bins are referred to in the Odyssey system as Waste Containers and may have a status of “opened”, “closed” or “archived”. Bins are held in the Safety Office Department until a request is made for a new bin, where it is then shipped to the Department in a “closed status”. It was agreed that all bins are shipped in a “closed status” in order that the Department will control which bin is open and in which lab. Some Departments have a number of bins that remain in their local storage until they are ready to use them. Other Departments may have only 1 or 2 bins which may be open in a lab until they are ready to be closed and collected by the Safety Office.

Cardinus Data Import Process (Updated – Automated)
The data import process into Cardinus is now fully automated, replacing the previous manual extraction and processing approach.
Current Process
User data is extracted directly from PeopleXD.
The data is processed and transformed by the University’s Azure team to ensure compatibility with Cardinus.
The processed file is automatically transferred and uploaded to Cardinus via SFTP.
This process runs on a scheduled basis every Wednesday at 4:00am.
Key Features
No manual intervention required: The previous use of Excel processing, and CSV preparation has been retired.
Improved consistency and accuracy: Automated transformation reduces the risk of discrepancies caused by manual handling.
Regular synchronisation: Weekly automated updates ensure that user records are kept up to date.
Data Management Notes
The SSO (format: xxxx1234@ox.ac.uk) remains the unique identifier for users in Cardinus.
Any users present in Cardinus but not included in the latest automated file will continue to be archived automatically.
The process ensures that all active users are maintained, while leavers are appropriately removed. This is of course now reliant on PeopleXD being accurate. 
Process Improvements
Eliminates the need for: 
Manual reconciliation of affiliations and email addresses
Department filtering and validation in Excel
File formatting and concatenation steps
Manual uploads via FileZilla
Reduces risk of large-scale import errors associated with manual processing.
Removes the requirement for the “Pre Cardinus Date” field.

﻿Summary of Roles in Cardinus

Authorisation levels available in Cardinus:

DSE Coordinator 
Role Description
No longer inviting/monitoring/chasing DSE Completion. This role will apply to those departments where there are multiple assessors who traditionally work reactively so are not aware of a definitive list of ppl in their remit. Rather than coordinating employees to complete their assessments, they will be coordinating the assessors. 
Functionality needed
PACE Access to view the list of staff in their section and ability to assign assessors to users. Possibly reporting needs to analyse completion rate
Recommend Auth Level: Sub Administrator
DSE Assessor
Role Description
Access to departmental lists in Cardinus. Can view all assessments but will be focussing on those assessments with risks that need advice, further equipment purchasing. Some assessors will need input from DSE Coordinator/DSO to identify those staff they are responsible for.
Functionality Needed
PACE Access to view the list of staff in their PACS section and ability to assign themselves to users or assign other assessors to users.
Recommended Auth Level: Assessor
Departmental Safety Officer

Role Description
Overseeing completion rates for their PACS level 3 areas which constitute their department. The role will serve to offer second line of support after DSE Coordinators to assessors who work reactively and are unsure of who is in their remit.
 Functionality Needed
PACE Access to view the list of staff in their PACS section and reporting functionality.

Recommend Auth Level: Sub Administrator

Divisional Safety Officer
Role Description
Overseeing completion rates for division-wide PACS DSE places.
Functionality Needed
PACE Access to view dashboards for their division and ability to break it down by department.
Recommend Auth Level: Sub Administrator
Safety Office Admin Team
Role Description
Sending out invitations to employees to complete DSE Assessment, 
Functionality Needed
Changing auth levels of staff in the system and what departments they can view.
Recommended Auth Level: Master Administrator

Cardinus Import Process 
Version Control 
Version Date Comments 
0.1 06/02/26 Initial Draft including options 
   
 
  
Data import to Cardinus 
Kye Maddox produces a huge list of ppl data from Work Tribe- separated into CUD and OAK users. 
Ray Stacey uses Alteryx to process this data and create a flat txt file.  It rationalises multiple 
affiliations and email addresses but due to the complexity of the data, there are some 
discrepancies. E.g if a dept name is different in the source data from the PACS structure, it doesn’t 
import those users. 
Txt file is sent to RW listing these fields which are needed for Import to Cardinus: 
 
 
Tasks to then prepare csv file for Cardinus: 
1. Remove any commas 
 
2. Save file locally as a csv. 
 
3. Reopen csv file in excel and delimit according to ¦ so that you can filter on the department 
columns. 
 
4. Remove any records with no department information in each of the 3 PACS columns. 
 
5. Remove any records for those PACS departments not in scope for Cardinus. 
These are: 
Subsidiary Companies 
Said Business School/OSBS Ltd 
Other 
 
6. Add extra column on file called Last Assessment Date Pre Cardinus. V -Lookup to “Last 
Assessment date” spreadsheet from old DSE system and return the date in the format “dd 
mmm yyyy” 
 
7. Concatenate all the columns in this file into one column with | as the separator  
 
8. Paste into new document as values:  and save this as a CSV . 
 
9. Check a few rows from different points in the spreadsheet that SSO, Name, Department 
and email address are correct and lined up against the right people. 
 
10. The file can now be uploaded to Cardinus using Filezilla. 
 
 
 
 
 

Notes: 
 
Any names already in Cardinus but not in the latest file will be archived in Cardinus.  This is why 
each import file has to have all active users listed and not just additions. 
 
The unique id column (SSO in the format xxxx1234@ox.ac.uk) is the main look-up column in this 
import process. You can have identical names/depts/email addresses but not the SSO. 
 
Now we have completed roll out across the departments, there is probably no further need to 
include “Pre Cardinus Date” look up in the process. 
 
 
Short Term Options 
1. Stop any more data imports and have new starters added manually as and when by Safety 
Office 
 
• Existing entries in system won’t be open to import errors. 
• Likely too burdensome for Safety Office to manage. 
• Numbers of active users in the system will gradually increase as there will be no 
archiving of leavers. 
 
2. Request lists of new starters to be appended to the previous import file and re -import 
each month. 
 
• Existing entries in system won’t be open to import errors. 
• Potentially less labour intensive than processing a whole new list of 20,000 names 
each month. 
• Who would carry out this process? 
• Numbers of active users in the system will gradually increase as there will be no 
archiving of leavers. 
 
 
3. Carry on with monthly import following steps above. 
 
• Who would carry out this process? 
• Number of active users in the system will be managed so leavers will be 
automatically archived. 
• Potential for import errors affecting thousands of user records in Cardinus.
